title: John Spytek: Fernando Mendoza passed every test, allowed us to make a hard decision
summary: It took longer than it has for most quarterbacks drafted first overall, but Fernando Mendoza's time has come in Las Vegas.
full_text: ''' It took longer than it has for most quarterbacks drafted first overall, but Fernando Mendoza's time has come in Las Vegas. Tuesday's trade of Kirk Cousins means that Mendoza is now the No. 1 quarterback for the Raiders and he'll make his first NFL start in Sunday's game against the Seahawks. The Raiders went into the season determined to give Mendoza as much time as possible to learn from Cousins and their 4-5 start made it possible to stick with the plan rather than turn attention to the future. The move would have waited a little while longer if the Vikings were not motivated buyers in the wake of Monday night's disastrous performance against the Bills, but General Manager John Spytek said at a Tuesday press conference that the trade would not have happened without Mendoza showing the team that he's ready. “It’s something that he’s worked very hard for since the moment he walked into this building," Spytek said. "He passed every test. I want to stop short of saying he’s earned it, but he put us in a position where we had to make a really hard decision today with his growth as a person, as a teammate, as a leader, as a quarterback." While the Raiders feel Mendoza is ready, it is a big change to go from the practice field to game action and the Seahawks are a tough first opponent for the rookie. The Raiders drafted Mendoza to be their leader, however, and head coach Klint Kubiak said Mendoza has "exceeded those expectations" while learning from a good teacher. "I think with the right role model that will accelerate his growth and we had, you know, we had the right role model," Kubiak said. Becoming the starter is just the beginning for Mendoza and it kicks off an era the Raiders hope will bring them back to the upper rungs of the AFC in the years to come.
author: Josh Alper

title: Fran Tarkenton raves about Kirk Cousins's return to Minnesota
summary: On Monday night, I was explaining to my wife the bizarre situation in Minnesota, where a championship-caliber defense has been paired with an offense that would have trouble scoring a touchdown in the lower divisions of college football.
full_text: ''' On Monday night, I was explaining to my wife the bizarre situation in Minnesota, where a championship-caliber defense has been paired with an offense that would have trouble scoring a touchdown in the lower divisions of college football. She said, "Is Fran Tarkenton still around?" Actually, he is. And the end result to the expedited search came from the Tarkenton playbook: The Vikings brought back a former Vikings quarterback in trading with the Raiders for Kirk Cousins. On Tuesday, Tarkenton gushed about the return of Cousins. "I think it's the greatest thing that could have happened to us ," Tarkenton told Darren Wolfson of KSTP. "We were lost. We were winning on defense. We had no offense. We had no quarterback. And now we've got Kirk coming back, who is having a great year. He's a great player. He's a better person than player. Our team should lift up now. And we're in the best division in football. Our defense has kept us in the hunt. "And having Kirk — I cannot tell you how happy I am for the Vikings, for the fans, for the Wilfs, and for all the players and the old-timers like myself. We've got a chance with Kirk Cousins." Tarkenton spent 1961 through 1966 with the Vikings before returning from 1972 through 1978. And, as it turns out, his comments about Cousins weren't the only news he made this week. Tarkenton apparently earned a mere $1.2 million during his entire 18-year NFL career. But that was just the starting point. He has amassed enough of a fortune in the business world to recently buy — at age 86 — a $51.89 million home in Palm Beach . Tarkenton blazed the trail for today's former quarterbacks who work even harder in retirement. He was the first NFL player to host Saturday Night Live , and his TV career included a co-hosting gig on That's Incredible and a four-year stint in the Monday Night Football booth. The big money came in the business world, specifically computer software. He also has made many millions as an early investor in Apple. And, if you watch the clip, you'll see that Tarkenton still has a verbal and mental fastball. The return of Cousins definitely conjures memories of Tarkenton's second act in Minnesota, which resulted in three Super Bowl appearances. The Vikings would be thrilled if, with Cousins back in the fold, they could manage just one.
author: Mike Florio

title: Jonah Jackson on Luke Goedeke's grievances: "This is football, man"
summary: After Sunday night's game between the Buccaneers and Bears, Tampa Bay tackle Luke Goedeke had some grievances to air about Chicago defensive tackle Jeffery Simmons.
full_text: After Sunday night's game between the Buccaneers and Bears, Tampa Bay tackle Luke Goedeke had some grievances to air about Chicago defensive tackle Jeffery Simmons. Bears guard Jonah Jackson was unpersuaded by Goedeke's complaints about Simmons launching himself at and/or holding Bucs linemen. "The guys on his team tried to launch themselves at us on every play ," Jackson said on 104.3 The Score. "I don't know any different. That's on him how he feels. It is what it is. This is football, man. Especially in the trenches. It gets rough and rowdy. . . . Did you see that big guy, number 50 [Vita Vea], launching at us? . . . It is what it is. We signed up for this." As to Simmons holding Goedeke, Jackson was equally blunt. "They all do it. It is what it is. You've got find ways to combat it," he said. It really is anything goes when it comes to line play, subject to what the officials see and are willing to call. Especially when there are so many uncalled holding penalties on offensive linemen, arguably since defensive ends are so good and the powers-that-be prefer to keep quarterbacks in one piece. The best, most recent example of that came in Carolina on Sunday, on the play when Broncos linebacker Nik Bonitto forced a fumble by Panthers quarterback Bryce Young to seal the game. Bonitto was being held the entire play . And he still got it done. That's the message for all offensive and defensive linemen. Do whatever you have to do to get it done. It's only a foul if a flag is thrown.
author: Mike Florio

title: Rams more likely to miss the playoffs than make the playoffs, according to betting odds
summary: After opening the season as the betting favorites to win the Super Bowl, the Rams are now underdogs to make the playoffs.
full_text: The Rams entered the season as the overwhelming favorites to win the Super Bowl. As the dust settles on the NFL trade deadline, the Rams are now not even favored to make the playoffs. The latest betting odds have the Rams as -130 favorites to miss the playoffs, and +110 underdogs to make the playoffs. That represents a massive shift from before the season, when the Rams were -500 favorites to make the playoffs, the best playoff odds of any team in the league. The Rams are a disappointing 5-4, and if the playoffs started today they'd be a game behind the Packers for the third and final NFC playoff spot. They're also 2.5 games behind the 49ers in the NFC West race. Perhaps more importantly, injuries are mounting for the Rams, with the latest big one being that wide receiver Puka Nacua is heading to injured reserve, where he'll join Davante Adams, as Matthew Stafford is running out of healthy receivers. If the Rams get healthy and make the playoffs, they'll be a major threat to any postseason opponent, which is why they still have the seventh-best odds in the league to win the Super Bowl at +1300. But as the 49ers pull away in the NFC West, and the NFC wild card race looks increasingly competitive, the Rams' chances of being in it in January are dwindling.
author: Michael David Smith

title: Aaron Rodgers is one win away from tying Drew Brees for fourth-most of all time
summary: The Steelers' next win will give Rodgers 181 in his career, counting the playoffs, the same number as Brees.
full_text: If the Steelers beat the Bengals on Monday night, Aaron Rodgers will move into a tie for fourth time on the NFL's all-time wins list. Rodgers' teams have won 180 games he has started, counting the playoffs. His next win will give him No. 181, the same number Drew Brees retired with, and the fourth most of all time. The only quarterbacks in NFL history who have won more starts are Tom Brady with a preposterous 286 wins, Peyton Manning with 200 and Brett Favre with 199. Rodgers has said this will be his last NFL season, so he won't catch Favre for third place. Rodgers won 158 games as starting quarterback for the Packers, six with the Jets and has now won 16 with the Steelers.
author: Michael David Smith

title: CBA allows 49ers to not pay Brandon Aiyuk during two-week roster exemption
summary: When unusual situations emerge in the NFL, it becomes a piece-by-piece exercise in figuring out the specific rules that apply.
full_text: ' When unusual situations emerge in the NFL, it becomes a piece-by-piece exercise in figuring out the specific rules that apply. And few situations have been more unusual than 49ers receiver Brandon Aiyuk's odyssey of the past year. He's back on the 49ers, at a salary of $13.75 million for the rest of the season. That fact pointed to the 49ers releasing him by 4:00 p.m. ET on Tuesday, in order to avoid owing him one-ninth of the total amount ($1.52 million) for Week 10. But here's where yet another obscure wrinkle applies. Under Article 20, Section 4 of the Collective Bargaining Agreement, the 49ers owe Aiyuk nothing during his two-week roster exemption. From the relevant provision: "If a Club obtains a roster exemption for a player under contract who does not report to his Club at least five days before the final day of Preseason Training Camp as defined in Article 23, Section 10, the player will not be entitled to preseason or regular season compensation until such exemption is removed, provided the player is given written notice of such fact upon reporting to the Club. If such notice is not given to the player, the player must be paid his Paragraph 5 Salary during his exemption." So if the 49ers gave Aiyuk written notice that he won't be paid during the two-week roster exemption (and they surely did), they don't have to pay him. Which pushes their deadline for avoiding owing him a game check until Tuesday, November 24 — one day after the expiration of the exemption. Why not just cut him? The 49ers are delaying the move because they can, postponing by up to two weeks his passage through waivers and, given his salary, inevitable free agency. In the interim, he's on the team. But Aiyuk won't be reporting for work on Wednesday. He has been excused, we're told, from team activities and he's working out on his own. The 49ers could release him at any moment. There's no reason not to do so, other than to apply the brakes to his ability to join another team. The circumstances counter the notion that he was reinstated by the league subject to any type of agreement with the 49ers. If that had happened, the agreement surely would have included a requirement that the 49ers promptly cut him. Which means that the NFL, after apparently working with the 49ers to delay Aiyuk's reinstatement in order to help the 49ers recover bonus money from Aiyuk, finally decided that reinstatement from the reserve/left squad list can't be delayed in order to advance a team's strategic objectives. So, yes, Aiyuk eventually will be released. He wasn't released today because the 49ers don't owe him a game check for Week 10, or for Week 11. Eventually, when the roster exemption expires, they'll cut him. For now, the team's delay in doing the inevitable points to a desire to keep another team from getting him, sticking it to Aiyuk, or some of both. It's petty, but the 49ers have the power to do it.
author: Mike Florio

title: Nick Sirianni denies giving subtle middle finger to fans
summary: After Sunday's loss to the Giants — Philadelphia's seventh loss in a row — a video emerged of Eagles coach Nick Sirianni leaving the field, along with Dom DiSandro.
full_text: After Sunday's loss to the Giants — Philadelphia's seventh loss in a row — a video emerged of Eagles coach Nick Sirianni leaving the field, along with Dom DiSandro. It appeared, based on the manner in which Sirianni manipulated the fingers on his right hand, that he sent a one-fingered message to those who were heckling him. Sirianni was asked about the apparent gesture during a Monday press conference. "When [senior vice president of communications] Bob [Lange] told me that, absolutely not," Sirianni replied. "That was a surprise to me, but absolutely not." Frankly, what else would Sirianni say? "Yes, it was a middle finger." If he admits it, he'll be fined — and the precedent for coaches is $100,000 . Beyond that, why would anyone believe him? Last Friday, Sirianni admitted that he misled reporters regarding the team's supposed commitment to quarterback Tanner McKee. There's one other relevant factor, based on my own personal experience. My dad used to use that exact same move, during periodic verbal household disagreements with my mom. I saw it. She never did. But that was the move. And, if she'd seen it, he would have denied it. Just like Sirianni did.
author: Mike Florio

title: In Kirk Cousins, the Vikings landed their first choice
summary: After last night's abysmal performance by the offense against the Bills, the Vikings mobilized to trade for a quarterback.
full_text: ''' After last night's abysmal performance by the offense against the Bills, the Vikings mobilized to trade for a quarterback. Ultimately, they got the guy they wanted. Per a source with knowledge of the situation, Kirk Cousins was Minnesota's first choice. The Vikings explored other options. Multiple players, including fellow former Vikings quarterback Daniel Jones. Cousins's history with the team makes it easier to get him up to speed. He had 25 regular-season games with coach Kevin O'Connell, and four seasons with receiver Justin Jefferson. The existence of options may have helped the Vikings keep the compensation to only a third-round pick. Given the level of desperation, the Vikings seemed destined to give up more than that to fix a problem that threatened to implode the season. That's not an overstatement. The dam was breaking. Frustration was rampant during the debacle against the Bills, on both sides of the ball. It was a simple proposition. If the Vikings didn't trade for a quarterback on Tuesday, they could not be considered a serious franchise. In the end, they managed to stop the bleeding by sending their third-round pick (their own, not the one they acquired from the Eagles for defensive end Jonathan Greenard) to the Raiders for Cousins. It's unclear how much better things will be with Cousins back in the fold. It can't get worse than what they put on the field for Week 9.
author: Mike Florio

title: Jaguars-Ravens averages 13.96 million on Prime Video
summary: When it comes to interpreting press releases regarding the audiences for sporting events, there's a rule of thumb.
full_text: When it comes to interpreting press releases regarding the audiences for sporting events, there's a rule of thumb. The higher the number appears in the release, the better the company thinks the audience is. The lower the number appears in the release, the less impactful the figure is. And if the number is really bad, there's no release at all. For the Week 9 Thursday night game between the Jaguars and Ravens— which was destined to have a non-stellar audience thanks to the Ravens being down to their third-string quarterback — Prime Video led with the fact that the eight-game season-to-date average has outperformed last year's numbers. The 33-10 win by the Jaguars, which Prime Video accurately called "lopsided" in the release, generated an average of 13.96 million viewers. It nevertheless was, as Prime Video notes, a 13-percent bump over last year's Week 9 Thursday night game. And for good reason. The Week 9 Thursday night game in 2025 featured the Ravens at the Dolphins, a 28-6 Baltimore win. Even with an audience of less than 14 million in the eighth TNF game of the season, the package is offering 17.15 million per week for 2026. This week's game — Commanders at Giants — should do well, given that the Giants are both doing well and occupy the nation's top market. In Week 11, it's Colts at Texans. Which won't be great. The following week, Prime Video has a potentially massive game on Black Friday between the currently 7-2 Broncos and 6-2 Steelers. After that, it's Chiefs-Rams, Vikings-Patriots, 49ers-Chargers, Texans-Eagles (on Christmas Eve), and Ravens-Bengals.
author: Mike Florio

title: John Spytek: First "real" call on Kirk Cousins came this morning
summary: As NFL trades slip into hibernation until March, it's important to remember something the next time players can be sent from one team to another.
full_text: ''' As NFL trades slip into hibernation until March, it's important to remember something the next time players can be sent from one team to another. Teams push plenty of BS to the media — and the media often passes it along without scrutiny. Case in point: The internally inconsistent claim made by ESPN on Saturday, undoubtedly based on information straight from the Raiders. "As of this weekend," Adam Schefter of ESPN tweeted, "the Raiders had not received any trade inquiries regarding their starting quarterback Kirk Cousins, nor are they interested in dealing him , per league sources. They plan to keep sticking with him until they believe their No. 1 overall pick Fernando Mendoza is ready." So the Raiders hadn't received any trade inquiries, but they weren't interested in the trade inquiries they hadn't received? Right. In a press conference with reporters on Tuesday, Raiders G.M. John Spytek addressed how it all came to be. "I never made one call on Kirk Cousins," Spytek said. "And I got a few phone calls. But one real one this morning." The "real one" ultimately entailed getting a third-round pick for Cousins. Which further highlights how silly it is for a team to claim — and for the media to share — the idea that "WE'RE NOT INTERESTED." Everyone is interested in a trade offer for all but a small handful of players in the entire league. Anything else is posturing. And, as is often the case when it comes to NFL reporting, the insiders allow themselves to become extensions of the team's P.R. department in an effort to send a given message. The Raiders weren't interested, until they were. And it didn't take all that much to make them interested in giving up their starting quarterback. It was easier to make the decision because they were surely thinking about when to bench him for rookie Fernando Mendoza. And it surely was easier for Cousins to embrace the trade, given that he's now in a position to keep playing for a team that has a chance to get to the postseason and to make some noise in January.
author: Mike Florio

title: Raiders sign DL Tim Keenan to the active roster from the practice squad
summary: The Raiders traded quarterback Kirk Cousins to the Vikings, leaving an open roster spot.
full_text: ' The Raiders traded quarterback Kirk Cousins to the Vikings, leaving an open roster spot. They filled it by signing rookie defensive lineman Tim Keenan to the 53-player roster from the practice squad. Keenan was out of elevations from the practice squad after the Raiders elevated him for the past three games. In three games, Keenan totaled seven tackles and a sack while playing 35 percent of the snaps. The Rams selected Keenan in the seventh round this year out of Alabama. They waived him out of the preseason, but he signed back to their practice squad. The Raiders signed him to their practice squad on Sept. 7. The team also announced it signed defensive tackle Chris Williams to the practice squad.
author: Charean Williams

title: Commanders upgrade WR Treylon Burks to limited practice participation
summary: Commanders wide receiver Treylon Burks missed last Sunday's loss to the Rams with a foot injury, but he's moving toward a return to the lineup.
full_text: Commanders wide receiver Treylon Burks missed last Sunday's loss to the Rams with a foot injury, but he's moving toward a return to the lineup. Burks was upgraded to limited practice participation on Tuesday. The Commanders only held a walkthrough, so that's an estimated level of work but it's still a positive sign for Burks's chances of returning against the Giants on Thursday night. Burks has 12 catches for 233 yards and two touchdowns this season. Center Lucas Patrick (concussion) and tight end Colson Yankoff (knee) were listed as out for the second straight day. Head coach Dan Quinn said earlier in the day that Nick Allegretti will start at center on Thursday. Tight end John Bates (shoulder), quarterback Jayden Daniels (left elbow), center Matt Gulbin (knee), tight end Chig Okonkwo (hip), cornerback Amik Robertson (ankle), and defensive lineman Shy Tuttle (shoulder) were all listed as full participants.
author: Josh Alper

title: Malik Nabers: I felt like it was a lie for Fox broadcast to attack my character
summary: "Don't tell the world something that's not me."
full_text: '' Giants wide receiver Malik Nabers elaborated on his issues with comments made about him during last Sunday's Fox broadcast during a press conference on Tuesday. Fox announcers Joe Davis, Greg Olsen, and Pam Oliver discussed Nabers's body language at several points during the game and shots of an agitated Nabers on the sideline were shown multiple times. Davis was particularly critical about Nabers's response to a touchdown by teammate Isaiah Likely and Olsen said in response that "there's a very fine line between being demanding, being a competitor, and all those great things" before adding that Nabers has "just got to keep it in check." Nabers responded to those comments and misattributed quotes that claimed Olsen called him a bad teammate in a social media post after the 19-11 win over the Eagles. Nabers said the broadcast tried to "create a narrative" that wasn't true and shared more thoughts on the matter Tuesday. "I just feel like the narrative on me is always all the bad body language things that people have been saying about me," Nabers said, via a transcript from the team. "But as far as that, if it's a problem with anybody, the cameras can stay off me. The thing about it is, don't tell the world something that's not me. I'm [going to] speak up for myself all the time because there's nobody else that's going to be able to speak up for me. So, I'm going to use my own voice and be able to speak up about me being a bad teammate. And I felt like that was just a lie, just attacking my character as a football player and as a teammate. Like I said, I've never been on a team where anyone has called me a bad teammate that I know of." Olsen took issue with the incorrect quotes about Nabers being a bad teammate and the wideout was asked if he's heard from directly from him since Sunday. Nabers said he hasn't, but "he can reach out and we can have a simple conversation." Beyond that, Nabers said he's done talking about the subject and that he's moved on to Thursday's game against the Commanders.
author: Josh Alper

title: Cardinals place QB Gardner Minshew and WR Michael Wilson on IR
summary: The Cardinals placed quarterback Gardner Minshew and wide receiver Michael Wilson on injured reserve Tuesday, the team announced.
full_text: The Cardinals placed quarterback Gardner Minshew and wide receiver Michael Wilson on injured reserve Tuesday, the team announced. Minshew tore the UCL in his elbow and will miss the rest of the season. Wilson's neck injury will end his season. "Not the ending I had envisioned, but grateful for the journey," Wilson wrote on social media. "Regardless of what happens, my love for the game will never change! Thank you for all the love and support. The story is still being written." Wilson played eight games in 2026, making 51 receptions for 546 yards and two touchdowns. In two appearances, Minshew completed 38 of 53 passes for 354 yards and three touchdowns, and led the Cardinals to an overtime win in Dallas in Week 8. He is scheduled to be a free agent at the end of the season. The Cardinals signed veteran quarterback Josh Johnson and rookie quarterback Joey Aguilar to back up rookie Carson Beck. Beck will get his first NFL start on Sunday against the Rams. Aguilar was on the Jaguars' practice squad, and Johnson was on the Bengals' practice squad. The Cardinals also signed receiver Phillip Dorsett II to the practice squad and released tight end Rivaldo Fairweather and running back Jermar Jefferson from the practice squad.
author: Charean Williams

title: Ravens release TE Nick Vannett, waive G Kyle Hergel
summary: The Ravens parted ways with guard Andrew Vorhees in a trade with the Falcons on Tuesday and they also cut a couple of other players from the active roster.
full_text: The Ravens parted ways with guard Andrew Vorhees in a trade with the Falcons on Tuesday and they also cut a couple of other players from the active roster. They announced that they have released tight end Nick Vannett and guard Kyle Hergel. They did not make any corresponding signings, but they did add center Ryan Neuzil in the Vorhees trade. Vannett played in the Ravens' last five games and made three starts. He was used primarily as a blocker during his time in Baltimore and did not catch any passes. The 11-year veteran has 108 catches for 1,012 yards and nine touchdowns over his entire career. Hergel made one appearance for the Ravens and played two special teams snaps.
author: Josh Alper

title: 49ers put DT Gracen Halton on IR
summary: 49ers rookie defensive tackle Gracen Halton was placed on injured reserve on Tuesday.
full_text: ' 49ers rookie defensive tackle Gracen Halton was placed on injured reserve on Tuesday. The team's announcement of the move did not come as any surprise. Halton broke his ankle in last Sunday's win over the Raiders and he will miss the rest of the season as a result. Halton joined the 49ers as a fourth-round pick in April. He started six of the team's first eight games and ends his rookie season with 15 tackles, five tackles for loss, two sacks, a forced fumble and a fumble recovery for a touchdown. DeForest Buckner, Osa Odighizuwa, Sebastian Valdez, and James Thompson are the remaining defensive tackles on the 49ers' roster.
author: Josh Alper

title: Cam Skattebo on Giants not adding a running back: They know what I can do
summary: Cam Skattebo is set to return to the Giants lineup for Thursday night's game against the Commanders and he won't be looking over his shoulder at any new additions to the team's running back depth chart.
full_text: '' Cam Skattebo is set to return to the Giants lineup for Thursday night's game against the Commanders and he won't be looking over his shoulder at any new additions to the team's running back depth chart. The Giants were reportedly bidders for Jonathan Taylor at one point and they were linked to other potential moves in the backfield, but they stood pat on deadline day. Skattebo said on Tuesday that he understands why some would be "skeptical" that the Giants have enough at running back while citing his average of around 60 rushing yards per game, but that he wasn't bothered by any interest the Giants had in other backs because "they know what I can do" “You’ve seen what I can do ,” Skattebo said, via Darryl Slater of NJ.com. “When I come out and I’m ready to play football, I can be one of the most dangerous backs in the league. Simple as that.” Skattebo was up to full practice participation Tuesday after missing Week 9 with a hamstring injury, so he should have every opportunity to prove himself right about what he's capable of doing for the Giants offense.
author: Josh Alper

title: Vikings release WR Odell Beckham Jr., but will re-sign him to the practice squad
summary: The Vikings terminated the contract of wide receiver Odell Beckham Jr. on Tuesday, the team announced.
full_text: ''' The Vikings terminated the contract of wide receiver Odell Beckham Jr. on Tuesday, the team announced. The team needed a roster spot for Kirk Cousins after the trade with Las Vegas. The Vikings will re-sign Beckham to the practice squad, according to multiple reports. Beckham made his Vikings debut on Monday after signing from Minnesota's practice squad but played only two snaps. The Vikings previously elevated Beckham from the practice squad in Week 5, but he did not appear in the game against the Saints. The Vikings also announced they released guard C.J. Hanson and tackle Corey Robinson II from their practice squad.
author: Charean Williams

title: Dolphins place QB Malik Willis on IR with core muscle injury
summary: The Dolphins placed quarterback Malik Willis on injured reserve, the team announced.
full_text: ''' The Dolphins placed quarterback Malik Willis on injured reserve, the team announced. Willis has had a groin injury that has limited his mobility, and an MRI showed it developed into a core muscle injury, Tom Pelissero of The Ringer reports. Pelissero said the injury is not season-ending. The Dolphins have Kyle McCord behind Willis, along with Brady Cook on the practice squad. McCord, a sixth-round pick of the Eagles in 2025, has never seen action in a regular-season game. He presumably will start Sunday's game against the Colts. Willis will miss at least four games before returning. He has a 58.2 percent completion percentage for 1,396 yards with six touchdowns and six interceptions. The Dolphins also announced they placed defensive lineman Zach Sieler on injured reserve and waived cornerback Reese Taylor.
author: Charean Williams

title: 2026 NFL Trade Deadline live updates: Tracker, deals, news, rumors, analysis
summary: Jordan Davis, Jeffery Simmons, DeForest Buckner, Quenton Nelson and more big-name NFL players are on the move.
full_text: '' The NFL trade deadline is at 4 p.m. ET on Tuesday, November 10, and PFT has you covered with news and analysis of every trade, potential trade, rumor of a trade and trade that won’t be happening. Here’s what’s happening on the NFL trade front: Kirk Cousins to Vikings : Cousins is returning to Minnesota , while the Vikings are sending a 2027 third-round pick to Las Vegas. Falcons and Ravens swap offensive linemen : Baltimore acquired offensive lineman Ryan Neuzil in exchange for offensive lineman Andrew Vorhees and a 2028 sixth-round pick. Josh Downs to Chiefs : The Colts have traded Downs to the Chiefs for 2027 fourth- and fifth-round picks, with the Colts also throwing in a 2027 seventh-round pick. Daiyan Henley to Broncos : The Chargers have traded Henley to the Broncos for a 2027 fourth-round pick and a 2028 fifth-round pick. Keenan Allen to San Francisco : The Colts traded Allen to the 49ers for a sixth-round pick. Amani Hooker to Buffalo : The Bills will second a second-round pick to the Titans for Hooker and a fifth. Jordan Davis to Jacksonville : The Eagles traded Davis to the Jaguars for a 2027 first-round pick and a 2029 second-round pick. The Bengals won't trade for Eagles pass rusher Arnold Ebiketie : The deal was agreed upon, but it was called off after its impact on the compensatory draft pick formula came to light. Will the Vikings trade for a quarterback? Coach Kevin O'Connell says he’ll defer to GM Nolan Teasley. Giants are looking to add : John Harbaugh is prioritizing now over the future . Will the Cowboys make any deadline deals? Team owner Jerry Jones doesn't see anything " significant " happening in Dallas. Falcons agree to trade S Jessie Bates to the Jaguars : The Falcons will pick up most of Bates's remaining salary in exchange for a 2027 second-round pick and a 2028 fifth-rounder. Saints agree to trade DT Davon Godchaux to the Jaguars : The Jaguars doubled down on defensive additions. Jets send Andre Cisco to Lions : The Lions are sending the Jets a 2028 sixth-round pick . Bengals won't make a trade : Zac Taylor says they’re good where they are . Jonathan Taylor trade appears likely : The Colts are expected to take the best offer they get for Taylor. Jets LB Will McDonald requests a trade : The 2023 first-round pick would like to be on a new team. Colts may trade more players : Indianapolis has told teams it wants more than a fourth-round pick for Josh Downs . Jonathan Taylor and Daniel Jones could both be traded, perhaps both to the Vikings . Jacoby Brissett is headed to Baltimore : The Ravens and Cardinals announced a deal sending the veteran quarterback and a 2027 fifth-round pick to the Ravens for a 2027 fourth-round pick and a 2028 seventh-round pick. Derrick Henry says he's not thinking about changing teams : The Ravens star expressed a desire to help the team improve after a fourth-straight loss. Jonathan Taylor wants to know where he'll finish the season : Taylor said no one likes uncertainty when asked about talk that the Colts will trade him. Chargers say they're not trading Khalil Mack : Chargers coach Jim Harbaugh said, " I want Khalil Mack to be here and Khalil Mack wants to be here ." Jeffery Simmons to Bears : Chicago receives Simmons and a 2028 fifth-round pick. Tennessee will receive 2027 and 2028 first-round picks along with a fourth-round pick in 2027. Quenton Nelson to Seahawks : The Seahawks will send a 2027 third-round pick and a 2028 fifth-round pick back to Indianapolis. DeForest Buckner to 49ers : Indianapolis will receive a 2027 fourth-round pick from San Francisco. Jonathan Taylor trade talks have picked up : The Colts may not be done making deals. The Jets have reportedly rebuffed Garrett Wilson trade interest : The Jets are not expected to deal their top wideout. The Colts are open for business : Indianapolis is building for the future after firing General Manager Chris Ballard. Jonathan Taylor hasn’t requested a trade. Josh Downs says he's " open to whatever. " Budda Baker's name surfaces in trade rumors : Baker says he hasn’t asked to be traded from Arizona and also hasn't asked not to be traded. Brian Thomas is a name to watch : The Jaguars trading Thomas frequently comes up in trade rumors . Garrett Wilson wants to remain a Jet : The talented receiver says he is hoping not to get traded .
author: Michael David Smith

title: Rams bring back WR Xavier Smith, sign him off 49ers practice squad
summary: The Rams did not bring in a receiver via trade before the deadline, but they have acquired one who knows their system.
full_text: The Rams did not bring in a receiver via trade before the deadline, but they have acquired one who knows their system. Los Angeles announced on Tuesday that the club has signed Xavier Smith off of San Francisco's practice squad. The Rams previously let go of Smith earlier in the season. He had been serving as the team’s primary returner with poor results. Last season, Smith appeared in 16 games for the Rams, catching 18 passes for 303 yards. L.A. needs depth at receiver with both Puka Nacua and Davante Adams on injured reserve and Jordan Whittington also being placed on IR as a corresponding move to add Smith. Tight end Terrance Ferguson is also dealing with a hamstring injury, further limiting the team’s pass catchers.
author: Myles Simmons

title: Report: Cowboys to sign RB Kendre Miller to the practice squad
summary: The Cowboys are expected to sign running back Kendre Miller to the practice squad, Joseph Hoyt of the Dallas Morning News reports.
full_text: ' The Cowboys are expected to sign running back Kendre Miller to the practice squad, Joseph Hoyt of the Dallas Morning News reports. He visited the team facility today after the Saints cut him last week. The Cowboys need depth at the position, with Tyler Goodson expected to miss multiple weeks with a knee injury. Fullback Hunter Luepke is the only player behind starting running back Javonte Williams on the active roster. Israel Abanikanda and Jashaun Corbin are on the practice squad, and it is unclear whether the Cowboys will cut one of them to sign Goodson. Miller had 57 carries for 159 yards and two touchdowns in six games for New Orleans this season. The 2023 third-round pick had 184 carries for 656 yards and five touchdowns during his injury-plagued run with the Saints. He also caught 29 passes for 217 yards.
author: Charean Williams

title: Ravens trade for OL Ryan Neuzil, send OL Andrew Vorhees to Falcons
summary: The Falcons and Ravens executed one last trade before the 4 p.m.
full_text: The Falcons and Ravens executed one last trade before the 4 p.m. ET deadline. Baltimore has acquired offensive lineman Ryan Neuzil in exchange for offensive lineman Andrew Vorhees and a 2028 sixth-round pick. Neuzil is in the final year of his contract. He's primarily played center for Atlanta, which could signal a move back to guard for Cam Jurgens, who the Ravens also recently acquired. Baltimore has been ailing along the interior of its offensive line all season. Neuzil has appeared in 69 career games with 38 starts, all for Atlanta. Vorhees has appeared in 37 career games with 22 starts, including five appearances with two starts in 2026.
author: Myles Simmons

title: J.J. McCarthy, Cam Skattebo return to full participation Tuesday
summary: Giants quarterback J.J.
full_text: Giants quarterback J.J. McCarthy and running back Cam Skattebo returned to full participation in Tuesday's practice. The two players were listed as limited in Monday's walk-through. McCarthy has a hip injury that briefly forced him out of Sunday’s 19-11 win over the Eagles, and Skattebo has a hamstring injury. Wide receiver Darnell Mooney (chest) also returned to full participation on Tuesday's report. Right tackle Jermaine Eluemunor (calf), tight end Theo Johnson (neck), wide receiver Charlie Jones (thumb), wide receiver Malik Nabers (knee) and left tackle Andrew Thomas (groin) were full participants again.

title: Jaguars waive CB Alijah Huzzie
summary: The Jaguars spent Monday adding players to their roster and they moved in the other direction on Tuesday.
full_text: The Jaguars spent Monday adding players to their roster and they moved in the other direction on Tuesday. They announced that they have waived cornerback Alijah Huzzie. The Jaguars acquired safety Jessie Bates, defensive tackle Jordan Davis, and defensive tackle Davon Godchaux in trades on Monday. Huzzie was signed off of the Jaguars' practice squad last month. He appeared in one game for the Jags and saw all of his playing time on special teams. Huzzie also played in two games for the Texans last season. He had four tackles and an interception while in Houston. Travis Hunter, Montaric Brown, Jourdan Lewis, Jaylon Jones, and Jarrian Jones remain on the roster at cornerback for Jacksonville.
author: Josh Alper

title: Vikings announce return of Kirk Cousins
summary: It's official.
full_text: It's official. Kirk Cousins is back in Minnesota. The Vikings have announced the trade that brings Cousins from the Raiders for a third-round pick in the 2027 draft. The deal hinges on Cousins passing a physical, which is usually (but not always) a formality. The Vikings would be out of luck at quarterback if Cousins fails the physical. That will make them far more likely to give it a passing grade. Cousins spent 2018 through 2023 with the Vikings. His return undoubtedly means he'll become the instant starter, with Carson Wentz undoubtedly being released. There's no reason to part ways with Kyler Murray. At $1.3 million, he's a low-cost insurance policy, in the event of a Cousins injury. It remains to be seen whether Murray or Max Brosmer will be the primary backup to Cousins.
author: Mike Florio

title: Chiefs agree to trade for WR Josh Downs
summary: Josh Downs has gotten his wish.
full_text: Josh Downs has gotten his wish. After requesting a trade from the Colts, the Chiefs have agreed to acquire the wide receiver, according to multiple reports. Kansas City will receive Downs and a 2027 seventh-round pick in exchange for 2027 fourth- and fifth-round picks. Downs, who is in his fourth season, has caught 33 passes for 354 yards with an interception so far in 2026. He had 58 catches for 566 yards with four touchdowns in 16 games last year. A third-round pick in the 2023 draft, Downs has recorded 231 career catches for 2,494 yards with 12 touchdowns in his 56 games. The Chiefs have been looking for more depth at receiver and now have a new weapon in Downs. He could also play 18 games, as the Chiefs have already had their bye while the Colts don’t have theirs until Week 13.
author: Myles Simmons

title: The Kirk Cousins contract points to a revised deal or termination after 2026
summary: The last time the Vikings brought back a key former player for a third-round pick, the reunion didn't last long.
full_text: The last time the Vikings brought back a key former player for a third-round pick, the reunion didn't last long. This time, it will last longer — but possibly not beyond the current season. In 2010, the Vikings sent a third-round pick to the Patriots for receiver Randy Moss, whom the Vikings had traded to the Raiders in 2005. Former coach Brad Childress, calling Moss a "programmatic non-fit," released Moss after four games. Now, quarterback Kirk Cousins returns for a third-round pick, and a contract that covers nine regular-season games. His deal with the Raiders was structured to maximize the amount the Falcons owed Cousins for 2026 ($8.7 million, on top of the $90 million he made in 2024 and 2025) with another $10 million paid by the Raiders to Cousins in 2027, in the form of a guaranteed roster bonus not subject to offset. The contract also includes a 2028 base salary of $78.655 million that becomes fully guaranteed on the fifth day of the 2027 league year. Coupled with a $1.345 million base salary in 2027 that becomes fully guaranteed that same day, the Vikings would be on the hook for $80 million over two years if he's not released by then. Without a revised deal, the current contract surely would be torn up by March. The question is whether the Vikings and Cousins would be able to come up with a new contract to replace it. Much of that depends on how the rest of the year goes. Still, Cousins has the ability to force his way to free agency, for the fourth time in his career, by simply declining to re-do the existing deal. However it plays out, Cousins can be counted on to make a good business decision. He has $333 million in career earnings, which has him at fourth on the all-time list . On-field success is a different story. He has made it to the postseason three times in his career, with one playoff win. If, as expected, the return of Cousins provides a B-12 shot to the Minnesota franchise, he has a realistic chance of getting back to the playoffs. And of winning a second postseason game. And maybe a third. Hell, maybe even a fourth.
author: Mike Florio

title: Panthers release WR David Moore

author: Charean Williams

title: NFL pretenders and contenders after Week 9: NFC North is fierce, no faith in Giants and Steelers
summary: Breaking down all 14 teams currently in playoff position at the midway point to separate the legitimate Super Bowl threats from the impostors
full_text:
Now that we are halfway through the 2026 NFL season, it's time to start paying attention to the playoff picture -- and it's a pretty wild picture to look at right now.
The NFC North is the only division to ever feature four teams three or more games above .500 through Week 9, while the NFC South is the only division to feature four teams two or more games below .500. Is every NFC North team going to make the playoffs? And which NFC South team will likely go one-and-done in the postseason?
Below, we will break down the pretenders and contenders in the NFL right now. We will look at the 14 teams that would make the playoffs if the season ended today, and examine if they have a legitimate shot to hoist the Lombardi Trophy. Let's begin with the contenders.
Credit to CBS Sports Research
The 7-1 Buffalo Bills are off to their best eight-game start to a season since 1993, which was when they made their last Super Bowl appearance. Josh Allen is again an MVP favorite, James Cook has rushed for at least 75 yards and a touchdown in seven straight games, and Jim Leonhard's defense left the Minnesota Vikings front office scrambling after Carson Wentz registered one of the worst quarterback showings in franchise history on Monday night. The Bills are again a contender.
The San Francisco 49ers are your Super Bowl favorites right now over at DraftKings Sportsbook (+540), and it's easy to understand why. They have started 7-1 or better for the first time since 2019, when they made the Super Bowl. Brock Purdy is an MVP favorite, and he leads an offense that is averaging 29.4 points per game -- which ranks No. 3 in the NFL. This past week against the Las Vegas Raiders , the 49ers scored two passing touchdowns, two rushing touchdowns and a defensive touchdown. However, health will again be a major talking point when it comes to San Francisco. Wide receivers Mike Evans and Deebo Samuel are still sidelined, and defensive tackle Gracen Halton suffered a broken ankle on Sunday. If they can return some players for the stretch run, this could be the 49ers' year.
The Denver Broncos have been dancing with the devil all season in these one-score games, but I'll remind you Bo Nix and Co. did the same thing last year, and probably would have made the Super Bowl if Nix didn't suffer that ankle injury in the divisional round. The Broncos have won five straight games since their 2-2 start, and while they have the worst yard differential (-699) by any team that started 7-2 or better in NFL history, all Nix has done is step up in crunch time. He's 18-12 in his career when trailing in the second half, and 13-12 when trailing in the fourth quarter. Those are the best win percentages by any quarterback since 1970, with a minimum of 20 games. Defensively, Denver is giving up more yards per game than last year, but still ranks top 10 in scoring with 20.7 points allowed per game. You could make the case that the Broncos are pretenders, but I'm leaning the other way. They beat Josh Allen and the Bills in the playoffs last year, and have already defeated the Jacksonville Jaguars and Kansas City Chiefs this season. Denver could make the AFC Championship again.
The Jaguars are all-in this year. At the trade deadline, they sent a first-round pick, second-round pick, a future second-round pick, a future fifth-round pick and a conditional sixth-round pick for defensive tackle Jordan Davis , defensive tackle Davon Godchaux and safety Jessie Bates III . Giving up first- and second-round picks for Davis was shocking, but there's no doubt the Jaguars roster got better this week.
The Jags are running away with the AFC South at 6-2, and have as many wins as the rest of their rivals combined. They are 14-2 in their past 16 games dating back to last year, and Trevor Lawrence has statistically been the best quarterback during that stretch with 42 total touchdowns and a 108.8 passer rating. The Jaguars have the second-best scoring defense in the NFL (15.1 points allowed per game) and one of the best run defenses in the league as well, allowing just 89.3 yards per game. Justice Hill actually just became the first running back to rush for 75 yards against the Jags in 25 games.
The Chiefs got back on track this past week against the New York Jets , registering their largest win (23 points) since Week 7 in 2025. Kenneth Walker III also got back on track with 143 total yards and three touchdowns. There's still some concern around Patrick Mahomes ' passing game, but the addition of Josh Downs will be helpful. Chiefs receivers are averaging 117.5 yards per game, which ranks 28th in the NFL. That hasn't stopped Kansas City from having what is statistically the second-best offense in the NFL (384.1 yards per game).
This may be Joe Burrow's year to win MVP. He's accounted for 26 total touchdowns through eight games. Five of the previous seven players to score that many touchdowns through eight games won MVP. Ja'Marr Chase and Tee Higgins have combined for 47 receptions, 693 yards and eight touchdowns just over the last three games. We know what Chase is capable of, but Higgins is having the best year of his NFL career. He's averaging 94.8 receiving yards per game and has caught six touchdowns in eight games.
Where there's concern with the Cincinnati Bengals is their rushing attack. The 85.6 rushing yards per game are the fewest by a team to start 6-2 or better since the 2014 Detroit Lions . We'll see if the Bengals can pass their way to a Super Bowl. Cincy's defense still isn't "great" statistically, but it's much improved compared to the past couple of seasons. That in itself gives the Bengals a legitimate shot.
It's hard not to like the Chicago Bears . They have an offensive madman scheming up talented weapons open downfield, a quarterback who looks like Josh Allen, and a defense that has been sparked by the addition of Jeffery Simmons . The Bears can't turn the ball over five times every game as they did on Sunday night, but I'm not too worried about that issue.
The Bears have the firepower offensively to be a Super Bowl contender, from the rushing attack to the passing attack, and a defense that is good enough to support a playoff run. The addition of Simmons affects that unit in more ways than one. He can stuff the run and can pressure the quarterback from the interior -- which in turn makes life easier on those in the secondary.
I'm on the fence with the Lions. We all know about the offense with Jared Goff , Jahmyr Gibbs and Amon-Ra St. Brown , but the issue has always been Detroit's defense.
The reason I'll place the Lions in the "contender" category is that Kelvin Sheppard's unit has been better in recent weeks. After a disastrous start, the Lions have allowed just 15.5 points per game during this current four-game win streak. They were allowing 31.8 points per game during the 2-2 start. With Brian Branch back, hopefully Kerby Joseph soon, and the addition of Andre Cisco , I think the Lions can be a contender.
If I were power-ranking the teams in the NFC North, I would have the Green Bay Packers third or fourth. So, does that make them a contender or pretender? I'm still trying to figure that out.
The turnaround in Green Bay has been incredible. After that horrific 1-2 start, the Packers are playing better on both sides of the ball. Jordan Love is the best deep-ball thrower in the NFL, and Christian Watson and Matthew Golden are looking like Tyreek Hill and Jaylen Waddle did in Miami during those fun Mike McDaniel years. The two have combined for 1,662 receiving yards thus far. However, like the Bengals, the Packers can't run the ball. They rank dead last in rushing offense with 68.2 yards per game, and just lost Josh Jacobs to a broken finger.
I'm not placing money on the Packers to win the Super Bowl, but I can't get over how good this passing attack has been. Plus, the defense just picked off Drake Maye three times and will return Micah Parsons soon.
The Vikings were perhaps the most obvious pretender in…
author: Jordan Dajani

title: NFL trade deadline: Ranking all 18 in-season deals as Kirk Cousins, Jeffery Simmons reshape Super Bowl race
summary: The Jaguars, Bears and Bills are among the teams that pulled off home-run moves
full_text:
The fourth-most active trade deadline in NFL history is complete. Teams completed 18 in-season moves by the time the clock struck 4 p.m. ET on Tuesday as they positioned themselves for postseason runs and rebuilds. The biggest blockbusters that defined the deadline sent star defensive tackles to Super Bowl contenders and quarterback help to sputtering offenses, and those should prove with time to be the most impactful deals of the year.
Some moves that occurred well in advance of the deadline have already paid dividends. Jeffery Simmons , for instance, is already a difference-maker for the Chicago Bears and was integral in their building a four-game winning streak. Others delivered mixed results, as is the case with the Quenton Nelson and Joey Porter Jr . deals since both players are dealing with injuries early in their tenures with the Seattle Seahawks and Dallas Cowboys , respectively. As for those that flew in just ahead of the deadline, the next few weeks will determine which teams won or lost their trades.
Trades are about more than just coming away with more talent than the other team involved. Evaluating the impact of a transaction comes down to specific team needs, the capital sent back in return and how the move addresses short-term contention prospects and long-term roster outlooks.
With those factors in mind, below are all 18 in-season trades ranked from most to least impactful.
There was one missing piece in Minnesota that, if found, could turn the Vikings into a force to be reckoned with in the Super Bowl race. It took until the last minute, but they found it. Kirk Cousins promises to give the Vikings the offensive lift they need to capitalize on their league-best defense. This year has been a renaissance for the 38-year-old who is on pace to threaten for his first 40-touchdown season. That late-career surge and his familiarity with the offense in Minnesota should allow him to step right into action and help the Vikings avoid the tight, low-scoring battles of the campaign's first nine weeks and start blowing opponents out. His arrival ought to also unlock Justin Jefferson and turn him back into the superstar-level producer he is meant to be.
There is a strong case to be made that Jeffery Simmons is the best in-season acquisition, because he already proved to be a game-changer for the Bears. The impacts of the other trade deadline moves are speculative, while Simmons' is known. He wreaked all kinds of havoc over his first two games in the middle of the Chicago defensive line, was paramount in the Bears' win over the Seahawks and was one of the few reasons why they survived their five-turnover disaster on "Sunday Night Football" in Week 9. The three-time All-Pro turned the defense into a significant asset overnight. That is a transformational impact that will help this team maximize its potential with Caleb Williams leading the charge on the other side of the ball.
The Jaguars were one of just two teams to trade a first-round pick. They also packaged a 2029 second-rounder to land Jordan Davis . It was a high price, but that was to be expected, since Davis is a franchise-building block who signed a contract extension with the Eagles earlier this year and will be under team control for three years beyond this one. The trade should pay dividends both straight away and over the long term as the Jaguars step into their championship-contention window. It was about as big of a swing as Jacksonville could have made in the wake of the torn quad that knocked DaVon Hamilton out for the year. They did not just replace Hamilton; they upgraded.
The impact Jessie Bates III delivers to the Jaguars' defense in 2026 might be even greater than that of Davis, but he checks in one spot lower in the rankings because of the potential short-term nature of his stay in Jacksonville. The star safety is in the final year of his contract and may turn out to be a rental. If that is all he is, then the secondary will enjoy every minute of his half season in town, because as a three-time All-Pro, there are few defensive backfield stalwarts as talented as he is. Bates elevates the starting lineup but also minimizes the impact of losing Eric Murray for the season due to an elbow issue. Pass defense has been one of the few knocks against the otherwise elite Jaguars, as they rank 22nd in slowing teams down through the air. This helps immensely in that regard.
Amani Hooker is tied for the league lead in interceptions and already has five takeaways for the second time in three years. That kind of turnover prowess in the defensive backfield through 2028 is worth spending a second-round pick and a fifth-round pick. The Titans captain has allowed a passer rating of just 79.3 this season, which is his best mark since his rookie season in 2019. For a Bills team that scores at will and just needs its defense to hold up its end of the bargain, Hooker's arrival raises the floor and the ceiling. Safety was a need after the Bills released C.J. Gardner-Johnson, and they filled it in an emphatic way.
The 49ers ' reunion with DeForest Buckner addressed a serious deficiency on the defensive line, where injuries once again reared their ugly heads. Alfred Collins and CJ West remain on injured reserve, and Gracen Halton just suffered a season-ending ankle fracture in Buckner's first game back in the Bay Area. San Francisco can seemingly never have enough playmakers amid its never-ending injury woes. Bringing Buckner back was more than just insurance, though. It is a step up in the trenches, which will aid the NFC West leaders as they pursue a championship.
Jaxson Dart's season is over, but the Giants ' campaign is far from done. Even though the J.J. McCarthy trade did not make all the sense in the world when it happened, it has aged phenomenally, with the third-year quarterback stepping up as a commendable replacement for the injured starter. McCarthy is 2-0 as a starter and is playing the best football of his career (albeit in a small sample size) and has done nothing but keep the Giants comfortably in first place in the NFC East. This is not a long-term answer for New York since Dart will reclaim the No. 1 job next year, but if it allows the Giants to win the division and flip McCarthy -- or keep him as a renowned backup -- then it is a massive victory in the face of unfortunate circumstances.
The jury is out on whether Jacoby Brissett can keep the Ravens afloat until Lamar Jackson returns from thumb surgery. On one hand, he has been a premier backup for years and should be far more capable of directing the ball in the way of Zay Flowers and Derrick Henry than Joe Fagnano was in his spot start. But on the other hand, the Cardinals benched him before they moved on from him. This was a desperation trade for the Ravens that, if it pays off, will result in them remaining on the fringes of postseason contention. If Brissett is nothing more than a bottom-tier starter, though, Baltimore can kiss this season goodbye.
Quenton Nelson underwent a minor knee procedure to remove loose bodies in his knee, which is a hiccup in his young Seahawks tenure and slightly downgrades the value of the trade. The expectation should be for Nelson to return within a couple of weeks and play at an All-Pro level. But he did not impress in his debut in Seattle, will miss at least some time, and is set to become a free agent at the end of the year, so the amount of time he spends making a real impact in the trenches could be slim when it is all said and done. The Seahawks need his supreme blocking ability in the lineup to help jump-start their dormant run game.
When he is on the field, Joey Porter Jr. is a lockdown corner for the Cowboys. But he missed his first game upon arrival in Dallas with an illness and missed time over the last two weeks with an ankle issue, and it is not as if the middling defense was all that much better overall in the four games he did play to date. Unless Jerry Jones re-signs Porter in the…
author: Carter Bahns

title: NFL trade deadline aftermath: Which teams improved, which teams should have made moves
summary: The Vikings and Chiefs were among the teams that got better, but the Chargers really dropped the ball on Tuesday
full_text:
The 2026 NFL trade deadline came and went Tuesday afternoon at 4 p.m. ET, and the league provided a flurry of activity.
Of the NFL's 32 teams, 23 teams combined to make 18 trades, with 19 players and 34 picks changing hands in 2026. That is right in line with the average of 19.3 traded midseason since 2019, which is way up from the average of 7.5 between 2009 and 2018. The volume of trades wasn't the only thing that has increased around the trade deadline lately. There have been 11 future first-round picks swapped since 2019, up exponentially from the three that changed hands from 2001 to 2018.
Three first-round picks alone were traded in 2026, with All-Pro defensive tackle Jeffery Simmons going from the Tennessee Titans to the Chicago Bears (two) and defensive tackle Jordan Davis going from the Philadelphia Eagles to the Jacksonville Jaguars (one).
So which teams improved and which teams should have made moves? Let's dive into a 2026 NFL trade deadline evaluation on who did well and who should have done more.
The Jaguars smell blood in the AFC waters. On Monday, the Jaguars relinquished a 2027 first-round pick, a 2027 second-round pick, a 2028 fifth-round pick, a 2028 sixth-round pick and a 2029 second-round pick for the services of Philadelphia Eagles Super Bowl champion defensive tackle Jordan Davis, Atlanta Falcons Pro Bowl safety Jessie Bates III and New Orleans Saints defensive tackle Davon Godchaux .
It makes sense. The Jaguars are right to go all in for the 2026 season. The Buffalo Bills (7-1) have one of the leakiest secondaries in the NFL, allowing 238.8 passing yards per game (fourth-most in the NFL). The Denver Broncos (7-2) have offensive inconsistency issues because of quarterback Bo Nix . His 5.6 air yards per pass attempt is mere decimal points ahead of Kansas City Chiefs (6-2) quarterback Patrick Mahomes ' 5.6 air yards per pass attempt to avoid being dead last in the league. However, Mahomes' figure has more to do with the Chiefs' limited passing-game options than with an unwillingness to throw the ball downfield, as with Nix.
The AFC North-leading Pittsburgh Steelers (6-2) have Aaron Rodgers at quarterback, and he will be 43 years old by the time the playoffs begin. Jacksonville beat the Cincinnati Bengals (6-2) in a narrow, one-score game earlier this season, and the New England Patriots (5-4) just got decimated at home (45-27) by quarterback Jordan Love and his Green Bay Packers .
Jacksonville's timing is definitely right: They have the NFL's No. 4 scoring offense (28.6 points per game) and the NFL's No. 2 scoring defense (15.1 points per game). Quarterback Trevor Lawrence has what he needs to soar, and now his defense does too.
The Minnesota Vikings (6-2) needed to make a trade for a quarterback after the monstrosity that was their Carson Wentz-led offense in a 23-6 loss on "Monday Night Football." Wentz completed just 8 of his 25 throws for 81 yards and two interceptions for an 8.9 passer rating. That's right, Wentz's 8.9 passer rating is not a typo. It is the worst passer rating by a Vikings quarterback in a game since 1984, when Tommy Kramer registered a 7.5.
Wentz's 32% completion percentage is tied for the worst in a game in Vikings history, which is how the Vikings recorded their lowest time of possession (17:28) in 40 years.
It would have been a slap in the face to defensive coordinator Brian Flores and his No. 1 scoring defense (14.5 points per game allowed) for the Vikings not to trade for a quarterback. Minnesota did what they had to do Tuesday by sending a 2027 third-round pick to the Las Vegas Raiders to acquire old friend Kirk Cousins .
At the age of 38, Cousins ranks second in the NFL in touchdown passes in 2026 (20), three behind Joe Burrow's and one ahead of Jordan Love. That's also eight more passing touchdowns than the total number of touchdowns the Vikings' offense has this season. Twelve offensive touchdowns is tied for the fewest by a team with a 6-2 record or better through eight games played since 1950.
The good news is four-time Pro Bowl wide receiver Justin Jefferson's production should return with Cousins. In the only fully healthy season the duo shared in 2022, Jefferson won NFL Offensive Player of the Year honors after leading the league in targets (184), catches (128), receiving yards (1,809), and receiving first downs (83). The 98.9 passing yards per game that Cousins averages to Jefferson is the most by a quarterback-receiver duo in NFL history (min. 50 games). Minnesota definitely improved on Tuesday.
MIN Kirk Cousins/Justin Jefferson
HOU Matt Schaub/Andre Johnson
DET Matthew Stafford/Calvin Johnson
The NFC-leading San Francisco 49ers (7-1) bolstered their two biggest areas of weakness — defensive tackle and wide receiver — with two highly decorated veterans: three-time Pro Bowl defensive tackle DeForest Buckner and six-time Pro Bowl wide receiver Keenan Allen .
The great news is San Francisco didn't have to invest too much draft capital into either player, sending the Indianapolis Colts a 2027 fourth-round pick for Buckner and a 2027 sixth-round pick for Allen. Buckner's 4.0 sacks through nine weeks are tied for the seventh most in the NFL among defensive tackles, while his 22 quarterback pressures rank as the 15th most among defensive tackles. That's fantastic production for any player, let alone a 32-year-old the 49ers know incredibly well after he played the first five seasons of his career in San Francisco. Allen, whose 12,402 career receiving yards rank as the fourth most in the NFL among active players, is a nice, reliable depth addition for a 49ers receiver room that can't manage to stay healthy.
Buffalo led the NFL in scoring defense with 19.3 points per game allowed from 2021 to 2025 under ex-head coach Sean McDermott, but under first-year defensive coordinator Jim Leonhard , they're allowing 23.4 points per game, ranking 16th in the league. They're also 14th in expected points added (EPA) per play and 17th in EPA per dropback, but those numbers were artificially deflated by Wentz and the wheezing Vikings offense on Monday. Through the first eight weeks of the season, the Bills were tied for 24th in scoring defense (25.9 points per game allowed), 24th in defensive EPA per play and 27th in EPA per dropback.
Enter Titans safety Amani Hooker , whom they acquired along with a 2027 fifth-round pick in exchange for a 2027 second-round pick.  Hooker, who is 28 years old, leads the NFL in interceptions (5) after picking off Bengals quarterback Joe Burrow three times in an overtime defeat in Week 8. The Bills could certainly see Burrow in January.
Hooker is just the third player in the past 40 years with 50-plus tackles (52) and five-plus interceptions (5) in his first seven games of a season, along with Washington cornerback DeAngelo Hall (2010) and Colts linebacker Cato June (2005). He and Green Bay Packers All-Pro safety Xavier McKinney are also the only two players in the last three seasons with 200-plus tackles (204) and double-digit interceptions (10). Acquiring Hooker also came at a steep price. His three-year, $40.5 million contract is now a team-friendly asset that has him under team control through the 2028 season.
On Monday night, Minnesota had open wide receivers throughout the game, but Wentz was unable to find them. That won't be the case against stiffer quarterback competition in the postseason. Teams are throwing at Buffalo's secondary at the second-highest rate in the NFL (62.6%) as they are allowing the fourth-most passing yards per game (238.8) in the league, per NFL Pro. That's why Buffalo parted with a second-round pick to acquire Hooker.
General manager Howie Roseman built two Super Bowl championship teams with the Eagles in 2017 and 2024, and he may be well on his way to doing so again after his wheeling and dealing in 2026. The Eagles have 10 picks in the first two rounds across the next three drafts — five first-round picks and five second-round picks.
Roseman turned…
author: Garrett Podell

title: Cam Skattebo responds after Giants fail to trade for Jonathan Taylor: 'They know what I can do'
summary: New York reportedly pulled an offer of two draft picks for the Colts star, leaving the division-leading offense in the hands of a confident Skattebo
full_text:
The New York Giants decided to stand pat at the NFL trade deadline. While they showed interest in adding a defensive tackle like Jeffery Simmons and a running back such as Jonathan Taylor , John Harbaugh and Joe Schoen elected not to ship off valuable draft capital as the Giants prepare for the second half of the season.
New York was one of several teams that could have benefitted from a new running back like Taylor. Fox Sports reported that the Giants offered the Indianapolis Colts second- and fifth-round picks for their star back, but eventually took that offer off the table.
No one may be happier about that than running back Cam Skattebo, who will now still be responsible for the bulk of the carries for the Giants. In the locker room after the trade deadline passed, Skattebo was asked about holding onto his starting spot after the Giants' pursuit of Taylor ended.
"I've been that guy," Skattebo said. "Obviously, we had that one-week hiccup where I got in trouble. That was it. I came back that next week and handled business. They know what I'm capable of. They know what I can do."
The Giants couldn't reach a deal with the Colts, who were likely asking too high a price for Taylor. Now, New York will stick with what it has.
"You don't want to make a bad deal," Harbaugh said on Tuesday, per NJ.com . "You make a bad deal, that doesn't make you better. That makes you worse. Sometimes, the best deal is the deal that you don't make.
"We're willing to pay a price to make our team better. But it's got to be something that really makes our team better. It's got to be worth it. I would want a player that we love."
Skattebo has rushed for 418 yards and two touchdowns in seven games played this season. It's already been a dramatic year that has included a benching, followed by a career performance.
Skattebo was given zero touches in Week 6 following his costly overtime fumble in the eventual tie against the Washington Commanders the week prior. However, he bounced back to rush for a career-high 124 yards and a touchdown against the Houston Texans in Week 7. It was an epic redemption game , which included a play where Skattebo broke loose for 42 yards in overtime to set up New York's fourth win of the season.
SKATTEBO BREAKS FREE FOR 42 YARDS NYGvsHOU on FOX/FOX One Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/CqU4A2DpOE
Skattebo suffered a hamstring injury on this play, which forced him to miss the Week 9 win over the Philadelphia Eagles , but he's expected to return this Thursday against the Commanders.
"You've seen what I can do," Skattebo said. "When I come out, and I'm ready to play football, I can be one of the most dangerous backs in the league. Simple as that."
The 5-2-1 Giants are currently two games ahead of the Dallas Cowboys in the NFC East. Maybe adding the player who has recorded the fifth-most rushing yards per game (88.8) in NFL history could have taken the Giants' offense to another level, but Skattebo clearly believes he's capable of being an effective bell cow.
author: Jordan Dajani

title: 2026 NFL trade deadline grades for every team: Four teams earn an A, Rams and Chargers among disappointments
summary: The 2026 NFL trade deadline has come and gone, and we've got a full report card for the league
full_text:
The 2026 NFL trade deadline has come and gone, a whirlwind of activity changing the NFL landscape halfway through the season. After countless rumors, reports and hypothetical moves, there were 18 trades between the beginning of the regular season and the trade deadline, including six on deadline day itself.
A quarterback reunion stole the show on Tuesday, with Kirk Cousins heading back to the Vikings in exchange for a third-round pick going to the Raiders . It's the second quarterback deal by Minnesota this year; the Vikings also sent J.J. McCarthy to the Giants . And if the postseason started today, McCarthy's Giants would host Cousins' Vikings in a wild-card matchup.
Defensive tackle, normally not a headlining position, was in the spotlight, with the Bears acquiring Jeffery Simmons from the Titans and the Jaguars acquiring Jordan Davis from the Eagles . Also on the move at the position were DeForest Buckner and Davon Godchaux .
Sometimes, though, it's the moves not made that tell a bigger story. Here's how all 32 teams fared with trade deadline grades for everyone in the league.
The Bills saw several other Super Bowl contenders making significant win-now moves and decided to make their own on deadline day, acquiring safety Amani Hooker and a 2027 fifth-round pick from the Titans for a 2027 second-round pick. It's a big move for a player in the middle of his best year: Hooker has five interceptions this year, including three off Joe Burrow in one game. Other Bills safeties have one pick combined. He is a versatile defender who's willing to tackle -- a strong addition to a Bills secondary that needed help. It was expensive, but worth doing. Buffalo got significantly better Tuesday.
It was a rough deadline day for the Dolphins : Quarterback Malik Willis landed on IR, and veteran defensive tackle Zach Sieler -- a potential trade candidate -- is done for the season with ruptured biceps. The timing couldn't have been worse regarding Sieler. It might have been nice for this one-win team to get some compensation there.
The Patriots not making any moves was a bit of a surprise considering Rhamondre Stevenson is hurt (knee), TreVeyon Henderson is dealing with an illness, and the offensive line and wide receiver group are truly beat up. This felt like a chance for New England to improve Drake Maye's surroundings, even if it was just via modest improvements, but New England didn't make any moves.
The Jets got a sixth-round pick for trading Andre Cisco to the Lions but held otherwise. That was probably the right move, even with Will McDonald IV asking for a trade amid decreased playing time. If needed, they can act on that request this coming offseason. The Jets already did tremendous work last trade deadline and will have three first-round picks next year, giving them great flexibility.
The Ravens needed to make a move for a quarterback -- Joe Fagnano simply wasn't going to cut it -- and they did, paying a reasonable price, given the situation, for Jacoby Brissett . Best-case scenario, the Ravens stay alive long enough for Lamar Jackson to return. Worst-case scenario, at least they have a workable product. Trading for center Ryan Neuzil right at the deadline buzzer was an interesting move considering Baltimore had already traded for Cam Jurgens earlier this season; perhaps Neuzil moves to guard. The Jurgens move was a bit of an overpay.
The Bengals would hypothetically get a C for their effort on Tuesday, but they earned an F for the execution. They aimed to add EDGE Arnold Ebiketie from the Eagles on deadline day, but the deal fell through after Cincinnati realized it would have lost its 2027 third-round compensation pick by acquiring Ebiketie. Oops! Bad look by Cincy, which did not end up making any moves.
The Browns held firm at the trade deadline, neither buying nor selling. Names such as wide receiver Jerry Jeudy's were in the rumor mill, but it's fine that Cleveland didn't make a move. He has ceded targets to talented rookies Denzel Boston and KC Concepcion , but he is still playing over 60% of the team's offensive snaps. The Browns will battle for a playoff spot or at least to play spoiler and look to really make strides in 2027, when Deshaun Watson's contract ends.
The Steelers were reportedly on the hunt for a wide receiver, but nothing materialized for the AFC North leaders. Cornerback reinforcements might have been nice as well, considering the past health issues of Jamel Dean and Asante Samuel Jr . and the age of Jalen Ramsey , but for now, Pittsburgh will look to keep it rolling with the group it has.
The Texans paid more for the name than the game when they traded for Marvin Harrison Jr. , sending a second-round pick to the Cardinals for a player who hasn't come close to living up to the hype. Harrison is yet to top three catches in any of his three games for Houston this season, and he still played less than half of his new team's snaps coming out of the bye in Week 9. Unless he becomes a more major contributor soon, the overpay looks even worse.
The Colts were the busiest sellers, sending Quenton Nelson to Seattle, Buckner and Keenan Allen to San Francisco and Josh Downs to Kansas City, but them not trading Jonathan Taylor was a gigantic missed opportunity. Taylor is almost 28 years old, and keeping him will only add wear and tear on his body. A contending team likely would have paid more now, with a half-season to go, then next year, when he will only be older and more worn down. The Colts have no chance of contending soon, either. Furthermore, the Colts also decided against moving Grover Stewart , who reportedly garnered mid-round pick interest. One can also wonder if the Colts got enough in the trades they did make, especially for Buckner.
The Jaguars did well acquiring safety Jessie Bates III , even if second- and fifth-round picks were a bit pricey. Bates is a tremendous playmaker (28 career interceptions, 14 career forced fumbles) joining a play-making unit; Jacksonville's defense has forced 15 turnovers, third-most this season. After losing defensive tackle DaVon Hamilton for the season, getting defensive tackle Davon Godchaux to help in the middle was reasonable. But a first-round pick and a second-round pick for hulking defensive tackle Jordan Davis was a massive overpay, even if Davis were playing like he did last year, which was a contract year. He's a one-dimensional run plugger who had nine tackles for loss in 2025; he has eight in the rest of his career combined. The Jaguars paid a near-Jeffery Simmons price for a player nowhere near Simmons in terms of all-around talent or disruptiveness, even at his best. He can be a good player who helps -- the Jags will hope they get his best now that he's on a winning team -- and stopping the run is important. But from a value perspective, this was a poor deal. Keeping Brian Thomas Jr . was smart. For an all-in season, they had no need to trade him for future assets, and they can revisit a move this coming offseason.
Whether the Titans should have parted ways with Simmons or not is worth arguing, but the return is inarguable. Tennessee having extra first-round picks each of the next two years is outstanding business, and Cam Ward's recent improved play should make the Titans feel all the better. The extra picks will allow Tennessee to surround him with talent at several positions. Getting a second-round pick for Hooker is also good work; Tennessee wanted a strong return, and it got it. The Titans had other players to trade away, such as Tony Pollard , and it's worth wondering if they should have. For now, though, keeping a hot hand helps the young quarterback.
The Broncos quietly made a helpful deal, acquiring Chargers linebacker Daiyan Henley for a couple of mid-round picks. Henley has plateaued a bit the past couple of seasons after a strong start, but he's an impressive athlete who could benefit from a change of scenery. Vance Joseph has gotten the most out of lots of players, and…
author: Zachary Pereles

title: NFL trade deadline winners and losers: Kirk Cousins heads home, Bengals seemingly fail to understand the rules
summary: Kirk Cousins heads back to Minnesota, the Jaguars go all-in for a championship run and a front-office blunder leaves Cincinnati red-faced
full_text:
