The 2026 NFL trade deadline has come and gone, and while we did see a couple of blockbuster trades in recent weeks, such as the Chicago Bears trading for Jeffery Simmons and the Jacksonville Jaguars swinging deals for three players in one day, the final 24 hours of the trade deadline were relatively quiet.
On Tuesday, the Minnesota Vikings brought back Kirk Cousins to replace Kyler Murray, and the Kansas City Chiefs added a new wide receiver in Josh Downs . However, there were plenty of other teams perceived to be "buyers" who stayed put, while other "sellers" were hesitant to part ways with their assets. In all, 23 teams combined to make 18 trades with 19 players and 34 picks changing hands. It was the Indianapolis Colts who led the way with an NFL-high four trades for six draft selections, although star running back Jonathan Taylor was not moved.
So, who won and who lost at the trade deadline? Let's take a look.
Credit to CBS Sports Research
The Vikings and Las Vegas Raiders made the deal of the day, as new general manager Nolan Teasley sent a third-round pick to "Sin City" for Kirk Cousins. It feels like everyone is a winner in this situation.
The Vikings are a winner because they absolutely had to do something at the quarterback position. Kyler Murray wasn't cutting it, and then Carson Wentz registered one of the worst performances by a Vikings quarterback ever on Monday night with an 8.9 passer rating and a 32% completion rate. The Vikings were wasting the efforts of the best defense in the NFL and found themselves in a spot where they were forced to make an addition. Bringing back a familiar face who has been performing well this season with 20 touchdowns and eight interceptions is a good move.
Cousins actually has the most passing touchdowns (20) and career passing touchdowns (318) by a quarterback changing teams midseason, all-time. During his six seasons in Minnesota (2018-2023), he ranked top five in completion percentage, passing yards and passing touchdowns while going 50-37-1 as the starter.
The Raiders are a winner because they got a third-round pick for their rental quarterback in a season where they likely aren't making the playoffs. The Vikings didn't enter this year expecting to trade for a quarterback in November, which allowed the Raiders to drive up the price.
Kirk Cousins is a winner because he upgrades his own situation. He goes from 4-5 to 6-2, and has the opportunity to spark a legitimate Super Bowl run. That may sound like an exaggeration, but with Justin Jefferson , Jordan Addison and T.J. Hockenson , the Vikings have everything in place to make a run. All they needed was better quarterback play. It could be a storybook ending for Cousins.
Fernando Mendoza is a winner because he's the new starter in Vegas, although the No. 1 overall pick has to begin his NFL career against some aggressive defenses with the Seattle Seahawks on Sunday and then the Denver Broncos the following week.
Another winner is Justin Jefferson, because he gets his quarterback back. JJ began his NFL career with three straight 1,400-yard seasons — including a 1,809-yard campaign in 2022. Jefferson barely crossed 1,000 yards receiving last season. Now, he can suit up next to the best quarterback he's ever played with again. His 98.9 receiving yards per game when catching passes from Cousins are the most by a QB-WR duo all-time (min. 50 games).
Tuesday morning, it was reported that the Cincinnati Bengals were sending a sixth-round pick to the Philadelphia Eagles for pass rusher Arnold Ebiketie . This wouldn't have been a massive story, except the Bengals front office didn't realize they would also be giving up a third-round pick in the deal!
Nick Korte of Over The Cap pointed out that Ebiketie was signed as a compensatory free agent by the Eagles. The Bengals lost three compensatory free agents and signed two, with Cordell Volson not qualifying as a CFA lost since he hasn't played a snap this year. So, adding Ebiketie means the Bengals would lose a 2027 compensatory third-round pick that was coming after Trey Hendrickson signed with the Baltimore Ravens .
Oh that's brutal on the 3rd round comp pick! as noted by @nickkorte pic.twitter.com/OwwyNB71PA
From the NFL Collective Bargaining Agreement :
"If a Club trades for a player who was a CFA during that League Year, whether the player was another Club's CFA or the acquiring Club's own CFA, the player will be considered a CFA gained by the acquiring Club and will be included in the Compensatory netting process described above."
It's believed Cincinnati initially thought Volson counted toward the formula.
Naturally, when the Bengals discovered this, they backed out of the deal. This isn't even the first time Korte has had to correct the league about compensatory picks. He actually helped the Bengals secure a top-100 pick in the 2024 NFL Draft after a compensatory mix-up.
Duke Tobin and the Bengals look silly because they almost gave up a third-round pick for Ebiketie. They should hire Korte in the front office after helping them twice in three years.
There's no questioning the Jaguars' goal this season: They are all-in on a Super Bowl. Here's what they traded just this week:
Jacksonville saw Eric Murray go down with a season-ending injury, so they targeted Bates to replace him. He's tied for the second-most interceptions (28) since entering the league in 2018 and is the only NFL player to have recorded a pick-six in each of the last three seasons.
The Jaguars also lost defensive tackle DaVon Hamilton for the remainder of the season after he tore his quad, so the front office went out and acquired a couple of legitimate starters in Godchaux and Davis.
The Jaguars are "winners" because it's exciting when a team gets this aggressive and pushes all of their chips to the middle of the proverbial table. Fans have all the reason in the world to be excited about this run for the No. 1 seed in the AFC.
However, while Jacksonville's roster got better this week, I am questioning all the capital the Jags just spent.
Trading second- and fifth-round picks for Bates is expensive, but giving up first- and second-round picks for Davis was shocking. He's a solid player in the middle, but no one had any idea the Eagles would fetch that kind of return for him. He's recorded 31 tackles and 1.5 sacks in nine games played this season, and he recorded a career-high 4.5 sacks in 2025. Just eight months ago, Davis signed a three-year, $78 million extension that made him one of the highest-paid defensive tackles in the NFL.
If the Jaguars win the Super Bowl, then we can't complain about the compensation. But Jimmy James Gladstone is clearly in an "eff them picks" mood.
2027 second-round pick, 2028 fifth-round pick
2028 sixth-round pick (conditional)
2027 first-round pick, 2029 second-round pick
There was a lot of oxygen given to running backs at this year's trade deadline. The Colts' Jonathan Taylor was a player everyone was watching, the Ravens' Derrick Henry was another big name brought up in rumors, the Tennessee Titans ' Tony Pollard was viewed as a potential target and Breece Hall had seemingly fallen out of favor in New York with the emergence of Braelon Allen . However, not one running back was moved.
It's understandable if a team didn't want to trade a Christian McCaffrey-like package for Taylor, but what about Pollard? He shredded the Cleveland Browns for 129 yards and three touchdowns in Week 7, and then racked up 117 rushing yards and two touchdowns in Week 8 against the Bengals. He's averaging a career-high 74.4 rushing yards per game and ranks top 12 in rushing yards and rushing touchdowns this season. Pollard and Henry are the only players to have rushed for 1,000 yards in each of the last four seasons. Isn't that worth a fourth-round pick?
There were multiple Super Bowl or playoff hopefuls that could have used a new running back, such as the Vikings, Broncos, Green Bay Packers and New York Giants . Instead, Taylor,…
author: Jordan Dajani

title: Fernando Mendoza inherits a 4-5 Raiders team and NFL history offers two wildly different outcomes
summary: Jared Goff lost all seven rookie starts, Lamar Jackson went 6-1 and made the playoffs. Now Mendoza faces the same challenge.
full_text:
In 2016, the Rams were 4-5 when they benched Case Keenum and handed the offense to No. 1 overall pick Jared Goff. He lost all seven of his starts, threw five touchdowns and seven interceptions, and LA finished 4-12. Jeff Fisher was fired with three games remaining, the Rams hired Sean McVay that offseason, and the rest is history.
Two years later, the Ravens were also 4-5 when Lamar Jackson, the final pick of the first round in 2018, replaced an injured Joe Flacco. He won six of his first seven starts, and Baltimore won the AFC North before losing to the Chargers in the wild-card round. Jackson threw just five touchdowns, but his ability to run transformed everything about the offense.
Same record. Same point in the season. Two completely different outcomes.
And now comes Fernando Mendoza, the No. 1 pick in April's draft, who inherits a 4-5 Raiders team after Las Vegas traded Kirk Cousins to Minnesota on Tuesday for a third-round pick. Mendoza will make his first start Sunday against the Seahawks, and while it's tempting to think nine weeks on the bench may have helped prepare him for what's next, history suggests it could be a little more complicated than that.
Since 2000, 148 quarterbacks have started at least one game as NFL rookies. Just 22 made their first start between Weeks 10 and 13, and their collective debuts were not pretty.
They completed just 53.8% of their passes, averaged 5.8 yards per attempt and threw interceptions on 5.3% of their dropbacks – the worst marks of any group. Only five of those 22 won their debuts, and their interception rate was more than 1.6 times that of rookies who started in Week 1.
How rookie QBs performed in their first career start, 2000-2025
Of course, circumstances matter. Some quarterbacks sat because they weren't ready. Others played because the starter got hurt or was ineffective. But the takeaway remains: Sitting for half a season doesn't guarantee a smoother transition to the top of the depth chart.
Five teams had winning records when they turned to a rookie in Weeks 10-13. They were a combined 30-19 before the change and went 10-20 afterward. The 17 teams with losing records fared slightly better when they installed a rookie under center, improving their winning percentage from 28.9% to 33.7% – though they still lost twice as often as they won.
Team performance before and after a rookie's first start, Weeks 10-13
Team entering debut had a:
Only three of those 22 teams made the playoffs. The 2011 Texans turned to T.J. Yates after injuries to Matt Schaub and Matt Leinart. The 2017 Bills benched Tyrod Taylor for Nathan Peterman despite sitting at 5-4. Peterman threw five interceptions in the first half of his debut, Taylor reclaimed the job at halftime, and Buffalo eventually made the playoffs with Taylor back under center.
Jackson was different. Baltimore initially needed him because Flacco was injured, but he played so well that they stuck with him even after Flacco was healthy. Obviously, that's a blueprint the Raiders would love to follow, but it's fair to say the organizational infrastructure isn't quite there yet.
And then there are the more immediate concerns for the Raiders rookie…
Mendoza's first three starts come against Seattle, Denver and Cleveland, which also happen to be three of the league's best defenses. The schedule gets less daunting after a Week 13 bye, though matchups against the Broncos and Chiefs make up two of the Raiders; final four games. So yeah.
There is a bigger issue: Mendoza could play well and still lose a bunch of games, and Vegas' first nine weeks help explain why.
Kirk Cousins wasn't the reason for all the losing when Vegas traded him. He had thrown 20 touchdowns and just eight interceptions, and the team was averaging 25.4 points per game. Their passing offense ranks fifth in yards per game and ninth in EPA per play, so Mendoza isn't walking into a no-win situation.
The problems lie everywhere else. Las Vegas ranks dead last in yards per carry (2.9), 31st in rushing yards per game (71.3) and 30th in rushing success rate. The defense hasn't been much better, allowing 35.7 points per game over the last six weeks, five of them losses.
That's a tough combination for any quarterback, future Hall of Famer or fresh face of the franchise. Kubiak's system can help, but even the best-designed offense needs a run game that provides some balance.
Back in June, I wrote that Mendoza might be the most NFL-ready quarterback in the class but had landed in the least quarterback-friendly situation . My rookie QB model had him completing 61.4% of his passes, averaging 6.6 yards per attempt with an 82.1 passer rating.
Which brings us back to Goff and Jackson.
They started their careers headed in opposite directions, yet both eventually became two of the NFL's best quarterbacks. Goff didn't reach his current level until Detroit surrounded him with a strong offensive line, dependable running game and playmakers (and early on, Ben Johnson). Baltimore built its offense around Jackson's unique abilities rather than asking him to become something he wasn't.
The Raiders already have their quarterback of the future. Mendoza has eight games to show what he can do, but whether he goes 0-8, 6-2 or somewhere in between won't tell us much about the quarterback he could become. His job is to prove he belongs. The organization's job is to make sure he has a chance to succeed.
author: Ryan Wilson

title: Josh Downs trade grades: Chiefs, Patrick Mahomes get help, Colts get value for disgruntled WR
summary: Downs asked for a trade, and now he'll catch passes from Patrick Mahomes
full_text:
Everyone got what they wanted in the Josh Downs trade. Downs, who demanded a trade earlier this season, got his wish just before the 2026 NFL trade deadline buzzer Tuesday afternoon. The Indianapolis Colts sent him, along with a 2027 seventh-round pick (via the Buffalo Bills ), to the Kansas City Chiefs in exchange for a 2027 fourth-round pick and a 2027 fifth-round pick.
🚨 TRADE 🚨 pic.twitter.com/SGLL7zz2e3
Downs now goes from catching passes from Daniel Jones , whose 82.3 passer rating ranks 34th out of 35 qualified quarterbacks this season, to catching passes from Patrick Mahomes , a three-time Super Bowl MVP. That's why he tweeted the gif of Vince Carter expressing gratitude in reaction to the news that he is now a Chief.
He quickly followed up that post by tweeting , "I am beyond grateful and blessed for my time in Indy. Nothing but love for the [horse] Shoe."
pic.twitter.com/SWGjirDe9N
So how did the Colts and Chiefs make out in this trade deadline deal? Here is a look at the grade for each squad.
The Chiefs (6-2) are always in win-now mode, with Mahomes (31 years old), tight end Travis Kelce (37), defensive tackle Chris Jones (32), defensive coordinator Steve Spagnuolo (66) and head coach Andy Reid (68) getting up there in age. Kelce, Rashee Rice , who is coming back from an offseason knee surgery, and former first-round pick Xavier Worthy haven't been getting the job done.
Kansas City is averaging 117.5 receiving yards per game by wide receivers this season, which is the fewest of the Mahomes era (since 2018) and ranks 28th in the NFL this season. That's why the Chiefs went out and traded for Downs.
The 25-year-old Downs has been a weapon out of the slot since entering the league as a third-round pick in 2023: His 1,995 yards receiving out of the slot are the second most in the entire NFL in the span of his career, trailing only Detroit Lions All-Pro wide receiver Amon-Ra St. Brown (2,160).
* Downs was drafted in the third round of the 2023 NFL Draft
Sure, Downs is a rental playing out the final year of his rookie contract in 2026, but Kansas City was desperate. Plus, if Downs builds a nice rapport with Mahomes, this deal could lead to a second contract come the 2027 offseason. It's also a huge win that the Chiefs didn't have to part with any Day 2 draft capital.
Downs requested a trade, and he is playing out the final year of his rookie contract. There was no chance he would be open to re-signing with Indianapolis in the 2027 offseason, especially with the Colts set to dive headfirst into a rebuild with a new general manager. The Colts did well to get multiple early Day 3 draft picks for a disgruntled player who already had one foot out the door.
author: Garrett Podell

title: 2026 NFL trade deadline tracker: Vikings reunite with Kirk Cousins as in-season moves wrap up
summary: Track every completed deal before the Nov. 10 deadline, including Jacksonville's blockbuster Monday and a Tuesday splash at the quarterback position
full_text:
A steady stream of blockbuster moves in advance of the 2026 NFL trade deadline redistributed some of the league's top talent at numerous positions. A grand total of 18 in-season trades made the 2026 campaign the fourth-most active year of player movement and defined where teams stand in the playoff race and the hunt for the No. 1 overall pick in the 2027 draft.
Teams including the Chicago Bears and Jacksonville Jaguars went all-in ahead of the deadline when they spent premier draft capital on defensive standouts like Jeffery Simmons and Jordan Davis. Those swaps made the Super Bowl contenders two of the deadline's biggest winners.
On the other hand, the Indianapolis Colts emerged as by far the most aggressive sellers when they parted with Quenton Nelson , DeForest Buckner , Keenan Allen and Josh Downs . That dichotomy shows exactly how teams used Nov. 10 as a pivot point in their quest for either a championship or a jumpstart in the rebuilding process.
A bevy of big-name trade candidates stood still when the deadline passed. The Colts' fire sale did not extend to Jonathan Taylor or Daniel Jones , while defenders like Khalil Mack, Will McDonald and Budda Baker remained with their respective teams, too.
Below is every in-season trade processed in advance of the NFL's 2026 deadline.
Just over a month ago, the Ravens pulled off the league's third in-season trade to acquire Cam Jurgens. The move landed them a long-term solution at center following Tyler Linderbaum's exit in free agency. Now they have another center on the roster. Neuzil was the Falcons' starter at that position this season but appears poised to take on a backup role for the Ravens unless he moves to guard (a position he played to an extent in Atlanta and exclusively in college). Olaivavega Ioane is locked in at right guard, so it will come down to John Simpson and Neuzil on the left side. The other will head to the bench as the primary interior offensive line reserve.
The Falcons will not walk away empty-handed, as Vorhees brings starting experience at guard. There will be some shifting around to do on that offensive line.
Kansas City owns the 10th-best passing offense in the NFL but is more reliant on yards after the catch than any team in football. Additionally, wide receivers accounted for only 46.0% of the Chiefs' receiving yards through Week 9, the second-lowest rate, behind only the Raiders at 36.8%, according to Next Gen Stats. This team needed another weapon for Patrick Mahomes and secured one just minutes before the trade deadline in the form of Downs. Although he is not much of a field-stretcher, he could free up Rashee Rice and Xavier Worthy or expand his own role now that he is on a new team.
That concludes the Colts' fire sale, bringing the tally to four players traded. All of them were on expiring contracts, so Indianapolis prioritized landing guaranteed draft capital for players likely to leave in free agency, who may or may not have netted compensatory picks. There are now only five healthy wide receivers on the Colts' active roster: Laquon Treadwell , Deion Burks , Ashton Dulin , Anthony Gould and Nick Westbrook-Ikhine .
One AFC West team got stronger while the other slipped further into the abyss. The Broncos added Daiyan Henley to their linebacker group and now own high-end depth behind locked-in starters Alex Singleton and Justin Strnad . Henley, a former third-round pick, was an every-week starter for the Chargers and brings excellent coverage and run defense skills to the vaunted Denver unit as it gears up for a postseason push. The Broncos anticipate receiving a compensatory pick for John Franklin-Myers ' departure in free agency, which will help offset the cost of this deal.
It was puzzling to see the Chargers sit on their hands for most of the pre-deadline, considering they are the only winless team in the league, and while the Henley deal finally made them sellers, it was also a surprise for them to strengthen a division rival. They latched onto their other tradeable assets — players like Khalil Mack and even Justin Herbert , who would have commanded far greater returns— while securing only Day 3 capital for Henley.
For the second time in his career, Cousins is a Viking. Minnesota had the most glaring need at quarterback of any team in the league heading into deadline day, and Cousins was the most obvious target given his familiarity with the franchise and offensive system and his status as a bridge for the Raiders to No. 1 pick Fernando Mendoza . He is coming off his worst performance of the year (a three-interception day in a loss to the 49ers) and seemed destined to cede the job to Mendoza in the weeks to come, so the trade makes all kinds of sense for both teams.
Minnesota's two losses this season emphasized its inability to capitalize on owning the league's stingiest defense. It was most apparent on "Monday Night Football" when Carson Wentz struggled mightily in a 23-6 loss to the Bills. Cousins' arrival gives the Vikings a rest-of-season solution and an upgrade over Wentz and Kyler Murray -- one who should be able to force-feed the ball to superstar wideout Justin Jefferson and more accurately distribute it to the secondary options, too.
The Vikings sent their own 2027 third-round pick to the Raiders in the deal and still possess the Eagles' third-rounder, which projects to be a more valuable asset. Las Vegas now owns more Day 2 capital and will put that to use in its construction of a young core around Mendoza.
Following the release of C.J. Gardner-Johnson, the Bills were down to the starting tandem of Cole Bishop and Damar Hamlin at safety. The depth in that group was minimal, and the starting production was that of the fourth-worst pass defense in the NFL. Enter Hooker, who is tied for the league lead with five interceptions. The Titans captain is in the midst of a career year and is allowing a passer rating of just 79.3, which is the best mark of his starting career and the best number since his rookie year when he played off the bench.
The rebuilding Titans now have two second-round picks to go with their two first-rounders in 2027. They are in the throes of a defensive tear-down after they also moved on from Jeffery Simmons and will be among the richest teams in draft capital as they work to stockpile young talent and building blocks for the long-term future.
San Francisco has been dealing with injuries in the receiver room all season. It started during training camp, when Ricky Pearsall went out for the year. It continued in Week 1 with De'Zhaun Stribling injuring his ankle. It got worse in recent weeks with both Mike Evans and Deebo Samuel Sr. experiencing injury issues of their own.
Now, the Niners are adding another veteran to the mix: six-time Pro-Bowler Keenan Allen. He's several years removed from playing at that Pro Bowler level, but he does have 40 catches for 351 yards and a touchdown with the Colts this season.
He should probably be expected to fill snaps at the Z receiver position and in the slot while Evans and Samuel are out. He'll likely rotate in with those guys, Stribling upon his return, and players like Demarcus Robinson and Jordan Watkins . His addition gives the 49ers a reliable option while they deal with injuries and provides solid depth when their main pieces return.
The Cincinnati Bengals were reportedly trading a sixth-round pick to the Eagles for pass rusher Arnold Ebiketie . However, the Bengals front office didn't realize they would also lose a third-round pick in the deal.
Nick Korte of Over The Cap pointed out that Ebiketie was signed by the Eagles as a compensatory free agent. The Bengals lost three compensatory free agents this offseason and signed two. With the addition of Ebiketie, the Bengals would lose a 2027 third-round compensatory pick that was coming after Trey Hendrickson signed with the Ravens.
About an hour later, the trade reportedly collapsed. Korte noted that the Bengals may have thought offensive…
author: Carter Bahns

title: Jonathan Taylor stays with Colts: Why Indianapolis demanded a first-round pick
summary: Indianapolis may be rebuilding, but Taylor's team-friendly contract and place among the NFL's most productive running backs gave the franchise little reason to accept a discounted offer
full_text:
Jonathan Taylor isn't going anywhere. The Indianapolis Colts decided to keep their 27-year-old, three-time Pro Bowl running back at the 2026 NFL trade deadline. The Colts  turned down offers of second-round picks and more for Taylor, indicating they required at least a first-round pick to trade him away, according to Tom Pelissero .
Basically, it seems like Indianapolis turned down trade offers comparable to what the San Francisco 49ers sent the Carolina Panthers in 2022 to acquire running back Christian McCaffrey , who was 26. Back then, San Francisco sent Carolina the following picks: a 2023 second-round pick, a 2023 third-round pick, a 2023 fourth-round pick and a 2024 fifth-round pick.
So why would the Colts walk away from such a deal for Taylor? Let's break it down.
The Colts are overcompensating in their Taylor trade demands after not getting market value for Quenton Nelson (a 2027 third-round pick and a 2028 fifth-round pick from the Seattle Seahawks ). They also don't have their own first-round pick ahead of the highly anticipated 2027 NFL Draft because they traded it to the New York Jets a year ago to acquire cornerback Sauce Gardner . That's why Indianapolis probably rebuffed trade packages that lacked first-round picks: they were trying to clean up their mistake from last year's trade deadline.
Also, Taylor is one of the best running backs of his generation: he averages the fifth-most rushing yards per game (88.8) in NFL history. It's understandable why Indianapolis maintained the stance that they won't trade him away for anything less than a first-round pick.
The running back contract market has also changed, and they were able to lock Taylor down on a two-year, $44 million extension with $39 million in guaranteed money before the 2026 season began. That's a great value. The Colts now have him locked down through the 2028 season, the rest of his 20s, and there isn't any guaranteed money left on the deal in 2027 or 2028. That makes it really easy to move him via trade in the future or keep him around for whatever quarterback they eventually add to replace Daniel Jones next year. Those are the reasons why Taylor won't be relocating at the 2026 NFL trade deadline on Tuesday afternoon.
author: Garrett Podell

title: Kirk Cousins trade grades: Vikings hope to salvage offense; Raiders get 'A,' turn to Fernando Mendoza
summary: Cousins returns to the place he played from 2018-23
full_text:
Kevin O'Connell and the Minnesota Vikings are making one last-ditch attempt to save their offense, reuniting with Kirk Cousins and sending their 2027 third-round pick to the Las Vegas Raiders in return.
Cousins, 38, was in the middle of a renaissance year in Sin City, with 20 passing touchdowns and just eight interceptions. He is now being called upon to save a dire situation in Minneapolis. The Vikings have scored just 11 offensive touchdowns this season, tied with the Chargers for the fewest in the NFL . Offseason addition Kyler Murray and veteran backup Carson Wentz have both struggled mightily, with Murray at or near the bottom of most major passing categories and Wentz throwing for just 81 yards and two interceptions starting for Murray (hamstring) on "Monday Night Football."
Cousins spent 2018-23 in Minnesota, where he made three of his four career Pro Bowls. He was especially good in 2022, when he led an NFL-high eight game-winning drives, and Minnesota went 13-4 before being bounced in its first playoff game. The next year, Cousins was arguably even better — on pace for maybe the best year of his career — before tearing his Achilles. Now, three years later, he gets to leave a different lasting legacy in Minnesota.
Teammates until Monday, Fernando Mendoza and Cousins now step into very different spotlights. The Raiders will hope the Mendoza era lasts for years to come and that he can make some positive strides this year. The Vikings, on the other hand, are all-in on this year. Here's how both teams fared:
That the Vikings are even in this situation is worthy of an "F." Ever since Cousins left, they have failed to find a suitable replacement: Sam Darnold was excellent in 2024, but the Vikings let him go in favor of J.J. McCarthy . McCarthy played poorly and was hurt several times last year, as the Vikings rode a quarterback carousel. Minnesota traded McCarthy, who had been demoted to third-string behind Murray and Wentz, to the Giants early this season. Murray — always a curious-at-best fit for this offense — clearly wasn't cutting it, and Wentz was never going to, either.
Cousins has been good this year — not great, but good. He looks far better than what he had been in Atlanta, where it was clear his mobility hadn't returned post-Achilles tear. He's still never going to win with his athleticism, but his negative play rate is down to 6.7%, on pace for a career best, and he is only being sacked on 9.8% of his dropbacks, also on pace for a career best. How much of that praise belongs to Klint Kubiak is up for debate, but it's clear Cousins has regained some of his spryness. He doesn't have to be Michael Vick, but he can't be a statue.
Really, though, this all comes down to fit. Murray never fit. Cousins, hypothetically, does. Obviously, there is proof of concept here given his past in Minnesota. He attacks the middle of the field and delivers on intermediate throws. Plus, he is comfortable off play action. These are crucial parts of O'Connell's scheme. Cousins, if nothing else, should do a much, much better job keeping the offense on schedule.
Given the circumstances, this grade can only be so high, and given the solution, it cannot get that much higher. Cousins is not a star. His arm strength is not what it once was, and for all the good things he did in Las Vegas, he is coming off a three-interception game. We'll see how he holds up, physically, over the rigors of an 18-game regular season (he will not get a bye) plus expected postseason. His accuracy is a bit down from his best years, though it's still a clear major improvement over Murray and Wentz, who at times seemed unable to hit water if they fell off a boat.
It's also nice that the Vikings still have a third-round pick — the Eagles ' from the Jonathan Greenard trade — next year. It will be better than Minnesota's, too.
Even though Cousins can unlock the best part of this offense — Justin Jefferson , who is the biggest winner of this deal — he cannot fix everything. The offensive line has been up-and-down at best, and the running game has been poor. Minnesota's running backs are 31st in percentage of carries with a missed tackle forced and 26th in EPA per rush. There's not much juice there.
Overall, Minnesota got better with this trade. Much better. But it couldn't get much worse, either. Even with a truly outstanding defense, is average-to-slightly-above-average quarterback play and, in turn, average offense good enough to cash in on Super Bowl aspirations? The Vikings are about to find out, but at least they're giving themselves a chance.
P.S. O'Connell had better be right about this move. He has missed on two straight quarterback evaluations. He cannot miss on a third.
If you told a Raiders fan before the season that Mendoza would make his first start in Week 10, they'd probably say that's about right. If you told them he'd start because the Raiders got a top-100 pick for Cousins, they'd be very happy with that outcome.
Cousins well exceeded the mere placeholder role he was given. He played well and, at times, very well. He kept an offense that's very much in the early building stage moving — the Raiders are eighth in points per drive this season. He did this all alongside one of the league's worst running games and worst/youngest wide receiver corps. He leaned on Brock Bowers , who looks like a superstar once again, and fellow tight end Michael Mayer . The Raiders went 4-5 under Cousins and were competitive in several losses. This was a 99th-percentile outcome.
Now, it's Mendoza's turn. It's a little bit tough to drop him into the starting role in these circumstances — not knowing he's starting until Tuesday, and facing Seattle's ferocious defense — but that will be of little matter in the long haul. Kubiak did a great job with Cousins, and the fruits of his labor are a valuable draft pick as Las Vegas continues its build. Strong work all around.
author: Zachary Pereles

title: Chiefs agree to acquire WR Josh Downs in trade with Colts, per report
summary: Indianapolis' rebuild is a benefit to Kansas City, which secured much-needed help in its receiving corps
full_text:
An influx of reciever talent is headed to the Kansas City Chiefs offense, as the team agreed to terms with the Indianapolis Colts on a trade for wide receiver Josh Downs . According to ESPN , the Chiefs will receive Downs and a 2027 seventh-round pick and send a 2027 fourth-rounder and fifth-rounder back to Indianapolis.
The Chiefs land an immediate-impact upgrade for their passing offense, which lacks depth and has become more one-dimensional than at any point in the Patrick Mahomes era. Mahomes now has another weapon to throw to alongside Rashee Rice , Xavier Worthy and his stable of tight ends which includes Travis Kelce .
Kansas City owns the 10th-best passing offense in the NFL but is more reliant on yards after the catch than any team in football. The downfield attack is not nearly as prolific as it was during the height of the Chiefs' offensive dominance. Downs was not much of a field-stretcher during his time with the Colts, seeing just 21 targets of 20-plus yards over the last three seasons in Indianapolis per NFL Next Gen Stats, but perhaps his arrival will either come with an expansion of his role or allow the existing receivers to run deeper routes.
Chiefs wide receivers accounted for just 46.0% of the team's receiving yards through Week 9, which marked the second-lowest rate of any team, ahead of only the Las Vegas Raiders at 36.8%, according to Next Gen Stats.
The concerning state of Kansas City's passing game also led to a reliance on running back Kenneth Walker III as both a ball carrier and a receiver. He is the league's second-leading rusher and last week against the New York Jets recorded his first career game with multiple receiving touchdowns. Any addition to the receiving unit should help reduce some of the strain on the Chiefs' prized running back while also potentially opening up greater opportunities for him in the run game as defenses respect the pass to a greater extent.
Downs is the second Colts receiver to be moved in the hours leading up to the NFL trade deadline and follows Keenan Allen (who is headed to the San Francisco 49ers ) as another casualty of the franchise's commitment to a rebuild. The Colts emerged as the biggest sellers of the deadline following a two-win start to the season.
Indianapolis parted with four players who are on expiring contracts and thus secured draft capital for standouts who were likely to leave in free agency anyway. Quenton Nelson , DeForest Buckner , Allen and Downs netted the Colts a plethora of picks for them to use as they reconstruct their roster from the ground up under a new general manager who has yet to be hired.
The fire sale leaves the Colts' wide receiver group barren. There are only five healthy receivers on the roster, including Nick Westbrook-Ikhine , who the team signed from its practice squad in the midst of its deadline day trade flurry. Those active receivers are as follows:
Standout field-stretcher Alec Pierce is expected to return from injured reserve at some point this season, but the Colts have no reason to rush him back into action as they barrel toward a lost campaign.
Downs is the No. 42 wide receiver in fantasy football through nine weeks but is poised for a potential leap into relevance beyond a flex role. CBS Sports senior fantasy writer Jamey Eisenberg detailed how this trade could make Downs a more viable starting option.
"Kansas City wasn't my favorite destination for Josh Downs, but this move gives him the chance to remain a starter in three-receiver leagues, especially if Xavier Worthy (hamstring) has an extended absence after getting hurt in Week 9 against the Jets. Downs should eventually emerge as the No. 3 target for Patrick Mahomes behind Rashee Rice and Travis Kelce, and this is clearly a quarterback upgrade for Downs with Mahomes over Daniel Jones . As long as Mahomes (elbow) is healthy for Week 10 at Atlanta, Downs will be ranked as a potential top-30 Fantasy receiver in most formats." -- Eisenberg
You can follow the latest in trade deadline news via the CBS Sports live blog .
author: Carter Bahns

title: Amani Hooker trade: Bills gets secondary help from Titans for second-round pick, per report
summary: Buffalo had a clear need in the secondary, and they addressed it with one of the NFL's best safeties
full_text:
The Buffalo Bills, who are the AFC's top seed through nine weeks with a 7-1 record, watched the Jacksonville Jaguars load up and decided they needed to make a splash before the 2026 NFL trade deadline at 4 p.m. ET on Tuesday.
They acquired Tennessee Titans safety Amani Hooker and a fifth-round pick while sending Tennessee a second-round pick, per an ESPN report . Hooker, who is 28 years old, leads the NFL in interceptions with five after picking off Cincinnati Bengals quarterback Joe Burrow three times in a 43-36 overtime defeat in Week 8.
Hooker is just the third player in the past 40 years with 50-plus tackles (52) and 5-plus interceptions (5) in his first seven games of a season, along with Washington cornerback DeAngelo Hall (2010) and Indianapolis Colts linebacker Cato June (2005). He and Green Bay Packers All-Pro safety Xavier McKinney are also the only two players in the last three seasons with 200-plus tackles (204) and double-digit interceptions (10). Acquiring Hooker also came at a steep price because his three-year, $40.5 million contract is now a team-friendly asset that has him under team control through the 2028 season.
This was a deal the Bills had to make, all things considered. Buffalo led the NFL in scoring defense with 19.3 points per game allowed from 2021 to 2025 under ex-head coach Sean McDermott, but under first-year defensive coordinator Jim Leonhard, they're allowing 23.4 points per game, ranking 16th in the league. They're also 14th in expected points added (EPA) per play and 17th in EPA per dropback, but those numbers were artificially deflated by Wentz and the wheezing Vikings offense. Through the first eight weeks of the season, the Bills were tied for 24th in scoring defense (25.9 points per game allowed), 24th in defensive EPA per play and 27th in EPA per dropback.
On Monday night, Minnesota had open wide receivers throughout the game, but Wentz was unable to find them. That won't be the case against stiffer quarterback competition in the postseason. Teams are throwing at Buffalo's secondary at the second-highest rate in the NFL (62.6%) since they are allowing the fourth-most passing yards per game (238.8) in the league, per NFL Pro. That's why Buffalo parted with a second-round pick to acquire Hooker.
author: Garrett Podell

title: Cover 32: What every team should do at 2026 NFL trade deadline, plus game balls and gaffes from Week 9
summary: Tyler Sullivan analyzes which contenders should go all-in and who needs to sell before it's too late
full_text:
There was an elephant in the room during Week 9: the 2026 NFL trade deadline.
Was it just me, or did Tuesday's deadline loom over everything? With each development, it felt as if it crystallized whether or not a team should buy, sell, or hold at the deadline. Moreover, it was hard not to watch these games through the lens of which players could be dealt and playing on a new squad by this time next week. That's what makes this weekend -- the week before the trade deadline -- so fascinating.
There's an odd finality that takes over as there are no more games to further analyze a team for what they need or should sell off. Now, it's all in the hands of the front office to either improve themselves for the stretch run or potentially move an expendable piece to help themselves down the line.
As we wrap up Week 9 and barrel towards the deadline, now is as good a time as ever to give some snap impressions on every team in the NFL and how I think they should operate before 4 p.m. ET on Tuesday.
How Game Balls work: Six are awarded to standout players from the slate of teams that won their contests, and only one player on a team can get a game ball.
Chase was unstoppable in Madrid in Cincinnati's convincing 34-17 win over the Falcons. No matter what Atlanta tried to do to slow down the Bengals star receiver, they were left in the dust. This was his second straight game with at least 10 catches, 100 yards receiving, and a touchdown. That also gives him 13 such games in his career, which is the second-most in NFL history.
BURROW. JA'MARR. TOUCHDOWN. CINvsATL on NFL Network Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/hxTp4hwro5
Lamb had another prolific day as the Cowboys fended off the Colts in Indy. The wideout was targeted 16 times and turned that into 195 yards receiving, which is the second-most receiving yards in a game this season (most on the road). This was Lamb's fourth career game with at least 180 receiving yards, which is tied with Bob Hayes for the most in Cowboys history.
CEEDEE TD 🔥 📺: #DALvsIND on FOX 📲: Stream on NFL+ https://t.co/XM2vIx7C1d pic.twitter.com/QRTQGv4NZd
Welcome back, Myles Garrett ! In his first game back since undergoing a procedure on his knee after the Week 1 opener, Garrett made his presence felt immediately. He took down Jayden Daniels three times in the 20-13 win, making the ninth career game he's tallied at least three sacks. Garrett also punched the ball free on one of those sacks on Daniels, which resulted in a Rams field goal drive right before halftime.
Myles Garrett strip sack! LARvsWAS on FOX/FOX One Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/5RBIONmDIR
After cooling off over the past two weeks, Walker heated right back up in Kansas City's Week9 win over the Jets. The Chiefs back accounted for three total touchdowns in the win, which tied his career-high (2024 at Lions). Walker is the first player with five multi-touchdown games through eight games since Terrell Davis in 1998. Already, Walker is up to 1,044 scrimmage yards and 11 scrimmage touchdowns this season.
Mahomes to Walker again! NYJvsKC on CBS/Paramount+ Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/9NbsfKzOBB
We talked about this a few weeks ago ; C.J. Stroud is balling out. The Texans quarterback has reestablished himself as a top quarterback in the NFL and just tossed five touchdowns in a blowout win over the Chargers. This was the second career game that Stroud posted at least five passing touchdowns and is just the second quarterback in franchise history to have multiple five-plus passing touchdown games.
C.J. Stroud and Kayshon Boutte with a 63-yard TD 👏 HOUvsLAC on CBS/Paramount+ Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/d6CjZxnTHH
Jordan Love and the Packers steamrolled the Patriots in Foxborough, 45-27. The Green Bay QB totaled four touchdowns in the winning effort and was dialed in from the jump. His 372 passing yards were the third-most in any game of his career. He's also just the second Packers quarterback with at least 270 passing yards in five straight games, joining Aaron Rodgers (did it four times).
JORDAN LOVE CHRISTIAN WATSON PACKERS ARE DOMINATING GBvsNE on FOX/FOX One Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/hxEPzs2KdC
CeeDee Lamb makes a diving catch He doesn't get touched Gets up and picks up several yards Fumbles while getting tackled Colts recover it after the play is reviewed FOOTBALL DALvsIND on FOX/FOX One Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/ApA5vJgMM4
One of the wildest plays of Week 9 came in the Cowboys-Colts matchup in the early seconds of the fourth quarter. Dak Prescott completed a deep ball to a sliding CeeDee Lamb , but Colts defensive back Kenneth Harris didn't touch him. Lamb realized he was untouched, got up, and ran all the way to the Indy 13-yard line. That's when Lamb fumbled, and the loose ball was recovered by the Colts.
Dan Quinn made another puzzling late-game decision. Thanks, in part, to a 42-yard catch-and-run by Stefon Diggs, the Commanders had the ball at the Rams' 31-yard line with seconds left in regulation and down by seven. One would think that Jayden Daniels would drop back and throw a prayer to the end zone in hopes of tying the game and forcing overtime, particularly as they were well within throwing range.
Instead, Daniels threw underneath for tight end Chig Okonkwo over 10 yards away from the end zone. After a lateral, the ball was fumbled and recovered by the Rams for the win.
The final play of Rams vs. Commanders featuring some laterals pic.twitter.com/9M7WYnoC2w
This is Washington simply getting too cute. At that point in the game, opt for the Hail Mary and hope for the best. Not even attempting a touchdown was ... interesting, to say the least.
Harrison Butker's struggles continued in Week 9 and included one of the major blunders of the slate. Just before halftime, the Chiefs lined up for a 56-yard field goal, but Butker's attempt was no good to the right. However, the Jets were called for an offsides penalty, which not only gave Butker another chance to put up points, but also inched him even closer for a 51-yard attempt. Despite the second attempt, he again missed wide right.
Harrison Butker misses back-to-back attempts in similar fashion following a penalty. Chiefs fans boo loudly as they head to halftime pic.twitter.com/F1BfHbIiPT
Butker has missed a total of 17 kicks since the start of last season, which is the most in the NFL over that span.
If you are a fantasy football manager that has Jonathan Taylor on your squad, you were vultured by Seth McGowan in the most peculiar way. During Indy's second possession of the day, Taylor brought the Colts to the Dallas 2-yard line after a 6-yard line. On the play, Taylor lost his shoe, which required him to go to the sideline. McGowan came in and scored on the ensuing play.
Jonathan Taylor loses a shoe, giving Seth McGowan a chance at a goal line carry which he converts into his first NFL touchdown! Awesome for him. Horrible for fantasy managers. pic.twitter.com/mil6bMm4mA
That was McGowan's first career touchdown.
The Saints first-round pick made his NFL debut on Sunday, but had a rookie blunder amid the team's overtime victory over the Browns. Tyson recorded his first career catch on a second-and-10 pass from Tyler Shough at the Cleveland 11-yard line, and it looked like he might score. As he dove towards the goal line, however, Tyson didn't protect the football well enough, and Browns linebacker Carson Schwesinger punched the ball free.
Carson Schwesinger punches the ball loose for a Browns takeaway! CLEvsNO on CBS/Paramount+ Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/t5eYGIrmOM
Tyson finished his debut with four catches for 30 yards to go along with that fumble.
During halftime of the Broncos-Panthers matchup, Bank of America Stadium held a corgi race. However, after the festivities, one of the dogs went rogue and was running all over the field. The corgi, named Lennox, bobbed and weaved a number of would-be tacklers before ultimately being run down.
Corgi loose on the pitch in Carolina! 🐾…
author: Tyler Sullivan

title: Keenan Allen trade grades: 49ers acquire WR help from Colts for Day 3 pick, per report
summary: San Francisco adds a veteran receiver at the trade deadline
full_text:
The San Francisco 49ers are adding another weapon for Brock Purdy as they gear up to race for the No. 1 seed in the NFC. At the trade deadline, the 49ers acquired veteran wide receiver Keenan Allen from the Indianapolis Colts for a sixth-round pick, per ESPN .
This is the second trade John Lynch and Colts interim general manager Ed Dodds have pulled off in the past few weeks, as the 49ers sent a fourth-round pick to Indianapolis for defensive lineman DeForest Buckner at the end of October.
Allen, who turned 34 in April, signed a one-year deal with the Colts in August and has caught 40 passes for 351 yards and one touchdown in eight games played. During Sunday's loss to the Dallas Cowboys , he caught four passes for 26 yards. Allen's 40 receptions led the Colts prior to the trade and would lead all 49ers on the season.
The 49ers were in the maket for wide receiver help, as Mike Evans (Achilles/ribs) and Deebo Samuel (hamstring) have been sidelined in recent weeks. Christian Kirk was also recently placed on injured reserve with a knee injury, where he joins fellow injured wideouts Ricky Pearsall and De'Zhaun Stribling .
Jordan Watkins , Brandin Cooks , Demarcus Robinson , KhaDarel Hodge and Jacob Cowing were Purdy's wide receivers during the 49ers' 38-17 win over the Las Vegas Raiders on Sunday. Watkins led the team with 86 yards on four receptions. The injuries haven't held San Francisco's offense back yet, as through Week 9, the 49ers rank sixth in yards per game (376.8) and third in points per game (29.4). This is a well-rounded team that registered two passing touchdowns, two rushing touchdowns and a defensive touchdown on Sunday for the first time since 2022.
Allen is a six-time Pro Bowler that spent 12 of his 14 NFL seasons with the San Diego/Los Angeles Chargers , and is the franchise's second-leading receiver behind Hall of Famer Antonio Gates . He has recorded six 1,000-yard seasons and five 100-catch seasons, which is tied for third all-time.
Let's attempt to grade this trade:
According to the Associated Press , the 49ers have had a record seven players 30 years or older catch touchdowns this season. Only the 1998 Denver Broncos , 2007 New England Patriots and 2002 Raiders have had more total touchdowns by different players 30 or older. Imagine going back in time and telling a 49ers fan that they would have Mike Evans and Keenan Allen at wide receiver. It's true that both are older players now, but Kyle Shanahan is going to be able to get the most out of them in his system.
Allen still has some tread left on the tires, and he was the Colts' most reliable receiver despite the fact that he was not brought in to play that role. Alec Pierce has been sidelined by an ankle injury, while Josh Downs hasn't reached 25 yards receiving ever since his trade request went public. Just last year, Allen caught 81 passes for 777 yards and four touchdowns with the Chargers.
The 49ers winning this trade of course hinges on health. It remains to be seen if Evans will be able to return to 100% this season with his Achilles strain, and if Allen can remain available as well. Ultimately, the 49ers didn't have to pay a high price for a veteran pass-catcher that could upgrade the offense.
It's worth mentioning that Allen is facing a minimum three-game suspension following his OWI arrest in Indianapolis earlier this year, but we don't know when that suspension will be coming down.
The Colts are obvious sellers at the trade deadline. They are losers of five straight, fired general manager Chris Ballard last month and have already shipped off Quenton Nelson , DeForest Buckner and now Keenan Allen.
Allen wasn't helping the Colts win games by himself, and he was a piece Indy felt fine parting ways with prior to Tuesday's 4 p.m. deadline. The more interesting storylines to follow with the Colts come after: what will Indianapolis end up doing with star running back Jonathan Taylor and wide receiver Josh Downs?
author: Jordan Dajani

title: Vikings trade for Kirk Cousins: Minnesota turns to familiar face to salvage its season, Raiders begin new era
summary: Minnesota's 6-2 start is being dragged down by dreadful quarterback play, while Las Vegas looks ready to hand the offense over to rookie Fernando Mendoza
full_text:
The Minnesota Vikings may have just solved their quarterback crisis.
Minnesota traded for veteran Kirk Cousins on Tuesday in the run-up to the NFL trade deadline, CBS Sports' Matt Zenitz reports, sending the Las Vegas Raiders their 2027 third-round NFL Draft pick in exchange. The 6-2 Vikings have lost consecutive games and are at risk of wasting an all-time defense with atrocious quarterback play, as seen Monday night when Carson Wentz went 8-for-25 with two interceptions.
The move puts Cousins back in purple -- he spent six seasons with the Vikings -- and also hands the keys to the Raiders to No. 1 overall pick Fernando Mendoza, who has been sitting behind Cousins.
Cousins is 4-5 in his nine starts for the Las Vegas Raiders this season, completing 64.1% of his passes at an average of 7.4 yards per attempt, with 20 touchdowns against eight interceptions. He was signed to a one-year deal this past offseason to start ahead of and mentor Mendoza but with the Raiders sitting behind the eight-ball in the playoff picture and the Vikings desperate for even adequate quarterback play (the injured Kyler Murray did not light the world on fire, either) the two teams worked out a trade that makes sense for both sides.
Cousins previously spent six seasons with the Vikings. He went 50-37-1 as the starter, completing 67.9% of his passes at 7.6 yards per attempt, with 171 touchdowns and 55 interceptions. Minnesota went to the playoffs twice in those seasons, with Cousins going just 1-2 in his three postseason games.
Cousins originally signed signed a fully-guaranteed, three-year, $84 million contract with the Vikings in 2018. He signed a two-year, $66 million extension in 2020 and a one-year, $35 million extension in 2022. Minnesota allowed him to play out the final year of his contract in 2023, a season during which he tore his Achilles just prior to hitting free agency.
Rather than re-signing with Minnesota, Cousins signed a four-year, $180 million contract with the Atlanta Falcons . However, the Falcons drafted Michael Penix Jr . with the No. 8 overall pick mere months after he signed, seemingly putting an expiration date on Cousins' tenure as the starter.
He struggled during his two seasons with the Falcons, leading the NFL in interceptions during the 2024 campaign and entering 2025 as the backup behind Penix. After Penix suffered a knee injury, Cousins was named the starter for the remainder of the 2025 season and seemingly proved enough that the Raiders were willing to sign him after he was released by the Falcons.
Now, Cousins may return to Minnesota with the charge of leading the 6-2 Vikings back to the playoffs, where they'll hope to have more success than they did during his first tenure with the team.
The Vikings have started Kyler Murray and Carson Wentz under center this season and they have gotten dreadful play out of the quarterback position, with their Monday Night Football loss to the Buffalo Bills hammering home just how badly they needed to find an upgrade. Murray and Wentz (and Max Brosmer ) combined to complete just 60.9% of their passes at an average of 6.4 yards per attempt, with eight touchdowns and five interceptions across eight games.
Justin Jefferson , one of the best receivers in football, can't get the ball into his hands (31 catches for 393 yards and four touchdowns on 51 targets) because the quarterbacks can't make the proper reads or throws. Jordan Addison , a quality deep threat, is being totally wasted (18 catches for 277 yards and one touchdown). And the Vikings can't run the ball because nobody respects their ability to throw it.
With Minnesota's defense looking like arguably the best in the league, the level of quarterback play the Vikings were getting was, frankly, unacceptable. You can't let a defense this good to go waste.
The No. 1 overall pick in the 2026 NFL Draft , Mendoza got to sit behind and learn from a veteran player to whom he has some similarities for the first half of his rookie season. Mendoza has a significantly stronger arm and is much more mobile than Cousins at this stage of his career, but they are similar in their size and stature, as well as their style of play.
Mendoza has made one appearance so far this season, completing 6 of 8 passes for 48 yards at the tail end of a blowout loss against the New England Patriots . He's got Klint Kubiak calling his plays and Brock Bowers catching his passes, but the run game he'll be married with has been extremely ineffective so far, which will put a lot of pressure on him to carry the offense the rest of the way if the Raiders cannot correct it quickly.
Mendoza will face a tough series of tests in his first few games as the starter. His first action comes against the Seattle Seahawks and the famed Dark Side defense, and he'll follow that up with a trip to Denver to take on a strong Broncos defense and then another to Cleveland to take on the Browns before the Raiders go on their bye. Post-bye week, the schedule does ease up a bit with games against the Los Angeles Chargers , Tennessee Titans and Arizona Cardinals , but he will still face the Broncos again in Week 15, and then the Kansas City Chiefs in the regular-season finale.
author: Jared Dubin

title: Jonathan Taylor mock trades: How Giants, Broncos, Vikings could target Colts star RB
summary: The Colts need to replenish their draft assets, and dealing their three-time Pro Bowl running back could produce a significant return
full_text:
The Indianapolis Colts are in free fall, having lost five straight games after a 2-2 start to the season. During the losing streak, Indianapolis has fired GM Chris Ballard (after the first of the five straight losses, to previously winless Titans ) and traded two franchise cornerstones. Interim GM Ed Dodds shipped guard Quenton Nelson to the Seahawks and defensive tackle DeForest Buckner to the 49ers .
Trades often beget more trades -- or at least trade rumors, and that's been true for the Colts. Ahead of the trade deadline, plenty of Indianapolis players have been thought of as trade candidates, though one stands out above the rest: running back Jonathan Taylor .
He had 20 touchdowns and nearly 2,000 yards from scrimmage last year, and he's on his way to another big season, but the Colts are stuck going nowhere once again. He's 27 and has played in just one playoff game -- as a rookie in 2020. He would command a huge return haul, and the Colts could very much use it, especially because they don't have their 2027 first-round pick (currently No. 4 overall) after last year's disastrous Sauce Gardner trade.
Taylor would have plenty of suitors if made available, and the situation isn't too dissimilar from what the Panthers were going through with Christian McCaffrey in 2022. McCaffrey is a more versatile player than Taylor in the passing game and was younger than Taylor is now when that deal happened, but he had also been more injured. In the deal with the 49ers in 2022, Carolina received second-, third-, fourth- and fifth-round picks.
With that in mind, here are four teams who could come calling about Taylor and what a mock trade might look like:
Giants receive: RB Jonathan Taylor Colts receive: RB Cam Skattebo , 2027 second-round pick, 2028 fourth-round pick
Last month, John Harbaugh said he "would love" to have a " Derrick Henry circumstance or a " Saquon Barkley circumstance." Whether he meant to or not, it was surely a bummer for Giants fans to hear Harbaugh mention his running back from last year and a former Giants running back in the same sentence. Regardless, Taylor could be that type of workhorse. Harbaugh even confirmed the Giants put an offer in on Taylor but retracted it . The Colts getting two high draft picks over the next two years, plus Skattebo, who showed promise as a rookie but has had an up-and-down 2026, would be a decent return. The Giants are leading a bad NFC East, and even if it doesn't finish that way, having Taylor next to Jaxson Dart next year would be an enticing prospect.
One thing to note, though, is that Harbaugh comes from one of the most patient, draft-and-develop franchises in Baltimore. This would be a significant departure from that.
Bengals receive: RB Jonathan Taylor, 2027 fifth-round pick Colts receive: RB Chase Brown , 2027 second-round pick, 2027 fourth-round pick
This would be similar to the package the Panthers got for McCaffrey, but instead of a third-round pick, the Colts would get Brown. At 26, he's younger and has less wear and tear than Taylor. He's also an accomplished player and productive pass catcher who has handled a bell-cow workload before. A change of scenery could do him good, as he has struggled to get going this season. For the Bengals , this would be a second major win-now move in just over six months; they sent the No. 10 pick to the Giants in April for Dexter Lawrence . The Bengals had tried to work in more under-center looks, but were among the worst teams using it. Now, they're once again a shotgun-heavy, pass-heavy team. In the playoffs or in iffy weather, though, they might need more balance. Cincinnati also has an extra third-round pick, which helps make giving up so many picks easier to swallow.
Broncos receive: RB Jonathan Taylor, 2027 sixth-round pick Colts receive: RB J.K. Dobbins , 2027 second-round pick, 2027 third-round pick, 2028 fourth-round pick
The Broncos traded a first-round pick for an upgrade at wide receiver in Jaylen Waddle this offseason (though it hasn't really worked out yet). Would they make another big deal for an upgrade at running back in Taylor? The Broncos have struggled to muster much on the ground, exacerbating quarterback Bo Nix's struggles -- though Nix has been better of late. Dobbins is on a two-year deal, though there's an out after this year should the Colts choose to use it.
Vikings receive: RB Jonathan Taylor Colts receive: RB Jordan Mason , 2027 second-round pick, 2027 third-round pick
The Vikings are in the quarterback market after an awful "Monday Night Football" loss to the Bills featured Carson Wentz throwing two picks with Kyler Murray (hamstring) sidelined. If they can't cash in there, though, perhaps they could try to upgrade the other part of their sagging offense. Mason would be a nice, young-ish piece for the Colts to get back to help the rest of the way. Plus, the Vikings have draft capital to spare, with an extra third, two extra fifths and two extra sixths.
author: Zachary Pereles

title: Dolphins lose captain Zach Sieler for season with ruptured biceps
summary: The Dolphins captain ruptured his biceps on the opening play against the Lions but remarkably finished the game
full_text:
The Miami Dolphins (1-7) didn't just lose a game in their 19-9 defeat against the Detroit Lions in Week 9, but they also lost one of their best players. Defensive tackle Zach Sieler , one of the team's best players and team captains, ruptured his biceps and will undergo surgery with a projected 5-6 month recovery, thus ending his 2026 season, per ESPN .
Sieler sustained the injury on the first play but finished the game. Sieler signed a three-year, $64 million extension in 2025 that has him under contract through 2029, but at the age of 31 for a rebuilding team, he may have been a prime trade deadline acquisition candidate had he not gotten injured.
The Dolphins captain totaled 24 tackles and two sacks in eight games played for Miami this season. Sieler joined the Dolphins in 2019, and he has 37.5 sacks and 235 quarterback pressures with Miami. Both of those numbers lead Miami in those two key pass-rush categories in the span of Sieler's Dolphins career.
author: Garrett Podell

title: Bengals call off Arnold Ebiketie trade with Eagles after nearly botching compensatory pick situation
summary: The Bengals were in line to lose a 2027 third-round pick awarded from Trey Hendrickson's departure
full_text:
The Cincinnati Bengals ' trade to acquire Arnold Ebiketie from the Philadelphia Eagles in exchange for a 2027 sixth-round draft pick has officially fallen through, as reported by NFL Network's Ian Rapoport . While the teams agreed to the deal, it had not yet become official before the Bengals realized major compensatory pick ramifications may be tied to finalizing the move.
On the surface, it looked like a fairly ordinary deal: Cincinnati would acquire a rotational pass rusher for a late-round pick. The Bengals are going for a Super Bowl this year, while Philadelphia has spent most of this deadline gearing up for a draft-heavy reload. As it turns out, though, Cincinnati's front office nearly committed a major gaffe with the trade. By acquiring Ebiketie, whom the Eagles signed as a compensatory free agent this offseason, the Bengals would have forfeited the 2027 third-round compensatory pick they were set to acquire after losing Trey Hendrickson in free agency. Nick Korte, who contributes to the contract source site OverTheCap, was first to point this out .
Oh that's brutal on the 3rd round comp pick! as noted by @nickkorte pic.twitter.com/OwwyNB71PA
Why does Ebiketie count against the Bengals' formula, you ask? According to Appendix V of the NFL Collective Bargaining Agreement ...
If a Club trades for a player who was a CFA during that League Year, whether the player was another Club's CFA or the acquiring Club's own CFA, the player will be considered a CFA gained by the acquiring Club and will be included in the Compensatory netting process described above.
It's important to note -- as Korte did -- that the Bengals may have believed former guard Cordell Volson counted as one of their CFAs lost. However, Volson has not played a single snap this year and, as the chart above shows, does not count toward the CFAs lost formula. Whether it's a miscalculation or a misunderstanding of Volson's standing, it's not a great look for Bengals director of personnel Duke Tobin and the rest of the front office.
Korte's compensatory pick expertise has now helped the Bengals twice. In March 2024, he noticed Cincinnati wasn't getting the appropriate draft compensation for losing Jessie Bates III in free agency. The NFL issued a rare correction, and the Bengals went from getting two sixth-round picks to getting a third-round pick and a sixth-round pick in the upcoming draft.
It remains to be seen if Cincinnati, who sit at 6-2 in the No. 6 seed of the AFC wild card as of the trade deadline, will look elsewhere for edge rushing help. The Bengals used both free agency (EDGE Boye Mafe , DL Jonathan Allen , S Bryan Cook ) and trade acquisitions (acquiring DL Dexter Lawrence from the Giants ) to boost their defense this year, but apparently felt it needed reinforcements at EDGE after rookie Cashius Howell (wrist) landed on injured reserve. Mafe has lived up to the offseason hype with 5.5 sacks in eight games, but no other edge rusher has more than two.
It is also uncertain as to what happens with Ebiketie. The 2-7 Eagles are having a massive sale amid a disastrous 2026. Monday, Philadelphia parted ways with standout defensive tackle Jordan Davis on Monday, sending him to the Jaguars for a 2027 first-round pick and a 2029 second-round pick. Earlier in the year, they sent center Cam Jurgens to the Ravens for a 2027 fifth-round pick and a 2028 second-round pick.
author: Zachary Pereles

title: After Puka Nacua injury, five receivers the Rams should target at the 2026 trade deadline
summary: With Puka Nacua and Davante Adams both out, the Rams suddenly need some help at wide receiver
full_text:
With NFL trade deadline coming up at 4 p.m. ET on Tuesday, one team to watch is going to be the Los Angeles Rams , who are currently in desperate need of some help at receiver.
The Rams first took a hit at the position back in October when Davante Adams went down with an injury and they took an even bigger one this week with the loss of Puka Nacua . The Rams' star, who is dealing with MCL and PCL sprains in addition to turf toe, is expected to be placed on injured reserve this week , which will knock him out until at least Week 15.
With Adams and Nacua both out until at least December, that means a Rams team that went all-in this season with a Myles Garrett and Aaron Donald juggernaut defensive line to maximize reigning MVP Matthew Stafford's remaining window is down to Konata Mumpfield , Tutu Atwell , and Jordan Whittington at receiver. That trio has combined for just 20 receptions, 273 yards, and one receiving touchdown this year. During an interview Monday, Sean McVay admitted that a trade might happen by the deadline.
"You look at all avenues to solve the situations that come up. I would never rule it out," McVay said.
If we know one thing about Rams general manager Les Snead, it's that he loves to wheel and deal. He's proven throughout his career that he's not shy when it comes to pulling the trigger on a big trade, so it's very possible we'll see the Rams make some sort of deal by 4 p.m. ET.
The options for those deals are narrowing quickly, though. According to ESPN, the Jacksonville Jaguars are planning to keep wide receiver Brian Thomas Jr . on their roster despite him having just one reception for 12 yards in their last four games.
With that in mind, let's check out five possible trade options for the Rams at receiver.
There is no team that loves to make a big trade more than the Rams, and this would be huge. Going after Pickens would make sense, and that's because the Cowboys actually might be willing to deal him. Pickens is playing on the franchise tag this year, and there's a good chance that he ends up leaving Dallas after the season. If that happens, the Cowboys would get nothing, but if they traded him now, they'd at least get something in return.
The only problem with this option is that the Cowboys play in a bad division, so it might not make any sense for them to start trading away their best players. The Cowboys are currently 4-5 and sitting just 1.5 games out of first place. Dallas may still think the NFC East is up for grabs and worth trying to win, especially as the Philadelphia Eagles begin to sell pieces and load up for the future.
On top of that, the Cowboys just might not be active at all this deadline, especially after already making a midseason deal for Joey Porter Jr . . Despite Dallas not playing Pickens in their Sunday win over the Colts , team owner and de facto general manager Jerry Jones said on his weekly 105.3 The Fan radio spot that the decision was "100 percent injury related" and not tied to any pending trades.
Cowboys owner Jerry Jones on @1053thefan said Joey Porter Jr. and George Pickens not playing Sunday was “100 percent injury related.” Jones said “don’t count out” the Cowboys potentially making a move today. But adds “I don’t look for us to make a significant trade today.”
Although the Cowboys are very much still in the division race, our reporter in Dallas, Garrett Podell, still thinks it makes sense for them to trade Pickens, and it's certainly possible that the Cowboys will at least be open to listening to offers at the minimum.
Pickens' production in Dallas has been underwhelming this year. He's caught just 39 passes for 533 yards for the Cowboys, but he might be able to put up bigger numbers if he became the top weapon in a Rams' offense that ranks seventh in the NFL in passing yards per game. A move to Los Angeles would also give Pickens a chance to play with the reigning NFL MVP.
Although adding Pickens would make some sense, it wouldn't be easy. The Rams don't have a lot of draft capital to send to Dallas, so they'd have to get that figured out. The Rams also don't have very much salary cap space, so they'd have to figure out a way to fit the rest of Pickens' fully guaranteed franchise tag salary under their cap. Pickens' deal is worth $27.3 million, and the Rams would owe him the pro-rated amount of that, which would be about $13.65 million.
When Jennings signed with the Vikings back in May, he probably figured he was going to have a big year. With opposing defenses worried about Justin Jefferson and Jordan Addison , that should have opened things up for Jennings, but that hasn't happened.
Through eight games, Jennings has caught just six passes for n54 yards, which is an extremely low total even when you take into account the Vikings' offense has been historically bad this year. Jennings has understandably been frustrated, and those frustrations are starting to show on the field.
Jauan Jennings was pissed off he didn’t get the ball when he was wide open in the end zone on Sunday A total of 5 targets in 4 games will do this to you pic.twitter.com/25tacVpI0f
Due to the Vikings QB situation, things likely won't be getting better any time soon. Jennings is a the third option in a loaded offense and even if the Vikings add a QB, that's going ot benefit Jefferson and Addison more than it will benefit Jennings.
One interesting to thing to keep in mind with Jennings is that he had a chance to return to San Francisco: The 49ers had a deal in place to acquire him from Minnesota, but he basically killed the trade . There appears to be some bad blood there and going to the Rams would be a way for him to get revenge on the 49ers.
The veteran receiver caught 55 passes for 643 yards and nine touchdowns while playing for the 49ers last season, and he would probably enjoy a return to the NFC West.
This move feels like it would make a lot of sense for both sides. On the Titans ' end, they have several solid receivers, but everyone is essentially going to waste while playing in a Tennessee offense that ranks in the bottom five in the NFL in passing yards per game. Rookie Carnell Tate leads the team in receiving yards (413) while free agent addition Wan'Dale Robinson is leads the team in receptions (35).
Ridley has basically been the odd man out this year: He's caught just six passes for 91 yards through eight games. If the 1-7 Titans decide to hold a fire sale, then it wouldn't be surprising at all to see them dump Ridley.
The 31-year-old actually took a pay cut this year to stay with the Titans. The upside for the Rams is that Ridley doesn't have any guaranteed money left on his contract after this season, so they wouldn't be on the hook for anything in 2027.
Ridley was recently involved in an incident at the Nashville airport and that could make the Titans more likely unload at him at an even lower price than they might have originally been hoping to get.
One thing that could scare the Rams away is that Ridley (Hip) was on the injury report for Tennessee's most recent game back in Week 8. He also missed a total of 10 games last season due to injury. Considering the Rams' luck with injuries right now, those two things might be enough of a red flag to keep them away, but the 2018 first-round pick would certainly be an intriguing option.
With Alec Pierce still out, the Colts might not be interested in trading one of these two receiver, but with the way their season is going, the Colts should really be open to trading anyone and everyone. At 2-7, the Colts aren't going anywhere this season, so there goal should be to stockpile as many draft picks for the future by trading players away.
On Downs' end, he's in the final year of his rookie deal, which is one reason why a trade could be win-win for both sides. The Colts would get something in return for a player they're possibly going to lose anyway, while the cash-strapped Rams would only have to worry about Downs' $3.9 million base salary. Since he's already…
