title: 2026 NFL trade deadline: Ranking Vikings quarterback options with Kirk Cousins as best fit in Minnesota
summary: After Carson Wentz exposed Minnesota's offensive problems on national television, the 6-2 Vikings must consider an aggressive move
full_text:
The Minnesota Vikings are the rare 6-2 team in crisis. After a brutal 23-6 loss to the Buffalo Bills , Minnesota finds itself looking for a new quarterback on trade deadline day. Starting in place of the injured Kyler Murray (hamstring), Carson Wentz went 8-for-25 for 81 yards and two interceptions, putting Minnesota's broken offense on display for everyone to see on national television.
Murray has been one of the worst full-time starters in the NFL , and "full-time" is a stretch, considering he's missed two games and most of a third due to two different injuries. Minnesota is 28th is offensive points per game (17.4), and its 11 offensive touchdowns are tied with the Chargers for fewest in the league.
Changing starting quarterbacks in the middle of the season is far from ideal, but so is the Vikings' current situation. Continuing to roll out this level of quarterback play would mean wasting a Super Bowl-caliber defense. What Minnesota does at the game's most important position will change the entire tenor of the trade deadline, and there are quite a few options.
Who says you can't go home? (Or, at least, back to one of your homes?) Kirk Cousins spent 2019-23 with the Vikings, the final two years of which were under Kevin O'Connell. Cousins played high-level football, especially in 2023 before tearing his Achilles, under O'Connell, and he has been a pleasant surprise for the Raiders , keeping the seat warm for No. 1 pick Fernando Mendoza .
This would not be a perfect solution -- there are none of those at this point -- as Cousins is coming off a three-interception game and isn't the player he was when he was in Minnesota previously. His mobility has taken a huge hit; he's 38 years old, and the arm strength has waned, too. But this would be the best option in a pinch. Cousins knows how to feed his best players the ball, and the Vikings have a great "best player" in Justin Jefferson . His experience in the system would help on a tight turnaround.
One big question would be why the Raiders would make this trade. Even with Mendoza waiting in the wings, Las Vegas has little reason to do this. It would force Mendoza to make his first career start on a short week of preparation against the Seahawks , one of the league's best defenses. Cousins has been an important part of Mendoza's development, too. Splitting that duo midseason doesn't make sense, and Cousins' presence would continue to pay dividends once Mendoza does eventually take over.
Another well-traveled veteran playing solidly in a placeholder role, Geno Smith would be the second-best option for Minnesota. Moreover, the Jets showed a willingness to make big trade-deadline sales before, having traded both Sauce Gardner and Quinnen Williams at the deadline last year for king's ransom. Trading Smith and getting back some solid trade compensation would add to their considerable war chest of 2027 picks, which currently includes three first-round selections.
Smith had a miserable 2025 with the Raiders but has been much better with the Jets, cutting down on the turnovers while still delivering on some of his trademark downfield aggression. His 16 completions for 20+ yards downfield are the fourth-most in the league this season. Downfield passing has been a disaster for Minnesota this season.
One issue here could be the Jets not having a proven backup. The only other quarterback on the 53-man roster is rookie Cade Klubnik , and Will Levis is on the practice squad. Would the Jets want Murray, who is on a cheap one-year deal anyway? If not, it might be hard to make this move; playing nearly half the season with a middle-round rookie is a tough look, even if New York is well out of the playoff picture. It's important to have a viable offensive ecosystem, if only to evaluate your personnel and keep the team engaged.
The Colts reportedly told Daniel Jones they will not trade him, but what if the Vikings came in willing to overpay? The Colts have already sold off Quenton Nelson and DeForest Buckner and could move other veterans ( Jonathan Taylor , Josh Downs , Grover Stewart ) before Tuesday's 4 p.m. ET deadline. Jones has endured a brutal season, but he's also had brutal surroundings, including one of the league's most underwhelming groups of pass catchers.
Jones spent time on the Vikings' practice squad in 2024, but this would be an underwhelming reunion. Jones has been a turnover machine and one of the worst starters in the NFL this year, even worse than Murray. He has not had a single game with more passing touchdowns than interceptions. Perhaps O'Connell sees something we don't, but it's hard to envision Jones providing any meaningful upgrade.
author: Zachary Pereles

title: Josh Allen, Bills suffocate Vikings; NFL trade deadline day arrives with big names on the market
summary: Plus, Georgia has taken over the top spot in our CFB Power Rankings
full_text:
This is an article version of the CBS Sports HQ AM Newsletter, the ultimate guide to every day in sports. You can sign up to get it in your inbox every weekday morning here .
Welcome to NFL trade deadline day! Teams have been making moves over the last week or so, but there are quite a few big names left on the board. Be sure to follow along with all the latest rumors, news and analysis throughout the day.
Fortunately, our own Zach Pereles has put together a comprehensive trade deadline preview -- full of buyers, sellers and key players to watch. As the clock ticks toward the deadline, everyone is waiting to see whether the Colts will deal star running back Jonathan Taylor .
Taylor is one of the best rushers in the entire league, and he would be a great fit for any team hoping to add some explosiveness and some finish to its backfield
Our own Tyler Sullivan also ranked the 20 most impactful players who could be on the move ahead of the deadline, but Taylor was not No. 1. That distinction went to Raiders QB Kirk Cousins , who could save the Vikings or Seahawks . Despite those fits, it sounds like Cousins will be remaining in Las Vegas .
Here are a few more key players who could change teams:
16. Tuli Tuipulotu, EDGE, Chargers 17. Tony Pollard, RB, Titans 18. Riq Woolen, CB, Eagles 19. Jerry Jeudy, WR, Browns 20. Landon Dickerson, OL, Eagles
Finally, here is what every single team should do on this glorious trade deadline day. Enjoy the drama, everyone!
What was supposed to be a marquee SEC showdown between Georgia and Ole Miss turned into a beatdown before the first quarter was over. The Bulldogs slaughtered the Rebels 42-7 and that was more than enough for them to take over the No. 1 spot in our updated College Football Power Rankings .

title: NFL Week 10 picks and score predictions: Lions run over Patriots in Germany, Bengals survive
summary: John Breech predicts every Week 10 game, including a Lions victory over the Patriots in Munich
full_text:
I just got back from the NFL game in Spain, and I think I should probably start going more often, since Week 10 ended up being my best week of the year for picks.
I went 14-1 straight up, and yes, I should probably just retire at this point, but I don't want to retire while I'm on top; I want to retire when I hit rock bottom, which might actually happen this week. Speaking of rock bottom, I went to McDonald's four times while I was in Spain, and let me just say, I only went there because Madrid had the nicest McDonald's I've ever seen. I mean, just look at this place.
I'm now starting to understand why those Falcons players went to McDonald's. This is like the nicest McDonald's I've ever seen in my life. Wouldn't put it past Madrid to have a Michelin rated McDonald's #Bengals #Falcons #Spain https://t.co/w8WixT6iN2 pic.twitter.com/TMAeeXm9Fk
There were also people tailgating inside of a Taco Bell.
Taco Bell is in fact a mad house. NFL fans everywhere.  Nothing like a pregame cheesy gordita crunch. #Bengals #Falcons #Spain #Madrid https://t.co/0uAafegmaM pic.twitter.com/cpjfyWy33X
If you need just one reason to ever visit Spain, tailgating at Taco Bell has to be it. Unfortunately, there's no game in Spain this week, so there will be no tailgating at Taco Bell, but there is a game in Germany, and it will be the final NFL game of this year that kicks off at 9:30 a.m. ET, which is definitely for the best, because I've reached my maximum limit for 9:30 a.m. ET games.
The Patriots and Lions will be playing in the early game on Sunday. So who's going to win? Let's get to the Week 10 picks and find out.
Actually, before we get to the Week 10 picks, here's a quick reminder that you can check out the weekly picks from every CBSSports.com NFL expert by clicking here . Also, I'm in charge of the NFL newsletter here at CBSSports.com and if you want me invading your inbox twice a week, then you should definitely sign up. If you want to subscribe, all you have to do is click here and enter your email address . If you do that, it will instantly make us best friends and you don't even have to feel bad about that because I've already let all my best friends know that they might be replaced this week.
Alright, now let's get to the picks for real
Based on everything I've seen from the Commanders , I already know exactly how this game is going to play out: Washington is going to keep this thing close until the end only to lose (or tie) because no one in the organization has any idea what to do in any key late-game situation.
For instance, let's go back to Week 5 when the Commanders pulled off one of the all-time worst late-game gaffes in a tie with the Giants . Washington had the game won. All Jayden Daniels had to do was literally anything except what he actually did.
The Commanders can't get the play off in time and this game ends in a tie pic.twitter.com/WmPp6q5hU0
Look at the Giants players in that clip. They're celebrating. When the other team is CELEBRATING a tie, that means you lost.
Surely Daniels and the Commanders learned their lesson, right? Wrong. In their Week 9 game against the Rams , they needed a 32-yard touchdown on the final play, but instead of throwing it in the end zone, Daniels threw the ball five yards past the line of scrimmage because the Commanders apparently thought they were going to be able to lateral the ball to each other all the way into the end zone. There's a reason that never works.
With the game on the line Jayden Daniels can’t get the ball out of his hand. pic.twitter.com/2D8I1YWsiA
Now, you could blame Daniels for this stuff, but ultimately, it falls on the coaching staff. In the Rams' game, Daniels said he was just running the play that was called . In the Giants' game, someone on the coaching staff should have made it clear to everyone on the field that the clock has to come to a stop on that play, whether it's a spike or a player running out of bounds.
So what does this mean for this game? It means that the Commanders are actually playing decent football and if their coaching staff doesn't let them down, I think they have a good chance of winning. The Giants are beat up at quarterback, they're beat up at running back, and they're surviving by the skin of their teeth. Four of their five wins have come by one score. Good teams win close games -- are you taking notes, Commanders -- and I'm starting to feel like the Giants might be a sneaky good team.
To me, this is arguably the most fascinating game of Week 10. If the Commanders lose, their season is all but over, but if they win, they'll be right back in the NFC East race. I feel like this is a pick I'm going to regret as soon as I make it, but I'm taking the desperate Commanders.
PICK: Commanders 24-17 over Giants
With this game being played in Munich, I feel like this would be the perfect time to answer the one question that has been on all of our minds over the past few months: Who would win a beer-chugging contest between Mike Vrabel and Dan Campbell?
With these two guys heading to the beer capital of the world, there's no reason not to find out. And to be honest, based on how the Patriots have been playing recently, Vrabel could probably use a few beers right about now. I'm not in charge of scheduling events for the NFL in Germany this week, which is probably for the best, but if I were, I would rent out the Hofbrauhaus and then give both Campbell and Vrabel one full stein of beer to chug. Instead of a coin toss on Sunday, this is how we would decide who's getting the ball first.
I was at the Hofbrauhaus once and it took me an hour to finish my beer. The Germans were definitely laughing at me.
What's the record for most beers drank in one sitting here? I think I'm going to try to break it. pic.twitter.com/UQ5kOtxyPL
The Germans might be laughing at the Patriots, too, if they can't turn things around this week. Vrabel is known as one of the smartest defensive-minded coaches in the NFL, but he hasn't figured out how to stop any NFC North teams. The Patriots have faced two NFC North teams this year and not only have they gone 0-2, but they're surrendering an average of 37.5 points per game. Yikes.
The NFC North is so good that I might not pick against any of their teams for the rest of the season unless they're playing another NFC North team. If you've looked at the NFL standings at any point over the past 24 hours, you may have noticed that the NFC North is arguably the best all-around division in the NFL this year and possibly ever.
All four teams are at least three games over .500, which is the first time that's ever happened through the first nine weeks. Oh, and did I mention that the NFC North is 20-4 against all other divisions. They are destroying everyone. On the other hand, you have the Patriots, who are 3-1 against AFC East opponents, but 2-3 against everyone else. The Patriots have had one of the worst passing defenses in the NFL over the past several weeks, and now, they have to face off against a QB in Jared Goff who ranks in the top five in passing yards per game this year.
The Lions might put up 50 points. The good news for the Patriots is that even if the Lions do put up a 50-burger, New England might still keep up. Detroit has given up the MOST passing yards per game this year (260.9), so Drake Maye could certainly get some turkey carving practice for Thanksgiving here by carving up the Lions' defense. That being said, I've decided not to trust Maye against good teams.
The Patriots have faced six opponents this year with winning records, and in those games, Maye has thrown 11 interceptions to nine touchdowns. Based on how I think this game is going to go, Vrabel might need a Hofbrauhaus beer after it's over.
PICK: Lions 34-27 over Patriots
Deshaun Watson did not play in Week 9 for the Browns , but there's no chance he's going to miss this game. This is the ultimate revenge, though, I can't say for sure whether this is more about the Texans trying to get revenge…
author: John Breech

title: Prisco's NFL Week 10 Power Rankings: Top 5 remains same, Bengals and Packers surging thanks to MVP candidates
summary: Pete Prisco shares his Week 10 Power Rankings for the 2026 NFL season, including the Vikings dropping five spots
full_text:
Run the ball. Run the ball. Run the ball.
That's all we ever hear about NFL offenses. If you don't run the ball, you are dead.
Let's take a look at the Cincinnati Bengals and Green Bay Packers. They don't run it well at all. Yet both enter Week 10 as legitimate Super Bowl contenders. Why? They can throw the heck out of the football.
They are the top two passing offenses in the NFL, with the Bengals averaging 285.5 yards per game and the Packers right behind at 279.7. Both have averaged over 300 the past three games.
Run games? The Bengals are 30th in rush yards per game, while the Packers are dead last. Neither is close to 100 yards per game, although their numbers are slightly up over the past three games. Neither team averages 4.0 per rush; the Packers are at 3.0, which ranks 31st in the league.
Throw to score. Run to win.
Both will have to run it better when they need to run it late in games, but, for now, having Bengals quarterback Joe Burrow and Packers quarterback Jordan Love sling it around is the way these teams need to play.
I jokingly say that neither should ever call a run play until they are leading late in games. Ok, so I'm half-joking. But you get the idea. If they keep playing with the foot on the pedal, with two big-play quarterbacks, each with a pair of down-the-field receivers, they will be tough to beat.
Both are now in my top 10 of the Power Rankings, with Green Bay moving up to No. 10 this week, with the Bengals a few spots ahead at No. 7.
Staying there for both of them will mean continuing to play the same style of football, which means not allowing the old, tired run-it folks to influence play-calling. Play to the strengths and don't get caught up in the adages about running the football.
Run the ball? Not these two. Nor should they —and both just might ride the right arms of their quarterbacks to a Super Bowl.
author: Pete Prisco

title: Cardinals turn down trade offer for S Budda Baker
summary: Arizona Cardinals safety Budda Baker is one of those guys who everyone in the fanbase loves. You root for him and buy his jersey to be worn on game days. You want the best for him and are happy he is patrolling center field for your favorite NFL club. Early Tuesday, another team made a […]
full_text: ARLINGTON, TX - NOVEMBER 01: Budda Baker #3 of the Arizona Cardinals warms up prior to an NFL football game against the Dallas Cowboys at AT&T Stadium on November 1, 2026 in Arlington, Texas. (Photo by Cooper Neill/Getty Images) | Getty Images Arizona Cardinals safety Budda Baker is one of those guys who everyone in the fanbase loves. You root for him and buy his jersey to be worn on game days. You want the best for him and are happy he is patrolling center field for your favorite NFL club. Early Tuesday, another team made a offer to acquire his services. RELATED: CARDINALS SIGN QB JOSH JOHNSON It is reported by NFL Insider Jordan Schultz that the Buffalo Bills reached out to Arizona GM Monti Ossenfort about a trade offer for Baker. Although Ossenfort considered the offer, it was rejected. The Bills then moved on and traded for S Amani Hooker of the Tennessee Titans instead. Sources: Prior to trading for Amani Hooker, the #Bills made a very strong push for #Cardinals 8x Pro Bowl S Budda Baker. Arizona gave off the impression they don’t want to trade a franchise icon – despite a lost season – and Buffalo eventually got a deal done in Tennessee. pic.twitter.com/JkFizD66zf — Jordan Schultz (@Schultz_Report) November 10, 2026 No details on the trade offer for Baker have been made known, but the Titans received a second-round draft pick for Hooker plus a fifth-round selection. Hooker is in his eighth NFL season, all with the Titans. He has played in 103 games with 74 starts and has 468 total tackles, 14 tackles for loss, 1 sack, 45 pass defenses, 5 forced fumbles, 17 interceptions, zero 110+ tackle seasons, and 43 missed tackles. He has zero Pro Bowl accolades. In comparison, Baker is in his 10th NFL season, all with the Cardinals. He has played in 147 games with 137 starts and has 1,083 total tackles, 55 tackles for loss, 13.5 sacks, 48 pass defenses, 8 forced fumbles, 9 interceptions, 6 110+ tackle seasons, and 98 missed tackles. Oh yeah, he has been named to seven Pro Bowls and is assured to garner his eighth after this season. The numbers aren’t even close. Yes, Hooker is a seasoned veteran and a good tackler. He has good interception numbers, but he has yet to have a 100+ tackle season and has zero accolades. Every player who comes into the league has the same goal of being a part of a Super Bowl team. Since coming to the desert in 2017, the Cardinals, with Baker as a roster member, have won zero division titles, came in second once, went to the playoffs a single season (2021), and lost 34-11 to the Los Angeles Rams, and that is it. Ossenfort had the opportunity to free Baker from this annual situation. Looking at this year, is Arizona already out of the division title race? The playoff picture? Certainly, Ossenfort’s job is to secure quality players for the Cardinals’ roster. And that is what Baker is. He is considered the face of the franchise. Then again, Ossenfort could have done Baker a solid and sent him to a team that has a playoff future every year. They win games and have a franchise quarterback plus a great defense. The Cardinals have, well, Baker. He gave his all to the Arizona franchise, and they still aren’t close to sniffing a championship. Tell Baker that we love him, thank you for all he has done, and wish him well to a playoff contender. Look at what the Cleveland Browns did for Myles Garrett. They gave him the opportunity, late in his career, to get a ring. Even if the Rams don’t go to the Super Bowl this year or the next, Garrett still has more of a chance with the Rams than with the Browns. And yes, Cleveland got a first-round draft pick in the deal. Damn Budda is tired of losing man. Let him go. — Game Dey 🐅 (@GameDey513) November 10, 2026 And remember, the Bills did not negate the offer – it was Ossenfort. If the Bills gave up a second-round pick for Hooker, it just seems natural to assume that a first-round draft pick would have been involved in the offer for Baker. Not that we have gotten this information from any NFL Insider or the Cardinals’ front office. But a guy with no Pro Bowls or 100+ tackle seasons versus a player who has been voted to the Pro Bowl for the past seven consecutive years just seems likely. Right?
author: Barry Shuck

title: Cardinals QB room not finished yet, sign Joey Aguilar
summary: What a difference a few short weeks make in the National Football League. Take a look at the Arizona Cardinals quarterback room in training camp: Jacoby Brissett, seasoned veteran Gardner Minshew, third-round rookie Carson Beck, and 2025 holdover Kedon Slovis. RELATED: VETERAN QB JOSH JOHNSON SIGNED Take that same position group and view it today: […]
full_text: JACKSONVILLE, FLORIDA - AUGUST 21: Joey Aguilar #17 of the Jacksonville Jaguars throws against the Carolina Panthers during the second half of the preseason game at EverBank Field on August 21, 2026 in Jacksonville, Florida. (Photo by Mike Carlson/Getty Images) | Getty Images What a difference a few short weeks make in the National Football League. Take a look at the Arizona Cardinals quarterback room in training camp: Jacoby Brissett, seasoned veteran Gardner Minshew, third-round rookie Carson Beck, and 2025 holdover Kedon Slovis. RELATED: VETERAN QB JOSH JOHNSON SIGNED Take that same position group and view it today: Beck. In the past two days, Cardinals GM Monti Ossenfort has signed journeyman and free agent Josh Johnson, and has now claimed Joey Aguilar off the practice squad of the Jacksonville Jaguars. Apparently, Cardinals fans will get what they have been asking for since the 31-7 beating the team took from the Seattle Seahawks in Week 2. Beck seems the likely starter after Minshew is feared to have suffered a torn UCL in his throwing arm. Minshew injured his arm before the half, but continued to play. Currently, he is undergoing tests, so we will see. Meanwhile, the Cardinals signed 40-year-old journeyman Josh Johnson to the QB room, and today have claimed QB Joey Aguilar off the practice squad of the Jacksonville Jaguars. Just last week, Arizona shipped off their starting quarterback, Brissett, to the Baltimore Ravens for a 2027 fourth-round draft pick plus a 2028 seventh-round selection. Along with Brissett, the Cardinals gave up a 2027 fifth-round pick. Brissett was benched because of poor play, and the fact that the offense was stagnant. Minshew orchestrated two late comebacks in the same game, a 33-30 win over the Dallas Cowboys. Two days later, Brissett was traded. Given the Minshew news, perhaps the Arizona front office moved a little too early on that decision. The Cardinals were already down to two signalcallers before the Minshew injury. So, on Monday, GM Monti Ossenfort signed Johnson, who entered the league in 2009 and is now on his 19th NFL team. He has multiple stints with the San Francisco 49ers, New York Jets, Cincinnati Bengals, and the Ravens. His last contract was with the Bengals on a one-year $1.5 million deal. He played for the Sacramento Mountain Lions of the second version of the UFL in 2012. He was also signed to play with the San Diego Fleet of the AAF in 2019, but that league folded before he saw any game time. He was also signed by the Los Angeles Wildcats of the XFL in 2020, but COVID hit and all games were cancelled. Ossenfort was seeking a young arm to become QB3. Aguilar fits that bill at age 25. Aguilar (6’-3”, 229 pounds) went undrafted this past April in the NFL Draft out of Tennessee. Out of Freedom High School in Oakley, California, he went to the City College of San Francisco for two seasons, then transferred to Diablo Valley for the 2021 and 2022 seasons. For his junior year, he committed to Appalachian State and was finally playing D-1 football. In 2023, he was named the starter and played in all 14 games with 293 completions on 460 attempts for 3,757 yards, a 63.7% completion rate, and 33 touchdowns with 10 interceptions. His yardage numbers and total TDs set school single-season records. He was named the “Sun Belt Newcomer of the Year” and voted Second Team All-Sun Belt. The following year, he again started all 14 games and threw for 3,003 yards on 218 completions with 390 attempts and a 55.9% completion rate. His TD total was 23, while he threw a conference-high 14 picks. After his second season, Aguilar set numerous school passing records. He had one year of eligibility remaining and transferred to UCLA, but then changed his mind and enrolled at the University of Tennessee to get a taste of SEC football. Aguilar won the starting QB job and played in all 13 games. He threw for 3,565 yards on 272 completions in 404 attempts. He threw 24 touchdowns against just 10 interceptions and a 67.3% completion rate. He is also a good runner. His career totals with App State and Tennessee include 211 attempts for 553 yards, with nine TDs and an average of 2.6 yards per carry. After going undrafted, he signed with Jacksonville but was a final-day cut. After clearing waivers, he was signed to the Jags’ practice squad. Ossenfort had his pick of available quarterbacks. The Minnesota Vikings are actively seeking a quarterback as of Tuesday morning. Cardinals head coach Mike LaFleur has yet to name a starting quarterback for Sunday’s home game against the Los Angeles Rams.

(Photo by Rich von Biberstein/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images) | Icon Sportswire via Getty Images After Nick Folk missed for the first time since 2017 inside 40 yards, dropping his season field goal percentage to 72.2%, it seemed very likely the Falcons would move on. Now they’ve reportedly done so, signing away Baltimore Ravens practice squad kicker Jake Moody to replace him. The Falcons gave Folk a two-year deal in the offseason, banking on a player who led the NFL in field goal percentage in 2023, 2024, and 2025 reversing their kicking woes. Instead, Father Time finally wind sprinted to catch up with Folk, who went 13/18 on field goals and 17/18 on extra points through nine weeks in Atlanta, with some truly costly misses along the way highlighted by Week 1 struggles against Pittsburgh and the chip shot miss last Sunday against the Bengals. We’ll wish him well, but this may be the end of the road for a kicker with a long and storied career who is now 42 years old and declining. Sources: The #Falcons are releasing K Nick Folk, who was 13/18 on FGs this season. Jake Moody is the new kicker in Atlanta. https://t.co/Iqi0PKghTu pic.twitter.com/l4R6jsc0Si — Jordan Schultz (@Schultz_Report) November 10, 2026 Moody, meanwhile, will get a chance to audition for the Falcons’ kicking job going forward. He’s had a turbulent career as a former third round pick for the 49ers in 2023, hitting 84% of his field goal tries in year one but struggling badly in year two to the tune of a 72% hit rate. After he went just one-for-three in the first game of the 2025 season with the 49ers, he’s bounced around between the Bears (8/9), Commanders (10/11), and Ravens this year (1/1 from 53 yards). The early career struggles seem to have evened out for Moody, who has always had the leg to be a good kicker, and he was just hoping for an opportunity to prove he’s more than a fill-in option or practice squad elevation. He’ll get it for the Falcons, who would love to get an under-30 kicker who can can deliver consistent performance after the past few frustrating years at the position. Congratulations to Moody, and may he be the kicker the Falcons have been looking for.

full_text: ATLANTA, GEORGIA - SEPTEMBER 22: Justin Simmons #31 of the Atlanta Falcons intercepts a pass intended for Noah Gray #83 of the Kansas City Chiefs during the first quarter at Mercedes-Benz Stadium on September 22, 2024 in Atlanta, Georgia. (Photo by Kevin C. Cox/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Falcons dropped their second straight game in Week 9, falling to 3-6 at the hands of a pretty fantastic Bengals team. Atlanta’s playoff hopes continue to dwindle, but in the NFC South—where literally every team has 3 wins—they actually aren’t all that low! Unfortunately, things don’t get any easier for the Falcons over the next three games. In Week 10, Atlanta faces the 6-2 Kansas City Chiefs at home, followed by the Vikings and Lions. Atlanta opens as 3.5-point home underdogs against Kansas City, per FanDuel. I’m a little surprised it isn’t higher, to be honest. Sure, the Falcons beat the 49ers a couple weeks back, but that game is looking more and more like a fluke. With the team trading away star safety Jessie Bates III on Monday (and with more potential trades looming), it looks like Atlanta is starting to shift their focus towards the future. The Chiefs, meanwhile, look like a very good team once again. While Kansas City perpetually lacks quality receiving targets, that could change at the trade deadline. They’ve also finally got a quality rushing attack with Kenneth Walker, which is probably the most concerning thing for the Falcons in this one. Atlanta’s defense is very vulnerable to the run and Jeff Ulbrich hasn’t been able to figure out an effective counterpunch. Until he does, any team with a decent rushing attack is going to give the Falcons problems. I’m expecting the Chiefs to take full advantage on Sunday, but we’ll see if Atlanta can make any adjustments.

title: The Falcons aren’t giving up on 2026 because they exist in the NFC South
summary: After the Falcons traded away Jessie Bates yesterday, Kevin Stefanski had to get in front of microphones and talk to reporters about two seemingly contrary thoughts: The team is not “punting” on the 2026 season, in his words, but they couldn’t pass up the chance to trade one of their most impactful defenders nine weeks […]
full_text: After the Falcons traded away Jessie Bates yesterday, Kevin Stefanski had to get in front of microphones and talk to reporters about two seemingly contrary thoughts: The team is not “punting” on the 2026 season, in his words, but they couldn’t pass up the chance to trade one of their most impactful defenders nine weeks into that season. Those two warring thoughts, captured well in Tori McElhaney’s piece for AtlantaFalcons.com , seem difficult to square when you first look at them. How could trading Jessie Bates not undercut Atlanta’s 2026 fortunes? A team looking to take full advantage of a weak NFC South should be trying to acquire talent, not sell, right? Right? But spending a little more time with the seeming divide between selling off and contending reveals a simple truth: Their division is a gallon jug of steamed butt. If we’re being real about what’s happening here, the Falcons aren’t quitting on 2026 because it’s impossible to quit on 2026 in the NFC South. They are one game behind the Carolina Panthers, thanks to a head-to-head tiebreaker, and just a half game behind the New Orleans Saints. It’s not completely outlandish to suggest seven wins could actually earn the divisional title this year, and the Falcons are certainly good enough in their best weeks to win four out of their next eight games with matchups against the Browns, Commanders, diminished Lions, and rest of the NFC South still on the docket. If they continue to sell, as Carl Dukes at 92.9 suggested they would , it does nothing to change the fact that they’re still a team with some promising pieces and the same number of wins as everyone else in the division, and they have young players they wouldn’t mind getting a look at dotting the roster. That’s certainly true at safety, where Sydney Brown, Billy Bowman Jr., and DeMarcco Hellams could all be in the mix for snaps. It could prove true at inside linebacker, where the Falcons have been getting plenty from Kendal Daniels and Harold Perkins Jr. and may be willing to move Divine Deablo. It might be true at tackle, where the Falcons could potentially move Jawaan Taylor or even Jake Matthews if they get a really interesting offer and turn to Mike Jerrell, Cameron Williams, or Ethan Onianwa, though the prospect of Michael Penix Jr. getting pressured even more frequently is not an appealing one. And so on. For a team that is sitting on the highest projected cap space of any team in 2027 and now has two second round picks and eight selections overall, the prospect of continuing to stock resources to truly remake this team is an appealing one. Ian Cunningham didn’t have the draft capital to remake this team in one offseason and spent free agency rummaging around for appealing veteran on short-term deals, both to give a new coaching staff fresh faces and talent to work with, but to avoid making long-term investments the team could not easily pivot away from in 2027. They locked up the players they definitely want around for next year and can otherwise take off in any direction they please next year to give Kevin Stefanski and company a foundation that’s truly theirs, and Cunningham a roster that truly bears his philosophy. We’ve bandied about the term transformative for many offseasons in recent years, but 2027 has the potential to be that sort of year the way 2023, 2024, and 2025 were not. Viewed through the team’s obvious affinity for the near future, the deal for Bates makes a lot of sense; you’re not going to get a second round pick and change for a nearly 30-year-old safety on an expiring deal very often. It has a very apparent short-term cost given that nobody in line to replace him is Jessie Bates , an aging but still terrific safety and team captain, but this team’s modest 2026 ceiling was obviously only so high with him. Losing Bates makes the job tougher for Jeff Ulbrich and the defense, but the sledding was already difficult and the Falcons can bring numbers to bear at their new safety vacancy. It was a price the Falcons were willing to pay for a brighter future, and we should not be surprised to see them pay a price like that again before the deadline comes and goes. And they can do so with Stefanski insisting they’re not punting the season and meaning it, because all it will take is a couple of unexpected wins in the next few weeks for the Falcons to stay afloat. They still have the nucleus of their offense, young talent up front and in the secondary, and a coaching staff still trying to figure out how to squeeze more out of this roster all working to win, and they’re unlikely to blow any huge holes in the side of a team that does not look considerably worse than the flailing Panthers (who fired their defensive coordinator), Saints (who barely beat the Browns and seem to be a two game skid away from firing their head coach), and Buccaneers (who just sank a ton of money into Baker Mayfield just in time to see him shrivel into a raisin). It’s having your cake and eating it too, as Terry Fontenot once said , and if the cake isn’t very delicious right now there’s at least a specter of a more delicious one on the horizon. The Falcons aren’t quitting on the NFC South any time soon, in other words, even if they keep selling off today. The state of the division ensures that even a diminished Falcons team is likely going to be relevant for weeks to come.

full_text: Dec 10, 2023; Baltimore, Maryland, USA; Baltimore Ravens cornerback Arthur Maulet (10) celebrates after winning in overtime against the Los Angeles Rams at M&T Bank Stadium. Mandatory Credit: Jessica Rapfogel-USA TODAY Sports | USA TODAY Sports via Reuters Con Welcome back to Loose Feathers, a regular round-up of the latest news and analysis about the Baltimore Ravens. In today’s edition, we cover the retirement of a recent Raven, grades for Eric DeCosta’s acquisition of Jacoby Brissett, and an assessment of first-year offensive coordinator Declan Doyle, Let’s dive in: Former Ravens CB Arthur Maulet retires Arthur Maulet on Instagram BLESSED FOR THE 9 YEARS THANK YOU EVERYONE FOR THE SUPPORT @nfl NOT TO BAD FOR A UDFA #EGBB #GODWINS Arthur Maulet will be remembered fondly in Baltimore as a key part of Mike Macdonald’s elite 2023 defense. He posted the best coverage stats of his career, and his slot blitzes were the stuff of legend. A lingering injury sidelined him for most of 2024 and led to his release the following offseason. Maulet was originally a Saints undrafted rookie signing in 2017 and spent part of the 2018 season with the Colts. He then carved out rotational roles on defense during two-year stints with the Steelers and the Jets before arriving in Baltimore in 2023. He spent his final season in Detroit, appearing in nine games amid the Lions’ many secondary injuries. Maulet is on a fascinating list of players who played on both sides of one of the NFL’s biggest rivalries. Amont them are three of his 2023 teammates – Patrick Queen, Malik Harrison, and Chuck Clark – as well as Hall of Fame safety Rod Woodson and two-time All-Pro running back Le’Von Bell. Then there are less notable but still memorable names like Mike Wallace, Miles Boykins, Chris Wormley, Diontae Johnson, DeShon Elliott, and Jacoby Jones, among others. Evaluating Baltimore’s deadline moves NFL trade deadline winners, losers: Vikings find QB, Jags go all-in, Jonathan Taylor stranded – Mike Jones (The Athletic) Winners Baltimore Ravens The October acquisition of Jurgens from the Eagles met a need. Then last week, Baltimore filled a gaping hole at quarterback by trading for quarterback Jacoby Brissett . They’re hoping the 11-year veteran can keep them afloat in case Lamar Jackson returns from thumb surgery in time for a late-season playoff run. 32 grades on the 2026 NFL trade deadline: Who won, who lost and who did nothing? – Eric Edholm and Frank Schwab (Yahoo Sports) The Ravens traded for Jacoby Brissett just to have some hope on offense. There was none with Lamar Jackson and Tyler Huntley on IR. It was a little surprising to see a fourth-round pick involved, though Baltimore got a fifth-round pick back. But that move without any follow-up is a bit odd: Brissett isn’t going to save the season, there was nothing else added to help out but yet the Ravens traded picks to be … what exactly? The Ravens got center Cam Jurgens weeks ago, but that came at the hefty price of a second-round pick to Philadelphia. Chargers weaken defense ahead of MNF trip to Baltimore Chargers trade LB Daiyan Henley to Broncos for ‘27 4th, ‘28 5th – Michael Peterson (Bolts From The Blue) Henley is also a team captain and the “green dot” player who calls the defense for the Chargers. At the same time, Henley is currently in the final deal of his rookie contract and no real attempts at an extension had ever come to the table. It’s going to be a rough scene in that locker room as Henley has also been one of the most beloved players on the entire team during his young career. Through the team’s eight games this season, Henley has been their leading tackler with 51. He has also posted two tackles for loss, a half sack, two pass breakups, an interception, a forced fumble, and two fumble recoveries.

title: Ravens trade G Andrew Vorhees to Falcons for C Ryan Neuzil
summary: The Baltimore Ravens are acquiring center Ryan Neuzil from the Atlanta Falcons in exchange for guard Andrew Vorhees and a 2028 sixth-round pick, per Jonathan Jones of The Athletic. The draft pick heading to Atlanta is conditional, according to the NFL’s daily personnel notice. The attached conditions remain unreported. In Baltimore, Neuzil will reunite with […]
full_text: Oct 19, 2025; Santa Clara, California, USA; Atlanta Falcons center Ryan Neuzil (64) during the first quarter against the San Francisco 49ers at Levi's Stadium. Mandatory Credit: Darren Yamashita-Imagn Images | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect The Baltimore Ravens are acquiring center Ryan Neuzil from the Atlanta Falcons in exchange for guard Andrew Vorhees and a 2028 sixth-round pick, per Jonathan Jones of The Athletic . The draft pick heading to Atlanta is conditional, according to the NFL’s daily personnel notice. The attached conditions remain unreported. In Baltimore, Neuzil will reunite with Dwayne Ledford, his former offensive line coach in Atlanta who developed him from an undrafted free agent in 2022 into the Falcons’ starting center by the end of the 2024 season. Neuzil started all 17 games in 2025, earning a 82.1 run-blocking grade from Pro Football Focus that ranked sixth among centers – two spots behind Tyler Linderbaum. He also allowed just 14 pressures and one sack on the year with a 98.7 pass blocking efficiency, the league’s seventh-best at his position. This year, Neuzil started Atlanta’s first nine games with lower run-blocking grades but similar numbers in pass protection. He now seems headed for a backup role in Baltimore behind Cam Jurgens, who was acquired from the Philadelphia Eagles last month. The Ravens have been snakebitten by center injuries this year, and Jurgens has a history of back problems. Neuzil is a significant upgrade over Kyle Hergel, who took over the backup center job after Jovaughn Gwyn and Ethan Pocic suffered long-term knee injuries in Week 3. Baltimore’s center situation has been a black hole ever since Linderbaum left in free agency to sign a massive deal with the Raiders. Neuzil is now the fifth veteran center acquired by the Ravens this year and the second to follow Ledford from Atlanta after Gwyn. The 29-year-old seems unlikely to factor into the picture at left guard, where John Simpson has not played up to the $16 million APY contract he signed this offseason. Neuzil’s regular-season experience at the position consists of just four snaps when he was a rookie, though he was a three-year starting guard at Appalachian State. Vorhees, 27, will end a disappointing tenure in Baltimore. The former USC starter tore his ACL at the 2023 Combine, tanking his potential Day 2 draft stock and keeping him available until the end of the seventh round. The Ravens traded a future sixth-rounder to select him in the hopes that a strong recovery would yield a future starter. They proved themselves right, stubbornly starting Vorhees for all 17 games in 2025 despite clear deficiencies in his play. Baltimore’s offseason turnover removed Vorhees to the bench, but injuries still pressed him into five appearances (two starts) with 81 snaps, all at right guard. He will presumably add guard depth in Atlanta and is scheduled to hit free agency this offseason. There have been no reports regarding the financial implication’s of the Ravens’ deadline-day move. Neuzil and Vorhees will likely carry their respective salaries to their new teams, which should reduce Baltimore’s cap space and increase Atlanta’s by roughly $1.5 million.
author: Nikhil Mehta

title: Falcons steal K Jake Moody from Ravens’ practice squad
summary: The Baltimore Ravens need a new kicker. Again. The Atlanta Falcons are signing Jake Moody off of the Ravens’ practice squad, per NFL insider Jordan Schultz, robbing Baltimore of another kicker less than a week after Week 1 starter Tyler Loop landed on injured reserve with a groin injury. The move raises questions about the […]
full_text: BALTIMORE, MARYLAND - NOVEMBER 05: Jake Moody #45 of the Baltimore Ravens kicks a 53 yard field goal against the Jacksonville Jaguars during the first quarter of the game at M&T Bank Stadium on November 05, 2026 in Baltimore, Maryland. (Photo by Patrick Smith/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Baltimore Ravens need a new kicker. Again. The Atlanta Falcons are signing Jake Moody off of the Ravens’ practice squad, per NFL insider Jordan Schultz , robbing Baltimore of another kicker less than a week after Week 1 starter Tyler Loop landed on injured reserve with a groin injury. The move raises questions about the Ravens’ approach to their kicker situation with Loop sidelined for at least four games. The team had a roster spot available, but opted to elevate Moody from the practice squad to face the Jacksonville Jaguars last Thursday. With only two elevations remaining, he would have required a promotion to the 53-man roster to see out Loop’s absence, which would have also precluded his departure to Atlanta. Logic suggests that the Ravens should have just promoted Moody knowing they would need him to kick for the rest of the month, maybe longer. Additional reporting from Jeff Zrebiec of The Athletic indicated that the Ravens were “willing” to promote Moody to their active roster on Monday. The Falcons, though, offered a better situation after releasing kicker Jason Sanders: a potential long-term job for Moody and a home field enclosed by a dome. It still seems, though, that Baltimore could have headed off this entire issue had they promoted Moody to the active roster last week. It is possible that his agent was keeping tabs on the Falcons’ kicking situation and preferred a practice squad stay to preserve his options. However, Loop has not exactly inspired much confidence that he can deliver key kicks for a team that will need to win at the margins to make the playoffs this year. There is an argument that the Ravens should have identified Moody as their kicker for the foreseeable future and adjusted their roster accordingly. Instead, they will have to scour the NFL’s practice squads and free-agent pool to find their next kicker. Signing Nick Folk, who the Falcons cut to add Moody, would be an ironic twist. After three straight years of leading the league with a field goal conversion rate of 95.5% or better, the 42-year-old’s numbers have collapsed in 2026. He made just 72.2% of his field goals to start the season with two misses inside of 50 yards and a one-for-four mark from beyond.

title: We asked, you answered: Ravens should sell at deadline
summary: The Baltimore Ravens have been buyers so far this season, acquiring center Cam Jurgens from the Philadelphia Eagles in October and quarterback Jacoby Brissett from the Arizona Cardinals last week. But the Ravens’ 2026 season seems unlikely to turn around. The 4-5 squad now has a 7.5-win over/under and +560 odds to make the playoffs […]
full_text: INDIANAPOLIS, IN - FEBRUARY 24: Eric DeCosta of the Baltimore Ravens speaks during a press conference at the 2026 NFL Scouting Combine on February 24, 2026 in Indianapolis, Indiana. (Photo by Cooper Neill/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Baltimore Ravens have been buyers so far this season, acquiring center Cam Jurgens from the Philadelphia Eagles in October and quarterback Jacoby Brissett from the Arizona Cardinals last week. But the Ravens’ 2026 season seems unlikely to turn around. The 4-5 squad now has a 7.5-win over/under and +560 odds to make the playoffs ( via FanDuel Sportsbook ). 87% of fans think general manager Eric DeCosta should sell before Tuesday’s trade deadline, according to last week’s SB Nation Reacts survey, including a 57% majority who think an aggressive sale is warranted. Reasonable minds can disagree on some of Baltimore’s borderline core players, but three are irrefutably foundational: Lamar Jackson, Zay Flowers, and Kyle Hamilton. Players like Roquan Smith, Derrick Henry and Ronnie Stanley are signed through next season, but they may not be part of the team’s long-term plans. Here’s one out of left field: Nate Wiggins. The 23-year-old is allowing 11.1 yards per completion and 6.1 yards per target, both career-bests but still middling among starting cornerbacks. There was optimism about his development under Jesse Minter and his staff, but Wiggins’ strengths as a press-man corner may not be an optimal fit in Minter’s zone-heavy scheme. Is he going to be worth a high-end contract in a cornerback market that has exploded in the last year? If not, he could be a sneaky trade candidate. His fifth-year option is currently projected to be an affordable $14.25 million (via OverTheCap), making him an attractive short- and long-term addition to another team’s secondary. Teams are always more desperate around the deadline, especially for one of the NFL’s most important and often-injured positions. Of course, the Ravens’ remaining hope for Lamar Jackson to return and propel a playoff run will dissuade them from moving starters like Wiggins unless a truly ludicrous offer comes in. Adding another player at this point would seem like a mistake , unless DeCosta can dig up the kind of deal he normally swings in the offseason. It should be a quiet Tuesday in Baltimore.

title: Ravens news: Eric DeCosta gets mixed grades for Jacoby Brissett trade
summary: Welcome back to Loose Feathers, a regular round-up of the latest news and analysis about the Baltimore Ravens. In today’s edition, we cover a weak trade market for some of the Ravens’ veterans, grades for Eric DeCosta’s acquisition of Jacoby Brissett, and an assessment of first-year offensive coordinator Declan Doyle, Let’s dive in: ‘No real […]
full_text: Nov 1, 2026; Arlington, Texas, USA; Arizona Cardinals quarterback Jacoby Brissett (7) walks off the field after the game against the Dallas Cowboys at AT&T Stadium. Mandatory Credit: Jerome Miron-Imagn Images | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect Welcome back to Loose Feathers, a regular round-up of the latest news and analysis about the Baltimore Ravens. In today’s edition, we cover a weak trade market for some of the Ravens’ veterans, grades for Eric DeCosta’s acquisition of Jacoby Brissett, and an assessment of first-year offensive coordinator Declan Doyle, Let’s dive in: ‘No real market’ for Stanley, Andrews, Humphrey Apologies to the Ravens fans hoping to flip some of the team’s highly-paid, underperforming veterans for draft picks at the deadline. If Baltimore is holding out any hope of getting Lamar Jackson back, they will not trade away his left tackle, and neither Andrews nor Humphrey can be seen as upgrades right now. All three were listed under “no real market” in Jeff Zrebiec’s recent trade deadline round-up. One name remains: Roquan Smith. His contract seems untenable heading into the offseason, but another team could be interested in upgrading their linebacker corps this season. Getting rid of his future salary could help Baltimore’s tight future cap picture and maybe even free up the money to re-sign Trenton Simpson. Some would even argue that a Simpson-Teddye Buchanan duo might actually be an improvement over Smith’s up-and-down (mostly down) play this year. But the Ravens love Smith. They loved him coming out of Georgia in 2018, and they loved him enough in Chicago to send a second-round pick to the Bears. And again, Jackson is still in the picture, albeit on the margins. With no clarity to be had before Tuesday’s deadline, Smith seems likely to stay put. It’s worth noting that trading Smith might be less of an option in the offseason. Linebackers tend to have more value during the season when teams are desperate to make up for injuries and/or push all-in. But in the offseason, teams will have more (and cheaper) options at linebacker, allowing them to focus on premium positions instead. The same is true of running back. This might be the best time to trade Smith and Derrick Henry, but the Ravens will not pull the trigger. The Ravens should be sellers at the trade deadline. What do they actually have to offer? – Jeff Zrebiec (The Athletic) It’s hard to say whether there will be any interest in Smith. He’s still an effective player, but he’s 29 now, he’s not making the same number of impact plays and he still has another year left on a big-money contract. A purge of some veteran defensive players seems overdue, and moving on from Smith would save them $8 million in cap space, which would come in handy this offseason. However, shipping off the team’s vocal leader and defensive signal-caller could make it seem like the Ravens are waiving the white flag on the season. They probably wouldn’t get much in return, either. Ravens get mixed grades for Jacoby Brissett trades Jacoby Brissett trade grade: Ravens try to salvage season; Cardinals improve draft capital – Daniel Popper (The Athletic) Ravens grade: C I’m mostly unmoved by this deal. Brissett does give first-year coach Jesse Minter and offensive coordinator Declan Doyle a higher floor on offense. Still, it’s hard to see the Ravens contending in any meaningful capacity, especially with the disappointing way Minter’s defense is playing. General manager Eric DeCosta gave up marginal draft capital, so it’s a fine bet to try and salvage something from a season slipping away. NFL trade deadline grades: Deals for Jordan Davis, Jessie Bates III, Andre Cisco – Ben Solak and Seth Walder (ESPN) Ravens grade: B+ The Ravens lost 33-10 to the Jaguars on Thursday night with Fagnano (and also some Derrick Henry in the Wildcat) at quarterback. In all likelihood, Baltimore’s season is over with Jackson currently on injured reserve and the team at 4-5. Ravens coach Jesse Minter has said Jackson’s injury is “potentially” season-ending. But Brissett gives the team at least a sliver of hope of staying afloat long enough to hand the reins back to Jackson with a shot at the playoffs. But make no mistake, those chances are extremely slim. Even knowing Brissett is about to take over at QB (and assuming Jackson has, say, a 30% chance of coming back in games starting in Week 14, ESPN’s Football Power Index gives Baltimore only a 3% chance of reaching the playoffs. If Jackson is indeed able to come back, that number goes up, but it’s still a long shot. The cost here is low. By ESPN’s draft pick valuations, the swap works out to the equivalent of an early sixth-round pick. Considering the team’s upside if it does get Jackson back, I think that is easily worth it for Baltimore. Jesse Minter optimistic regarding Kyle Hamilton, Nate Wiggins injuries News & Notes: Jesse Minter Gives Injury Update on Kyle Hamilton – Clifton Brown (BaltimoreRavens.c0m) Head Coach Jesse Minter gave a positive update Monday on All-Pro safety Kyle Hamilton, who left Thursday night’s game against the Jacksonville Jaguars with a hip injury. “I think everything looks fairly good,” Minter said. “We’ll find out as the guys come back in tomorrow (Tuesday). But I wouldn’t expect that to be something where … hopefully he doesn’t miss time.” Minter was also optimistic about cornerback Nate Wiggins (illness) and safety Jaylinn Hawkins (knee) returning to action this week. Wiggins did not play against the Jaguars, while Hawkins has missed the last three games. “There’s definitely optimism there,” Minter said regarding Hawkins rejoining practice. “I think (Nate) will be okay. It was an unfortunate timing of an illness.”

title: Implications of Buffalo Bills trading for safety Amani Hooker
summary: Let’s break down some of the financial and draft-pick implications of the Buffalo Bills trading for veteran safety Amani Hooker before the NFL trade deadline. Hooker is a 28 year old in his eighth professional season, all of which, until now, were spent with the Tennessee Titans, the club that selected him in the fourth […]
full_text: Let’s break down some of the financial and draft-pick implications of the Buffalo Bills trading for veteran safety Amani Hooker before the NFL trade deadline. Hooker is a 28 year old in his eighth professional season, all of which, until now, were spent with the Tennessee Titans, the club that selected him in the fourth round out of the University of Iowa in 2019. Draft-pick value for Bills to acquire Amani Hooker On the Jimmy Johnson trade value chart — using the NFL draft order after Week 9’s action — the Bills paid the equivalent of between the No. 71 and No. 72 overall pick (Round 3) to acquire Hooker. How many picks do the Bills now have in the 2027 NFL Draft? After the Hooker trade, the Bills have nine picks in the 2027 NFL Draft: Round 1 – Own Round 3 – Own Round 4 – Own Round 4 – Expected compensatory selection for David Edwards’ departure Round 5 – Titans from Amani Hooker trade Round 5 – Own Round 6 – Colts from Sedrick Van Pran-Granger trade Round 6 – Own Round 7 – Raiders How long is Amani Hooker signed? Hooker is currently signed through the 2028 season. He has a prorated salary of $4.47M for the 2026 season. According ESPN NFL reporter Cameron Wolfe , the Titans are not eating any of Hooker’s remaining 2026 salary. Hooker is set count $10.28M in 2027 and $13.5M in 2028. Of course, the Bills can redo Hooker’s deal if the two sides can agree on terms, but for a team that is currently allocating the third-fewest amount of money to the safety position — and is currently set to allocate the seventh-lowest in 2027 and 12th-lowest to that position in 2028 — Hooker’s future cap hits are very manageable. Does Amani Hooker have any connections to any Bills players? Yes. Hooker and Bills practice-squad safety Geno Stone were teammates at Iowa in 2017 and 2018.

full_text: (Photo by Andy Lyons/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Buffalo Bills had a glaring need at the safety position and general mangaer Brandon Beane addressed it at the NFL trade deadline Tuesday. The Bills have traded for Tennessee Titans star Amani Hooker. Hooker is a former fourth-round pick of the Titans in 2019 and started 74 games for them, taking over as the starting strong safety in 2021. Hooker’s base salary for the rest of the season is somewhere around $2 million, so the Bills were able to fit him under their cap. No word on if Tennessee ate some salary to help Buffalo in the process. The Bills are sending a second-round pick to the Titans in exchange for Hooker and a fifth-rounder. Join the conversation! Earlier this week, we wrote on the report the Bills were “scanning the safety pool” before the trade deadline, and now they’ve made their move. Hooker was the fifth installment in our trade-deadline candidate series here at Rumblings. This is how I concluded that article I published on October 26: “Hooker would be an excellent in-season acquisition for this defense. At the outset, the cost of a late Round 3 pick feels a little rich for my liking, but Buffalo shouldn’t be overly concerned with next year’s draft right now. And, it wouldn’t be unreasonable for the Titans to eat some of Hooker’s future money — by converting future base salary into a signing bonus — to facilitate a trade that features Buffalo’s 2027 third-round selection. In that case, count me in. Hooker is a still reasonably young, super-steady, do-everything safety… which is kinda-sorta what this Bills defense needs right now. Plus, the financial obligations over the next two seasons for Hooker are hardly expensive for a player of his caliber who won’t be 30 until June of 2028.” Matt Warren had this thought regarding this trade and how it stacks up with the Jaguars trade to acquire safety Jessie Bates: “Unlike the Jaguars’ trade for Jessie Bates, the Bills can see a future with Hooker. Hooker is under contract for 2027 and 2028, where Bates is only under contract for the rest of 2026. Hooker is only 28 and turns 29 in June while Bates turns 30 in February.” As for the type of player the Bills are getting, Hooker was one of the youngest players in the 2019 NFL Draft, and has 5,293 snaps of NFL experience. He has 17 career interceptions — including five this season, three of which came against the Bengals in Week 8 — and averages 77 tackles, two tackles for loss, and seven pass breakups per season. At 5’11” and 210 pounds with plus ball skills and range, Hooker is legitimately versatile, but I wouldn’t be surprised if he moves into more of a ball-hawking free safety role in Jim Leonhard’s defense. Brandon Beane did it. He made a move at the trade deadline (which he’s done plenty of times before) to make the Bills better right now.

title: The quantitative proof of Buffalo Bills defense making strides
summary: The Buffalo Bills have allowed 16 total points the past two games, but the unit has certainly faced lesser competition at quarterback. How much should we take from Buffalo’s recent defensive efforts? Is it all a mirage because they faced one snap of Lamar Jackson, only a few attempts from Tyler Huntley, then Joey Fagnano, […]
full_text: The Buffalo Bills have allowed 16 total points the past two games, but the unit has certainly faced lesser competition at quarterback. How much should we take from Buffalo’s recent defensive efforts? Is it all a mirage because they faced one snap of Lamar Jackson, only a few attempts from Tyler Huntley, then Joey Fagnano, Carson Wentz, and Max Brosmer? Or is Buffalo really onto something defensively? These type of questions are precisely why I created Defensive Impact on Passing (DIP) . I introduced the new metric a few weeks ago, and if you missed that article, here’s how I can summarize DIP — it measures how well a defense performs against opposing quarterbacks relative to how those same quarterbacks perform against other defenses on their schedule. Pretty straightforward right? Baked into DIP is the exclusion of garbage time, and, like all EPA-based defensive stats, a negative figure is better. Also, quarterbacks need at least 30 attempts against other opponents to be counted toward a defense’s DIP. Here are the full DIP rankings after Week 9: You can see the Bills defense has moved all the way up to 15th in DIP. Buffalo’s unit made a steady climb after the first month or so of the season. It was 20th after Week 8 and 23rd through Week 6. And considering Buffalo’s current DIP placement, here’s where I land on what we can take from the club’s defensive efforts in Weeks 8 and 9 — for as much as the Bills defense was likely “helped” by low-level quarterback play these past two weeks it was close to equally as “hurt” by top-level quarterbacks it played in the first month-ish of the season. The analysis has to go both ways. And from that chart, you’ll notice that the DIP of the Bills defense is actually now into the negatives. That means, opposing pass games are actually performing slightly worse against the Bills than in their other games right now. That in an of itself is an encouraging development for a defense that was universally panned in the first six contests before the bye week. This quantitative truth feels incredible too — Buffalo’s defense is fifth in the AFC in DIP right now. Now, this metric only measures opposing pass games on a per dropback basis. Scrambles are counted. But there’s nothing regarding the opposition’s run game built into this stat whatsoever. In today’s NFL, efficiently passing and stopping the pass remain most vital. And through DIP we know, with quarterback — and overall pass game — competition being considered, the Bills defense is now playing respectably.
author: Chris Trapasso

title: Buffalo Bills make history in 23-6 win over Minnesota Vikings
summary: For a while Monday night, the Buffalo Bills and Minnesota Vikings seemed to be competing to see which offense could frustrate its fans the most.  Neither team could get much going, and Josh Allen wasn’t doing much to hide his irritation. Playing without both his starting left tackle and left guard as Dion Dawkins and […]
full_text: For a while Monday night, the Buffalo Bills and Minnesota Vikings seemed to be competing to see which offense could frustrate its fans the most. Neither team could get much going, and Josh Allen wasn’t doing much to hide his irritation. Playing without both his starting left tackle and left guard as Dion Dawkins and Alec Anderson watched from the sidelines, Allen spent far too much time trying to escape a Minnesota defense that was coming through Buffalo’s offensive line like it had been invited. Fortunately, the Bills’ defense was giving the Vikings just as much trouble, and the scoreboard wasn’t moving much in either direction. But there’s only so long you can keep Josh Allen and the Bills’ offense quiet. Once Buffalo had a chance to figure out what Minnesota was throwing at them, the adjustments started paying off. It wasn’t the high-octane, 30-plus-point offense Bills fans have grown accustomed to watching, but it didn’t need to be. James Cook got rolling, Allen found a way to move the ball, and Tyler Bass quietly put together an 11-point night that deserves a little more attention. And let’s not forget fellow special-teams specialist Tommy Doman getting in on the tackling action. Because who doesn’t love seeing a punter-moonlighting-as-a-kicker make a tackle ? By the time it was over, Buffalo had turned an aggravating start into a 23-6 win, improved to 7-1, and climbed to the top of the NFL standings. Not just the AFC East. Not just the AFC. All 32 teams. And while the offense was busy figuring things out, the defense was putting together another performance worth talking about. Three takeaways, fewer than 200 yards allowed, and a Minnesota offense that couldn’t convert a single third down. Of course, the win also came with a few entries in the record books. Josh Allen passed 5,000 career rushing yards and tied Peyton Manning’s mark of 322 total touchdowns through a player’s first 10 seasons. James Cook joined the 5,000-yard rushing club himself , giving the Bills two major career milestones in the same game. And that was just the beginning. Here’s who else earned a Shout! out in Monday night’s win. _____________________________________________________________________________ The best start in more than three decades The Bills are off to their best start in 33 years, matching the 1993 team’s record through eight games. It’s still early in the season, but Buffalo has put itself in a pretty good position heading into the second half. The Bills have improved to 7-1, marking the team's best start since 1993 (7-1). pic.twitter.com/l1QvxdcF51 — Buffalo Bills PR (@BuffaloBillsPR) November 10, 2026 _____________________________________________________________________________ Bass is perfect Tyler Bass has been one of Buffalo’s most reliable weapons this season, and Monday night was no exception. The Bills needed his leg against Minnesota, and he delivered every time. Tyler Bass improves to 18-of-18 in 2026, marking the best start to a season by a Bills kicker in team history. pic.twitter.com/83LTH0yKD6 — Buffalo Bills PR (@BuffaloBillsPR) November 10, 2026 _____________________________________________________________________________ Defense doing its job The Buffalo defense has been particularly impressive over the past two weeks, keeping opposing offenses from getting much of anything going. And the numbers show just how dominant the unit has been. Each of the last two games, the Bills defense has: – 3+ takeaways – Multiple sacks – Allowed under 200 total yards – Allowed under 50% completions – Allowed no passing TDs The last NFL team to do that in back-to-back games was the 1985 Bears (3 straight games from Nov. 10-24). pic.twitter.com/Au8kD3ubzF — Buffalo Bills PR (@BuffaloBillsPR) November 10, 2026 _____________________________________________________________________________ Brady’s road success continues Joe Brady has yet to lose a road game since taking over as Buffalo’s head coach. Monday’s win put him in some pretty good company among NFL coaches over the past 25 years. Joe Brady became the fifth coach this century to win each of his first four career road games, joining Sean McVay (2017), Jim Harbaugh (2011), Jim Caldwell (2009) and Herm Edwards (2001). pic.twitter.com/LQu8mjaT3C — Buffalo Bills PR (@BuffaloBillsPR) November 10, 2026 _____________________________________________________________________________ Cook keeps finding the end zone James Cook has been one of Buffalo’s most consistent offensive weapons this season. Whether the Bills are putting up 30-plus points or grinding through a defensive battle, Cook keeps finding ways to produce. James Cook III has recorded at least one rushing TD and 75+ rushing yards in seven consecutive games, the longest streak in team history. Cook's streak also marks the longest by any NFL player since LaDanian Tomlinson (8 games) in 2006. pic.twitter.com/4swQqzizjs — Buffalo Bills PR (@BuffaloBillsPR) November 10, 2026 _____________________________________________________________________________ Williams leads the way Dorian Williams added another interception to Buffalo’s growing collection of takeaways Monday night. He’s now leading the team in that category. Dorian Williams records his second interception of the season, which marks a team-high. pic.twitter.com/csfYaGd0d4 — Buffalo Bills PR (@BuffaloBillsPR) November 10, 2026 _____________________________________________________________________________ A first for Latu Keleki Latu picked up a career milestone Monday night, hauling in his first NFL touchdown on a pass from Josh Allen. The 25-yard score helped Buffalo finally get its offense moving against Minnesota. Keleki Latu catches his first career TD on a 25-yard pass from Josh Allen. pic.twitter.com/XDRk967BFC — Buffalo Bills PR (@BuffaloBillsPR) November 10, 2026 _____________________________________________________________________________ Rousseau isn’t slowing down Greg Rousseau is having another strong season along Buffalo’s defensive front. And with nine games still remaining on the schedule, he’s already reached a mark that twice took him an entire season to achieve. And that mark, it ties him for second in the NFL. Greg Rousseau tallies his 8th sack of the season, tying his career-high for sacks in a season (set in 2022 & 2024). pic.twitter.com/HNftTvn908 — Buffalo Bills PR (@BuffaloBillsPR) November 10, 2026 Through Week 9, Greg Rousseau is tied for second in the NFL with 8.0 sacks. pic.twitter.com/R2yXpn1zK4 — Buffalo Bills PR (@BuffaloBillsPR) November 10, 2026 _____________________________________________________________________________ It may not have been the prettiest win of the season, and there were certainly a few moments that tested the patience of Buffalo fans and players alike. But a win is a win, and the Bills are sitting at 7-1 with the best record in the NFL. Not a bad place to be as the season reaches its halfway point. And despite all the Monday night struggles, there was still plenty to Shout! about when it was over.
