title: Takeaways from Bills win over Vikings
summary: The Buffalo Bills beat the Vikings 23-6 in Week 9 on Monday Night Football, a dominant defensive effort that paired wonderfully with fine performances from Josh Allen and James Cook. The win moved Joe Brady’s team to 7-1 on the season. These are my takeaways from Buffalo’s victory. The defense was sensational… even if Carson […]
full_text: The Buffalo Bills beat the Vikings 23-6 in Week 9 on Monday Night Football , a dominant defensive effort that paired wonderfully with fine performances from Josh Allen and James Cook. The win moved Joe Brady’s team to 7-1 on the season. These are my takeaways from Buffalo’s victory. The defense was sensational… even if Carson Wentz was not The Bills defense had an epic performance in this game, I don’t care who the quarterback was. Carson Wentz was 8-of-25 for 81 yards with two picks. And the goalposts can’t be moved here. While rumors have swirled of Minnesota trading for a quarterback this past week, there were many who believed the Vikings weren’t really downgrading at the position going from Kyler Murray to Wentz for this primetime battle. Let’s not forget, in Week 1, in a relief appearance after Kyler Murray was injured, Wentz was 12-of-19 for 133 yards with three touchdowns and no interceptions. On paper, as a veteran pocket passer, he should be better suited for Kevin O’Connell’s offense. And it’s not as if Wentz had a pedestrian outing. He had a quarterback rating of 8.9 against the Bills defense. That’s the lowest rating a quarterback with at least 25 attempts in a game has managed since… 2019. Now, of course, Wentz missed on a handful of throws in this contest, but the Bills defense forced him to hold onto the football often — his 2.82-second average time to throw was higher than Josh Allen in this game — with outstanding coverage downfield for the vast majority of this matchup. The pass rush and coverage were married throughout, and Buffalo only had to blitz on 25.9% of Wentz’s dropbacks to affect the pocket consistently. And I’ll finish with this storyline that probably won’t be talked about enough given how abysmal the Vikings pass game was — Minnesota ran it 12 times for 51 yards, which equates to a 4.3 yards-per-tote average. Aaron Jones averaged 3.2 yards per carry. Only 27.3% of the Vikings runs were successful — determined by yards gained relative to down and distance — the fifth-lowest rate for a run game in Week 9. Buffalo’s run defense is steadily improving each week, and it’s already much more consistent than it was a season ago. Josh Allen was excellent The stats will miss the sheer brilliance of Allen in this game. His rating was only 87.3. But beyond his slightly floated interception — that did come on a 3rd and 23, mind you — the Bills quarterback excelled against the most unique and aggressive defense in football, a truly elite unit, on its home turf. To start 3-of-5 for 24 yards with a pick and finish the evening 21-of-31 for 234 with a touchdown through the air was immaculate from Allen. He commanded the offense, both pre and post snap exactly how it should be done. He made smart decisions and threw with proper velocity/touch starting with that touchdown drive near the end of the first half. His ball placement was superb as well. And, heck, no quarterback is going to be perfect for 60 minutes against that Vikings defense. Allen did all this without Dion Dawkins and Alec Anderson. MVP-caliber performance from him in this game. Hats off to Tylan Grable + Austin Corbett Grable and Corbett allowed four pressures each. Not exactly what clubs want from starting blockers. But after a few miscommunications early that led to quick pressures, I thought both depth players settled in nicely, and really got after it in the run game in the second half. The Brian Flores defensive scheme is designed to create offensive line miscommunication, and Grable and Corbett have never played alongside each other in an NFL game before. But instead of their presence on the field becoming a story throughout this game, an issue that severely hampered the Bills offense all night, Grable and Corbett were steady in the second half, as run and pass blockers. The Bills linebackers played tremendously The responsibilities in Jim Leonhard’s defense are starting to become second nature to Terrel Bernard, Dorian Williams, and Kaleb Elarms-Orr. Williams and Bernard snagged a pick each in this one, and Bernard dropped probably the most gift-wrapped interception opportunity of his NFL career. They are flowing freely in coverage, rapidly reacting to route concepts, and getting to proper depth at the intermediate level. Against the run, they’re triggering quickly and regularly not allowing blocks to stick to them. In this game, Bernard led the team with six tackles. Dorian Williams had three without a miss. And Elarms-Orr added three tackles of his own on just 13 snaps. This trio has become an underrated three-down group. Joe Brady called one heck of a game Sure, it wasn’t idyllic to start. But once Brady understood the outside pitch plays weren’t working on the ground, he went away from them. Then, later, when he realized the interior run game was doing just enough to keep the Vikings defense on its heels and burn clock, he stuck with it. But it wasn’t a one-dimensional attack for Buffalo in this game. There was a fine collection of play-action, throws to tight ends in the flat, running backs involved through the air. Lots of 13 personnel. Over-the-middle looks for Khalil Shakir, some classic first-read looks outside for DJ Moore, and well-timed quick screens to receivers. Again, it’s never going to be flawless against a Flores defense that has the horses on the Vikings roster. But Brady was in his bag as a play-caller in this convincing win. The special teams unit was damn good, again Whether it was Tyler Bass making his 18th consecutive field goal (a team record) to begin the season, Tommy Doman Jr. handling punt and kickoff duties and laying the lumber to force a fumble, or Greg Dortch’s big return to begin the game, special teams coordinator Jeff Rodgers has built a fantastic unit that was showcased in this Monday Night Football win. In a low-scoring, defensive clash like we got in the first half, I can’t stress enough how important Bass making those kicks was to avoid field-position and momentum shifts. Doman even proved capable of kicking a “dirty ball” that hits within the landing zone but isn’t immediately fielded by the returner. Buffalo’s special teams were once again stellar in victory.
author: Chris Trapasso

title: Panthers restructure Taylor Moton’s contract to free up cap room
summary: The NFL trade deadline is 4:00pm Eastern time today (Tuesday). There’s been more activity around the trade deadline in recent years as teams have started to find the utility in becoming buyers or sellers based on the way their seasons are going. The Carolina Panthers are just 3-5, but they do technically lead the NFC […]
full_text: The NFL trade deadline is 4:00pm Eastern time today (Tuesday). There’s been more activity around the trade deadline in recent years as teams have started to find the utility in becoming buyers or sellers based on the way their seasons are going. The Carolina Panthers are just 3-5, but they do technically lead the NFC South. That would suggest they’re more likely to be buyers at the deadline if anything, and they did a bit of bookkeeping to confirm that. The Carolina #Panthers converted $5.3M of Taylor Moton's salary into signing bonus, creating $3.5M of 2026 cap space. Updated Cap Hits 2026: $17.4M 2027: $30.2M 2028: $8.7M (void) — Spotrac (@spotrac) November 10, 2026 According to Spotrac, the Panthers restructured offensive tackle Taylor Moton’s deal to save themselves $3.5 million against this season’s salary cap. It’s the typical restructure move. They converted some of his base salary (which counts entirely against this season’s cap) to a signing bonus (which is spread across the length of the deal). The team was right at the salary cap before this move, and now they have some wiggle room to add a piece at the deadline if there’s one that suits them. The $3.5 million number isn’t going to fit any blockbuster acquisition, even if it is only a player’s base salary. If anything, the Panthers will peruse the league’s worst teams for some inexpensive veterans that can fill the void in the secondary while Jaycee Horn, Mike Jackson, and Will Lee recover from their injuries. Same could be said for the offensive line, where injuries have caused problems and subpar play has caused even more. However, it’s more likely that his move is to give the team some wiggle room to sign or claim free agents. The team hosted cornerback Jack Jones for a visit the other day but haven’t yet offered him a contract. Moves like that would require the kind of space the Moton restructure opens up, so that seems like the route in which the Panthers will spend the extra money they’ve freed up.

title: Carolina Panthers 2027 NFL Draft Prospect Profile: Trevor Lauck
summary: The 2027 NFL Draft feels like forever away, and we’re all caught up in the start of the NFL season. Regardless, it’s never too early to look ahead to the Draft. This weekly series will take a closer look at some of the prospects the Carolina Panthers could select in the 2027 iteration of the […]
full_text: IOWA CITY, IOWA- OCTOBER 26: Offensive lineman Trevor Lauck #59 of the Iowa Hawkeyes blocks during the second half against defensive lineman Michael Kilbane #47 of the Northwestern Wildcats at Kinnick Stadium on October 26, 2024 in Iowa City, Iowa. (Photo by Matthew Holst/Getty Images) | Getty Images The 2027 NFL Draft feels like forever away, and we’re all caught up in the start of the NFL season. Regardless, it’s never too early to look ahead to the Draft. This weekly series will take a closer look at some of the prospects the Carolina Panthers could select in the 2027 iteration of the Draft. In this series, we’ll only be looking at prospects the Panthers could seriously consider. Today our profile will focus on Iowa Hawkeyes offensive tackle Trevor Lauck. Bio Lauck (6’5”, 315 lbs.) was a three time all-state player in Indianapolis on both sides of the ball in high school. Earning a four star ranking while also playing basketball and throwing shotput, he committed to Iowa over powerhouse schools like Michigan and Ohio State. Lauck didn’t earn much playing time until 2025 when he won the starting left tackle job after a couple years of backup duty. He started all 13 games for Iowa that year, allowing zero sacks and just six pressures. He was rewarded with a Third Team All-Big Ten selection. So far this season, he has started all nine games so far for the Hawkeyes. He’s been rock solid, only allowing five pressures and one sack while earning a PFF grade of 80.7 overall. Strengths/Weaknesses Lauck’s technique is surprisingly good for his level of starting experience. He has advanced hand placement, strong punches, balanced mirroring, and excellent footwork. By the time the Draft rolls around, he’ll have two full seasons of left tackle starting experience, more than most other highly ranked tackles. His stunt and twist recognition is up to Iowa’s usual impressive standards, showing a level of coachability. In order to be as effective as he is, Lauck has to have that good technique because his physical abilities aren’t wowing anyone. He has average foot speed, so wide rushers are able to really test him on outside rushes. He also lacks the elite left tackle length the NFL looks for, so some teams might want to push him inside to guard. Projection Lauck is your typical Iowa offensive lineman. He’s big, strong, skilled in run and pass blocking, and very smart. He has plenty of starting experience on the blindside, rarely making mistakes (flagged just three times this season). While he already has a lot of veteran savvy at such a young age, his physical limitations will make it unlikely he ends up as an elite blindside protector. At this point, though, I doubt Bryce Young and the Panthers would turn their noses up at “good but not elite” protection. Rasheed Walker has been not good, and we still don’t know if/when Icky Ekwonu will return to the lineup. If the Panthers are concerned about Lauck’s length on the outside, they need help at guard as well. Lauck has shown the coachability to be able to pick up the nuances of the interior relatively quickly. What do you think, Panthers fans? If Trevor Lauck is available when the Panthers select in the 2027 NFL Draft, should they take him? Sound off in the comments!

title: Chicago Bears Bye Week Confidence Check!
summary: Welcome to SB Nation Reacts, a survey of fans across the NFL. Throughout the year, we ask questions of the most plugged-in Bears fans and fans across the country. Be honest: how many of you guys had the Chicago Bears at 7-2 and in first place at the bye? There’s a long way to go, […]
full_text: Nov 8, 2026; Chicago, Illinois, USA; Chicago Bears defensive end Austin Booker (94) reacts after a play against the Tampa Bay Buccaneers in the first half at Soldier Field. Mandatory Credit: Talia Sprague-Imagn Images | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect Welcome to SB Nation Reacts, a survey of fans across the NFL. Throughout the year, we ask questions of the most plugged-in Bears fans and fans across the country. Be honest: how many of you guys had the Chicago Bears at 7-2 and in first place at the bye? There’s a long way to go, but at the midpoint of the 2026 season, the Bears look like a legit threat to win the NFC. I know it’s cliché to say, but the bye is really hitting at an opportune time for the Bears. The running back room should get a boost with D’Andre Swift able to rest up and Kyle Monangai seemingly ready to return from his toe/thumb injury. Wideout Luther Burden III, who has 49 receptions and 644 receiving yards, exited the win over the Bucs with a concussion, so he needs the break. With how much the offense has dominated the time of possession through the first nine games, the offensive line could use some relaxing time away. The Bears didn’t add anything else to the defense at the trade deadline, but the huge trade for Jeffery Simmons paid immediate dividends. He’s a force multiplier who makes everyone better. Rookie Malik Muhammad II, who has been the Bears’ best corner, should be back after the bye. Jaylon Johnson has had a rough start to the season but is coming off his best game. Kyler Gordon and Tyrique Stevenson were both dinged up on Sunday night, so a week away will do them good, and defensive lineman Dayo Odeyingbo should be back from injured reserve soon. I also think the extra week for Caleb Williams to stew over his four-pick game will lead to an even hungrier player in the second half. The Bears are in a great place to continue their quest for back-to-back playoff appearances. How many wins will the Bears have? Are you confident in the Bears? title: Chicago Bears week 10 power rankings roundup
summary: Heading into their bye week, the 7-2 Chicago Bears remain on a fairly long list of contenders. The Bears stumbled, but did not fall against the Tampa Bay Buccaneers on Sunday Night Football. In fact, it was their first real test of a game this season. Their previous two losses came in a blowout without […]
full_text: CHICAGO, ILLINOIS - NOVEMBER 08: Dillon Thieneman #31, Devin Bush #12, and T.J. Edwards #53 of the Chicago Bears celebrate after a fourth down stop against the Tampa Bay Buccaneers during the second quarter at Soldier Field on November 08, 2026 in Chicago, Illinois. (Photo by John Fisher/Getty Images) | Getty Images Heading into their bye week, the 7-2 Chicago Bears remain on a fairly long list of contenders. The Bears stumbled, but did not fall against the Tampa Bay Buccaneers on Sunday Night Football. In fact, it was their first real test of a game this season. Their previous two losses came in a blowout without their starting QB and in the other, the backup was asked to come in cold and lead a comeback. But this game saw Chicago squander a lead, make uncharacteristic mistakes and still eke out a win. It is fair to ask, though, just over halfway through the season, if “uncharacteristic mistakes” are truly uncharacteristic for a team with the fourth-most turnovers and sixth-most penalties. The team has a lot to clean up during the bye week, but this is a good team and there is plenty to be excited about as they enter the back half of the season. Now, on to this week’s rankings. WCG – Aaron Leming 4. Chicago Bears (7-2) Mid-season Report Card Grade: A Coming into Sunday night, the Bears were off to their best start since 2012. All of that while missing quarterback Caleb Williams for three games and figuring out the defense along the way. The addition of Jeffery Simmons is huge, but it’ll come down to whether they can start winning divisional games. They should be a Super Bowl favorite, but if they have one weakness, that is it. We’ll see how things go coming out of the bye, because starting Thanksgiving, the road to finishing the regular season is a gauntlet. The Athletic – Chad Graff and Josh Kendall 6. Chicago Bears (7-2) Last week: 4 Sunday: Beat Buccaneers 27-24 Midseason grade: A Sunday night’s performance was far from their best, but another win meant another “Good, better, best” speech. Caleb Williams threw four interceptions, but the ceiling for this team is very high as they head into a week off. Profootballtalk – Mike Florio Bears ( No. 5 ; 7-2): Caleb Williams isn’t trying to become Patrick Mahomes; he’s hoping to morph into Michael Jordan. CBS Sports – Pete Prisco 4. Chicago Bears (4) Who was that playing quarterback for them Sunday night against the Bucs? Caleb Williams threw four picks and looked lost for much of the game, which was weird. Yahoo Sports – Frank Schwab 4. Chicago Bears (7-2, LW: 4) The Bears still got to 27 points and did enough to beat the Buccaneers on Sunday night, but it was startling to see Chicago struggle as much as it did. After scoring touchdowns on their first two drives, the Bears’ next 10 possessions were: four interceptions, a fumble, four punts and a field goal. Winning with that type of slump is notable. The Bears came up with the one play they needed, a 38-yard pass to a wide-open Colston Loveland, to get the game-winning field goal. It was particularly strange to see Caleb Williams throw four interceptions, considering he had never thrown more than two in an NFL game. But he never lost confidence, which allowed him to hit Loveland when the Bears needed it. “I’ll never not throw the ball,” Williams said. “I could throw 100 picks in one game. If it comes down to it, I’m going to throw that pass that I threw to Colston, or if it’s a tighter window, I’m going to rip it in there.” NFL.com – Nick Shook 4. Chicago Bears (3) In earlier portions of this season, Chicago might have lost Sunday night’s back-and-forth affair. The Bears were uncharacteristically sloppy with the football and encountered one of the greatest hurdles of their season when Tampa Bay turned up the heat and forced Caleb Williams into some mistakes, which would have spelled trouble for previous versions of this squad. Instead, Chicago’s defense rose to the occasion, burying Baker Mayfield in a key second-half sequence and all but carrying the Bears across the finish line, winning with complementary play that bodes well for this team’s future (as long as it doesn’t repeat the same offensive mistakes). USAToday – Nate Davis 2. Chicago Bears (2): If they’re going to win games on nights when QB Caleb Williams throws four picks, whether or not they’re his fault? Look out for these guys, especially with RB Kyle Monangai likely back on the other side of the bye week. ESPN/NFL Nation – Courtney Cronin 4. Chicago Bears (7-2) Week 9 result: Beat the Buccaneers 27-24 Week 9 ranking: 5 Most important game of the second half: Week 16 vs. the Packers The Bears need to gain ground in their division after early losses to the Vikings and Packers. Chicago’s home rematch with Green Bay on Christmas Day carries significant tiebreaker implications and is the first of three straight NFC North games to end the regular season. The Bears will be in good position to defend their division title if they can pick up two NFC North wins over their next six games, beginning with the Lions on Thanksgiving before the Dec. 25 matchup with the Packers. — Courtney Cronin What do you think of this week’s rankings?

title: Bears stay quiet at trade deadline after Simmons blockbuster
summary: The Chicago Bears made arguably the biggest midseason trade of the year on Oct. 29, giving up a package headlined by two first-rounds picks to the Titans for All-Pro defensive tackle Jeffery Simmons. Despite speculation going into Tuesday’s 2026 NFL trade deadline, that ended up being the only in-season trade the Bears will make this […]
full_text: CHICAGO, ILLINOIS - SEPTEMBER 28: General manager Ryan Poles of the Chicago Bears walks the field prior to the game against the Philadelphia Eagles at Soldier Field on September 28, 2026 in Chicago, Illinois. (Photo by Patrick McDermott/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Chicago Bears made arguably the biggest midseason trade of the year on Oct. 29, giving up a package headlined by two first-rounds picks to the Titans for All-Pro defensive tackle Jeffery Simmons. Despite speculation going into Tuesday’s 2026 NFL trade deadline, that ended up being the only in-season trade the Bears will make this year. Were the Bears to make another move before the deadline, positions like cornerback and defensive end were the ones that had rumored as potential needs to address. Insiders across the NFL linked them to Khalil Mack, though the Chargers ended up keeping him, despite their 0-8 start to the season. Obviously, Simmons is a blockbuster addition by himself. Through the first nine weeks of the 2026-27 NFL season, he leads the league with a perfect 100.0 PFN DT Impact grade. His 6.0 sacks lead all interior defensive linemen, and he also leads at his position with 48 total tackles. Through his first two games, he has had sacks in each of them and has been a force multiplier for the Bears’ defense. Bears head coach Ben Johnson indicated on Monday that the team was discussing a potential move, but that he showed faith in the current roster. “I think Ryan [Poles] is doing a phenomenal job every day,” Johnson explained. “He’s going through and seeing how we can improve this roster, what we need the most of. The coordinators are certainly talking every day right now, just with where their concerns lie within the roster. So we’ll see. We’ll see if there is another move or two to be made or if we stand put. I feel really confident about the guys we have in this locker room right now. And I think we’ve proven at this point that we can find a way to win each and every week with this group.”

Former Bear and current New York Jets corner Nahshon Wright continues to have insiders wondering about his return to the Bears. He’s been rumored to be unhappy in N.Y. and trying to get back to Chicago, so I suppose the speculation could be fueled by him or his representation. The Bears and the Detroit Lions continue to be linked to cornerbacks, including the Philadelphia Eagles’ Riq Woolen. The Minnesota Vikings, who lead the NFC North at 6-1, are rumored to be looking for help at running back, defensive tackle, guard, and quarterback, although if Carson Wentz plays well, they may be content at QB. title: 3 Reasons Why the Chicago Bears Won vs. the Buccaneers
summary: Well that was ugly. Unlike our beloved Denmaster, I do believe in such things as ugly wins. But one thing we all agree on is a win is a win and going into our BYE week at 7-2 is as good as it gets since the letdown in Lambeau back in week 5 that feels […]
full_text: CHICAGO, ILLINOIS - NOVEMBER 8: Devin Bush #12 of the Chicago Bears hypes up his teammates before before the game against the Tampa Bay Buccaneers at Soldier Field on November 8, 2026 in Chicago, Illinois. (Photo by Todd Rosenberg/Getty Images) | Getty Images Well that was ugly. Unlike our beloved Denmaster, I do believe in such things as ugly wins. But one thing we all agree on is a win is a win and going into our BYE week at 7-2 is as good as it gets since the letdown in Lambeau back in week 5 that feels like ages ago. Considering the Chicago Bears are on the verge of a certain level of success the franchise hasn’t experienced in decades thanks to Ben Johnson and Caleb Williams, I am going to leave them out of this piece from now on – as it is a given that both were instrumental to Chicago’s success. Go ahead and throw in All-World DT Jeffery Simmons into that category too. Instead, I will be highlighting 3 other factors that contributed to Chicago’s win or loss. So let’s get to it. 1. Devin Bush Though it’s been a while – we Chicago Bears fans have seen our share of exceptional linebacker play over the years. That’s not to say we haven’t seen flashes of brilliance from guys like T.J. Edwards, Tremaine Edmunds and even Jack Sanborn. But what we saw out of Devin Bush on Sunday night reminded me of prime Roquan Smith when the All-Pro roamed the middle for the Monsters of the Midway before he was shipped out to Baltimore. Similarly built at right around 6ft and 230lbs, both players provide unusual explosion from the position with an uncanny ability to zoom past reaching guards and/or tackles to blow up runs behind the LOS while also covering the middle of the field from sideline to sideline in the passing game. Ever since the arrival of Jeffery Simmons, Bush’s talents have been on full display and that continued against the Buccaneers. Whether it was blowing up a ball carrier on 3rd or 4th down for a loss or absolutely de-cleating Emeka Egbuka on a jet sweep, Bush was a force to be reckoned with, and I don’t think we win that game without him. Bush posted season highs in stuffs (tackles at or behind the line of scrimmage) and passes defensed Sunday night, and I would imagine those marks will be surpassed before we reach the playoffs. It is clear to see why Bears GM Ryan Poles brought in the former Michigan Wolverine, and Chicago will need more games like that if they want to make a deep run at the Lombardi Trophy. 2. 3rd Down Defense I could have said Dennis Allen here, but that isn’t specific enough for my liking. Additionally, Allen calls the plays but the players have to execute so it’s a team-effort with coaches included. Prior to Sunday nights game, Tampa was 38% on 3rd downs on the season. Against Chicago, Tampa went 2 for 12, which is 16.7%. That is a remarkable stat that shows how Chicago’s defense truly impacted the game. Additionally, only 1 of Chicago’s 4 sacks and neither interception came on 3rd down – meaning the team is playing technically sound and effective football when it matters most without relying on the big play or turnover like they seemed to do a year ago. Again, that can absolutely be credited to the coaching staff but the way these players were flying around on the most important down of a drive is encouraging. Especially after giving up 2 TDs and almost 5 yards per carry and 100 yards to Bucky Irving. They say 3rd down is the money down and if Chicago wasn’t as successful against Tampa on 3rd downs Sunday night – there is no way they win that ball game. 3. Jaylon Johnson This one was harder than I expected as Cam Lewis, Rome Odunze and Luther Burden III were all deserving. But at the end of the day, the pick-6 that Jaylon had absolutely was the difference in this game. Though Chicago turned the ball over 5 times, not one of them was returned for a score like Jaylon’s 67 yard interception return was and it couldn’t have come at a better time. Up by 4 points with Tampa primed for another drive, Jaylon put Chicago ahead with an 11-point lead, and they would never look back. After the disappointing season that Jaylon has had, it was great to see him read and react so quickly and snag the INT before racing more than half the field for a score. If Jaylon Johnson can use this game as a springboard for the rest of the season, it would be a huge boost to this defense and team down the stretch. It was easily his best game of the season and a great thing to see for Chicago’s CB1. Jaylon Johnson earned the lone game ball after the Bears' 27-24 win over the Bucs with his strongest performance of the season. Johnson allowed just one reception for six yards on five targets in coverage in Week 9 and returned a third-quarter interception for a 67-yard… — Courtney Cronin (@CourtneyRCronin) November 9, 2026 What about you? Who, outside of Caleb, Ben, and Big Jeff, felt most important to the Bears’ win on Sunday night?

full_text: Nov 8, 2026; Chicago, Illinois, USA; Chicago Bears defensive tackle Jeffery Simmons (99) reacts after the game against the Tampa Bay Buccaneers at Soldier Field. Mandatory Credit: Talia Sprague-Imagn Images | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect 1. Is it just me, or was there a lot of bad football happening this past week? The Monday night game between the Bills and Vikings, who were absolutely offensive offensively, was just the cherry on top. Maybe it’s just the number of backup/backup-level quarterbacks playing across the league due to injuries and ineptitude. It made teams and quarterbacks who are actually good, like Joe Burrow and Jordan Love, look like they’re playing an entirely different sport. Maybe we should just give everyone a bye week next week. 2. The Vikings are cooked. Brian Flores’ defense is awesome. But even they can’t carry quarterback play this bad for a whole season and postseason. It’s just unrealistic. Eventually, as happened against a persistent Bills offense in the second half, being on the field three-quarters of the game breaks you. Minnesota, to be fair, did try to address their QB situation by signing Kyler Murray. Unfortunately, he’s been hurt a lot and not that effective when on the field. Can’t get worse than what Carson Wentz just did against Buffalo, though. Their defense will win them a few games, but they can’t win their division like this. 3. Speaking of which…the Chicago Bears now lead the NFC North through nine weeks. Exactly how they drew it up! Slogging through a 2-1 record without Caleb Williams and then winning the ugliest offensive game since the Miracle in the Desert back in 2026? The Bears are back, baby. For real, though: being 7-2, with wins over both of last year’s Super Bowl participants, is a major accomplishment so far for a team many expected to take a step back. The road doesn’t get easier from here, including plenty of games against their divisional opponents (all of whom have six wins or more). But they’re built for it. 4. I don’t know whom the Chargers think they are, exactly. But there need to be a bunch of veteran players not on that team by the time the trade deadline passes this afternoon at 4 p.m. ET. That is a thoroughly uncompetitive, unserious football team, and they should have no delusions about making the playoffs. Follow the Eagles’ example. They just traded defensive tackle Jordan Davis to the Jaguars after trading starting center Cam Jurgens away to the Ravens last month. Khalil Mack, Rashawn Slater, Derwin James. Hell, trade Dicker the Kicker if anyone will send anything for him. Start selling. Now. Otherwise, everyone’s got to get fired immediately. 5. The Jags are getting cooked already for sending a 2027 first-round pick and a 2029 second-rounder to Philly for Davis. That’s a pretty steep price, and that’s coming from a guy whose team just traded two firsts for Jeffery Simmons. Draft capital—the idea of the unknown—is extremely valuable, which Eagles general manager Howie Roseman knows well. When you’re as good as he is at drafting defensive linemen, sending away a good one is no big deal. Here’s what I’ll say in Jacksonville’s defense, though: we as a football community might not be fully appreciating how “premium” a good/great defensive tackle is. But the league seems to be angling in that direction. Great interior defenders make everyone behind them better, meaning you don’t have to allocate as much capital to the positions behind them. Plus, interior pressure on quarterbacks is probably even more devastating than edge pressure. Bottom line: yeah, it’s an overpay. But that doesn’t mean the price isn’t worth it if Davis is even partly what Simmons has been for the Bears so far. 6. Not going to lie, I’m loving the trend of calling horrible, interception-worthy throws “deli meat” or “meatball subs.” I’m not sure if it originated with defensive players, reactor culture, or transitioning from baseball, where throwing one right down the middle to a hitter is a “meatball.” I don’t care. Give whoever came up with this idea a raise, and give Tom Brady a few million more for leaning into it. It’s hilarious. 7. I hope the Eagles start Joe Milton for the rest of the year for the entertainment value alone. Because yeah, this guy is going to struggle to complete the most basic throws (and might accidentally kill one of his receivers with a screen pass). But when it comes to rolling out or chilling way back in the pocket on play-action, the anticipation of wondering how far/how hard he’s about to chuck the ball is intoxicating. Just once, we need him to try to air one out from like his own 25-yard line to the end zone. I bet he could do it. And the Eagles are going absolutely nowhere. So you might as well live with it. 8. For a guy leading a 3-5 football team, C.J. Stroud has been playing some insane ball. He’s on track for easily the best statistical year of his career with 16 touchdowns (his previous season-high is 23) and just two interceptions, and he just dropped 384 yards and five scores on the Chargers with a patchwork-quilt offense around him. The Texans might not do anything this year, unfortunately, especially with the Jaguars running away with the AFC South. But if there’s any argument for still extending Stroud after this season is over, even if they miss the playoffs, this is as good as any. It won’t be what, say, Caleb Williams or Drake Maye is likely to sign in the next few years. But someone’s going to pay Stroud handsomely as long as he keeps this up. 9. My verdict on the Shedeur Sanders performance, since you’re so interested in it? If I’m grading on a curve, let’s call it “B+,” especially because of the plays he made down the stretch to get the Browns in position to send the game to overtime and eventually challenge for a shot to win it in the end. He definitely outperformed most backups pressed into service this week. But in terms of “representative NFL starting quarterback,” that game is a C at best. Not discounting what he did down the stretch, but even some of the big plays he produced down the field were on underthrown balls his receivers had to adjust to or make incredible catches on. It’s hard to come away thinking anything but, “Thanks for your service, kid. Now sit right back down on that bench.” Again, not bad after that rough first half. But let’s not get ahead of ourselves saying he needs more burn. He really doesn’t. 10. Question for the group: who’s the next head coach to get the axe this season? My hot take: Jim Harbaugh. Because ain’t no way that Chargers team should be this awful. Others, like Aaron Glenn with the Jets or Shane Steichen with the Colts, are playing for teams actively tanking/blowing things up. They know the score. The Harbaugh experiment has run its course, and one more loss might send him. Let us know what you think.

title: Week 10 NFL Power Rankings: Midseason Report Cards
summary: The halfway point of the season has concluded, which means it’s time to take a look at each team’s first half and see if they have lived up to expectations. As always, when grading teams, it’s best to do it on a curve. Expectations provide needed context, which helps shape our mid-season grades. Please note […]
full_text: MINNEAPOLIS, MINNESOTA - NOVEMBER 09: Josh Allen #17 of the Buffalo Bills walks the field with teammates prior to the game against the Minnesota Vikings at U.S. Bank Stadium on November 09, 2026 in Minneapolis, Minnesota. (Photo by Stephen Maturen/Getty Images) | Getty Images The halfway point of the season has concluded, which means it’s time to take a look at each team’s first half and see if they have lived up to expectations. As always, when grading teams, it’s best to do it on a curve. Expectations provide needed context, which helps shape our mid-season grades. Please note that these grades reflect no moves made on Tuesday before the deadline. With that in mind, let’s dive into our WCG Week 10 NFL Power Rankings! 1. San Francisco 49ers (7-1) Mid-season Report Card Grade: A+ Injuries have continued to be an issue, but the 49ers have somehow persevered. So far, San Francisco has consistently been the best team in the league, and with better health, they’ll be very hard to beat down the stretch. Overall, it’s hard to ask for much more than what we’ve seen from them so far this season, but don’t sleep on the other two teams in this division to make things interesting over the final two months of the season. 2. Buffalo Bills (7-1) Mid-season Report Card Grade: A If you were asleep all offseason and didn’t know the Bills made a change at head coach, you’d probably think this was just business as usual for Buffalo. In many ways, it has been, but it’s been pretty impressive to see them pick up as nothing changed with the coaching staff. Quarterback Josh Allen is awesome, but the defense will once again define how their season ends. Right now, it hasn’t been good enough, but they’ve kept winning anyway. Will a deadline move (or two) get that unit heading in the right direction? We shall see. 3. Jacksonville Jaguars (6-2) Mid-season Report Card Grade: A What’s not to like about the Jaguars right now? They have three wins by 23 points or more, Trevor Lawrence is playing like a top-tier quarterback, and the defense continues to dominate, especially in the run game. This is an extremely well-rounded team that shouldn’t be discounted because of the division they are in. This is a Super Bowl contender with a very good roster and coaching staff. 4. Chicago Bears (7-2) Mid-season Report Card Grade: A Coming into Sunday night, the Bears were off to their best start since 2012. All of that while missing quarterback Caleb Williams for three games and figuring out the defense along the way. The addition of Jeffery Simmons is huge, but it’ll come down to whether they can start winning divisional games. They should be a Super Bowl favorite, but if they have one weakness, that is it. We’ll see how things go coming out of the bye, because starting Thanksgiving, the road to finishing the regular season is a gauntlet. 5. Detroit Lions (6-2) Mid-season Report Card Grade: A The Lions are playing their best football in two seasons, and knock on wood, their defense is finally improving. Losing All-Pro linebacker Jack Campbell was scary and a big blow to this team, but getting back both high-level safeties should help. The offense will ultimately dictate how far this group can go, but they are well-coached and have plenty of talent. Don’t sleep on the Lions over the second half of the season. 6. Cincinnati Bengals (6-2) Mid-season Report Card Grade: A The Bengals have been hard to figure out so far this year, mainly because of their slow starts. The talent is there, and the defense is better, but can they improve enough to chase down the Steelers for the AFC North title? A lot will come down to how much the defense improves over the last two months of the season. It’s all in front of them, and with the Ravens fading fast, the road gets a little easier. 7. Green Bay Packers (6-3) Mid-season Report Card Grade: A- This season started as a disaster for Green Bay, but they’ve found a way to push through adversity and come out looking like a much better team on the other side. Quarterback Jordan Love is playing at a high level, and the defense has rounded into form, despite missing star pass rusher Micah Parsons. Existing in the NFC North is tough, and like the other three teams, there’s going to be little margin for error down the stretch. The good news is, the Packers have plenty of experience pushing through to the postseason. 8. Denver Broncos (7-2) Mid-season Report Card Grade: B+ Despite a slow start, mostly due to the offense, this is still a very good team that might have its best football ahead of it. The biggest issue has been Bo Nix’s play. Without a step up, it’s hard to imagine they’ll be able to win the AFC. That said, with a step in the right direction, they are as dangerous as any team in the conference. Finding another playmaker on the offensive side of the ball should be a priority, so we’ll see how it all plays out. 9. Kansas City Chiefs (6-2) Mid-season Report Card Grade: A Their 5-0 start felt like a dream, but reality has hit over the last few weeks. The good news is that this is clearly a good team. The question remains whether or not they can ultimately win the division. This team desperately needs at least another pass catcher, but if they get into the playoffs, which they should, they’ll be dangerous with the high-level experience of winning the big game. 10. Pittsburgh Steelers (6-2) Mid-season Report Card Grade: A Color me surprised that the Steelers have somehow been better under Mike McCarthy than they were in Mike Tomlin’s final seasons. In many ways, their defense has carried the momentum. Still, credit goes to this offense, and especially 43-year-old quarterback Aaron Rodgers, for continuing to play at a high enough level. I’m still not sold that they can maintain this all season, but the last month they have looked like a very good team. We’ll see if it lasts. 11. Minnesota Vikings (6-2) Mid-season Report Card Grade: B+ The defense is playing at a 1985 Chicago Bears level, but the offense is bottom three in most key statistical categories. Maybe a change at quarterback (although head coach Kevin O’Connell hasn’t made it permanent) will make the difference, but the schedule ahead will be the ultimate test to show how good this team is as a whole. Adding a high-level running back will help, but without better quarterback play, their ceiling is limited. 12. Los Angeles Rams (5-4) Mid-season Report Card Grade: D+ In many ways, it’s been a disastrous start to the season for the Rams, yet they come out of Week 9 above .500. Getting back Myles Garrett will be big, but the injuries they’ve suffered on the defensive side of the ball can’t be ignored. If all goes well, the Rams and Seahawks will be fighting for a playoff spot, but this team has a long way to go to find enough consistency to live up to being heavy Super Bowl favorites. If they make the playoffs, it will likely be from a Wild Card spot, which is a tough ask for any team. 13. Seattle Seahawks (5-4) Mid-season Report Card Grade: D Are the Seahawks a good team? I believe they are. They have too much talent and too much already established for them to fall off completely. That said, they are in a tough division and conference, and so far this year, it’s shown. The defense is still elite, but without better quarterback play, they are severely capped. All in all, it’s been a disappointing start, but I expect to see them in the playoffs come January. 14. New York Giants (5-2-1) Mid-season Report Card Grade: A+ Count me as one of the people who didn’t quite believe that John Harbaugh’s presence would automatically make the Giants a good team. I was wrong, and I’m totally OK admitting that. Not only are they leading the NFC East, but they’ve done it starting three quarterbacks. Once Jaxson Dart was lost, it would have been easy to write them off, yet they’ve kept their pace and have played solid football along the way. The Giants aren’t likely to be a big threat in the playoffs, but count this as a…

title: Bengals Film Room: Joe Burrow now a frontrunner for MVP?
summary: The Cincinnati Bengals put on a show in Madrid, Spain, defeating the Atlanta Falcons 34-17. Quarterback Joe Burrow was 24 for 29 for 271 yards. He threw 3 touchdown passes and, most importantly, did not throw an interception this week. Jordan Love currently leads the NFL in passing yards with 2,618 yards on the season. […]
full_text: The Cincinnati Bengals put on a show in Madrid, Spain, defeating the Atlanta Falcons 34-17. Quarterback Joe Burrow was 24 for 29 for 271 yards. He threw 3 touchdown passes and, most importantly, did not throw an interception this week. Jordan Love currently leads the NFL in passing yards with 2,618 yards on the season. Burrow is currently second with 2,386 passing yards. It is important to note that Burrow has also played one less game than Jordan Love this year. Burrow has a better completion rate, completing an elite 74% of his passes this season. Burrow is also leading the league in touchdown passes, having thrown 23 of them already this season. It isn’t just the stats that are jumping out for Burrow; he is in full control of an explosive Cincinnati offense that is firing on all cylinders. Let’s take a look at some of his biggest plays from the win against Atlanta. After the Falcons drove down the field and scored a touchdown to start the game, Joe Burrow and the offense were able to answer right back. The biggest play of the drive came on a 47-yard touchdown strike to Ja’Marr Chase. The Bengals tried to hit that play last week, with Burrow not getting enough on the ball and ultimately throwing an interception. That wasn’t the case this week, as he hit Chase in stride to help tie the game up 7-7. Burrow missed Chase on this deep ball last week, but not this time. Perfect throw from Burrow to Chase. The camera guy must have thought he was Jeff Blake for a second… pic.twitter.com/S5SARC48zJ — Bengals & Brews (@BengalsBrews) November 9, 2026 After an Atlanta Falcons field goal, the Bengals offense was able to drive right down the field again. Burrow got some incredible catches from his wide receivers on this drive. The first one was a 7-yard completion to Tee Higgins on a third down that allowed the Bengals to keep the drive alive. Higgins caught the ball with strong hands in traffic. He was also being held on the ball, though no flag was thrown. Joe Burrow to Tee Higgins for 7 yards and the 1st down conversion. pic.twitter.com/A6MQTC2aKF — Bengals & Brews (@BengalsBrews) November 9, 2026 Not long after that completion, it was Ja’Marr Chase making a spectacular play for his quarterback. Burrow threw a pass a bit too far out in front of Ja’Marr. The defender thought he had an interception, until Ja’Marr decided to snag the ball out of the air with one hand. He immediately turned upfield for yards after the catch. Nah Ja’Marr, you are an alien pic.twitter.com/bXbNmGTAva — Bengals & Brews (@BengalsBrews) November 9, 2026 Burrow and the offense were able to get up to the line quickly after getting down to the 1-yard line on this drive. Burrow caught the Falcons off guard and called his own number for the quarterback sneak. He recorded his second rushing touchdown in as many weeks as a result. This score put the Bengals up 14-10. Falcons moving around and Burrow sneaks it in for the touchdown and 14-10 lead. pic.twitter.com/BTXWk3Mati — Bengals & Brews (@BengalsBrews) November 9, 2026 After the defense forced a Falcons punt, Joe Burrow and the offense were back on the field for their third series of the game. They started the drive with Burrow going to Ja’Marr Chase once again. This time for a 31-yard catch-and-run. Burrow to Chase for 31 yards kicks off the Bengals third drive of the game. Shoutout to the 🐐Drew Sample getting down the field to pick up a block. pic.twitter.com/hKPYGcESBa — Bengals & Brews (@BengalsBrews) November 9, 2026 Burrow displayed his toughness on a crucial third down during the drive. He had to scramble out to his right and was able to extend the play just long enough to get a patented Ja’Marr is down there somewhere pass off. Burrow got leveled on the play, but the result was a big completion to a diving Chase down the field for another first down. Burrow gets absolutely leveled here but still gets enough on the pass for Ja’Marr to come back and dive for the reception and keep the chains moving. pic.twitter.com/dzlJqkJZW1 — Bengals & Brews (@BengalsBrews) November 9, 2026 With pressure coming off the left side of the line, Burrow was able to convert another crucial third down on this drive. He had to double clutch, but stood tall in the pocket and delivered a pass that only his receiver could catch. That receiver just so happened to be Ja’Marr Chase again, who made a spectacular extension for the ball while getting his feet down just in bounds in the process. The Joe Burrow to Ja’Marr Chase connection was strong in the first half, with Chase going for over 140 receiving yards and a touchdown. Filthy stuff from Burrow to Chase. Huge conversion with 6:34 left in the first half and up 14-10. Phenomenal toe tap job by Ja’Marr. pic.twitter.com/TMobi9T99X — Bengals & Brews (@BengalsBrews) November 9, 2026 Speaking of quarterback-to-receiver connections that have been on fire all season, Joe Burrow found Tee Higgins for the touchdown to cap off this drive. Burrow threw a perfect strike to Higgins just inside the end zone. Tee once again displayed strong hands to extend the Bengals’ lead to 21-10. The Joe Burrow to Tee Higgins connection has been en fuego all season pic.twitter.com/VFN3Bsnbsj — Bengals & Brews (@BengalsBrews) November 9, 2026 It isn’t just the top two receivers that Burrow has been finding for big plays this season either. Dohnte Meyers had a big play last week to help the Bengals ultimately force overtime and get the victory against Tennessee. This week it wasn’t as dramatic of a moment, but Burrow once again scrambled out and was able to hit Meyers for a big play before halftime. The Bengals would ultimately kick a field goal on this drive, making their lead 24-10 at halftime. Joe Burrow to Dohnte Meyers for 42 yards before the half to set up an Evan McPherson field goal. pic.twitter.com/MY6SDCeNLZ — Bengals & Brews (@BengalsBrews) November 9, 2026 Burrow and the rest of the offense didn’t have to do a whole lot the rest of the way, but after Atlanta cut the lead to 24-17 in the third quarter, they did need to put together another scoring drive. That is exactly what they were able to do. Maybe one of the most impressive plays of the game for Joe Burrow was the touchdown at the end of this one. He went through his progression, stood tough in the pocket, and delivered an absolute strike to Tee Higgins in the middle of the end zone. That touchdown put the Bengals back up by two scores, a lead that was too much to overcome for the Atlanta Falcons. Burrow stands in the pocket as long as possible going through his progressions, and then throws a strike to Tee Higgins in the middle of the end zone while taking a hit. pic.twitter.com/QbDuqZahxH — Bengals & Brews (@BengalsBrews) November 9, 2026 It is only halfway through the season, so there is a ton of football to be played. With that said, Joe Burrow is firmly in everyone’s midseason conversations for MVP. It won’t just be up to him to keep playing at the level he is; the defense will also have to find ways to continue helping to win games. The MVP award is typically going to be given to a player who is part of a team with a lot of regular-season wins. A win against Pittsburgh in primetime Sunday Night Football would ramp up the MVP talk even more.
author: Dale Altman

title: Bengals now have best 8-game start under Zac Taylor
summary: The Cincinnati Bengals put together another convincing win over the Atlanta Falcons this morning in Madrid. Joe Burrow, Ja’Marr Chase, and Tee Higgins put on an absolute show in front of a massive international audience, leading the Bengals to 6-2 on the season. With the win over Atlanta, the Bengals have officially put together the […]
full_text: The Cincinnati Bengals put together another convincing win over the Atlanta Falcons this morning in Madrid. Joe Burrow, Ja’Marr Chase, and Tee Higgins put on an absolute show in front of a massive international audience, leading the Bengals to 6-2 on the season. With the win over Atlanta, the Bengals have officially put together the best start through eight games in the Zac Taylor era at 6-2. Cincinnati has started 5-3 through their first eight games twice under Taylor (2021, 2023), but 2026 now takes the cake as the best start under their current head coach. The Bengals truly are just two plays away from being 8-0 on the season, but it is hard to complain about where the team is right now. With Burrow playing at an MVP level and the defense doing enough to support the best offense in the NFL, it could be an exciting year for Bengals fans. Taylor and the Bengals will now return home for a massive, and I mean massive, AFC North showdown with the Pittsburgh Steelers next weekend on Sunday Night Football.

title: Bengals News: Embarrassing Trade Deadline for Cincinnati
summary: The 4 PM NFL trade deadline came and went on Tuesday, and the Cincinnati Bengals didn’t make a single addition to their team. Not for lack of trying, though. They tried to send a sixth-round pick to the Eagles in exchange for edge rusher Arnold Ebiketie, a move most would have celebrated. At least at […]
full_text: Cincinnati Bengals director of player personnel Duke Tobin takes questions from the press during the annual season kickoff media day event at Paycor Stadium in downtown Cincinnati on Monday, July 27, 2026. | USA TODAY Network via Reuters Co The 4 PM NFL trade deadline came and went on Tuesday, and the Cincinnati Bengals didn’t make a single addition to their team. Not for lack of trying, though. They tried to send a sixth-round pick to the Eagles in exchange for edge rusher Arnold Ebiketie, a move most would have celebrated. At least at first. They backed out, though, after they learned—likely on X from OverTheCap.com’s Nick Korte and not even someone from inside their own building—they’d lose the third-round compensatory pick they earned in the ‘27 draft if the trade went through. So yeah. We learned the Bengals likely don’t even have anyone on the staff that could foresee how trading for a guy who was signed as a compensatory free agent could affect their future. We also learned the defense that has shown flashes of really good and flashes of really bad is the one Joe Burrow and the offense is going to be tethered to for the entire season. What a day. Here’s what else is going on: Bengals Face Harsh Reality After NFL Trade Deadline People are going to put a lot of blame on the Bengals and their front office for not making a swing. In some ways, it will be unfair. In other ways, they have built up a reputation of not going all-in when they have to. How Bengals’ top opponents in the AFC handled Tuesday’s NFL trade deadline There wasn’t a more aggressive team in the AFC than the Jacksonville Jaguars, however, who added three veterans before the deadline. Former Bengals safety Jessie Bates III came over from Atlanta, defensive tackle Jordan Davis was dealt from the Eagles to the Jaguars and defensive tackle Davon Godchaux arrived in a trade with the New Orleans Saints. Hidden strength of Bengals’ roster just took a hit and there was nothing they could’ve done to stop it The Bengals were lucky to bring Johnson back on their practice squad. Having both him and Flacco behind Burrow was such a luxury, and made the QB room arguably the best in the league. Even if Johnson wasn’t on the active roster, his presence in the building and experience of nearly 20 years playing professional ball were valuable on their own. WEEK 10 NFL MVP TRACKER: BENGALS’ JOE BURROW LEADS RACE AT MIDPOINT OF 2026 SEASON We’ve seen some ridiculously high-level quarterback play recently, from Joe Burrow dicing up defenses like a Top Chef on deadline to Jordan Love dive-bombing opponents into oblivion.

title: Twitter bashes Bengals for fumbling Arnold Ebiketie trade over compensatory draft pick

They had a trade in place to send a sixth-rounder to the Philadelphia Eagles to acquire defensive end Arnold Ebiketie. The issue was that the move would have canceled out the third-round compensatory pick the Bengals are set […]
full_text: The Cincinnati Bengals nearly made a move similar to one they had made the past two seasons. They had a trade in place to send a sixth-rounder to the Philadelphia Eagles to acquire defensive end Arnold Ebiketie. The issue was that the move would have canceled out the third-round compensatory pick the Bengals are set to receive for Trey Hendrickson signing with the Baltimore Ravens. So the trade would have cost Cincinnati a sixth-round pick and a potential third-round pick for a rotational defensive end to replace Cashius Howell. Needless to say, Bengals fans were embarrassed and frustrated. Because preserving the ~98th pick in the draft does not outweigh – valuing hendrickson like a 1st round pick but not paying him like one – denying day 2 pick offers to then operate like the 98th pick is coming back to you a year later – getting caught being ignorant https://t.co/WJJmL4Onhp — John Sheeran (@John__Sheeran) November 10, 2026 Just reeks of complacency. Bengals are really good. Can beat anyone. All the other contenders in the AFC strengthened their teams, the Bengals sit still, again. Not asking for ground breaking moves, but nothing, is so frustrating. — Bryce Spalding (@bryce_spalding) November 10, 2026 A lot of people (justifiably) saying the comp pick formula is confusing It’s definitely confusing for fans It should not be confusing for someone who has a whole team to understand the CBA and the business side of the game https://t.co/ZiC28HmrOH — Jay R (@JayRBP) November 10, 2026 That is a fair reaction. That is a lot for the Bengals. What makes all of this even worse is watching all the other top AFC teams get better at the deadline. The optics are horrible for the Bengals. Not only did they fail to add to a defense that clearly needs more quality depth, they botched a trade that would’ve given them an edge rusher with Cashius Howell out. And on top of that, nearly all of their AFC competition made moves to… — Mike Petraglia (@Trags) November 10, 2026 There are certainly worse positions to be in. It is unfortunate that it seems several bets on young defenders are not paying off, and the refusal to put together a contingency plan in the offseason or correct it now is just frustrating. The only bright side is they went the route of not looking incompetent and losing a pick that could be valuable next offseason. There's room for these thoughts to co-exist: The Bengals have a very good team, with a solid roster that's largely the result of some really good, smart, and aggressive work by the front office. The quarterback is an MVP candidate. full_text: Update : The Bengals have now called off this trade. ———————————————————————————————————————————— The Cincinnati Bengals have heard your pleas to be active before the trade deadline at 4 PM ET on Tuesday afternoon. According to NFL insider Ian Rapoport, the Bengals traded a 2027 sixth-round pick to the Philadelphia Eagles for edge rusher Arnold Ebiketie. Ebiketie was selected in the second round, No. 38 overall, by the Atlanta Falcons in the 2022 NFL Draft out of Penn State. He recorded his first sack in his very first professional game and worked his way into the Falcons’ starting lineup by halfway through his rookie year. After his rookie contract, he signed a one-year deal with the Eagles this past offseason. Now the Eagles are riddled with injuries, sit at 2-7, and are shedding contracts in exchange for draft picks. This is clearly a move the Bengals made in response to the injury that landed rookie edge rusher Cashius Howell on IR. It is also a clear signal the Bengals lack trust in their 2025 first-round pick, Shemar Stewart, who only played 10 snaps on Sunday in Spain. Ebiketie hasn’t made any sacks so far this season, but he has racked up 10 pressures, per PFF. He’ll be a rotational asset for the Bengals’ defensive line and will join Stewart and Cedric Johnson behind Boye Mafe and Myles Murphy. Stay tuned for new possible trade news as we near the deadline. title: Bengals Tuesday Trenches: Super in Spain, SNF and more
summary: The Cincinnati Bengals won their fourth game in a row on Sunday morning in front of a national audience from Santiago Bernabéu Stadium in Madrid, Spain, by a score of 34-17. Now, at 6-2 along with Pittsburgh, the Bengals are set to host the Steelers for what kind of feels like the AFC North title […]
full_text: The Cincinnati Bengals won their fourth game in a row on Sunday morning in front of a national audience from Santiago Bernabéu Stadium in Madrid, Spain, by a score of 34-17. Now, at 6-2 along with Pittsburgh, the Bengals are set to host the Steelers for what kind of feels like the AFC North title game even though we’re only in Week 10. The Bengals were almost perfect on offense. They scored on six of their eight drives (I’m not counting the last drive in which they could have scored but were able to kill the clock), and four of those scores were touchdowns. Joe Burrow completed 24/29 passes for 271 yards and three touchdowns — two to Tee Higgins and one deep bomb to Ja’Marr Chase to cap off their first drive of the game. The defense had its moments, but the familiar struggles were there too. In the end, the Falcons’ offense just couldn’t hope to keep up, even though they seemed to hang around a little, especially early in the second half. Still, it never felt like the Bengals were potentially going to lose control of the game. Here are some random thoughts on their three-score win before we get into the Steelers game: Tee Higgins is a monster. He didn’t have a ton of yards (32), but he caught two touchdown passes, and multiple passes—including one of those touchdowns—with guys draped all over him. Higgins looks like a man among boys when he catches the ball in traffic. Ja’Marr Chase is a generational talent. His ability to turn into a running back as soon as his hands touch the ball is remarkable. He breaks tackles like a running back and has 220 yards after the catch so far in 2026. What I’d really like to see, though, is a yards-after-contact stat for him. The offensive line held up beautifully against the Falcons, who came into Sunday morning’s game with 18 sacks and weren’t too far behind the Bengals. Burrow was sacked twice, but one of those sacks was much more of a coverage sack than anything to do with the line. If they can continue to protect Burrow like they did Sunday, the offense can break records. The run game finally made an appearance on Sunday. To be clear, I think Burrow can beat about any defense with Chase, Higgins, and the other weapons he has, but it’s hard to win in the playoffs if you can’t run the ball. The Bengals were able to kill the clock with a solid running game in the fourth quarter. Chase Brown had multiple explosive runs, including one for 19 yards—a season-long for the Bengals’ offense. Dexter Lawrence. That’s it. That’s all I have to say. Okay, a bit more: Lawrence didn’t show up on the stat sheet much, but he lived in the backfield and forced Michael Penix into throwing early or on the run. He almost caused an intentional grounding penalty at one point. It’s amazing how much one man can change the face of a defense. The Bengals were unable to sack the quarterback on Sunday. This was their first game without a sack, and hopefully it’s their last game. Cashius Howell is on IR, and the Bengals pretty much relied on Boye Mafe and Myles Murphy. Cedric Johnson only played 13 snaps, and Shemar Stewart played just 10. It would be nice to see a little more rotation to help keep the starters fresh. Regardless of DJ Turner’s PFF score, remember the receiver he’s covering doesn’t get targeted very often. Money Mac strikes again—good from 57 and 43 yards, and that 43-yard kick in the fourth quarter put any hope of a comeback out of reach for the Falcons. Speaking of the Falcons, we can credit the Bengals for breaking Atlanta—The Falcons traded Jessie Bates Monday morning. STEELERS WEEK I honestly don’t think it’s an exaggeration to say that Sunday night’s game against the Steelers at Paycor Stadium is one of the biggest games to be played there in the last several seasons . The Steelers are also 6-2, and with the injuries in Baltimore and the Browns doing Browns things, it’s not crazy to think the winner of this game likely wins the division. The Bengals are not the same team they were that lost to the Steelers in Week 3. The offense is awake and clicking. The defense has its moments, but could use some help. Tuesday (today) is the last day they can make an addition via trade, as the deadline is at 4 PM Eastern. I highly doubt the Bengals make a move, but I also highly doubt they’d trade a first-round pick for Lawrence. Can they pull off another trade just five months after the Lawrence trade? If there was a time to do it, it’s now. The Bengals are in prime position to make a run, and they obviously need a little help, especially on defense, to get things right. They could use depth at cornerback as well as linebacker. They could probably get by without any additions on offense, but adding Jonathan Taylor sure would be cool. The Bengals are favored by 3.5 points, which is a half point over home-field advantage, and a win would put them at 7-2 with a firm grasp on the division, and a handful of winnable games before they host the Chiefs in a little over a month. This is where we hoped the Bengals would be at this point in the season. Relative Song Lyrics: Well, I never been to Spain But I kinda like the music Say the ladies are insane there And they sure know how to use it They don’t abuse it Never gonna lose it I can’t refuse it

title: The Good, The Bad and The Ugly in Bengals’ 34-17 win over Falcons in Madrid
summary: ¡Olé! The Cincinnati Bengals took their show to Madrid on Sunday, and the stripes looked right at home at the Bernabéu. Cincinnati spotted the Atlanta Falcons a touchdown on the opening drive, then took over behind Joe Burrow and Ja’Marr Chase on the way to a 34-17 win. It’s the first victory in franchise history […]
full_text: ¡Olé! The Cincinnati Bengals took their show to Madrid on Sunday, and the stripes looked right at home at the Bernabéu. Cincinnati spotted the Atlanta Falcons a touchdown on the opening drive, then took over behind Joe Burrow and Ja’Marr Chase on the way to a 34-17 win. It’s the first victory in franchise history in a game played outside the United States. That’s four straight wins; the Bengals are 6-2, and Pittsburgh comes to Paycor for Sunday Night Football next week. Before we turn the page, let’s break this one down. The Good Joe Burrow, MVP candidate. Burrow went 24-of-29 for 271 yards, three touchdowns, no turnovers, and a 140.1 passer rating, then added a 1-yard sneak for a fourth score. He was nearly perfect in the first half, at 16-of-18 for 234 yards and two touchdowns. His 21 touchdown passes lead the NFL, and he has 16 total touchdowns over the last four games. After last week’s three interceptions, this was the clean, surgical Burrow we know. Ja’Marr Chase, “best in the world.” That’s how Zac Taylor described him after the game, and it’s hard to argue. Chase answered Atlanta’s opening score with a 47-yard touchdown on the Bengals’ first possession. He had eight catches for 142 yards in the first half alone, the most first-half receiving yards of his career, and finished with 10 catches for 155 yards. His seven receiving touchdowns lead the AFC. Tee Higgins in the red zone. Higgins only had five catches for 32 yards, but two of them were touchdowns, from 4 and 8 yards out. That’s six touchdown catches on the year, and four in the last two games. A run game that showed up. For the first time this season, the ground game gave defenses something to think about. Chase Brown ran nine times for 57 yards and added three catches for 18 more, and the Bengals ran for 123 yards at 5.1 yards a carry. One week doesn’t fix a season-long problem, but it’s a start. Evan McPherson’s leg. McPherson drilled a 57-yarder right before halftime to make it 24-10 and added a 43-yarder in the fourth. He has now made 23 straight field goals, the longest streak in franchise history and the longest active streak in the NFL. Taking care of the football. Zero turnovers, one week after four of them. Linebacker Barrett Carter also picked off Michael Penix Jr. in the fourth quarter for his first interception of the season. History, twice. It’s the Bengals’ fourth straight game with 30 or more points, tying a franchise record, and their first win ever outside the U.S. Taylor called the turnout of Bengals fans in Spain “unbelievable.” The Bad The run defense, again. Atlanta ran for 157 yards on just 24 carries, a 6.5-yard average, and Bijan Robinson punched in a 1-yard touchdown in the third quarter. For the second straight week, an opponent ran wherever it wanted. Pittsburgh will have watched the tape. No pass rush. The Bengals finished without a sack, and the box score credits them with zero quarterback hits. Penix was never forced into a rushed decision. Against better quarterbacks, a clean pocket all day gets you beat. Getting off the field on third down. Long third downs have been a problem all season, and this game was no exception. On a third-and-13, Robinson took a screen past a missed tackle and moved the chains. That’s a drive that should’ve ended. The slow defensive start. The offense finally started fast, but the defense gave up a touchdown on Atlanta’s opening drive. It’s the third straight week the Bengals trailed early. The Ugly The back end units of the defense. This one’s tough to watch from the back end of the defense’s perspective. It will be interesting to see if this is a position that the Bengals explore for possible trade depth. DJ Turner II was flagged twice for defensive pass interference covering Drake London, and both penalties set up Falcons touchdowns. He also missed the tackle that let Robinson convert that third-and-13 screen. Turner has had many good moments this year, but Sunday was one to forget. The whole back end, including safeties and linebackers in coverage, struggled to rally and tackle in space. Bijan Robinson, including on that third-and-13 screen, finished with six catches for 47 yards on top of his 100 rushing yards. The safeties and linebackers kept letting Atlanta off the hook on third-and-long, a problem that has followed this defense all season. Jordan Battle had an opportunity at an interception after jumping a route, and let a game-sealing interception through his hands (Barrett Carter later atoned for that mistake). To be fair, the raw passing numbers weren’t bad. Michael Penix Jr. threw for just 162 yards, Kyle Pitts was held to three catches for 23 yards, and Drake London had five for 68. The problem is timing. The flags, missed tackles, and third-down breakdowns came at the worst moments and kept Falcons drives alive. Against the Steelers on Sunday night, those mistakes will cost points. Free yards. An offside penalty turned an Atlanta punt into a field goal, and the defense let a late first-half Falcons drive stretch until just 57 seconds remained. Atlanta helped the Bengals out with 12 penalties for 88 yards of its own, plus a missed field goal. A sharper team won’t be so generous. The bottom line: when the offense scores 30-plus every week, the defense can survive days like this. Come January, it won’t be enough. Your turn What was your Good, Bad, and Ugly from Madrid? Is Burrow the MVP front-runner right now, and how worried are you about the run defense with the Steelers coming to town on Sunday night? Let me hear it in the comments.

full_text: (Photo by Nick Cammett/Diamond Images via Getty Images) | Diamond Images/Getty Images It was a quiet day for the Cleveland Browns as the NFL trade deadline came and went on Tuesday afternoon. Whether or not general manager Andrew Berry tried to bring anyone on board to help keep the team’s playoff hopes alive is unknown. And while there was speculation that the Minnesota Vikings, who were desperately in need of anyone with a pulse to play quarterback, might come calling about the greatest backup quarterback in NFL history, that did not come to pass as the Vikings instead decided to reunite with Kirk Cousins after three years apart. Minnesota is returning to Cousins after cycling through eight different starting quarterbacks since the beginning of the 2024 season. If he starts this week against Green Bay, it will be the 15th time the Vikings have changed the starting quarterback from the previous week since moving on from Cousins. Those numbers highlight something that has been evident for a long time now. While the Browns get more than their share of grief for continually messing up the quarterback position, they are far from being alone in the league in that regard. And speaking of the Browns and quarterbacks, maybe today will be the day that head coach Todd Monken stops playing silly games and lets everyone know who the starting quarterback will be for this week’s game against the Houston Texans. title: Week 10 Browns NFL Power Rankings: Cleveland essentially maintains same spot despite two-game losing streak
summary: It is Week 10 of the 2026 NFL season, and the Cleveland Browns are coming off of their second straight loss to drop to a record of 5-4. Overall, the Browns went down by 0.7 spots from week-to-week to have an overall ranking of 16.7. Cleveland has a four-game home stretch (with a bye mixed […]
full_text: NEW ORLEANS, LA - NOVEMBER 8: Todd Monken of the Cleveland Browns on the sideline during the first half of a game against the New Orleans Saints at Caesars Superdome on November 8, 2026, in New Orleans, Louisiana. (Photo by Derick Hingle/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images) | Icon Sportswire via Getty Images It is Week 10 of the 2026 NFL season, and the Cleveland Browns are coming off of their second straight loss to drop to a record of 5-4. Overall, the Browns went down by 0.7 spots from week-to-week to have an overall ranking of 16.7 . Cleveland has a four-game home stretch (with a bye mixed in), so this part of the schedule is vital for the team to capitalize on. Here is a summary of how the Cleveland Browns are viewed across mainstream media outlets in NFL Power Rankings heading into Week 10 of the 2026 NFL season. CBS Sports – No. 17 (no change) Shedeur Sanders did some good things in the loss to the Saints, but Deshaun Watson has to be their quarterback for the time being. If he falters, then you go to Watson. ESPN – No. 16 (no change) Most important game of the second half: Week 18 at the Bengals The Browns haven’t faced the Bengals this season, but both teams are firmly in the AFC playoff picture. That gives the regular-season finale a good possibility of holding tiebreaker implications for the AFC North, wild-card spots or overall playoff seeding. Cleveland has a 2-1 record in the division, including home wins over the Steelers and Ravens. And despite their recent struggles, the Browns have played the Bengals close over the years. Quarterback Joe Burrow has a 4-6 record against Cleveland. NFL.com – No. 19 (down 4 spots) One can excuse away Cleveland’s second straight loss by pointing to the fact that Shedeur Sanders was required to start in place of Deshaun Watson (concussion). One can blame the Browns for keeping the offensive handcuffs on Sanders until they needed him to push the ball downfield in the final minutes of regulation. Or one can honestly admit this defense isn’t the same without Maliek Collins, struggles to stop the run and hasn’t won 1-on-1 matchups (not including Denzel Ward) for a while. Cleveland is a middling team that could sneak into the playoffs .. but feels more like a 9-8 squad that falls just short. Sporting News – No. 16 (down 1 spot) The Browns’ aggressive nature with first-year coach Todd Monken should be applauded. Even though they didn’t win the overtime game in New Orleans, seeing their passing game click so much with Shedeur Sanders is inspiring. Making the playoffs is less important than finding out whether Sanders can be their franchise QB. Yahoo Sports – No. 18 (down 2 spots) The Browns are going back to Deshaun Watson at quarterback, according to ESPN’s Jeremy Fowler, even after Shedeur Sanders had multiple clutch drives against the Saints and came a 2-point conversion in overtime of leading a big road win over the Saints. Sanders wasn’t perfect, but Watson hasn’t been either. Sanders had a 112.3 passer rating on Sunday. Watson’s passer rating this season is 91.2 and he has taken a league-high 33 sacks. Browns head coach Todd Monken wouldn’t reveal his decision Monday, but apparently the Browns believe in quarterback wins so Watson will take his job back after missing last week (concussion protocol). If the Browns do go back to Watson it will lead to a quarterback controversy every time Watson struggles. Monken praised Sanders after Sunday’s game. “He wasn’t perfect. I wasn’t perfect,” Monken said after the game, via USA Today. “But for a guy that really hasn’t taken snaps with the ones in 10 weeks … to come in there and continue to battle — really, really proud of him.” Bleacher Report – No. 16 (no change) The Cleveland Browns have their first losing streak of 2026. And they may also have a quarterback controversy. Despite clearing the concussion protocol, the Browns sat Deshaun Watson Sunday in favor of second-year pro Shedeur Sanders. Sanders played well, throwing for 297 yards and a pair of scores while adding 28 yards on the ground. After the loss, head coach Todd Monken praised Sanders’ performance—but wouldn’t give an indication while addressing the media who will start under center in Cleveland moving forward. “How long has it been? 30 minutes since the game ended? I’m not getting into quarterback,” he said. “If we want to talk about Shedeur, we can talk about Shedeur.” Per ESPN’s Jeremy Fowler, it will be Watson out there Sunday when the Browns host the Houston Texans. But if he falters and the Browns appear headed toward a third straight loss, fans are going to start clamoring for Sanders. USA Today – No. 15 (up 1 spot) While the Bengals and Steelers prepare to beat one another up, the Browns, regardless of who their QB1 is, need to take advantage of their upcoming stretch of games − none that will require them to leave Cleveland before Dec. 20.
