full_text: Cleveland Browns quarterback Shedeur Sanders and Browns running back Raheim Sanders take a water break, July, 31, 2026, in Berea. | USA TODAY Network via Reuters Co No one outside the walls of the Cleveland Browns complex in Berea, Ohio, seems to know what the team’s plan is at quarterback for Week 10. Okay, that might be slight hyperbole, as some Browns folks might have shared with their family and friends, but besides that, no one knows. On Monday, ESPN’s Jeremy Fowler reported that QB Deshaun Watson would be returning to the starting quarterback spot, but Cleveland HC Todd Monken refuted that, noting how proud he was of QB Shedeur Sanders in his Week 9 start against the New Orleans Saints . Fans and media have read that as Monken leaning toward naming Sanders the starter. Others noted that the Browns head coach stated that they watched the film and then had a meeting with “personnel,” which most assume is GM Andrew Berry and the front office. With the NFL trade deadline on Tuesday at 4 PM, could that mean Cleveland’s starting quarterback decision could be in the air because of a potential trade? The Browns do have four quarterbacks on their active roster, three of which have tradable contracts (Watson’s is as close to untradable as possible in the NFL), so the team could be open for business at the position. Whether or not Sanders, Dillon Gabriel , or Taylen Green have much trade value is up for discussion. On Monday Night Football, it became clear to everyone that the Minnesota Vikings, now owning a 6-2 record, have a serious quarterback issue, leading many, including Josina Anderson, to suggest trading with Cleveland for Sanders could be part of the solution: Anyways, #Vikings will be on the ☎️ at sunrise tomorrow. If you ask me, they should be on the phone with #Browns GM Andrew Berry. Raiders and 49ers should not give up their options at QB analyzing their depth at the position. Makes no sense for Jets to decline the trades they… — JosinaAnderson (@JosinaAnderson) November 10, 2026 With his big name, Sanders will often be one of the first quarterbacks discussed in these situations. The Browns seem uncertain about the second-year quarterback’s future with the team, so fans and media are likely to speculate about the popular Sanders being traded. In the end, a young quarterback learning a brand new system for a team with Super Bowl aspirations does not seem to be the likely outcome. If the Vikings want to add a quarterback, a veteran with experience in multiple systems is more likely. For now, with eight or so hours left until the NFL trade deadline, a lot of speculation and suggestions will occur, including the idea of the Browns trading Shedeur Sanders. full_text: The Cleveland Browns suffered another loss this season, falling 23-22 to the New Orleans Saints in a tough overtime battle. This came after another tough loss, a 27-6 defeat by the Pittsburgh Steelers . While both games were setbacks in a season that was starting to look promising, which of the two losses was more disappointing for the Browns? One of the major differences between the two matchups was that Deshaun Watson started against the Steelers and Shedeur Sanders stepped in against the Saints. Neither quarterback performed at a high level, but Sanders was able to create more offense in the New Orleans game. In some ways, the loss to Pittsburgh was more disappointing because it was a divisional matchup in which the Browns were completely outplayed. Expectations were lower for the game against the Saints since the team did not have their starting quarterback. At the same time, losing in overtime is especially disappointing when the Browns had several opportunities to secure the win. Sanders showed flashes of strong offensive play, making it disappointing that the Browns couldn’t capitalize on those opportunities against a lesser opponent. title: Browns punter Corey Bojorquez is quietly having a Pro Bowl year
summary: The Cleveland Browns are having a roller coaster of a season. They have beaten only one good team, the Pittsburgh Steelers in Week 4, defeated four other clubs considered mediocre, and lost to two bad teams. And now they are faced with some difficult games on their schedule, namely playing their division foe, the Cincinnati […]
full_text: The Cleveland Browns are having a roller coaster of a season. They have beaten only one good team , the Pittsburgh Steelers in Week 4, defeated four other clubs considered mediocre, and lost to two bad teams . And now they are faced with some difficult games on their schedule, namely playing their division foe, the Cincinnati Bengals, twice. RELATED: BOJORQUEZ INTERVIEW Consider the fact that there aren’t any really good teams left on their schedule. Could they still make the playoffs? A division title seems out of reach, but it takes 10 or 11 wins to get that #7 seed, and they are already halfway to that goal. There are several players on the Browns roster who are having a good year. Guys like TE Harold Fannin, LBs Carson Schwesinger and Quincy Williams, plus DT Mason Graham are getting their fair share of press regarding possibly getting some major Pro Bowl votes. But one player stands out, and nobody is talking about his season: Browns punter Corey Bojorquez. The Boot is back 🥾 We've re-signed P Corey Bojorquez! 📰 Read more: https://t.co/wQ4NPLBAHA pic.twitter.com/r7RsK8WdCa — Cleveland Browns (@Browns) March 12, 2026 Guys who make their living on special teams are usually only noticed when they miss a field goal, or both a punt, or skip a pass to the holder. Bojo has quietly been killing it as Cleveland’s punter this season. He was re-signed during last March’s free agency period. Currently, he is listed #5 in the league in net average per punt with 44.0 yards. The league leader is just 46.1, so Bojorquez is keeping the rankings tight. He is ranked #4 in average distance per kick at 50.4. Again, the leader’s number is close at 51.8, so one game could alter these numbers. Usually, the punters with the most kicks in a season are on teams whose offensive units can’t finish drives, or are unable to sustain drives. Bojo is ranked #3 in the most punts with 43. The league leader plays for the Philadelphia Eagles, which backs up this stat goes to guys who are on struggling offensive teams. He booted a season-high eight punts in the loss to the New York Jets when the offense could not move the ball. Bojo is considered a field flipper . This means his kicks can alter the opposing team’s field position just off one punt that has traveled 50+ yards. Case in point, in Week 3 against the Carolina Panthers, Bojorquez’s first punt was for 68 yards. Pretty good, eh? His first punt of the second half was 60 yards. Then his final kick was for a whopping 81 yards that went from Cleveland’s 19-yard line into the end zone. The NFL record for the longest punt is Steve O’Neal’s 98-yarder in 1969 while playing for the New York Jets: Take a look at Bojorquez’s 2026 season stats: Week 1 Punts: 3 Yards: 130 Yards per punt average: 43.3 Net yards per punt average: 45.0 Downed inside the 20: 1 Blocked: 0 Long: 48 yards Week 2 Punts: 4 Yards: 198 Yards per punt average: 49.5 Net yards per punt average: 45.0 Downed inside the 20: 2 Blocked: 0 Long: 57 yards Week 3 Punts: 5 Yards: 243 Yards per punt average: 48.6 Net yards per punt average: 45.8 Downed inside the 20: 3 Blocked: 0 Long: 62 yards Week 4 Punts: 4 Yards: 251 Yards per punt average: 62.8 Net yards per punt average: 50.3 Downed inside the 20: 1 Blocked: 0 Long: 81 yards Week 5 Punts: 8 Yards: 421 Yards per punt average: 52.6 Net yards per punt average: 41.8 Downed inside the 20: 1 Blocked: 0 Long: 67 yards Week 6 Punts: 7 Yards: 315 Yards per punt average: 48.0 Net yards per punt average: 36.7 Downed inside the 20: 1 Blocked: 0 Long: 62 yards Week 7 Punts: 3 Yards: 144 Yards per punt average: 48.0 Net yards per punt average: 45.0 Downed inside the 20: 1 Blocked: 0 Long: 59 yards Week 8 Punts: 4 Yards: 199 Yards per punt average: 49.8 Net yards per punt average: 49.8 Downed inside the 20: 3 Blocked: 0 Long: 58 yards Week 9 Punts: 5 Yards: 267 Yards per punt average: 53.4 Net yards per punt average: 39.8 Downed inside the 20: 1 Blocked: 0 Long: 59 yards When a running back breaks a play for 15 yards, those numbers are added to his game rushing stats. But with a punter, he could boot one for 56 yards, and then have it returned for 25 yards, which affects his net average; in this case, that stat would be 31.0 yards. Whereas a fair catch or a touchback gives the punter the exact distance of the kick. So, something the punter has zero control over can affect his overall stats. What is not considered is what kind of 56-yarder this is. Let’s say that this punt has a hangtime of 3.91 seconds and comes down in the center of the field. Even factoring in a long operation time, can one of the gunners get to the spot where the ball finally descends? Even if the gunner had nobody blocking him, there wouldn’t be a chance of this happening because that gunner would need to travel nearly 60 yards in just over 6 seconds. The punt is going to be returned. Another obstacle on a punt is if the returner doesn’t catch the ball and lets it hit the turf. We all know that because of the shape of a football, it can go almost anywhere. Including backwards. This could take off as much as 10 yards on a punt before it is downed. Yet another obstacle to getting larger numbers for punters is the pooch kick. This usually happens when the offense stalls out within 10 yards of the midfield stripe. A long field goal attempt is considered, but the coach decides it is out of the question. And the coach doesn’t want to go for it, whether that is because of field position or an unreasonable down-and-distance. So, the punter trots out. Now, there isn’t much advantage to boom the kick for a touchback, so the kicker wants the ball to land inside the 10-yard line, preferably. And if he accomplishes this, the kick itself may have been downed at the three-yard line, but the punt only traveled less than 40 yards. That is a huge plus for flipping field position for the team, but it hurts the punter’s average. The only positive stat is the “inside the 20” tabulation. But that is pretty vague in itself. There should be another stat that says “inside the 5” to distinguish punters who have the ability to make the ball travel higher so that it descends closer to the goal line. For the past eight games, Bojorquez has had at least one kick of 58 yards or longer. He routinely has contests where he has multiple punts in the 50+ range. That becomes a weapon. His talents were on full display in the loss to the New Orleans Saints . The Browns had to punt after their first possession. Bojo punted from Cleveland’s 26-yard line and was downed at the Saints’ 26. Their next possession was also a punt that went from the Browns’ 40-yard line to New Orleans’ 14-yard line. That’s flipping the field. ball back baby!!!!! #CLEvsNO on CBS pic.twitter.com/JJcPTOYU9p — Cleveland Browns (@Browns) November 8, 2026 Bojo’s only punt in Quarter 2 went to the 20-yard line, where Saints returner Barion Brown fumbled, and Cleveland safety Donovan McMillan recovered. But the kick had traveled 57 yards first. His fourth punt also went 57 yards, while his final punt in the fourth quarter traveled 59 yards from Cleveland’s 16-yard line to the Saints’ 25. This is Bojorquez’s ninth year in the league. In 202, he led the league in yards per punt average with 50.8 while with the Buffalo Bills, kicking about a third of his punts in freezing weather. In 2024, he led the league in number of punts (89) and total yardage (4,387). Last year, Bojo led the league in the same two categories, kicking 91 total punts and gaining 4,165 yards. In three different years, he had the longest recorded punt: 2020 – 72 yards, 2021 – 82 yards, and 2024 – 84 yards. He is also leading this year with that 81-yarder in the Steelers game. Three of these punts are listed in the “Top-30 NFL Punts of All Time.” And yet, with all these accolades and league-leading accomplishments, Bojorquez has never made a single Pro Bowl. This year seems promising.

title: Cleveland Browns news: It’s the most insufferable time of the year
summary: The Cleveland Browns have entered the annual part of the calendar that everyone was hoping to avoid. Welcome to Quarterback Controversy Season! The Browns had barely left the field on Sunday following a loss to the two-win New Orleans Saints before head coach Todd Monken was asked who the starting quarterback will be for this […]
full_text: (Photo by Nick Cammett/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Cleveland Browns have entered the annual part of the calendar that everyone was hoping to avoid. Welcome to Quarterback Controversy Season! The Browns had barely left the field on Sunday following a loss to the two-win New Orleans Saints before head coach Todd Monken was asked who the starting quarterback will be for this week’s game against the Houston Texans. Monken rightly pointed out that, you know, the game had just ended, so maybe it wasn’t the right time to discuss such things. On Monday, presumably having had time to sleep on the matter, Monken had the opportunity to put the nonsense to bed before it started, but instead decided to start digging his own grave and state that he has still not made a decision. Let’s assume Monken and the coaching staff are not planning to pull the surprise of the season and start either Dillon Gabriel or Taylen Green against the Texans. So that leaves Monken with two options: The quarterback he handpicked to start the season and, through some form of voodoo, played a role in helping the Browns to a 5-3 record and a spot to play meaningful games in the final two months of the season. The backup quarterback, who was just 5-of-8 for 38 yards at halftime against the two-win Saints, but rallied the troops in the second half thanks to impressive YAC totals from the receivers in a one-point loss. At this point it may not matter much as the defense is worn down after being overrun the past three weeks to the tune of 501 rushing yards. And for all the “explosive plays” on Sunday, the offense needed almost five full quarters of football to score 22 points on a New Orleans defense that was allowing 28 points a game. All Monken needs to do is pick someone- it doesn’t matter who- and stick with them the rest of the season. It’s simply too exhausting to go through all this stupidity again. full_text: Photo by Sam Hodde/Getty Images | Getty Images After a career game against the Indianapolis Colts, backup running back Tyler Goodson is expected to miss some time with a knee sprain. Instead of signing someone from their practice squad to the active roster, the Dallas Cowboys looked outside their building for some help. The trade deadline also came and went without the Cowboys making a move. Let’s check in on today’s headlines. Dallas Cowboys signing former TCU leading rusher for needed running back depth – Nick Harris, Fort Worth Star-Telegram Kendre Miller has been circled by Cowboys fans since coming out of the draft a few years ago. Miller was cut on Saturday by the New Orleans Saints in his fourth season since being drafted by the franchise in the third round of the 2023 draft. He reunites with Cowboys running backs coach Derrick Foster who coached him in New Orleans in 2024. In his three-year TCU career, Miller rushed for 2,410 yards and 26 touchdowns while also grabbing 29 receptions for 229 yards and one touchdown. In 2022, he led the Horned Frogs with 1,399 rushing yards, and his 7.5 yards per carry as a sophomore in 2021 led the nation. His career rushing total is 14th in program history and the fourth-most for a running back that played just three seasons in Fort Worth. Transactions: Reddy Steward released from PS – Staff Writers, DallasCowboys.com To make room for Kendre Miller, Dallas released a former starter from their practice squad. On Tuesday, the Cowboys released DB Reddy Steward from the practice squad. Steward played in three games for the Cowboys this season, starting in two, after being elevated from the practice squad for Dallas’ games against the Baltimore, Houston and Tampa Bay. He tallied 11 total tackles in those three games this season. Steward initially joined the Cowboys in August of 2025, and last season played in all 17 games, starting five. Cowboys let NFL trade deadline pass quietly. What could lack of moves mean for Dallas’ roster? – Joseph Hoyt, Dallas Morning News The Cowboys stayed quiet during a crazy trade deadline. The Cowboys didn’t make any trades before Tuesday’s deadline passed. Instead of seeking external improvement, they opted to see what this year’s team could do in its remaining 10 games and where it could improve on its own. “I’m very comfortable in our team,” Cowboys head coach Brian Schottenheimer said Monday when asked about potentially making a trade. While Davis is a very good player who was a key part of a championship defense, he comes with some issues. title: Cowboys defense played their best game of the year against the Colts
summary: The Dallas Cowboys defense nearly collapsed again this week, but tightened up late, sealing the win in their best game of the season against the Indianapolis Colts. Team stats allowed The Cowboys allowed 23 points to the Colts. They forced a punt on six-of-seven drives to start the game, with the lone score resulting from […]
full_text: Photo by Michael Hickey/Getty Images The Dallas Cowboys defense nearly collapsed again this week, but tightened up late, sealing the win in their best game of the season against the Indianapolis Colts. Team stats allowed The Cowboys allowed 23 points to the Colts. They forced a punt on six-of-seven drives to start the game, with the lone score resulting from a Dak Prescott fumble deep in Cowboys territory. Dallas gave up just two touchdowns on the day, while also giving up three field goals. The Colts went 3/13 on third down conversions. Dallas held Indianapolis to 105 rushing yards and 166 passing yards, 55 of which came on a single screen pass. The Cowboys finished with two sacks and two turnovers, including the game sealing interception from Caleb Downs. Individual stat leaders on defense Quinnen Williams continues his strong season, finishing the day with seven tackles, three tackles-for-loss and a key forced fumble. Rashan Gary and Caleb Downs both added a full sack to their season totals. Quinnen Williams remains the team’s sack leader on the season with five. Caleb Downs sealed the game with the lone interception on the day, the first in the standout rookie’s career. Advanced analytics SumerSports recorded the Cowboys defense finishing with a -0.26 EPA/play allowed. This is by far their best EPA allowed on the season. The defense held up well against explosive plays on the day, limiting the Colts to just two. But as we’ve seen before, those explosives can open the game up for the Cowboys opponents. Dallas has a tough time rebounding after giving up a big play, which we saw at times again this week. The Cowboys dominated the time of possession, 35:43 to 24:17, and total plays, 71-59. They kept the Colts offense sidelined while giving their own offense a chance to get themselves figured out. Final grade: B The Cowboys defense played well enough to earn their highest grade of the season this week. They came in against a weak offense and didn’t allow them to steal the game, which we’ve seen multiple times this year. It was one of Dallas’ cleaner games on defense this season, driven by interior disruption from their star defensive tackle Williams, while also making timely plays. But not everything was perfect. They once again allowed a bad offense to make a huge game-changing play late in the game. As we watched the second half, we were reminded of the atrocious ending to the Cardinals game. The defense nearly gave it all away until the late interception from Caleb Downs coming after the offense regained the lead. Still, the performance by the defense was enough to put the ball back into the hands of the Cowboys offense consistently throughout the day. The game should never have come down to the final moments if the offense was able to convert their highest yardage total of the season into corresponding points. The defense did their part for most of the day while the offense struggled to find their way. For the fifth time in nine weeks, the defense allowed just 24 points or less in a game. If you surveyed Cowboys fans before the season began, most would tell you Dallas would have won all five of those games. Unfortunately, only three of those performances have ended with a victory. Next week will be a good litmus test for the Cowboys defense. Most, including myself, expect a lopsided matchup favoring the 49ers. But if this defense can hold the 49ers to under 24 points, as they’ve done more often than not to their opponents this season, we should feel good about their progress under Christian Parker, regardless of the game’s final result.

title: 2026 NFL Week 10 Power Rankings: A win bumps Dallas up
summary: The Dallas Cowboys are one of last week’s 15 winners from across the NFL and so you would assume that all is sunshine and rainbows around here. That isn’t exactly the case. Aside from the fact that some cooler weather and cloud cover are over much of the country, the mood around America’s Team is […]
full_text: Mandatory Credit: Robert Goddin-Imagn Images | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect The Dallas Cowboys are one of last week’s 15 winners from across the NFL and so you would assume that all is sunshine and rainbows around here. That isn’t exactly the case. Aside from the fact that some cooler weather and cloud cover are over much of the country, the mood around America’s Team is a bit grim. That’s what happens when you barely beat a bad team. Where would you say the Cowboys rank against the rest of the NFL right now? Where should they rank? And how do other people feel that they rank? Let’s answer all of those questions with this week’s power rankings. 1. Buffalo Bills (LW: 1) Monday night was not the prettiest game, but they got it done. 2. San Francisco 49ers (LW: 2) They are a monster sent to destroy everyone, but most specifically the Dallas Cowboys. 3. Jacksonville Jaguars (LW: 5) This team has the feel of the new-age group. They get things in a way others don’t want to. Good for them. 4. Green Bay Packers (LW: 10) The Cowboys getting destroyed by them doesn’t feel any better, but wow this looks like a juggernaut. 5. Detroit Lions (LW: 3) Just a really good and well-coached football team. 6. Chicago Bears (LW: 4) You win however you have to. 7. Cincinnati Bengals (LW: 7) It has felt like they have gotten less love than the other contenders this season. They are very much for real. 8. Denver Broncos (LW: 8) Another team that always finds a way. 9. New England Patriots (LW: 6) Sunday was rough. But they will be back. 10. Seattle Seahawks (LW: 9) It is starting to feel like the wheels are falling off a little bit here. 11. Pittsburgh Steelers (LW: 12) The whole world will get to see Mike McCarthy on Sunday night against the Bengals. How will he handle it? 12. Los Angeles Rams (LW: 13) As noted a win is a win, but things still feel harder here than they seem like they should. 13. Minnesota Vikings (LW: 11) The defense is remarkable, but until they get a proper quarterback they aren’t going anywhere. 14. Kansas City Chiefs (LW: 15) Does anybody really fear them anymore? I don’t mean that dismissively. They are very good. They are just different good than the past. 15. New York Giants (LW: 16) I do not see how they finish shy of 10 wins. 16. Houston Texans (LW: 23) Good for C.J. Stroud. He really needed this season. 17. Tampa Bay Buccaneers (LW: 19) I think that I think they are the best team in the NFC South. 18. Atlanta Falcons (LW: 14) It was fun for a little while. 19. Dallas Cowboys (LW: 24) Again… a win is a win. But this was about as ugly of a win as anyone could have possibly had. 20. Cleveland Browns (LW: 17) Back to earth. 21. Baltimore Ravens (LW: 18) It always sucks when you feel like you are enduring a lost season. 22. Las Vegas Raiders (LW: 20) Everything just feels so blah here. We want to see Fernando Mendoza. Spice it up. 23. Carolina Panthers (LW: 22) Another team that was fun for a while and has relaxed. 24. New Orleans Saints (LW: 26) Good for Kellen Moore! 25. Washington Commanders (LW: 25) If they lose on Thursday night… is that it for Dan Quinn? 26. Arizona Cardinals (LW: 21) You mean they didn’t light it up in the fourth quarter? Why not? 27. Miami Dolphins (LW: 30) Next year. Maybe. 28. Philadelphia Eagles (LW: 27) Yikes. 29. Indianapolis Colts (LW: 28) Thanks for the good times or whatever. 30. New York Jets (LW: 29) How are they always so bad? 31. Tennessee Titans (LW: 31) Welcome back. 32. Los Angeles Chargers (LW: 32) 0-8 is incredible stuff. ESPN : 20 (LW: 23) Here we go. Most important game of the second half: Week 17 vs. the Giants Quarterback Dak Prescott said every game the rest of the way is a “must-win” for the Cowboys, and he might not be wrong considering their record. But let’s say the Cowboys manage to string together some wins and find themselves in the NFC East chase since the path to a wild-card bid is just too packed. That puts the Week 17 rematch with the Giants in the crosshairs as a potential winner-take-all meeting. From 2011 to 2013, the Cowboys faced a de facto NFC East title game in each regular-season finale and lost them all. They would love to have that kind of opportunity this season. — Todd Archer NFL.com : 22 (LW: 24) A little bump up. The Cowboys won a game against an opponent in the Colts whom most have written off because their own front office is already looking toward the future. This victory won’t carry much weight in the larger picture, but hey, at least the offense broke 500 yards and the defense recorded a win-sealing takeaway. USA Today : 21 (LW: 25) And another. They outgained the Colts by 237 yards in what was easily their best defensive performance of the season − yes, that’s a very low bar − and still barely beat a team taking its roster down to the studs. Yahoo : 20 (LW: 25) A bit of a leap. With 1:37 left in Sunday’s game, the Cowboys fell behind a Colts team that had previously traded two of its best players and was embarrassed 42-7 by the Jaguars the week before. The Cowboys won, with a huge 46-yard completion to Ryan Flournoy leading to a game-winning touchdown, but it was still a performance that showed the Cowboys are not capable of being much better than they’ve been this season. Had they lost, there would have been serious questions about whether players like George Pickens should be traded from a 3-6 team. Instead, the Cowboys stayed alive in the NFC East. If there was a positive that gives hope for a better second half, Dallas’ defense played its best game of the season. It came against an Indianapolis offense that has been miserable, but Dallas will take progress where it can get it. The Cowboys allowed a season-low 271 yards. The Colts had 70 net yards and seven points (on a 19-yard drive after a turnover) through their first eight drives. Rookie safety Caleb Downs had a long-awaited impact with a sack and a game-sealing interception. The Cowboys’ defense isn’t suddenly good, but at least there can be optimism it’s getting better. CBS Sports : 18 (LW: 22) The highest ranking so far. Will anyone go higher? They made it interesting against a bad Colts team, which isn’t a good sign. But they found a way. Now comes a tough test against the 49ers. The Athletic : 17 (LW: 22) Yes! Someone will! Midseason grade: C With another monster game Sunday (10 receptions for 195 yards and a touchdown), CeeDee Lamb became the first player in NFL history to record at least 70 catches and at least 900 yards in each of his first seven seasons. But the only team with a worse defense based on EPA per play is the lowly Dolphins, which is why the Cowboys are still under .500. ProFootballTalk : 25 (LW: 26) That’s that. Even the games against the bad teams are a struggle. Week To Week Movement Full Power Rankings

title: Cowboys working out free agent RB as possible Tyler Goodson replacement
summary: Just when it looked as if Tyler Goodson was on his way to earning a bigger offensive role after rushing for 77 yards on 12 carries last week against the Indianapolis Colts, he picked up a knee injury that is expected to cause him to miss multiple weeks. He could end up on IR, and […]
full_text: Photo by Derick E. Hingle/Getty Images | Getty Images Just when it looked as if Tyler Goodson was on his way to earning a bigger offensive role after rushing for 77 yards on 12 carries last week against the Indianapolis Colts, he picked up a knee injury that is expected to cause him to miss multiple weeks. He could end up on IR, and the Cowboys only have one more designated to return spot. With Goodson sidelined for an unknown time, the Cowboys need to find a new backup running back to help spell/complement Javonte Williams for the next several games. Jerry Jones indicated they would bring in a free agent. We now have a name as a possibility. Per sources, the Cowboys have RB Kendre Miller coming in for a visit today as they look for help after Tyler Goodson (knee) was hurt vs. the Colts. He was released last week by the Saints. Jerry Jones said on @1053thefan the Cowboys will add a RB, most likely a free agent.… — Todd Archer (@toddarcher) November 10, 2026 Kendre Miller was released by the New Orleans Saints earlier this week. Miller, a former third-round pick (71 st overall) by the Saints in 2023, is a Texas native from Mount Enterprise. He was one of the best backs in the nation in 2022 TCU where he rushed for 1,399 yards and 17 touchdowns. Unfortunately, he’s been plagued by injuries since entering the league and it not only stunted his growth, but ultimately led to his release. Despite that, there’s still a lot to like about the former Horned Toad. As a potential Goodson replacement, Kendre Miller checks a lot of the boxes. Talent-wise he possesses a lot of skill. At 5’11” and around 220 pounds, give or take, he meets the prototypical size of a starting RB and he has some surprising juice/wiggle that would help complement Williams’ hard-nosed running style. Miller would also be an asset in the receiving game. He’s a natural hands catcher and has proven to be a weapon out of the backfield when given the opportunity. He still has work to do as a pass protector, but with the Cowboys that wouldn’t be as much of a concern because that’s something Williams usually handles. What makes Miller an even more of an attractive option as Goodson’s replacement is his special teams value. Goodson took over for KaVontae Turpin when he was sidelined with a rib injury as Dallas’ kick returner and has been just as good if not better. Miller has the experience/ability to fill those shoes as well in the return game. All in all, there’s a lot to like about Miller. If he can finally overcome his unfortunate injury history he has the makings to become a serviceable running back in the league. Add in his special teams value and he’s a solid replacement for Goodson as their new RB2.
author: Brian Martin

title: Despite win, complementary football continues to evade the Cowboys
summary: The Dallas Cowboys finally got back into the win column Sunday, but nobody should mistake a 27-23 victory over the Indianapolis Colts for a complete performance. Dallas dominated the statistical categories that usually determine the outcome of a football game, outgaining Indianapolis by more than 200 yards, controlling the clock and producing over 500 yards […]
full_text: Photo by Andy Lyons/Getty Images | Getty Images The Dallas Cowboys finally got back into the win column Sunday, but nobody should mistake a 27-23 victory over the Indianapolis Colts for a complete performance. Dallas dominated the statistical categories that usually determine the outcome of a football game, outgaining Indianapolis by more than 200 yards, controlling the clock and producing over 500 yards of offense. Yet somehow, the Cowboys needed a touchdown with just over a minute remaining to escape with a victory. That is the frustrating reality of this team. Dallas has shown it can move the football and generate enough defensive stops to compete. What it still cannot do consistently is put all the phases together. The offense wastes opportunities, the defense gives up momentum-changing plays, and the entire team continues to shoot itself in the foot with undisciplined mistakes. The Cowboys won Sunday, and at 4-5, they will gladly take it. But against a Colts team that had lost four straight games, this should never have been as close as it was. Dominating the stat sheet means nothing if you cannot finish drives Dallas finished the afternoon with 508 total yards of offense. The Cowboys also held a commanding advantage in time of possession, keeping the ball for 35 minutes. Dak Prescott threw for 335 yards and two touchdowns, completing 21 of 34 passes without an interception. CeeDee Lamb was spectacular, catching 10 passes for 195 yards and a touchdown. Javonte Williams added 101 rushing yards and a score, while former Colts running back Tyler Goodson contributed another 77 yards on the ground, a career high. On paper, that is a dominant offensive performance. The Cowboys averaged 6.4 yards per play and moved the football at will for long stretches. Yet, somehow, after all those yards and all that success moving the ball, Dallas found itself losing with 1:38 left. Dallas converted just 5 of 16 third-down opportunities, a 31.3% conversion rate. The offense also committed two turnovers, including a wacky Lamb fourth-quarter fumble that wiped out a huge play and a Colts error that could have sealed the victory earlier in the game. The fumble was weird. It felt like the same kind of voodoo magic that rears its ugly head just as the Cowboys have a chance to win. Part of the malaise of the losing culture that this team is stewing in. The Cowboys also had to settle for field goals on multiple occasions, including another missed 50-yard attempt by Brandon Aubrey in the fourth quarter. Aubrey’s miss came after a bad snap, but it still wasted another possession in a game Dallas should have been controlling. This play and the result of it explain the emotional rise and fall of being a Dallas Cowboys fan pic.twitter.com/YJdOmdb2nG — RJ Ochoa (@rjochoa) November 8, 2026 The defense continues to surrender momentum-changing plays Christian Parker’s defense deserves credit for holding Jonathan Taylor to just 46 rushing yards on 13 carries, forcing two turnovers and ultimately delivering the interception that sealed the victory. Quinnen Williams also made a huge impact, forcing a Taylor fumble in the fourth quarter that gave Prescott and the offense another opportunity. But the defense still struggled when the game entered its most important moments. After Dallas built a 20-10 lead in the third quarter, Indianapolis found a way back in with a 55-yard touchdown reception by Ashton Dulin. Cowboys fans had just seen this a week ago with Tyler Allgeier, then had to watch Dulin do it again. Dulin found space and never looked back after more questionable tackling reared its ugly head again in this game. That kind of breakdown has plagued this defense throughout the season. Dallas can generate pressure, make tackles and occasionally force turnovers, but one missed assignment or poor angle seems to undo this defense any time the game gets close. The fourth quarter brought even more problems. DaRon Bland was flagged for a 40-yard pass interference penalty after a deep throw from Daniel Jones, and Dee Winters followed it with a 15-yard unnecessary roughness penalty. Those two flags gave Indianapolis an enormous field-position advantage and helped keep the Colts’ comeback alive. The Cowboys surrendered 16 points in the second half, including two long field goals from Spencer Shrader that gave Indianapolis its first lead of the afternoon. They finished with a positive note, of course. Rookie safety Caleb Downs made the biggest defensive play of the game, intercepting Jones’ desperation throw with 35 seconds remaining to preserve the victory. One clutch play doesn’t erase the problems that came before it. Dallas still has to become more consistent defensively. Yes, there were some bright spots, even against a bad team, but this defense still hasn’t put together a complete game and regularly falls apart when the going gets tough. The penalties are becoming a weekly embarrassment Brian Schottenheimer has been the Dallas Cowboys head coach for 26 games. The team has had double-digit penalties in 8 of them. They are 5-2-1 in those games, though. (via @Stathead , @pfref ) pic.twitter.com/CPO6TSNe1k — RJ Ochoa (@rjochoa) November 9, 2026 If one statistic perfectly captures the Cowboys’ inability to play complementary football, it is the penalty total. Dallas was flagged 14 times for 153 yards against Indianapolis. One hundred and fifty-three yards! That is an absurd amount of free yardage to give an opponent, even in a game Dallas largely controlled. Penalties repeatedly put the offense behind the chains and gave Indianapolis extra chances. Lamb had an 18-yard reception wiped out by offensive pass interference, while multiple flags on the same drive forced Dallas to overcome unnecessary obstacles just to move the ball. The defense was equally guilty. Bland’s 40-yard pass-interference penalty and Winters’ unnecessary roughness call gave Indianapolis a chance to capitalize on mistakes instead of earning every yard. We’ve seen this before, though, haven’t we? Dallas has struggled with discipline throughout the season, and the coaching staff has repeatedly talked about correcting those mistakes. Yet here we are, watching the Cowboys commit another double-digit penalty performance. Dallas finally finished, but not because it seized the victory There is something to be said for the way the Cowboys responded after Indianapolis took a 23-20 lead with 1:38 remaining. Prescott didn’t panic, and the offense finally produced the kind of clutch drive that has been missing in several of Dallas’ losses this season. Prescott connected with Ryan Flournoy for a 46-yard gain, putting the Cowboys in scoring position. A pass-interference penalty moved Dallas to the 1-yard line, and Williams finished the drive with a touchdown run to put Dallas back in front. . @RyanNumba9 makes a big play 👏 📺: #DALvsIND on FOX 📲: Stream on NFL+ https://t.co/XM2vIx7C1d pic.twitter.com/ITQ6dK3HQ2 — Dallas Cowboys (@dallascowboys) November 8, 2026 Then Downs sealed the game with his first career interception, stopping Indianapolis’ final attempt to respond. That is complementary football in its simplest form: the offense scores when it needs to, and the defense makes the play necessary to preserve the lead. Dallas waited until the final minute to put those pieces together. The Cowboys should be encouraged by how their stars played individually. There were legitimate positives, and the team deserves a sliver of credit for finding a way to win a game that could easily have slipped away. Alas, the larger concerns remain. Dallas still struggles to finish drives, still commits far too many penalties and still allows opposing offenses to hang around when it has opportunities to put games away. Schottenheimer and his staff have to find a way to make these performances more consistent. The Cowboys cannot expect Prescott to throw for 335 yards and Lamb to approach 200 receiving yards every week just to survive against…

title: Dak Prescott’s deep shot to Ryan Flournoy rescues Dallas
summary: Another fourth-quarter lead had disappeared. Another disappointing finish was staring Dallas in the face. Then Dak Prescott and Ryan Flournoy changed the game with one throw. Trailing Indianapolis 23-20 with 1:37 remaining, the Cowboys opened their final touchdown drive by attacking downfield. Prescott connected with Flournoy for a 46-yard gain, immediately putting Dallas in position […]
full_text: Photo by Michael Hickey/Getty Images | Getty Images Another fourth-quarter lead had disappeared. Another disappointing finish was staring Dallas in the face. Then Dak Prescott and Ryan Flournoy changed the game with one throw. Trailing Indianapolis 23-20 with 1:37 remaining, the Cowboys opened their final touchdown drive by attacking downfield. Prescott connected with Flournoy for a 46-yard gain, immediately putting Dallas in position to chase the winning touchdown. It was the decisive swing in a much-needed 27-23 victory. Reaching that point was unnecessarily painful. At halftime, Dallas led 17-7 and later held a commanding 20-10 advantage. However, turnovers and penalties kept Indianapolis alive. Despite moving the ball far more effectively than the Colts, Dallas’s 14 penalties for 153 yards and two fumbles prevented them from converting their advantage into a win. Quinnen Williams made a crucial defensive intervention in Dallas territory, forcing Jonathan Taylor to fumble, which Shemar James recovered. However, the offense couldn’t cash in. Indianapolis eventually tied the game, and Brandon Aubrey missed a potential important field goal. Spencer Shrader then kicked a 50-yard field goal with less than two minutes remaining, putting the Colts ahead. Dallas needed an immediate response, and Prescott trusted Flournoy to deliver it. This was no uncontested catch against a defender who had been left behind. Sauce Gardner stayed alongside Flournoy downfield, but failed to turn his head toward the football. Instead, he tried to disrupt the catch through the receiver’s hands and actually grabbed one arm. Flournoy maintained his concentration and secured the pass with the other hand against his body, producing the biggest reception of the afternoon when Dallas needed it most. The importance of that completion went beyond the yardage. Dallas had started the possession needing to move quickly just to give itself a chance. One snap later, the offense could realistically pursue a touchdown and force Indianapolis to answer. The pressure had shifted straight back onto the Colts. Dallas finished the job with help from Indianapolis penalties, and Javonte Williams scored from one yard out with 1:08 remaining. The Cowboys had turned a three-point deficit into a four-point lead in just 29 seconds. There is still plenty to fix. Winning does not erase the mistakes that made this game so difficult. But when Dallas needed a play to prevent another late disappointment, its quarterback and receiver delivered, and the catch was the late-game turning point that helped seal the victory.

title: Ugly wins cannot save these underperforming Cowboys
summary: The Dallas Cowboys found a way to win a football game on Sunday, but the mood across Cowboys Nation remained surprisingly somber. Losing this matchup would have been absolutely devastating, for all intents and purposes ending their season. Falling four games behind the New York Giants in the loss column is a hole simply too […]
full_text: Photo by Michael Hickey/Getty Images The Dallas Cowboys found a way to win a football game on Sunday, but the mood across Cowboys Nation remained surprisingly somber. Losing this matchup would have been absolutely devastating, for all intents and purposes ending their season. Falling four games behind the New York Giants in the loss column is a hole simply too deep to climb out of, especially with a brutal stretch of schedule coming soon. This made Sunday’s win super important, yet at the same time, it offers very little reassurance. The Cowboys may have secured the victory, but once again, what they showed on the field revealed a team that continues to make life incredibly difficult for themselves, even when facing bad opponents. The game looked eerily similar to the prior week’s letdown against the Arizona Cardinals. In a game where it felt like the Cowboys were in complete control, they chose to play around rather than put their opponent away, eventually leading to another shocking moment where they suddenly found themselves trailing late in the fourth quarter. The most troubling part of this situation is how familiar this has become. Over the last two weeks, the team has reproduced that exact gut-wrenching feeling that gave fans major anxiety during those consecutive nail-biting weeks against Baltimore and Houston earlier in the year. It’s the same story. They begin slowly, eventually start to get their act together to build a lead, and then watch it gradually wither away. Fortunately, against the Texans earlier in the season, they were able to escape with a victory thanks to a game-winning drive on the back of a clutch fourth-down conversion. But down in Rio, they weren’t so lucky. Instead of punching the ball into the end zone with just a handful of seconds left on the clock, the offense sputtered and settled for a field goal, allowing the Ravens to make the game-winning play themselves. The heartbreaking finish left fans playing the what-if game and asking why the Cowboys keep letting this happen. Fast forward a month later, and the exact same scenario is unfolding all over again, except this time it is happening against even worse teams. The Arizona debacle last week was an absolute horror show. The Cardinals did not score a single point until late in the first half and were down by two touchdowns in the fourth quarter before things completely fell apart. The most infuriating part is that the offense had the opportunity to run out the clock if they could have secured one measly first down late in the game. They failed, the Cardinals mounted a comeback, and fans everywhere watched their team collapse. On Sunday, it looked like it was happening again. It was painful to watch the offense struggle so mightily to score touchdowns against a poor Colts defense. Up until the final 70 seconds of the game, the offense had only found the end zone twice, and it required a clutch fourth-down grab by Jake Ferguson and a huge coverage breakdown for CeeDee Lamb’s big touchdown right at the end of the first half. Strangely enough, clutch fourth-down execution from Ferguson and Lamb exploding for over 180 receiving yards were identical saving graces in each of their close victory against their AFC South opponents this year. Imagine if those two things didn’t happen? The Cowboys would be sitting at an abysmal 2-7 with a completely dead season, and the entire fanbase would be stressing over how the New York Jets are about to inherit a top-five draft pick courtesy of the front office. All of this is to say that the Cowboys are an absolute mess right now. Are they still within striking distance of the NFC East crown? Sure, but we must remind ourselves that the schedule gets significantly tougher over the second half of the season, and this group has not beaten a single opponent with a winning record all year. In fact, they are 1-5 against teams with a record of 3-6 or better. That is a scary statistic. Of the final eight opponents left on the schedule, five currently boast winning records. The month of December looks particularly ominous, featuring a four-game stretch against teams who all currently have a winning record. The storm is coming. For a team that struggles to put away struggling teams, anticipating how they will hold up against stronger opponents is frightening. This team shows zero signs of turning the corner or correcting their chronic mental lapses. Instead, they prefer to lollygag and repeatedly engage in unnecessary wild finishes. All of this seems avoidable. They have to be better than this, but sadly, they just refuse to play like it. Hang on to your drama subscription because it won’t be going away anytime soon.
author: Dan Rogers

title: Cowboys news: Dallas will be missing a starter, role players due to injury
summary: The Cowboys are happy to get out of Indianapolis with their fourth win of the season, but still left a lot of things that will need a quick fix on the field before returning home to play the 49ers. They come out of the Colts game with some injuries that won’t make dealing with a […]
full_text: Photo by Michael Hickey/Getty Images | Getty Images The Cowboys are happy to get out of Indianapolis with their fourth win of the season, but still left a lot of things that will need a quick fix on the field before returning home to play the 49ers. They come out of the Colts game with some injuries that won’t make dealing with a 7-1 San Francisco squad any easier. The team will need to be firing in all three phases, which means finding a way to continue getting stops on defense, and scoring off of them more than they have been on offense. Dallas Cowboys rule out 3 players for Week 10, while Jake Ferguson and a rising player are set to miss multiple games – Mauricio Rodriguez, A to Z Sports The Cowboys have some key injuries for the 49ers game, including starting TE Jake Ferguson. When asked to walk through the injuries from the Colts game, Schottenheimer didn’t sugarcoat it. “Busy week in the training room for us,” Schottenheimer said. “PJ Locke will not be available this week. Jake Ferguson and Tyler Goodson should both miss multiple weeks. We’re working through that.” Additionally, the Cowboys have a large group of players whose statuses will be up in the air as the week progresses. Cowboys’ emerging RB ‘probably going to miss some time’ with knee injury – Todd Brock, The Cowboys Wire The Cowboys are going to be very thin at running back, after Tyler Goodson played through injury in week nine. The 25-year-old exited the game in the first half and spent some time in the sideline medical tent but was able to return after the break to notch 33 of his 77 rushing yards. He and starter Javonte Williams combined to put up 178 yards on the ground, with Goodson averaging an impressive 6.4 yards per carry. “I’m going to do everything I can to get out there on the field,” Goodson said after the win . “If it’s just a little pain, I’m going to go. But if it’s something where I just can’t go, then I won’t go.” The Cowboys Defense Got 14 Stops: What Did the Offense Do With Them? – Cody Warren, Inside The Star The Cowboys defense is getting off the field, but the offense can’t stay on it as much as they need to either. Dallas led the Colts 10-7 in the second quarter when Parker’s defense forced three consecutive three-and-outs. The Cowboys punted it right back three times. On the last of those possessions, Williams opened with a 14-yard run, Lamb was flagged for a false start, the penalties piled up, and Dallas eventually punted on fourth-and-18. It took a fourth straight Colts punt before Brian Schottenheimer and Dak Prescott made them pay. Dak got the ball at his 25 with 49 seconds left and found Lamb for a 44-yard touchdown before halftime . Download the SB Nation app today! Fewer ads Seamlessly jump between communities and conversations Faster commenting and posting experience! Download the SB Nation app on iOS or Android . Caleb Downs makes his mark in crucial victory over Colts – Matthew Holleran, Blogging The Boys Every week, Caleb Downs is doing more and more to show why he was one of the top defensive players in this year’s draft class. Expectations were sky-high for Downs at the beginning of his rookie campaign. While the 21-year-old had shown flashes of greatness in Dallas’ first eight games, we’d yet to see him take over a game as he did at Ohio State. For the first time in his NFL career, Downs did just that on Sunday. Downs and Quinnen Williams were the best defenders on the field on Sunday afternoon. Downs showed his ability to impact the game in multiple ways, finishing with a sack, a PBU, and a game-sealing interception in the fourth quarter. Cowboys should relish in Eagles throwing in the towel with Jordan Davis trade – Levi Dombro, The Landry Hat Someone has to win the NFC East, and the Cowboys win over the Colts allows them to keep hoping it can be them, especially with the Eagles waving the white flag. Currently on a seven-game losing streak and having dropped three straight contests against division foes, Howie Roseman is throwing in the towel on the 2026 season. On Monday afternoon, less than a day before the trade deadline, the Eagles traded star nose tackle Jordan Davis to the Jaguars. Eight months after they signed him to a three-year, $78 million deal. And while Roseman is now sitting on a pile of draft picks in Philadelphia, that doesn’t really move the needle a whole lot anymore. This is a good day for Cowboys fans to victory lap their bitter rivals and feel good that they at least have hope for the rest of the season. Brian Schottenheimer on Cowboys’ penalty struggles vs. Colts: ‘It wasn’t good enough’ – Tommy Yarrish, DallasCowboys.com The Cowboys not separating from bad opponents because of penalties is going to continue hurting them against better teams, and the head coach knows it. Through nine games, the Cowboys are now tied for the second-most penalties accepted against them with 42, and have the most penalty yards accepted against them in the NFL with 667. Evidently, it had an impact on their Week 9 game against the Colts and will continue to impact their season if it isn’t corrected. “It wasn’t good enough, and that’s why that came down to the way it came down,” Schottenheimer said. “That game should’ve been where we win by a couple touchdowns maybe, but we let them hang around, we put ourselves behind the sticks on offense a bunch. Explained to the guys, if we don’t clean that up, it’s going to hurt our ability to do what we want to do.”

title: No Bull thoughts on the ILB room after the Daiyan Henley trade
summary: I’ve been hammering the Broncos on their reluctance to upgrade the inside linebacker position for years. No serious draft picks spent on it, no trades, and no serious free agent pursuit. One of the most overlooked reasons that our 2015 defense was so dominant was the quality of talent we had at ILB. We had […]
full_text: INGLEWOOD, CALIFORNIA - NOVEMBER 08: Daiyan Henley #0 of the Los Angeles Chargers walks onto the field before an NFL game against the Houston Texans at SoFi Stadium on November 08, 2026 in Inglewood, California. (Photo by Ryan Sun/Getty Images) | Getty Images I’ve been hammering the Broncos on their reluctance to upgrade the inside linebacker position for years. No serious draft picks spent on it, no trades, and no serious free agent pursuit. One of the most overlooked reasons that our 2015 defense was so dominant was the quality of talent we had at ILB. We had Danny Trevathan and Brandon Marshall. Both of those guys could cover. Both defended the run. They were playmakers just like everyone else on that defense. The Broncos signing Daiyan Henley is an A+ move, and I darn near would give them the same grade if they had traded a 3rd-round pick for him. Henley is a player that has been loved and respected in the Chargers’ locker room. He’s a captain of the team. He’s also a guy who has worn the green dot for the defense (calling the plays for the defense). This is yet another high-character player added to a locker room built on high character and positive culture. Athletically, he’s the most talented linebacker on the inside we have seen in a very long time. His capability at coverage is excellent. He’s also a more sure tackler than either of our current starters. So the question for this team becomes: what happens with our defense? While I think he’s a real option for the future captain of our defense over Alex Singleton, that day will not be soon. He’s going to have to learn the defense and be in the system a while before the Broncos can even think of that. I expect him to be in the mix in nickel downs coming out of the bye. I think he’s likely going to take Justin Strnad’s spot as the starter before the season is over. No matter what happens with the snap count, having depth at inside linebacker is a big deal. Having a linebacker who can cover running backs in the flat and tight ends could very well be the missing piece for this defense to take a big step forward. title: How does ILB Daiyan Henley fit into Broncos’ long-term plans?
summary: The Denver Broncos trade with the Los Angeles Chargers for inside linebacker Daiyan Henley was one that few of us were expecting with all eyes watching for running back news. But it was an underrated move that may pay big dividends down the road. Henley is in the final year of rookie deal, so he’ll […]
full_text: INGLEWOOD, CALIFORNIA - NOVEMBER 08: Daiyan Henley #0 of the Los Angeles Chargers reacts during the second half against the Houston against the Houston Texans at SoFi Stadium on November 08, 2026 in Inglewood, California. (Photo by Ryan Sun/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Denver Broncos trade with the Los Angeles Chargers for inside linebacker Daiyan Henley was one that few of us were expecting with all eyes watching for running back news. But it was an underrated move that may pay big dividends down the road. Henley is in the final year of rookie deal, so he’ll clearly be looking at an extension from the Broncos now that they’ve spent two picks to acquire him. Where does that leave Justin Strnad and Alex Singleton after this season? From a cap savings perspective, the green dot holding veteran Singleton would be the odd man out next March. Denver would save $4M in cap with $5M in dead money. Plus Strnad is three years younger and would incur $7M in dead money and no cap savings. The move seems to signal the teams willingness to move on from Singleton either next March or after his contract runs its course through 2027. Additionally, Henley has worn the green dot for the Chargers the last several seasons and is the leader of that defense — one that was pretty good until the whole team became a dumpster fire this season. Aside from cap and roster, Henley also fits well into the Broncos’ long-term plans through his coverage ability. This has been an annoyingly difficult area to address and this defense’s biggest weaknesses in pass defense. Coming out of college, scouting reports noted his upside and his sideline-to-sideline speed. He was considered underweight and not a great tackler. However, in the NFL that slight weight hasn’t stopped him from being the Chargers’ leading tackler every season. I think this trade is exactly what the defense needs to take things to an elite level. All that remains to be seen is how well he fits into the Vance Joseph scheme this year. title: Broncos trade for Chargers LB Daiyan Henley
summary: According to ESPN’s lead league insider, the Denver Broncos have traded for Chargers linebacker Daiyan Henley. The Broncos will be sending a 2027 4th-round pick and a 2028 5th-round pick to the Chargers for Henley. Henley is a 6-0, 225-pound linebacker who was a third-round pick by the Los Angeles Chargers in the 2023 NFL […]
full_text: KANSAS CITY, MISSOURI - OCTOBER 18: Daiyan Henley #0 of the Los Angeles Chargers stands on the field during the first quarter of an NFL football game against the Kansas City Chiefs at Arrowhead Stadium on October 18, 2026 in Kansas City, Missouri. (Photo by Brooke Sutton/Getty Images) | Getty Images According to ESPN’s lead league insider, the Denver Broncos have traded for Chargers linebacker Daiyan Henley. The Broncos will be sending a 2027 4th-round pick and a 2028 5th-round pick to the Chargers for Henley. Trade: Chargers are sending LB Daiyan Henley to the Denver Broncos for a 2027 fourth-round pick and 2028 fifth-round pick, per sources. — Adam Schefter (@AdamSchefter) November 10, 2026 Henley is a 6-0, 225-pound linebacker who was a third-round pick by the Los Angeles Chargers in the 2023 NFL Draft. Throughout his career, Henley has appeared in 56 games and totaled 317 tackles, 5 sacks, 1 forced fumble, 4 interceptions, and 15 pass deflections during his time with the Chargers. This season, Henley has appeared in 8 games and totaled 51 tackles, 0.5 sacks, 1 forced fumble, 1 interception (which happened this past Sunday), and 2 pass deflections. Henley turns 27 years old here in a few days and is in the final year of his rookie deal, but figures to have a role in the Broncos’ defense moving forward. In the short term, Henley will play behind veteran starters Alex Singleton and Justin Strnad , according to reports, but he is a talented linebacker who can cover and blitz, so he should earn some playing time rather quickly. The Broncos are sending a 2027 4th-round pick to the Chargers, but are expected to get a 4th-round compensation pick due to John Franklin-Myers signing with the Titans in free agency this offseason. I really like this pick. Henley is a talented player who gives the Broncos something they really need. An athletic linebacker with sideline-to-sideline speed that can cover and cover well. He’s an excellent coverage linebacker and can cover tight ends and running backs in the pass game, which has been a multi-year issue for the Broncos. Justin Strnad has graded out as one of the better coverage linebackers in the NFL, while Alex Singleton has struggled in that area. Singleton has been solid in the run game, but if he were to come off the field on third downs for Henley, I think that would improve the Broncos’ third-down defense. However, we have to see how the Broncos handle this moving forward, but obviously they have a vision for him since they traded for him. With Henley in the final year of his deal, and the fact that the Broncos traded a 4th-round pick for him, he seems like a player the team views as part of their future. Time will tell there, but it seems like a move for a player they plan on having beyond this season.

They have been widely connected to Colts star running back Jonathan Taylor in the days leading up to the deadline , but according to 9NEWS Denver’s Mike Klis, the team could explore adding a weapon or two to their offense. He mentions running back, tight end, and wide receiver as the positions that they could add. With Harvey injury and Badie also on IR and injuries across the offense, would expect Broncos to explore adding a weapon or two before trade deadline (RB, TE, WR). https://t.co/TSad3tJ2d3 — MikeKlis9NEWS (@mikeklis9news) October 31, 2026 Looking at the Broncos’ needs heading into the deadline, the most glaring one is running back. Now, the emergence of rookie running back Jonah Coleman helps, but the Broncos still need more from the position. RJ Harvey and Tyler Badie are on the injured reserve, and veteran JK Dobbins has been struggling all season. So, adding another back to pair with Coleman would make sense. The question is, will they go big and add a Jonathan Taylor or Breece Hall? Or make a smaller move for someone like Tony Pollard or someone else? Klis mentions wide receiver, and while it may not be the most pressing need right now, it could be in a few months. Jaylen Waddle has not performed as expected thus far; Courtland Sutton will be 32 next season and has a large cap hit(Also restructured his deal and could be off the team next season); Pat Bryant has been very good, but has been on the IR; Marvin Mims is a pending free agent, while Troy Franklin is buried on the depth chart. Could the Broncos be looking to add a wide receiver who could contribute to this team this season and moving forward? This doesn’t seem as likely, but I wouldn’t rule it out if the right deal comes their way. As for tight end, I don’t know. The only name that could move the needle and that might be available is Dallas Goedert, but is that even worth it? He would certainly improve that room, but the Broncos really do not utilize their tight ends in the passing game. Evan Engram has had a disappointing year, and blocking specialist Nate Adkins leads the group (and, funny enough, the team) in TD receptions with 3, but he only has 6 total catches thus far. We’ll be tracking all the Broncos news and rumors throughout the weekend and right up to the deadline. title: Broncos at Panthers: The No Bull Review
summary: The phrase I kept hearing heading into this game was the dreaded “trap game.” This plucky Carolina Panthers team was supposed to catch the Denver Broncos napping as they look forward to their bye week after a grueling game with the Kansas City Chiefs. Rest assured, Broncos Country, that this Broncos team does not overlook […]
full_text: CHARLOTTE, NORTH CAROLINA - NOVEMBER 08: Devon Key #26 of the Denver Broncos intercepts a pass during the third quarter against the Carolina Panthers at Bank of America Stadium on November 08, 2026 in Charlotte, North Carolina. (Photo by Grant Halverson/Getty Images) | Getty Images The phrase I kept hearing heading into this game was the dreaded “trap game.” This plucky Carolina Panthers team was supposed to catch the Denver Broncos napping as they look forward to their bye week after a grueling game with the Kansas City Chiefs. Rest assured, Broncos Country, that this Broncos team does not overlook anyone. The Panthers fired their former defensive coordinator, Ejiro Evero, leading up to this game. They added some tweaks to their defense. They have a seriously talented quarterback in Bryce Young. All to no avail. The Broncos adjusted. They adapted. They overcame all obstacles. It is just who they are and what they do. This was a hell of a win for the Broncos. Losing both Jaylen Waddle and Riley Moss was rough. While the offense did a good job of staying on track, the defense was honestly shook with the loss of Moss. It completely changed how the defense played, which led to the defense needing to rely on turning the ball over more than playing consistent, effective defense like we are used to. Offense Week after week, this offense continues to evolve in a positive direction. The passing game looked arguably the best it has all season (granted it was against a very dinged-up secondary). The run game had significant trouble being a focal point against the Panthers’ tenacious front. They made do and made plays in fits and spurts on the ground while mainly leaning on Nix’s arm to do the bulk of the offensive work. The playcalling this week was honestly some of the best I’ve seen all season. I personally would like to see a more balanced approach, but that wasn’t going to work this week against this opponent. It was refreshing to see a matchup like this where there’s an obvious weakness in the defensive secondary that the Broncos fully took advantage of. Sean Payton started the game wanting Nix to attack the secondary, and that never changed until it was time to turtle up and run the clock. Quarterbacks Bo Nix sure did respect the position of quarterback in this game (AMARITE, Ditzpatrick!?). He went downfield early and often in this game with air yard numbers that would make Patrick Mahomes cry (still waiting for the talking heads to start wondering if Mahomes is washed with how short his throws are lately). He did throw another boneheaded pass where he decided the route he was throwing immediately and was completely oblivious to the underneath defender that earned him an interception. Outside of that, I thought he played a superb game. What I liked most about Nix in this game was how often he was looking off defenders to set up his passes. What’s cool about this is that it not only manipulates the defenders, but shows how much he’s getting in sync with the receivers and knows where their routes are. He was impressively quick on the trigger a couple of times during these look-offs. Line The biggest thing causing this offense to look clunky is the line. Ben Powers was practically a turnstile on more than a few plays. Luke Wattenburg had a couple of head-scratchers. Mike McGlinchey just got beat multiple times (he got spun backwards on one play I saw that had me seeing visions of Ty Sambrailo). The front for the Panthers won the day from what I saw throughout the game. It honestly had me wondering if they changed up how they were playing vs. what Evero had them doing previously. I’d be curious to know what Panthers fans who know the game would have to say on this…hit us up in the comments. Is your front just that good, or did they change things up? Running Backs Jonah Coleman rightly took over the starting duties this game and emerged as the #1 RB on the team. With the line having so many troubles, he wasn’t producing what we would like to see. He was able to cook with what he was given, though. He showed impressive burst and speed on his touchdown run around the edge. He was also very effective as a receiver out of the backfield with 4 catches for 31 yards. The fumble late in the game was very tough to see. I feel like he and Nix will both need to work their pitches during the bye week to shore that up. JK Dobbins made an excellent cutback and jump step to gain 11 on his first run. He only got 4 carries on the day total, with his other 3 gaining only 7 yards. Receivers Welcome back, Pat Bryant! Our young rock star of a receiver got a 12-yard gain on his second catch off a crossing route. He caught an 11-yard pass to move the chains in the 3rd quarter. Bryant benefitted from blown coverage for the easiest touchdown he will ever catch late in the 4th quarter for 26 yards. On one hand, Courtland Sutton led the team in targets and was a big focus for the offense. On the other hand, they missed 4 of his targets. He is cash money close to the goal line, though, with a quick slant to put 6 on the board. I like seeing him get the timing throws from Nix that allow him to use his frame to protect the catch. Evan Engram had a pretty active game this week as well. He took a screen for 19 yards right behind a blitz. He ended the day with 4 catches for 33 yards. Troy Franklin got involved late with a couple of really nice routes for 1st-down completions, with one of them inside the red zone. He caught another 13-yard pass on a curl. It was good to see Franklin step up and make plays with Waddle out. Franklin isn’t Waddle, but he produced this week when his number was called. Defense The defense had some pretty significant struggles off and on throughout this game. As the 4th quarter rolled around, it appeared to me that Bryce Young was going to be able to have success passing all the way down to the wire. The only way this team was going to be able to win was with some big-time turnovers. Vance Joseph put his players in position to make it work, and they provided the kind of soul-wrenching turnovers that make a fan base want to cry about refs, complain about takebacks, and call your team a bunch of big meanies. This was a gutsy victory for the Broncos defense. They were already out Kris Abrams-Draine, Talanoa Hufanga, and Brandon Jones to start the game. They lost Riley Moss early and seemed to me to switch mainly to zone calls that kept the defense in front of them which just isn’t what this defense is used to doing. It got the job done even though it wasn’t pretty. Many watching the game were complaining about the soft zone calls, but I don’t know that you’d like it if we just put in our normal match zone with the group of depth players we had on the field. Look, the players and coaches talk really big about “Next man up.” They talk about how they expect the backups to come in and have no drop-off. That’s absolute horse shit, honestly. I’m sorry, but Jahdae Barron is no Riley Moss. Taylor Rapp is no Huff. JL Skinner is no Jones. Devon Key isn’t either. These guys are lower down on the depth chart for a reason. Expecting them to be able to press man or match zone in one-on-ones across the board would have been disastrous. The one ace card the Panthers have is a superb young quarterback who knows how to drop dimes. All it takes is one bad half-step by a backup corner or safety, and it would have been 50+ yard touchdowns multiple times. Don’t get me wrong, I hate soft zone looks where your guys are starting 8 yards off their guys and give up pass after pass, just like all of you. The game of NFL football is not so simple that you can just wave a wand and turn a 4th string player into a solid press-man defender. Feel free to disagree, but my hat is off to Vance Joseph. Great defensive coordinators take a game like this and find a way to get the job done. The players made the plays to get the win. Joseph called the game in a way that put them in a position to make…

title: Horse Tracks: Are the Broncos lucky…or just good?
summary: Good morning, Broncos Country! In my pickleball league, we have a common saying, “Better to be lucky than good.” But if Sean Payton were playing in my league, he’d say that because we were good, we got lucky. At least I assume he’d say that…since that’s how he feels about the Broncos’ 16-game streak of […]
full_text: CHARLOTTE, NORTH CAROLINA - NOVEMBER 08: Devon Key #26 of the Denver Broncos celebrates after defeating the Carolina Panthers 26-21 at Bank of America Stadium on November 08, 2026 in Charlotte, North Carolina. (Photo by Todd Kirkland/Getty Images) | Getty Images Good morning, Broncos Country! In my pickleball league, we have a common saying, “Better to be lucky than good.” But if Sean Payton were playing in my league, he’d say that because we were good, we got lucky. At least I assume he’d say that…since that’s how he feels about the Broncos’ 16-game streak of winning one-score games. “When those things keep falling your way, that’s not by accident,” he said. He makes a good point. You create your own luck. And while the Broncos have had some “lucky breaks,” it was because they played well enough to create those situations. Devon Key’s interception wasn’t lucky. It was a good (really good) heads-up play because he was focused on the ball. Last week’s amazing false start to save the day against the Chiefs wasn’t “lucky,” it was a good (really good) Mile High crowd making a huge difference. And 16 wins in a row by one score or less — an NFL record by the Broncos — is not luck. Devon Key on the Broncos winning 16-straight one-score wins: "I wouldn't say it's luck" — Zac Stevens (@ZacStevens) November 8, 2026 As Bo Nix would argue, it’s character, toughness and competitiveness. It’s also skill and practice. “We’re just comfortable in that moment,” Nix said, noting it’s not like they want it to only be winning by one score, but it’s a lot better than losing by one. “Until I figure something out about how to change it, just glad we’re on this side and winning them and not in a streak of losing them.” Nix is also not too interested in the streak, as much as he is what it means — the Broncos keep winning games. “I don’t care. …in 10, 15 years, nobody’s going to care about [the streak],” he added. “They’re going to talk about wins … but it’s cool right now. It’s great as we go, but it definitely would be nice to win by more than a score.” Yes. Yes it would. This is insane: Bo Nix is 8-1 the last two season when trailing by 8 or fewer points in the 4th quarter, per @doug_clawson . The rest of the NFL has a win percentage of 29.6% in those situations. pic.twitter.com/QjxSME7B54 — Zac Stevens (@ZacStevens) November 9, 2026 But as long as the team and its QB have the mentality that getting that go-ahead score, or saving it, is just something they need to do — while playing a lot of really good teams — then it’s probably going to keep happening. “I’ll be honest, it seems like it’s always the same feeling. There’s always a look in the huddle that, like, hey guys, we don’t have a choice right here. We got to go make something out of it,” Nix said, highlighting the second-half touchdowns on Sunday. “Those were really, really important.” Nix highlighted the touchdown drives — the first to go ahead after getting down, 14-13, and the second to extend that lead, 26-14, which became crucial when the Panthers fought for a comeback of their own and scored a touchdown. “I thought that was the best part of the game because it showed that we stacked two drives together, two critical moments and gave our defense some rest on the sideline with those longer drives,” Nix said. “Also, a good cushion and they did just a good job responding and scoring.” But that rest also allowed the defense to be fresh for the “lucky breaks” that came its way. Like after a near lost fumble on the offense’s three-and-out, giving the Panthers three minutes on the clock to try for the comeback win, only to be stymied by a strip sack from Nik Bonitto. “That was big,” said Payton. “We talked about the ball security, and it finally came and it was a huge play, obviously. It was a huge play.” Not lucky. Just good. "This Denver Broncos offense has a lot more rhythm right now.. Bo Nix looks more confident and he's really cutting it loose.. He's looked a lot more like he did last year the last couple of weeks" ~ @danorlovsky7 #PMSLive pic.twitter.com/gFgMbSRtyh — Pat McAfee (@PatMcAfeeShow) November 9, 2026
