title: For the Detroit Lions, ugly wins are a thing of beauty
summary: Winning the ugly ones is just as important as the pretty ones—they count the same in the standings, after all—and that’s where the Detroit Lions need to keep pace with an NFC North that refuses to ease up. For yet another week, everyone in the Black and Blue division with a quarterback capable of performing […]
full_text: Nov 8, 2026; Miami Gardens, Florida, USA; Detroit Lions head coach Dan Campbell celebrates with defensive back Brian Branch (32) after an interception during the second half against the Miami Dolphins at Hard Rock Stadium. Mandatory Credit: Nathan Ray Seebeck-Imagn Images | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect Winning the ugly ones is just as important as the pretty ones—they count the same in the standings, after all—and that’s where the Detroit Lions need to keep pace with an NFC North that refuses to ease up. For yet another week, everyone in the Black and Blue division with a quarterback capable of performing the forward pass picked up wins. It’s maddening, it’s odds-defying, it feels like it has to let up at some point, but until it does, winning is all that matters for this Lions team. Most of the noise on game day centered on the new guy at left guard, Miles Frazier, stepping in for starter Christian Mahogany . In real time, people scrambled to find an explanation. Was Mahogany hurt in pregame warmups? What were his PFF grades over the last three games? Did he catch the South Beach Flu? People hardly had enough time to investigate before Detroit took the field and mustered up a measly 110 yards and six points on offense in the first half. Prior to halftime, fans had lost their patience with Frazier’s performance. Jared Goff was sacked three times, Jahmyr Gibbs had four carries of zero or negative yards, and the Lions were up just three points at halftime against a 1-6 Miami Dolphins team. Enough was enough: Mahogany needed to be put in at left guard to help the Lions offense get back on track. Except that didn’t happen. Mahogany played just five snaps on Sunday in Miami, all of those opportunities coming on field goal kicks. The Lions offense turned things around just enough in the second half. Goff stayed upright, Gibbs broke into the end zone for the game’s only touchdown, and the Lions defense (!) made sure this one ended in a victory. Not for them, but for their leader, Jack Campbell, who had to watch his defense from a hospital room, still regaining his physical faculties—but determined to return to the field. Social media was filled with videos and photos of the Honolulu Blue takeover at Hard Rock Stadium, fans chanting and holding signs in support of Campbell and the Lions. Your feed was filled with as much love and support as it was with people wondering how Mahogany’s crime could justify the time he spent on the sideline. Dan Campbell offered no further insight into the infraction immediately after the game, but has since alluded to the fact that Mahogany had broken team rules “multiple times.” Dan Campbell made the right decision when it came to holding Mahogany accountable. There’s no room in their building for anyone to be above the standard, whether you’re a starter or a healthy inactive on game day. That isn’t a new sentiment—it’s been the foundation since the afternoon Campbell walked through the door. “But I’ll guarantee you this: these guys are gonna fight, and they’re gonna scratch and claw, and they’re gonna be something this city is proud of because they’re going to take on the identity of this city,” Campbell said in his introductory press conference. “It ain’t always going to be roses up here. ‘Everything’s gonna be the way that we all want it to be and look perfect,’ but I know this, man, we’re gonna fight, we’re gonna scratch, and we’re gonna claw, and I know the good teams find a way to get it done.” Campbell told us it wasn’t always going to be pretty, and we’ve been reminded over these past couple of weeks just how ugly football can get, but there’s something beautiful in it all. “If somebody goes down, the next one steps up, and he’s expected to produce enough to help those guys next to him when these guys are going to learn to play together, play for one another.” From the disciplinary action against Mahogany to Jack Campbell’s absence in the middle of Detroit’s defense, from the offense’s struggles to Kelvin Sheppard’s unit getting the job done, Sunday was a testament to how they’ve become that good team Campbell referenced over five years ago. Their 6-2 record is a reflection of the image this football team was built on by Dan Campbell. “It’s not about the best 53, it’s about the right 53.”
author: Ryan Mathews

title: NFL Week 10 power rankings: Despite 4 straight wins, Detroit Lions sit behind NFC North rivals
summary: The Detroit Lions (6-2) have now won four in a row, are 2-0 in the division with wins over the Packers and Vikings, and sit in second place in the NFC North, just a half-game back of the Chicago Bears. For the first time this season, the Lions rank in the top 10 of every […]
full_text: Detroit Lions head coach Dan Campbell watches a play Miami Dolphins during the second half at Hard Rock Stadium in Miami Gardens on Sunday, Nov. 8, 2026. | USA TODAY Network via Reuters Co The Detroit Lions (6-2) have now won four in a row, are 2-0 in the division with wins over the Packers and Vikings, and sit in second place in the NFC North , just a half-game back of the Chicago Bears. For the first time this season, the Lions rank in the top 10 of every national power ranking that we track. But it’s not all sunshine and roses in the Lions’ relationship with the national media. Of the eight rankings we track, the Lions dropped this week in over half of them. Even more surprising, they dropped behind the Packers in two (Yahoo Sports and Sports Illustrated) and remain behind the Vikings in two others (Sporting News and ESPN)—despite having the same (Vikings) or better (Packers) record—and winning both head-to-head matchups. Let’s take a closer look at this week’s national power rankings. Sports Illustrated: 6 ( Previous rank: 4) From Connor Orr : Having spent time in Buffalo after Damar Hamlin’s near-death experience in a Bills-Bengals game, I can still only begin to fathom the heaviness this Lions team is dealing with on a daily basis in the aftermath of the Jack Campbell injury . It makes the Dolphins victory feel very different… and somehow more amazing. USA Today: 6 (Previous rank: 7) From Nate Davis : WR Amon-Ra St. Brown hasn’t scored since September and only has two 100-yard receiving games this season. Think the German-American star might break out Sunday in Munich − especially given how the Pats secondary just got shredded? NFL.com: 7 (Previous rank: 5) From Nick Shook : Sunday’s victory wasn’t pretty by any means, but sometimes a team needs to find a way to win an ugly one. The Lions did that in Miami, getting just enough from Jahmyr Gibbs to leave with a W. That’s what I’d expect from a team in the top 10, but I’m hoping this was an informative experience to grow from, not a harbinger of things to come. The Athletic: 8 (Previous rank: 7) From Chad Graff and Josh Kendall : It hasn’t always looked pretty (including in Miami on Sunday), and the underlying defensive stats (they rank 30th in EPA per play) remain concerning. But the offense has been among the game’s best as they now head abroad to face the reeling New England defense. CBS Sports: 8 (Previous rank: 9) From Pete Prisco : It wasn’t pretty against the Dolphins, but they found a way. They can’t play that way this week against a wounded Patriots team or else. Yahoo Sports: 9 (Previous rank: 8) From Frank Schwab : Is the Lions’ defense good? It has been better recently. For the third straight game the Lions’ opponent failed to top 17 points. Two of those games happened against the offensively challenged Vikings and Dolphins; the third game in that streak was against the Packers. Advanced metrics are kind to the Lions’ defense over the past three weeks too, as Detroit is eighth in EPA per play allowed and fifth in success rate allowed. Star safety Brian Branch returned from an Achilles injury three games ago, and it’s not a coincidence the Lions’ defense is much better with him back. The Lions have held opponents to 21 or fewer points in four straight games, the first time that has happened since 2016, according to the team’s site. The Lions allowed just 228 yards and 12 first downs Sunday, and while that was against Miami, it’s still a lot better than Detroit looked on defense early in the season. “We’ve cleaned a lot up,” Lions head coach Dan Campbell said, via the team’s site. “Guys are trusting what they’re being taught, they’re executing it and with that execution comes confidence.” ESPN: 10 (Previous rank: 9) From ESPN Staff, excerpt from Eric Woodyard : International games are rare for the Lions, who haven’t played outside the U.S. since 2015. And this matchup in Munich is a homecoming of sorts for WR Amon-Ra St. Brown, whose mother is German and who has spent considerable time in the country. This contest also marks Detroit’s first game in Germany and the first time it is the designated home team for an international game, so this is certainly a huge deal. “You kind of need that extra story to tell,” NFL Germany GM Alexander Steinforth told ESPN. “You need that extra link into the market to have a really meaningful impact, and that’s Amon-Ra St. Brown.” Sporting News: 10 (Previous rank: 11) From Vinnie Iyer : The Lions’ once-maligned defense has allowed only a total of 62 points during their four-game winning streak. They will get a good test against the Patriots in Munich, Germany, in Week 10, where Jared Goff needs to shake off back-to-back sub 200-yard, one-INT games.

title: Detroit Lions Kerby Joseph won’t play in Germany
summary: On Tuesday morning, Detroit Lions coach Dan Campbell held his weekly interview with local sports radio station 97.1 The Ticket. When discussing the recovery progress of All-Pro safety Kerby Joseph, Campbell said that he doesn’t expect Joseph to be able to play in Week 10 against the New England Patriots in Germany. “I’ll cut it […]
full_text: Detroit Lions safety Kerby Joseph (31) looks on during warm up ahead of the New Orleans Saints game at Ford Field in Detroit on Sunday, Sept. 13, 2026. | USA TODAY Network via Reuters Co On Tuesday morning, Detroit Lions coach Dan Campbell held his weekly interview with local sports radio station 97.1 The Ticket. When discussing the recovery progress of All-Pro safety Kerby Joseph, Campbell said that he doesn’t expect Joseph to be able to play in Week 10 against the New England Patriots in Germany. “I’ll cut it out (the speculation). I don’t see him playing. I don’t see him playing in Germany,” Campbell told 97.1, per Will Burchfield . Joseph injured his knee in 2025 during training camp, and limped through the first month of the season before succumbing to his injury. For just over a year, Joseph underwent rehabilitation, working to build strength in his knee. In late October, Joseph finally gained enough stability in his knee to start practicing once again and started his 21-day injury evaluation clock. Over the last two weeks of practices, Joseph has slowly ramped up his participation levels, as he acclimates back to football activities. On Monday, Campbell said Joseph continues to make progress; they like where he is at and hope to get him even more involved this week. “He did a good job last week, so we want to get him some more work.” While Joseph is steadily improving, the early decision to keep him out of Sunday’s game overseas may seem premature, but for a player who hasn’t played in well over a year, it’s not unusual and shouldn’t necessarily be viewed as a negative regarding his progress. Campbell also noted on Monday, when discussing the trade for Andre Cisco, that he expected Joseph to return this season and would give the Lions’ secondary some flexibility. “We get Kerby back eventually here. Kerby gives you flexibility, keep him where you need him or move him back and forth.“ The Lions don’t want to rush Joseph back into game action, but they are working against the injury evaluation clock, which expires on Tuesday, November 17. At that time, the Lions will need to activate Joseph to the active roster, or they can elect to keep him on the PUP list, which would end his season. If activated, Joseph could potentially return to the field in Week 11 when the Lions host the Tampa Bay Buccaneers.

title: Discussion: What is your dream trade deadline move for the Detroit Lions?
summary: Welcome to NFL trade deadline day. After 4 p.m. ET on Tuesday, no more trades can be executed until the start of the league year in 2027. For the Detroit Lions, that likely means this is their last opportunity to make a roster upgrade for the 2026 season. And while the Lions don’t have any […]
full_text: PHILADELPHIA, PA - OCTOBER 18: Philadelphia Eagles linebacker Zack Baun (53) looks on after the game between the Carolina Panthers and Philadelphia Eagles on October 18, 2026 at Lincoln Financial Field in Philadelphia, PA. (Photo by Kyle Ross/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images) | Icon Sportswire via Getty Images Welcome to NFL trade deadline day. After 4 p.m. ET on Tuesday, no more trades can be executed until the start of the league year in 2027. For the Detroit Lions, that likely means this is their last opportunity to make a roster upgrade for the 2026 season. And while the Lions don’t have any massively pressing needs, they are in a bit of an arms race in the NFC. The Chicago Bears added DT Jeffery Simmons a couple of weeks ago. The Seattle Seahawks added guard Quenton Nelson. The 49ers brought back DeForest Buckner. Detroit is in a good spot in the NFC—currently holding onto the fifth seed in the NFL playoff standings—but just about everyone in contention for a postseason spot is playing decent football right now. The Lions have already made one minor move before the deadline, trading for reserve safety Andre Cisco . But I’m guessing most Lions fans want more. So today’s Question of the Day is: What is your dream trade scenario for the Lions? My answer: Trading for Eagles linebacker Zack Baun. Philadelphia has already shown a willingness to trade amid their 2-7 start to the season. On Monday, they sent defensive tackle Jordan Davis to the Jacksonville Jaguars for a first-round pick and a future second-round pick. That’s a pretty penny to pay, and it may be indicative that Baun will be costly if the Eagles are going to let him go. But in Baun, the Lions would be getting a dynamic playmaker. Baun does everything in that Eagles defense. He’s above average in coverage—grading 71.4 or better in each of the last three seasons, per PFF. He’s a pass-rushing threat, with nine sacks since 2024. And he’s an absolute force in the run game, as well. He’d also come with an insanely team-friendly contract, seeing as most of his money is currently tied up in signing and option bonuses that stay with the Eagles upon a trade. Detroit would only be due a prorated version of his $1.215 million salary this year, then they would have an option for 2027 to pay Baun a $14.4 million option bonus to keep him around in 2027. Now, that low salary would likely mean shelling out significant draft capital to lure him away from Philly. We’re likely talking about a second-round pick, minimum. But if that’s the price, I’d pull the trigger. The Lions don’t just have questions at linebacker this year—with Jack Campbell’s future in football unknown, Jimmy Rolder on season-ending IR, and Devin White also on IR. But Detroit also has questions beyond this year. Only Campbell, Derrick Barnes, and Rolder are signed for 2027, and there’s an out in Barnes’ contract if Detroit wishes to move on. Baun would give the Lions a head start on fortifying their linebacker room for the future. What is your dream trade for the Lions before the 4 p.m. ET deadline on Tuesday? Share your thoughts in the comment section below. Join the conversation! title: Malik Willis going on IR can cost the Packers a round in the 2027 draft
summary: The NFL’s compensatory pick formula is a little complicated, but to boil it down: Players are awarded points for their average salary over the life of the contract that they signed in free agency and receive playing-time bonuses based on the percentage of snaps they play during the regular season. If you lose players worth […]
full_text: (Photo by Carmen Mandato/Getty Images) | Getty Images The NFL’s compensatory pick formula is a little complicated, but to boil it down: Players are awarded points for their average salary over the life of the contract that they signed in free agency and receive playing-time bonuses based on the percentage of snaps they play during the regular season. If you lose players worth more points than the ones you sign, you get a draft pick from the NFL (which essentially mints an extra round of the draft, awarding 32 picks from the third to seventh rounds). That’s why the news of Malik Willis, a former Green Bay Packers quarterback, going on injured reserve impacts Green Bay in 2027. Already, Over The Cap has adjusted Willis’ compensatory draft pick projection to be a fourth-round pick, rather than the third-round pick he was initially expected to earn for the Packers. Willis was already a borderline third-round case (there are only two players currently set to earn third-round compensatory picks: edge defenders Jaelen Phillips and Trey Hendrickson), but losing at least four games of action is essentially a nail in the coffin for that selection. So instead of having what was projected to be the 98th pick in the draft for the loss of Willis, the Packers are now projected to receive the 133rd pick, according to Over The Cap. Former Packers leaving Green Bay haven’t had much luck this year. Offensive tackle Rasheed Walker, who was expected to net the Packers at least a fifth-round pick in free agency, overplayed his hand and signed late — leaving him with just a one-year deal. At the moment, the Packers are not expected to be awarded a pick for the loss of Walker. On top of that, receiver Romeo Doubs, who had a chance to earn Green Bay a fourth-round pick, is also on the injured reserve, which likely means that the Packers will only get a fifth-round pick for losing him. Overall, here’s the breakdown of the current outlook for the Packers’ compensatory picks in 2027: 4th round (Malik Willis) 5th round (Quay Walker) 5th round (Romeo Doubs) 6th round (Kingsley Enagbare) Teams are capped at four compensatory draft picks, or Walker (seventh round) would have been in play — had the team not canceled out that selection with the addition of cornerback Benjamin St-Juste in free agency. As a reminder, the Packers own their original draft picks outside of the first (Micah Parsons trade) and sixth (Darian Kinnard trade) rounds. They will also get the Cowboys’ fourth-round pick (Rashan Gary trade) and the Eagles’ sixth-round pick (Dontayvion Wicks trade) in 2027, bringing their overall total to 11 picks.

title: Packers Film Room: Packers defense picks off Drake Maye 3 times
summary: The Green Bay Packers stomped the New England Patriots this past weekend. Jordan Love was dealing, but so was the Packers defense. They picked off Drake Maye three times, and they started quickly, intercepting his first pass of the game. Play 1: 2nd & 9, 14:32 remaining in the 1st quarter The Patriots come out […]
full_text: (Photo by Kathryn Riley/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Green Bay Packers stomped the New England Patriots this past weekend. Jordan Love was dealing, but so was the Packers defense. They picked off Drake Maye three times, and they started quickly, intercepting his first pass of the game. Play 1: 2nd & 9, 14:32 remaining in the 1st quarter The Patriots come out in 12 personnel (1 RB, 2 TE, 2 WR), starting in a completely balanced, 2×2 look. They motion a TE under the formation before the snap. They run a playfake away from the motion, then Drake Maye [10] starts to boots away from the fake, ultimately pulling up deep on a half-boot look. The Packers are showing a single-high safety (Xavier McKinney [29]) before the snap, and that holds after the snap. Per SumerSports , the Packers rotate their safeties after the snap on 39.6% of their snaps, the 4th highest in the league. This time they stay in that single-high look (looks like Cover 3). The Patriots are running Kyle Williams [18] on a deep post from the left, then bringing Mack Hollins [13] on a deep crosser. Initially, it looks like McKinney is going to be running with Williams on the post, but, as Maye climbs in the pocket, McKinney breaks down on Hollins on the crosser. The Packers have the second level of their defense dropped extremely deep, which makes the throw to Hollins a difficult one. Evan Williams [33] is sitting right under the place Maye wants to go. Maye climbs up in pocket, and it looks like he’s doing that as a way to try to pull those defenders away from the window. While Hollins is looking to settle into a window behind Williams, Maye throws across the field, where McKinney is waiting. McKinney returns it 36 yards, setting up the Packers with 1st & 10 on the Patriots 14. They scored 2 plays later on a Jordan Love scramble to make it 7-0. Play 2: 1st & 10, 12:54 remaining in the 2nd quarter The Patriots are in 11 personnel (1 RB, 1 TE, 3 WR) in a 3×1 formation. Kyle Williams is the lone receiver on the left. They’ve got a concept on the right that Maye can work, or he can take Williams on a vertical route if he likes that match-up. The Packers are showing press coverage on the outside and their safeties are pulled up tight to the line. Evan Williams is the safety to the single receiver side. Just before the snap, he starts to bail to the middle. This looks like man-to-man coverage with the safety bailing away from the single WR side. That would put Kyle Williams man-to-man on Brandon Cisse [2] with no safety help, a match-up Maye clearly likes. It’s a really cool bit of deception from the Packers. Maye thinks he caught the Packers showing their hand a bit early, with Evan Williams bailing before the ball is snapped. Instead, it’s the Packers showing Maye what he believes is a single-high rotation, but it quickly turns into a two-high look at the snap. Evan Williams goes from bailing to the middle to dropping wide as soon as the ball is snapped, with Javon Bullard [7] dropping to a deep zone on the other side of the field. Really subtle bit of deception here. Maye has a bit of time so he ends up seeing that Evan Williams has dropped to a deep half-zone, but it’s not a wide drop so Maye still thinks he can hit Kyle Williams. As soon as Maye starts his throwing motion, Evan Williams looks like he’s shot out of a cannon to the sideline. Cisse is in great position and he tips the ball to Evan Williams, who makes the pick. Absolutely beautiful. It’s impossible for me to see a tipped INT and not think of the classic Mike-McKenzine-to-Tyrone-Williams tip against the 49ers in the 2001 Wild Card Game . Play 3: 2nd & 7, 5:47 remaining in the 2nd quarter Patriots are in 12 personnel in a shotgun, 3×1 formation. They are, once again, using Kyle Williams on a vertical route and bringing Eli Raridon [82] from the other side on a crossing route. To help spring that open, they’ve got Hunter Henry [85] on a curl route underneath. Push the defense vertical with Kyle Williams, pin down the second level with Henry and hit Raridon behind it. Nice idea. Packers are starting with McKinney as the single-high safety, aligned extremely deep over the trips side. At the snap, he sinks down into a deep-half zone, with Evan Williams dropping into a deep-half zone on the other side. This looks like Cover 2, with Cisse passing off the vertical route from Kyle Williams to McKinney. This should all work, but McKinney goes and makes a play. Maye hitches roughly a thousand times, looking to the route from Raridon in the middle. McKinney is still staying deep, but his hips are turned in and he’s not even looking at the streaking Kyle Williams: he’s looking to drive on Raridon. As soon as Maye starts his throwing motion, McKinney triggers down, beating Raridon to the ball. It was 17-7 at this point in the game. The Packers scored on a Kaleb Johnson rushing TD 3 plays later to take a 24-7 lead. Albums listened to: Brother Bird – The Lodge in Miller County ; Wilby – Center of Affection

title: NFL Deadline Trade Tracker: Who’s Moving in 2026?
summary: Many moves are expected over the next two days, whether or not they happen. To try to cut through the fat and keep everything contained, we’re going to launch a tracker to give you all the news from the trade deadline. Follow along and voice your opinion on these moves in the comments section, if […]
full_text: (Photo by Patrick McDermott/Getty Images) | Getty Images Many moves are expected over the next two days, whether or not they happen. To try to cut through the fat and keep everything contained, we’re going to launch a tracker to give you all the news from the trade deadline. Follow along and voice your opinion on these moves in the comments section, if you have the chance. Jets EDGE Will McDonald IV demands a trade McDonald wants out of New York after being displaced by Kingsley Enagbare and first-round rookie Joseph Ossai. McDonald was picked right after Lukas Van Ness in the 2023 draft, when the Packers and Jets flipped first-round picks as part of the Aaron Rodgers trade. Colts QB Daniel Jones isn’t being traded Multiple reports are claiming that Jones won’t be moved, even though the Indianapolis Colts’ season is functionally over. Minnesota is a team that would have made sense if Jones were made available. Falcons trade S Jessie Bates to Jaguars Jacksonville sent a 2027 second-round pick and a 2028 fifth-round pick to Atlanta for the 29-year-old All-Pro safety. In the deal, the Falcons agreed to eat most of Bates’ salary for 2026. He’ll be a free agent in 2027, so the Jaguars will be able to collect a 2028 compensatory pick to backfill for their losses if they don’t spend on outside additions next offseason. Saints trade DT Davon Godchaux to Jaguars This one is interesting, from a Packers perspective, because Godchaux was a pre-draft visitor for Green Bay — players that the Packers usually attempt to target when available. Jacksonville needed more depth at the position after some injuries, which is why Green Bay is in the same market. For what it’s worth, I’ve heard buzz about the Packers being interested in the running back and defensive line market. Other teams looking around at defensive tackles are the New York Giants and the Minnesota Vikings (Jacksonville seemingly called everyone for a lineman). Moro Ojomo is probably the biggest name that’s out there right now, but I’m not sure there’s an offer out there that Howie Roseman likes. Jets trade S Andre Cisco to Lions The Lions’ secondary needs help, and they’re getting it in the form of safety Andre Cisco. He’s being moved for a 2028 sixth-round pick, according to ESPN’s Adam Schefter . Eagles trade Jordon Davis to Jaguars Well, I told you guys that the Jaguars called everyone about defensive tackles, didn’t I? Can’t say I expected them to be able to pull this one off, though. Davis, who once set the market for nose tackle this offseason before being passed by Vita Vea and Dexter Lawrence, is being sent to Jacksonville for the cost of a 2027 first-round pick and a 2029 second-round pick. ESPN’s Adam Schefter is now reporting that the Eagles will not be trading Moro Ojomo, who is on an expiring contract. No team has gone more “all in” on the deadline than the Jaguars, who have now made three trades and have lost a first-round pick, two second-round picks, a fifth-round pick and a sixth-round pick today. Colts trade Keenan Allen to 49ers The first trade of the actual day of the deadline was Indianapolis moving an aging receiver to San Francisco. The 49ers have dealt with a lot of injuries at the position, with Mike Evans, Deebo Samuel, Christian Kirk, De’Zhaun Stribling and Ricky Pearsall all being out with varying degrees of injuries. Titans trade Amani Hooker to Bills It looks like the Jessie Bates trade from Monday set a new market at the position. Like Bates, the Titans sent safety Amani Hooker to a contender for a second- and fifth-round pick. Raiders trade Kirk Cousins to Vikings Kirk Cousins is back in purple. Netflix’s Tom Pelissero is now reporting that Cousins will be sent to Minnesota for a third-round pick. It was previously reported that the Raiders wouldn’t move off Cousins unless it was for a first-round pick. First overall pick Fernando Mendoza is now going to be the starting quarterback in Las Vegas. Chargers trade Daiyan Henley to Broncos The Chargers are finally moving some pieces, and it’s at a pretty easy cost for their in-division rivals. Henley, one of the better young linebackers in the league, was picked up for fourth- and fifth-round picks. Colts trade Josh Downs to Chiefs It’s going to get lonely for Daniel Jones in Indianapolis. He’s down two more receivers after the trade deadline. Kansas City is sending a fourth- and fifth-round pick for Downs and a seventh-round pick.

title: Packers Film Room: Jordan Love lights up the Patriots
summary: Another week, another three-TD performance from Green Bay Packers quarterback Jordan Love. Ho-hum. Let’s break them down. Play 1: 3rd & 5, 8:03 remaining in the 1st quarter Packers are in 11 personnel (1 RB, 1 TE, 3 WR) at the 5-yard line. They originally start in a split-backfield set, with Tucker Kraft [85] aligned […]
full_text: (Photo by Michael Owens/Getty Images) | Getty Images Another week, another three-TD performance from Green Bay Packers quarterback Jordan Love. Ho-hum. Let’s break them down. Play 1: 3rd & 5, 8:03 remaining in the 1st quarter Packers are in 11 personnel (1 RB, 1 TE, 3 WR) at the 5-yard line. They originally start in a split-backfield set, with Tucker Kraft [85] aligned to Jordan Love’s [10] right. He shifts out pre-snap to a bunch on the right, and the defense adjusts. Love then “Cans” the play, bringing Kraft in as the in-line TE. That gives a clear two-man look over the Christian Watson [9]/Matthew Golden [0] stack. Kraft then motions under the formation, dragging his man with him across the formation. This looks like Man coverage, but those DBs can still Banjo the coverage (essentially, they would switch coverage responsibilities in the event of a switch release at the line). At the snap, Watson pushes vertical on a corner route. This builds a wall for Golden: something that Christian Gonzalez [0] has to either go over or under if he wants to follow Golden inside. Golden angles out, pushing Gonzalez outside, then cuts back inside on an angle route. Gonzalez stays with Watson on the corner route, giving Golden room inside (although there are linebackers inside that Love has to deal with). Now, about Gonzalez, the LBs inside and the throw. This is something Love has been doing a lot this year as a way to pry open windows between the hashes. He’s got his shoulders and feet pointed to the outside, looking like he’s throwing to the outside. That’s likely why Gonzalez stays on Watson, and it’s also what holds the LBs in place to give Golden space to work with. Here’s the throw in slow motion. Watch his feet and the direction his helmet is pointing vs. where he ends up going with the ball. Play 2: 3rd & 7, 10:57 remaining in the 3rd quarter Packers are up 24-14 early in the 3rd quarter. They come out in 11 personnel, with Jonnu Smith [18] as the TE. They’re in a Bunch Nub formation (three receivers in a bunch to one side, with the TE as the lone receiver on the line opposite). Where we got a lot of motion on the last play, this is just line-up-and-go. Savion Williams [83] is the point man in the bunch, with Golden on the outside and Watson to the inside. Golden and Watson are running double-post – a nice concept in this area of the field – while Williams stutter-steps off the line and runs a fade. With Golden and Watson tying up the safety, this gives Williams a one-on-one against Karon Prunty [21], a 5th-round rookie seeing the first extended action of his career. (He had 3 defensive snaps against the Jaguars, but all of his other snaps this season have been on special teams). Love checks the safeties, then goes back-shoulder to Williams on the fade. Nice throw and a great catch from Williams. With the extra point, the Packers take a commanding 31-14 lead. Play 3: 1st & 10, 4:16 remaining in the 3rd quarter After forcing their 4th turnover on the day, the Packers immediately go big-game hunting. Starting at the Patriots’ 39-yard line, the Packers come out in 12 personnel (1 RB, 2 TE, 2 WR). They’re in a YY Wing formation on the left (both TEs in-line to the same side) and have both WRs in a stack to the right. They go max protect, keeping both TEs in to block and leaking out a RB as a checkdown option. From the inside of the stack, Golden pushes vertically, bending slightly inside. This draws the attention of the safety to that side. While he breaks down on Golden, Watson goes streaking right on by. The safety to the other side has originally flattened with the route of Golden, but tries to fall back under Watson late. That’s a losing battle, my friend. Love chucks this up and over the top, Watson nabs a TD and the Packers take a 41-14 lead. In the past, we’ve seen Love throw some of these routes a little flatter and across the field, allowing the WR a chance to adjust and run under the ball. With the safety falling under, Love goes over the top with this. Perfect throw. Albums listened to: Television – Marquee Moon ; Pixies – Doolittle ; Boys Noize – 7LLVISION ; Sennen – New Quiet ; Clinic – Wild In The Streets

title: Week 10 Power Ranking Round Up: Packers surge up rankings
summary: Just like that, Week 9 is in the books, and the Green Bay Packers rolled to a 45-27 win over the reigning AFC champion New England Patriots. Despite a very ugly start to the 2026 season, Green Bay finds itself with a 6-3 record, and actually trending upward. The national media has noticed the Packers’ […]
full_text: (Photo by Kathryn Riley/Getty Images) Just like that, Week 9 is in the books, and the Green Bay Packers rolled to a 45-27 win over the reigning AFC champion New England Patriots. Despite a very ugly start to the 2026 season, Green Bay finds itself with a 6-3 record, and actually trending upward. The national media has noticed the Packers’ marked improvement, with Jordan Love starting to find his way into MVP conversations. Xavier McKinney and Evan Williams are also entering the national conversation, after both recording interceptions in Sunday’s win, with McKinney hauling in two picks in the effort. To that point, Green Bay’s win over New England may have been the most complete game in all facets. Jordan Love was dealing, the rushing attack totaled over 100 yards as a team, the Packers defense got home for 4 sacks — also forcing 4 turnovers — and Trey Smack was 3 for 3 on field goals and 4 for 4 on extra points. Even further, Green Bay only committed 3 penalties for 14 yards in the game, a far cry from the team that was leading the league for most of the season. The Packers have won back-to-back games, and 5 of its last 6 contests. With the drubbing of New England, Green Bay has started to knock on the door of being one of the top teams in most outlets’ power rankings around the league. Let’s take a look at where the Packers stand after Week 9 around the NFL, prior to the trade deadline: NFL Power Rankings Entering Week 10: Sports Illustrated: 5th Sports Illustrated’s Conor Orr was the highest on Green Bay after Week 9, shooting them up into the top 5 after ranking them at 8th one week ago. Orr writes: “Here’s why I love what I do (honestly): I spent all offseason studying the run game, heavier personnel packages and the increased usage of 21 personnel. Jordan Love is going to come out and throw for 5,000 yards (seriously) with no running game to speak of whatsoever and the Packers are one of the best teams in the NFL.” USA Today: 7th NFL.com: 8th The Athletic: 9th Fox Sports: 9th CBS Sports: 10th Yahoo Sports: 10th Bleacher Report: 11th ESPN: 11th Pro Football Talk: 11th Even in the lowest-ranked piece, PFT notes Green Bay is certainly on the rise with Micah Parsons’ impending return. Should the Packers make any sort of trade at the deadline, whether it be offensive line, defensive line, linebacker, or running back, the sports world is buzzing about the team in Titletown.

title: Green Bay Packers News: Packers prep for NFL trade deadline
summary: Welcome to NFL Trade Deadline day! All trades need to be finalized by 4 p.m. Eastern time today as teams try to make the last-minute moves they think they need to become contenders or stockpile future assets. We’ve already seen quite a few moves leading up to the deadline with a few big-name players arriving […]
full_text: GREEN BAY, WI - OCTOBER 18: Green Bay Packers head coach Matt LaFleur and Green Bay Packers General Manager Brian Gutekunst talk prior to a game between the Green Bay Packers and the Dallas Cowboys on October 18, 2026 at Lambeau Field in Green Bay, WI. (Photo by Larry Radloff/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images) | Icon Sportswire via Getty Images Welcome to NFL Trade Deadline day! All trades need to be finalized by 4 p.m. Eastern time today as teams try to make the last-minute moves they think they need to become contenders or stockpile future assets. We’ve already seen quite a few moves leading up to the deadline with a few big-name players arriving at new teams, but the eternal question in these parts is whether or not the Packers will do anything. Certainly the Packers have needs. They could use some help on the offensive line, even as the guard situation seems to stabilize, and a running back with any amount of actual juice would be a blessing. And, if you believe the rumors going around, they’ve been sniffing around just about any trade-worth defensive lineman with a pulse. But the question is whether or not any of those moves would actually fix anything for them. Would throwing a new running back behind the offensive line as it’s presently constituted actually improve the running game? That seems doubtful, and I’m skeptical of the idea that they could add any linemen who would make a real difference, either. And there’s also the question of price. Take Jonathan Taylor, for instance. He’d definitely be a better running back option than anything the Packers currently have, but it sounds like it’s going to take a king’s ransom to pry him out of Indianapolis. The best intersection of price and value might be on the defensive line, but even then price is a huge consideration, since the Packers are already without a first round pick next year. Brian Gutekunst has gone on record about his high opinion of the 2027 draft class, and that seems to be the consensus view. Would he really surrender another valuable pick for a short-term player? The Packers, again, undeniably have needs. But what it’d take to fix them might take them out of the trade market this year. title: The Day After the Day After: The Houston Texans bolt past the LA Chargers 44-22
summary: The Day After the Day After…when the raw, immediate emotions from the aftermath of a game diminish into the realm of clarity and the proverbial (or literal) hangover no longer haunts the mind. With that, a review of Week 9 Get right game (part deux): It might be harder to find a better opponent to […]
full_text: INGLEWOOD, CALIFORNIA - NOVEMBER 08: Calen Bullock #2 of the Houston Texans reacts with teammates after recovering a fumble during the second half against the Los Angeles Chargersat SoFi Stadium on November 08, 2026 in Inglewood, California. (Photo by Ryan Sirius Sun/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Day After the Day After…when the raw, immediate emotions from the aftermath of a game diminish into the realm of clarity and the proverbial (or literal) hangover no longer haunts the mind. With that, a review of Week 9 Get right game (part deux): It might be harder to find a better opponent to face after a bye than the shockingly (pun somewhat intended) bad Chargers. While the Texans have underperformed based on preseason expectations, they are not like the Chargers. A fellow pre-season playoff contender, the Chargers opened the season 0-7. Catching a mercurial Texans team might have afforded them a chance to steal a win and salvage some pride in the season. Instead, this game went about as well as the Texans could hope for and then some. Houston put up a franchise-tying 44 points on the road, Stroud threw for 5 TDs and the defense got 8 sacks and 2 turnovers. Even the running game logged over 100 combined yards. All was not perfect, and Houston isn’t immediately back on the road to the Super Bowl, but this game checked a lot of boxes for Houston’s rebound hopes. Houston’s first get-well game came at the Titans to get off the winless streak. A second road-beatdown was a well-needed salve to start the second half of the schedule. Using the pass to set up the run: At times, it felt like the biggest problem for Stroud was not having enough footballs to throw around to all his receivers. 6 receivers had at least 2 receptions and over 20 yards receiving. Dell had his best game since he injured his leg at Kansas City in 2024, Boutte had a career day stretching the field and Collins merely added a catch-of-the-year option. Houston is never going to abandon the ground game but given that the offense moves more effectively through the air, the Texans might do well to favor the pass. Does it put pressure on the defense, especially if the team has multiple quick possessions? Yes. However, with the talent in the passing game and the noted shortfalls of the running game, Houston needs to play to their strengths. If nothing else, you borrow the Bill Walsh philosophy to use the pass to set up the run. Houston was more effective rushing the ball in the second half (69 yards vs. 35 1st half yards). With the Chargers needing to focus on limiting heavy aerial production, a decent ground game with Marks and company found a way to move the ball for effective gains. Trades all done?: At the time of publication, the Texans hadn’t added any new players via trade. If rumors are correct, the Texans are looking at help at the RB and safety position. Most might dream of Taylor, Barkley or Henry in the backfield, but would Houston want to pay up with their limited 2027/28 Draft capital for a back that is going to already stress a team that is going to be well over the cap at the start of the offseason. Pitre’s return aided the defensive backfield, but Blankenship’s absence and struggles are still issues. Plus, safety depth could help a squad that needs special teams reinforcements. While Caserio fears no trade, it does not seem likely that Houston will make another big move trade-wise (unlike division rival Jacksonville, which made some major trades in the past 36 hours to aid the defense). THE CRITICAL PLAY: 6:43, 2nd Quarter, HOU Ball @ HOU 37, 2nd and 5; QB CJ Stroud with a deep pass to WR Tank Dell for a 63-yard TD. Aside from the whole first-TD-in-almost-two-calendar-years-plotline, this play was actually critical to the game’s momentum. The Chargers just cashed in on Stroud’s INT to cut the deficit to 10-9. Houston, after scoring 10 points on their first two drives, had a punt and an INT on the next two. They needed to get something going. After a short 5-yard pass to Harrison, Houston set up in a shotgun passing formation. Dell, lined up in the slot on the right side, ran and out-and-up pattern, just getting behind the Chargers DB. Stroud hit Dell in stride with a deep strike, allowing Dell to sprint straight to end zone. While Houston would be forced to punt on its next possession, this TD seemed to uplift the overall play of the team, as it was the start of a 28-0 run in the game. FUN WITH NUMBERS: 12: Total number of TFLs for the Texans: This is what most expected from the Houston defense this year. This tied the Houston franchise for 3rd-most in a single game (@ TEN in 2023). The franchise record is 15, set against Seattle in 2009. The most in the Ryans’ regime: 14, against TEN in 2024. 2-1: Record in 2026 when Houston rushes for over 100 yards in a game. When we talk about Houston leaning into its effective passing game, this might be a counter to that. You can’t not run the ball (this isn’t the run-and-shoot), but finding that balance is critical. Play to your strengths, and if the passing game is doing its job, the running game will follow. GAME BALLS: WR Tank Dell: 4 receptions/105 yards/1 TD. Welcome back Mr. Dell. We’ve missed you. Now, about cleanly catching those punts… QB CJ Stroud : An INT…really? Well, he did make up for it with a 21-of-35/384 yard/5 TD day. I suppose that is adequate enough for a game ball. Texans DL: Logged 7 of the team’s 8 sacks and 9 of the teams 12 TFLs. Anderson, Clowney and Rankins are the first trio of Texans to ever record at least 2.0 sacks each in a single game. CB Kamri Lassiter: 2 tackles (1 solo)/1 TFL/4 PDs: If anyone needed a bounce-back game, it was Lassiter. Was he perfect? No (arguably the miscommunication on the Chargers’ 4th and 1 was more about miscommunication vs. individual corner play) but on this day, he looked more like the top CB2 of 2025 than whatever that was to start the 2026 season. Would be nice if he kept up that level of play. SHOULD BE FORCED TO PRESS ALL OF JIM HARBAUGH’S KHAKIS WHILE LISTENING TO HIS INANE PRESS CONFERENCES ON REPEAT: Texans punting game: If there was a part of the game that didn’t look all that great, it was the punting game. Only needed for 3 attempts, but Kroeger’s two first half punts are best not dwelt upon. Tank Dell, for all his receiving goodness, muffed a punt in the 1st half that could have seriously altered the momentum of the game. At least the squad didn’t allow the Chargers to even attempt a return. However, that part of the game is going to have to pick it up in the weeks ahead. Chargers OC Mike McDaniel: The Chargers did finally snap a 37 non-TD possession streak against the Texans, but that came in the 4th quarter of a game the Texans lead 38-9. The Chargers did add another TD, but aside from impacting the betting lines, the offense did not look good at all. title: Colts ownership just showed “Find a Way” was not to be taken lightly
summary: The challenge came down from the top. Was it a challenge or an ultimatum? Either way, the marching orders for 2026 were set in training camp by the owner of the Indianapolis Colts, Carlie Irsay-Gordon. The mantra was simple: “Find a Way.” The underpinnings were subtle but understood, win or else. After the trade deadline, […]
full_text: The challenge came down from the top. Was it a challenge or an ultimatum? Either way, the marching orders for 2026 were set in training camp by the owner of the Indianapolis Colts, Carlie Irsay-Gordon. The mantra was simple: “Find a Way.” The underpinnings were subtle but understood, win or else. After the trade deadline, the Colts are finding themselves on the “else” side of things. DeForest Buckner, Quenton Nelson, Keenan Allen, and Josh Downs all wear new uniforms now. Grover Stewart and Jonathan Taylor were on the chopping block too. Let’s not forget about Chris Ballard either. David Bowie sang about “changes,” and the Colts organization has gone through plenty. The worst or possibly best part of it all is that those changes don’t appear to be done. Irsay-Gordon inherited a mess with a team that hasn’t produced in a decade and a GM who was around for all of it. Her message sent a shot across the bow, seemingly, in the softest way possible. Find a Way was all she said. What she meant can be seen from top to bottom in this organization. Shane Steichen and Daniel Jones’ days appear to be numbered too. The production isn’t there, and they haven’t found a way, to say the least. New owners, coaches, or even CEOs of companies like to have their own people, those that fit their vision. The good ones don’t come in and start slashing without cause, though. If someone shows their worth and circumstances are right, chances are they stay. Irsay-Gordon did that. Everyone got another chance. She could have cleaned house when she took over. She would have been more than justified to do that after last year’s collapse too, but she didn’t. Everyone got plenty of grace, but the NFL isn’t built on grace. It is built on winning. It is built on finding a way to win no matter what. Pieces of this once-proud franchise are scattered on the ground. The facade is broken and all is exposed. When put under the microscope and intense pressure to perform, the Colts couldn’t. If they can’t do it, Carlie Irsay-Gordon will find someone who can because that’s what it’s about. Win, just win. Find a way to fight through it, make the play, and come out on top. Right now, the Colts are at the bottom. It’s going to take a lot, but this organization must find a way to rise, once again, to the top.
author: Jon Spradley

title: Stampede Blue Reacts Survey (Week 10): Are Colts fans confident after major roster changes?
summary: Welcome to SB Nation Reacts, where Colts fans and NFL fans nationwide share their opinions throughout the season. The Indianapolis Colts have officially entered a new chapter following one of the most eventful trade deadlines in franchise history. After parting ways with Quenton Nelson and DeForest Buckner two weeks ago, Indianapolis continued its roster overhaul […]
full_text: Welcome to SB Nation Reacts, where Colts fans and NFL fans nationwide share their opinions throughout the season. The Indianapolis Colts have officially entered a new chapter following one of the most eventful trade deadlines in franchise history. After parting ways with Quenton Nelson and DeForest Buckner two weeks ago, Indianapolis continued its roster overhaul Tuesday by sending veteran wide receiver Keenan Allen to the San Francisco 49ers and Josh Downs to the Kansas City Chiefs. The departures of four established players have allowed the Colts to accumulate additional draft capital, although they have also created significant holes across a roster that was already struggling to compete. With Chris Ballard no longer in charge and a new general manager expected to take over during the offseason, the organization appears increasingly focused on building toward the future rather than salvaging the remainder of 2026. Interestingly, Jonathan Taylor was one of the few major names who ultimately remained in Indianapolis despite considerable interest from around the league. The Colts reportedly received multiple offers involving second-round selections but maintained a much higher asking price for their star running back, deciding to retain him rather than accept compensation they considered insufficient. Keeping Taylor provides some stability for an offense that has already lost several important contributors, although questions remain about whether his remaining prime seasons will align with the franchise’s next competitive window. The decision also leaves the next general manager with an important choice regarding the long-term direction of the offense. Meanwhile, the situation on the field hasn’t improved much. Indianapolis suffered its fifth consecutive defeat Sunday, falling 27-23 to the Dallas Cowboys and dropping to 2-7 on the season. Last week’s Reacts survey showed that just 19 percent of Colts fans believed the franchise was headed in the right direction, down from 31 percent the previous week and 47 percent two weeks earlier. While the continued losing has understandably frustrated fans, the organization’s willingness to make significant changes could provide some optimism that a more sustainable future is being built. With several additional draft selections now available but plenty of uncertainty surrounding the roster, coaching staff and quarterback position, the question remains whether fans believe the Colts are finally taking the necessary steps toward returning to contention. summary: The Indianapolis Colts continued to dismantle their roster until the final hour of Tuesday’s NFL trade deadline, sending slot receiver Josh Downs, along with a seventh-round pick to the Kansas City Chiefs in exchange for a fourth and fifth-round pick in the 2027 NFL Draft. The aggressive fire sale marks the fourth trade the Colts […]
full_text: KANSAS CITY, MISSOURI - SEPTEMBER 20: Josh Downs #2 of the Indianapolis Colts catches a pass during an NFL football game against the Kansas City Chiefs at Arrowhead Stadium on September 20, 2026 in Kansas City, Missouri. (Photo by Kevin Sabitus/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Indianapolis Colts continued to dismantle their roster until the final hour of Tuesday’s NFL trade deadline, sending slot receiver Josh Downs, along with a seventh-round pick to the Kansas City Chiefs in exchange for a fourth and fifth-round pick in the 2027 NFL Draft. The aggressive fire sale marks the fourth trade the Colts have made to begin the rebuild during this disastrous campaign. Trade! The Chiefs are acquiring WR Josh Downs and a 2027 seventh-round pick from the Colts for 2027 fourth-round and fifth-round picks, sources tell @ringer @netflixsports . Kansas City lands a receiver at the buzzer, while Indianapolis keeps loading up for the future. pic.twitter.com/ctYRKBME8w — Tom Pelissero (@TomPelissero) November 10, 2026 Indianapolis granted Downs’ request and traded away a second starting receiver, along with Keenan Allen to the San Francisco 49ers, with intentions to stack as much draft capital as possible. The 25-year-old receiver made his request public in October, signaling he was ready to leave Indy. The Colts did all four former players a solid by sending them to active contenders and it’s fair compensation rather than losing Downs for nothing in free agency. pic.twitter.com/SWGjirDe9N — JD (@JoshDowns) November 10, 2026 Downs’ trade request came after weeks of frustration, while Indianapolis continued to sell off cornerstone pieces of its roster. In fact, each of the last four losses have prompted the organization to make a move. From the firing of GM Chris Ballard after the Titans loss, to the trades of two cornerstone captains on the front line after the Vikings loss, to the pair of starting receivers who were moved in the final hours before the deadline. In Sunday’s 27-23 loss to the Dallas Cowboys, Downs looked disengaged on the field and had two noticeable drops. It was a tough performance for a receiver on a contract year, realizing his final curtain call with the Colts was three catches for 24 receiving yards. Downs has collected just 33 catches for 354 receiving yards and one touchdown in nine games this season. Josh Downs pic.twitter.com/iUA5UF1rSq — Ian Hartitz (@Ihartitz) March 12, 2025 Indianapolis selected Downs in the third round (79th overall) of the 2023 NFL Draft. The North Carolina product instantly established himself as one of the most dependable rookie targets, fetching 68 receptions for 771 yards and two touchdowns. He made clear improvements in his second season and notably had the best footwork among the Colts receiver corps throughout training camp. Downs improved with 72 catches for 803 yards and five touchdowns in his sophomore campaign. However, his production steadily declined since Daniel Jones became the Colts starting quarterback. Downs endured a slight increase in drops during the 2025 season and recorded 58 receptions for 566 yards and four touchdowns. It looked bright out the gate as Downs started off the opening drive of the 2026 season with nearly 40 receiving yards, but he’s been held in check in essentially every game since checking out in October. Kansas City was desperate to add another weapon for franchise quarterback Patrick Mahomes II. The Chiefs aimed to acquire a young, talented receiver with a proven ability to create separation out of the slot. With injuries to Xavier Worthy (hamstring), and Tyquan Thorton (ankle) out on IR, Downs joins a receiver corps that features Rashee Rice, Jalen Royals and Nikko Remigio. Josh Downs Route Running. pic.twitter.com/nDEwFDKnUq — Football Performances (@NFLPerformances) September 21, 2026 Two weeks ago, the Colts traded All-Pro left guard Quenton Nelson to Seattle, then sent All-Pro defensive tackle DeForest Buckner back to San Francisco. On Tuesday, Indianapolis sent veteran receiver Keenan Allen to San Francisco for a 2027 sixth-rounder, then Downs became the fourth player shipped out of Indianapolis to stock more draft capital. Firing the GM of nearly a decade and trading away four starters in the span of three weeks is another reminder that the focus has entirely shifted toward the future. Downs wanted no part of what that future looked like in Indianapolis, so it was best to find a willing trade partner in the Chiefs.

title: Colts RB Jonathan Taylor will reportedly not be moved ahead of Tuesday’s NFL trade deadline
summary: According to NFL Insider and The Ringer’s Tom Pelissero, the Indianapolis Colts will not move star running back Jonathan Taylor ahead of the league’s Tuesday 4 PM EST trade deadline: This seems to be the recent league-wide consensus among NFL insiders, unless Indianapolis was blown away by an offer—which likely would’ve entailed either a “Christian […]
full_text: INDIANAPOLIS, INDIANA - NOVEMBER 8: Jonathan Taylor #28 of the Indianapolis Colts stands for the national anthem prior to a game against the Dallas Cowboys at Lucas Oil Stadium on November 8, 2026 in Indianapolis, Indiana. (Photo by Lauren Leigh Bacho/Getty Images) | Getty Images According to NFL Insider and The Ringer’s Tom Pelissero, the Indianapolis Colts will not move star running back Jonathan Taylor ahead of the league’s Tuesday 4 PM EST trade deadline: The Colts won’t trade star RB Jonathan Taylor by today’s deadline, sources tell @ringer @netflixsports . Multiple teams offered a second-round pick and more for Taylor. But the Colts wanted a blockbuster offer to even consider it. Instead, Taylor stays in Indy. pic.twitter.com/FH1NtHa8k6 — Tom Pelissero (@TomPelissero) November 10, 2026 This seems to be the recent league-wide consensus among NFL insiders, unless Indianapolis was blown away by an offer—which likely would’ve entailed either a “Christian McCaffrey-esque” package or first round draft pick. While the New York Giants reportedly recently offered a second round pick, plus a little more in draft pick compensation, the Colts immediately responded with a “no,” and head coach John Harbaugh’s team since withdrew the offer—although that trade negotiation likely still remained fluid the past 48 hours, subject to possible change. On the season, Taylor has 161 carries for 656 total rushing yards and 8 rushing touchdowns, but has seen his workload limited in recent weeks, as the Colts attempted to keep him healthy for a potential trade opportunity. Likewise, Taylor hasn’t been running like himself the past two weeks, perhaps making some “business decisions” before he would’ve imminently joined a new team. He had an untimely red zone fumble late in last Sunday’s home loss to the Dallas Cowboys, and has lost a fumble in 3 of his last 4 games, so his ball security needs to improve. That being said, since he’s staying in Indianapolis, I would expect to see the Colts give Taylor closer to 20 carries going forward, while having productive rookie running back Seth McGowan playing a more prominent role as a change-of-base rusher to keep Taylor fresher down the stretch and limit his mileage during what’s another lost season in Indianapolis. Taylor is one of those running backs who gets better the more touches he gets over the course of a game, wearing out the opposing defense with “body shots”, before a lot of times, finally breaking off a big run for the TKO. I would expect him to look more like his old self, now that he knows he’s staying in Indianapolis for the remainder of the 2026 campaign—and will assume his more prominent role within the Colts offense yet again.

title: Colts trade veteran WR Keenan Allen to 49ers for sixth-round pick
summary: The Indianapolis Colts have made another trade ahead of Tuesday’s NFL trade deadline, sending six-time Pro Bowl wide receiver Keenan Allen to the San Francisco 49ers in exchange for a 2027 sixth-round pick, according to NFL insider Tom Pelissero. The move marks the third significant departure from Indianapolis over the past two weeks, following the […]
full_text: JACKSONVILLE, FL - NOVEMBER 01:Keenan Allen #10 of the Indianapolis Colts runs during the game between the Jacksonville Jaguars and the Indianapolis Colts on November 1, 2026 at EverBank Stadium in Jacksonville, Fl. (Photo by David Rosenblum/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images) | Icon Sportswire via Getty Images The Indianapolis Colts have made another trade ahead of Tuesday’s NFL trade deadline, sending six-time Pro Bowl wide receiver Keenan Allen to the San Francisco 49ers in exchange for a 2027 sixth-round pick, according to NFL insider Tom Pelissero. Trade! The Colts are sending six-time Pro Bowl WR Keenan Allen to the 49ers for a 2027 sixth-round pick, sources tell @ringer @netflixsports . pic.twitter.com/tDt5H7HgId — Tom Pelissero (@TomPelissero) November 10, 2026 The move marks the third significant departure from Indianapolis over the past two weeks, following the trades of Quenton Nelson to the Seattle Seahawks and DeForest Buckner to San Francisco. With the Colts sitting at 2-7 and increasingly focused on rebuilding following the dismissal of general manager Chris Ballard, the organization continues to accumulate future draft capital while parting ways with established veterans. Allen, 34, joined Indianapolis in August on a one-year contract after spending the majority of his career with the Los Angeles Chargers, along with a brief stint in Chicago. The veteran receiver was brought in to provide experience and reliability to a receiving corps that had undergone significant changes during the offseason, while also reuniting with head coach Shane Steichen, who previously worked with Allen during their time together with the Chargers. Despite the Colts’ struggles offensively, Allen remained a dependable target for quarterback Daniel Jones, recording 40 receptions for 351 yards and one touchdown through eight games. Although he is no longer the explosive receiver he once was, his route running, ability to create separation underneath and experience against various defensive coverages continued to make him a useful contributor, even if the passing offense looked very ugly. For San Francisco, the acquisition addresses a position group that has been severely affected by injuries throughout the season. The 49ers have been searching for additional receiving help as they attempt to remain atop the NFC playoff race, and Allen provides an experienced option who can immediately contribute without requiring a substantial investment in draft capital. The trade also reunites Allen with Buckner, whom San Francisco acquired from Indianapolis on October 27 for a 2027 fourth-round selection. The 49ers have now added two former Colts veterans in the span of two weeks, strengthening both sides of the football as they pursue another Super Bowl run. From Indianapolis’ perspective, receiving a sixth-round selection for a 34-year-old receiver on an expiring contract represents a reasonable return, particularly given the organization’s current direction. Allen was not going to factor into the Colts’ long-term plans, and securing a guaranteed draft pick allows the team to gain something from a player who otherwise could have departed in free agency. His departure also creates additional opportunities for younger receivers (Burks notably) to earn playing time over the remainder of the season, while raising further questions about whether Indianapolis will make any additional moves before the 4 p.m. ET deadline. With Jonathan Taylor and Josh Downs continuing to attract trade speculation, the Colts may not be finished reshaping their roster.

title: Chiefs trade for Colts wide receiver Josh Downs. What to know:
summary: After a long wait on Tuesday, trade news finally broke for the Kansas City Chiefs at the position we all anticipated: wide receiver. According to NFL Insider Tom Pelissero, the Chiefs struck a deal with the Indianapolis Colts to acquire Josh Downs, a fourth-year receiver with 2,494 career receiving yards and 12 touchdowns to his […]
full_text: (Photo by Kevin Sabitus/Getty Images) | Getty Images After a long wait on Tuesday, trade news finally broke for the Kansas City Chiefs at the position we all anticipated: wide receiver. Trade! The Chiefs are acquiring WR Josh Downs and a 2027 seventh-round pick from the Colts for 2027 fourth-round and fifth-round picks, sources tell @ringer @netflixsports . Kansas City lands a receiver at the buzzer, while Indianapolis keeps loading up for the future. pic.twitter.com/ctYRKBME8w — Tom Pelissero (@TomPelissero) November 10, 2026 According to NFL Insider Tom Pelissero , the Chiefs struck a deal with the Indianapolis Colts to acquire Josh Downs, a fourth-year receiver with 2,494 career receiving yards and 12 touchdowns to his name. The 25-year-old wideout is in the final year of his original rookie deal after being selected in the third round of the 2023 NFL Draft. The Chiefs are sending the Colts a fourth- and fifth-round pick in the 2027 draft for Downs and a 2027 seventh-round pick. According to NFL Insider Jordan Schultz , Kansas City offered a fourth-round pick more than a week ago, but Indianapolis sat on it, hoping for more. Downs is just the latest Colts player to be traded in a lost season for Indianapolis; the team also traded away starters in defensive lineman DeForest Buckner, left guard Quenton Nelson, and receiver Keenan Allen. pic.twitter.com/SWGjirDe9N — JD (@JoshDowns) November 10, 2026 On X , after the news broke, Downs appeared to be excited to join the Chiefs . Kansas City will welcome Downs after he led the Colts’ offense in receiving yards (354) in the first nine weeks while playing 80% of the snaps. Keenan Allen (40) had more receptions for Indianapolis than Downs (33), but the two tied in touchdowns (1) and first downs (20). Downs has a career-low catch rate of 58% this season and has been faulted with four drops, according to Pro Football Focus , but that didn’t seem to be an issue in Week 2 against the Chiefs. In the overtime finish, Downs gashed Kansas City’s secondary with seven catches for 72 yards on nine targets. He has primarily been a slot receiver throughout his career in Indianapolis; this season, he has lined up as a slot receiver on 70% of his pass plays, per PFF . According to PFF, Josh Downs has seen the seventh-most targets vs. man coverage in the NFL this year (19) He's caught 11 passes for 126 yards and 9 first downs on those plays — Ron Kopp Jr (@RonOnChiefs) November 10, 2026 The Chiefs will insert him into the receiver rotation that features Rashee Rice (50% of his snaps in the slot) and Cyrus Allen (53%) as current options out of the slot; Xavier Worthy — who tweaked his hamstring just before the end of the Week 9 game — has played over 70% on the outside. Does this transaction move the needle for you on whether the Chiefs are a Super Bowl contender this season? Let us know in the comments.

title: Arrowhead Pride Midseason Awards: The Chiefs’ Most Improved Player
summary: There are eight games in the books — with nine more to go. The Kansas City Chiefs’ 2026 season reaches its midpoint in Week 10. Because the team’s bye came so early in Week 5, we have decided to move our annual awards to midseason. Nine members of the Arrowhead Pride writing staff each had one […]
full_text: (Photo by David Eulitt/Getty Images) | Getty Images There are eight games in the books — with nine more to go. The Kansas City Chiefs ’ 2026 season reaches its midpoint in Week 10. Because the team’s bye came so early in Week 5, we have decided to move our annual awards to midseason. Nine members of the Arrowhead Pride writing staff each had one vote for our seven midseason awards, so nine votes will be tallied for each award. In this post, we’ll reveal our most improved player to this point in the season. DB Chris Roland-Wallace VOTING: DB Chris Roland-Wallace (4), DE Felix Anudike-Uzomah (3), DE Ashton Gillotte (1), CB Nohl Williams (1) Defensive back Chris Roland-Wallace joined the Chiefs as a rookie free agent out of USC following the 2024 NFL draft. An impressive camp saw him succeed in his long-shot bid for the final roster, and he instantly became one of Kansas City’s best special teams players. He flashed on defense throughout his first two seasons, but Roland-Wallace’s versatility has been instrumental as the Chiefs have managed injuries throughout the secondary early on. He played mainly safety to start the year as Chamarri Conner worked his way back from a training camp knee injury. As a safety, Pro Football Focus has given him a grade of 72.2 , ranking 20th out of 100 grades for the position. His 77.6 coverage grade on their metric ranks sixth of the 100 safeties. Pro Football Focus also credits Roland-Wallace with 14 solo tackles in run defense or open-field situations. With much of his work coming in the slot, Roland-Wallace has surrendered a somewhat high 84.6% completion percentage. However, he has been outstanding at limiting the damage in the middle of the field. Over eight games, he has surrendered only 6.4 yards per completion. In two games since veteran L’Jarius Sneed was placed on the Reserve/Injured (IR) list with a chronic knee injury, Roland-Wallace has seen his defensive snap count rise above 70% each of the last two weeks. The results on the field suggest he probably shouldn’t give up the workload, even if Sneed eventually returns. Roland-Wallace may never be a star, but he plays multiple roles and should stretch out a decent career as at least a high-end backup. Kansas City could have an interesting decision on him after the season. Roland-Wallace is in the final year of the three-year rookie free agent contract he signed in 2024. He will qualify for restricted free agency (RFA) following the season. Over the Cap projects the minimum RFA tender to be $3.8 million for the 2027 offseason. Because Roland-Wallace went undrafted, he would not net the Chiefs any draft-pick compensation if he signed with a new team (although Kansas City would have the right to match any offer). It is not hard to imagine another team signing him to a contract that may be difficult for the Chiefs—always tight against the salary cap—to swallow. Don’t be surprised if one of the team’s first offseason moves is a modest extension for Roland-Wallace to get ahead of this scenario.

full_text: (Photo by Kevin Sabitus/Getty Images) | Getty Images In Week 9 of the 2026 NFL regular season, the Kansas City Chiefs beat up on the New York Jets to advance to 6-2. Let’s see how the national media reacted to it in this week’s sampling of power rankings: ESPN : 6 (No change) Most important game of the second half: Week 12 at the Bills If the Chiefs want any shot of earning the AFC’s top seed, which would include a first-round bye and home-field advantage in the postseason, they’ll have to go on the road and beat one of their biggest rivals. A win over the Bills on Thanksgiving night would also boost the Chiefs’ odds of passing the Broncos to win the AFC West crown. The Chiefs have played their best this season when at Arrowhead Stadium, averaging 30.0 points per game. — Nate Taylor The Athletic : 4 (Up from 5) Midseason grade: A Sunday was just another example of Patrick Mahomes leaning on Travis Kelce (four catches for 72 yards). The two have now connected for 9,365 yards, surpassing Phillip Rivers and Antonio Gates for the most of any NFL quarterback-tight end pair. The Chiefs may have injuries at wide receiver, but they still rank fourth in the league in EPA per play. — Chad Graff and Josh Kendall Pro Football Talk : 6 (Up from 7) The kicker position shouldn’t be a pick-your-poison proposition. — Mike Florio CBSSports.com : 6 (Up from 7) The defense came alive in a big way against the Jets, getting five sacks. That’s something they will need going forward. The good news was they escaped a possible major injury for Patrick Mahomes. — Pete Prisco Yahoo! Sports : 6 (Up from 7) The most promising part of the Chiefs’ win on Sunday against the Jets might be that Chris Jones and George Karlaftis each had two sacks. Karlaftis had two sacks for the season before Sunday, Jones had just half of a sack, and that’s a big reason the Chiefs’ pass rush ranked near the bottom of the league. Even with five sacks as a team Sunday, Kansas City still has just 14 sacks. That’s the fourth-lowest mark in the NFL. The Chiefs have been doing fine on defense without much of a pass rush, ranking top 10 in yards and points allowed. But it’s hard to be a top-10 defense while ranking in the bottom five in sacks. Perhaps the performance against the Jets will get the pass rush going, and in turn boost a defense that has already played well. — Frank Schwab USA Today : 9 (Up from 10) It’s easy to miss, but coordinator Steve Spagnuolo’s defense is starting to find a groove − allowing more than 300 yards just once since the Week 5 bye and surrendering more than 20 points just once over the same period. — Nate Davis Sports Illustrated : 9 (Up from 12) I wonder if there was a more wild series of events in a professional football game this year than, right before the half, Patrick Mahomes appearing to have sustained a horrific injury, the Jets squandering the subsequent possession with a missed field goal, Mahomes returning after mere minutes on the sideline and Harrison Butker missing both the initial field goal attempt and the post-penalty field goal attempt. The beautiful game, my friend. — Conor Orr Sporting News : 5 (Up from 6) Patrick Mahomes and Travis Kelce are up to connecting for 9,360 passing/receiving yards, a new record for a quarterback and tight end combination. Kenneth Walker III is on pace for 24 total TDs and can challenge the single-season franchise record of 27. — Vinnie Iyer FOX Sports : 4 (Up from 5) Patrick Mahomes ’ elbow injury gave everybody quite a scare, but the guy is just superhuman, I guess. He got right back in the game and led the Chiefs on a few more touchdown drives in their rout of the Jets, and Andy Reid made it sound like he’s going to be OK in his Monday morning press conference. Obviously, they’re not the same team without him, so his injury needs to be monitored. When healthy, the duo of Mahomes and RB Kenneth Walker is as dangerous as any combo the Chiefs have had during their dynasty. And don’t forget, they’ve got a great chance coming up to prove it in the game they circled on their calendar all along: Thanksgiving night in Buffalo against the Bills. Stat To Know : Patrick Mahomes improved to 18-0 against teams entering at least four games below .500, extending the best record by a quarterback since 1970 (minimum 15 such starts). — Ralph Vacchiano
