title: Chiefs Film Review: Analyzing the run game against the Jets
summary: The Kansas City Chiefs’ run game has powered their offense all season, and Sunday against the New York Jets was no different. The Chiefs’ running backs finished with 27 carries for 155 yards (5.7 yards per carry) with two touchdowns. What made the performance impressive was that Kansas City’s longest run of the day only […]
full_text: (Photo by David Eulitt/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Kansas City Chiefs ’ run game has powered their offense all season, and Sunday against the New York Jets was no different. The Chiefs’ running backs finished with 27 carries for 155 yards (5.7 yards per carry) with two touchdowns. What made the performance impressive was that Kansas City’s longest run of the day only went for 13 yards. It was a surgical performance on the ground, as the Chiefs finished with a 55% success rate. What powered the Chiefs’ impressive run game against the Jets? Let’s dive into some film: This is an impressive play from multiple offensive linemen on this play. Center Creed Humphrey creates displacement on the 1-technique, getting push and keeping him from falling back inside. Left tackle Kahlil Benson and left guard Kingsley Suamataia do a fantastic job on the backside of this run. Suamataia gives enough of a punch, and Benson is able to drive his hips into the defender’s outside shoulder and into the linebacker, opening up the cutback for Kenneth Walker to hit. This is impressive from a run-blocking and scheme standpoint. The pre-snap motion bumps the weakside linebacker out of the box, bringing a smaller safety straight into the run fit. The backside defensive end worries about the bootleg and stays home. This gives the Chiefs six blockers to block five, which creates a ton of space. The Chiefs run weakside zone here. Humphrey creates horizontal movement on the nose by driving on his inside shoulder. Benson cuts off the backside by getting around the three-technique again, which is not an easy block. Benson was dominant on the backside of these blocks, and that’s critical in the zone run scheme. This play is a good example of the value of having a player as dynamic as Walker in the backfield. The Chiefs run a shortside toss to Walker here, but Jets outside linebacker David Bailey is all over it. This should be a 1-2 yard run at most, but Walker’s ability to get all the way backside and make multiple defenders miss is rare. He puts an incredible amount of pressure on a defense horizontally. You’re not always going to get the right run call into the defense, so having a back that can mitigate those moments has transformed the offense. The Chiefs’ under-center run game has been rediscovered this year, and this was a great play using it. The Chiefs are running outside zone from 13 personnel. Benson gets stonewalled by the frontside defensive end to start this play. Benson actually does a good job sustaining his block, but there’s still no frontside gap. Fortunately, a massive gap opens on the backside as right tackle Jaylon Moore and right guard Trey Smith annihilate the three-technique and move him vertically, creating an easy cutback for Walker to hit. Being able to run both directions is an underrated part of a good run game. Kansas City’s offensive line can do that because both Moore and Benson can block frontside or backside in zone blocking, and the Chiefs’ interior offensive line does a great job clearing space to create cutback lanes. Walker’s footwork and vision set this up here. Walker gets the linebacker going the wrong way by getting backside, faking a cut left, then immediately bouncing it back to the right, which lets Humphrey cut him off. Smith and Moore help create the hole, but Walker’s ability to cut at full speed is rare and lets him set up defenders in the hole. Benson is excellent on the backside of these zone runs, and the Jets had no answer for it. Benson creates horizontal displacement and gives Walker the easiest cutback to get north on. Emmett Johnson didn’t get much run into late in the game, but in the limited run he got, he also flashed. The Chiefs run that weakside zone concept again, which Benson isn’t quite as good at. The defensive end is able to disengage his block and, in theory, has the angle to get to Johnson, but Johnson hits the jets to beat him to the spot and gets around the edge. Being able to hit that frontside edge is very important in any zone concept, as teams will overplay the cutback lane if you can’t hit that. Seeing Johnson do that on film is important. The Chiefs mainly run zone blocking with Walker, which makes sense with his skillset. However, this offensive line can block gap runs, and frankly, they should do it more. Johnson feels like a natural fit in that role, and the Chiefs give him a chance to do that here on his touchdown. The Chiefs are running power with Smith pulling. Suamataia and Benson set up this block again, annihilating the head-up defensive tackle. Johnson presses to the left, sees the space created by that block, and scores. The Bottom Line The Chiefs’ run game has been so much better this year for numerous reasons, including Andy Reid’s playcalling. But ultimately, personnel matters, and Kansas City’s personnel is better this year. Having Walker in the backfield has changed everything for the Chiefs. It’s brought life back to the Chiefs’ dormant zone run game, as they now have a back that can explode through the run lanes created by the offensive line. He can make people miss in space and is a threat to take anything to the house. Walker’s vision and agility have been special this year and power the offense. But the offensive line deserves credit too. Benson has been so much better than expected. Moore is shaky in pass protection, but he does give the team something as a run blocker. With Benson and Moore out there, it’s almost like the Chiefs have five guards on the field. Both Benson and Moore have guard traits as run blockers. They’re best when they can move defenders horizontally with their strength and first step. Having what is essentially five guards creates so much extra space for Walker to exploit, and that’s been huge this year.
author: Nate Christensen

title: Kingdom Keys revisited: Chiefs check most boxes in win over Jets
summary: Every week, “Kingdom Keys” identifies three things the Kansas City Chiefs must accomplish to win their upcoming game. Now, it is time to revisit those keys and determine whether Kansas City actually turned them. Against the New York Jets, the Chiefs accomplished two keys and partially accomplished another. Let’s revisit this week’s Kingdom Keys. Key […]
full_text: (Photo by Kevin Sabitus/Getty Images) | Getty Images Every week, “ Kingdom Keys ” identifies three things the Kansas City Chiefs must accomplish to win their upcoming game. Now, it is time to revisit those keys and determine whether Kansas City actually turned them. Against the New York Jets , the Chiefs accomplished two keys and partially accomplished another. Let’s revisit this week’s Kingdom Keys. Key No. 1: Stretch the field Verdict: Partially accomplished The offensive key was for the Chiefs to rediscover their ability to stretch the field. The Chiefs created explosive plays against the Jets, but they did not fully restore their vertical passing game. Patrick Mahomes connected with Travis Kelce for a 38-yard gain, while Rashee Rice produced a 21-yard reception and Walker scored on a 25-yard catch. However, those plays didn’t come from Mahomes consistently beating New York deep. Much of the production came after the catch. Rice’s 21-yard reception came mostly from his ability to gain yards after securing the football, while Walker’s touchdown came on a short pass that he turned into a 25-yard score. Even Kelce’s 38-yard reception was more of an intermediate completion that developed into an explosive gain than a true downfield strike. Mahomes finished 23 of 31 for 242 yards, two touchdowns and no interceptions, but Kansas City still did not show that it could consistently threaten a defense over the top without Thornton. The Chiefs did, however, accomplish the larger goal behind the key. Their ability to create chunk plays underneath forced the Jets to defend more than just the running game and helped create opportunities for Walker. Walker finished with 102 rushing yards, 41 receiving yards and three total touchdowns on 22 touches. After being held below 70 rushing yards in consecutive games, he again looked like the centerpiece of Kansas City’s offense. The Chiefs got the result they wanted, but they reached it differently than expected. Kansas City generated explosive plays and reopened the running game, but the offense still needs to prove it possesses a has an impactful vertical threat. Key No. 2: Bring back Sack Nation Verdict: Accomplished The defensive goal was clear: the Chiefs needed at least three sacks. They finished with five. Even more encouraging was how Kansas City generated that pressure. Steve Spagnuolo’s defense recorded all five sacks without blitzing. Chris Jones finally delivered the performance Kansas City had been waiting for, recording two sacks after entering the game with only half a sack this season. George Karlaftis added two more, while rookie Ashton Gillotte contributed the fifth. The pressure became especially important after halftime. New York moved the ball well enough to reach scoring range several times in the first half, but the Chiefs kept the Jets out of the end zone and forced them to settle for four field goals. Once Kansas City took control of the score, Jones and the defensive line attacked Geno Smith in obvious passing situations. The Jets never scored again after halftime. This was the return of Sack Nation the Chiefs needed. Jones played like his CEO again, Karlaftis provided pressure from the edge, and the defensive line closed the game without Spagnuolo having to expose his secondary by sending additional rushers. The challenge now is turning one dominant performance into consistent production. Key No. 3: Win on third down Verdict: Accomplished The X-factor was third-down efficiency on both sides of the football. Kansas City needed its offense to extend possessions while its defense found ways to get off the field. The Chiefs succeeded in both areas. Kansas City converted six of its 11 third-down opportunities, while New York finished just one of 11. That difference let the Chiefs sustain touchdown drives while forcing the Jets to settle for field goals or give the ball back. The Chiefs’ defense was particularly effective when it mattered most. New York reached Kansas City territory several times in the first half, but the defense kept tightening in critical situations. That kept the game within reach even when the Chiefs’ offense and special teams struggled early. Kansas City then controlled the second half. The Chiefs scored touchdowns on their first two possessions after halftime, while the Jets’ offense repeatedly stalled. By the fourth quarter, a two-point halftime margin had become a comfortable three-score lead. Third down told the story of the game: Kansas City finished drives, while New York did not. The bottom line The Chiefs did not completely turn all three Kingdom Keys against the Jets, but they accomplished enough to earn a convincing victory. The performance was not flawless. Mahomes took too many hits, the offensive line suffered another injury, and Harrison Butker missed a 51-yard field goal. Kansas City must also continue searching for a dependable way to threaten defenses downfield without Thornton. But after two consecutive losses, the Chiefs needed a convincing response. Scoring 35 points, shutting out the opponent in the second half, and accomplishing most of their Kingdom Keys provided exactly that.

It’s been that way since safety Eric Berry held that status for what felt like the entire 2018 season. So it’s hard to take much away from head coach Andy Reid labeling three Chiefs players — quarterback Patrick Mahomes (elbow), wide receiver Xavier Worthy (hamstring) and right tackle Jaylon Moore (ankle) — as “day-to-day” during his press conference on Monday. Download the SB Nation app on your mobile device! For Apple devices, click here . For Android devices, click here . The latest Kansas City Chiefs news Chiefs QB Patrick Mahomes day-to-day with elbow injury | ESPN Chiefs coach Andy Reid said Monday that quarterback Patrick Mahomes is considered day-to-day with his right elbow injury, an injury he sustained in Sunday’s win over the New York Jets. Reid shared that Mahomes was in the Chiefs’ training facility Monday morning to receive treatment for his injury. Following the game, an MRI scan didn’t reveal any major injury to Mahomes’ elbow, sources told NFL Network’s Ian Rapoport. “It was more positive news than negative news on Patrick,” Reid said Monday. “It looks like it’s just a matter of [getting] some rehabbing in there and getting rid of some of the soreness. We’ll just see where it goes from there. He’s in good spirits.” Former Chiefs player was roasted for his take on kicker Harrison Butker | The Kansas City Star At 11:21 a.m. on Sunday, roughly 40 minutes before kickoff of the Jets game, ex-Chiefs wideout Gehrig Dieter shared this message on X: “I’m calling it now. Butker going to go on a generational run. He won’t miss another kick the entire season.” Ninety minutes later, that generational run ended before it began as Butker missed a 51-yard attempt — after missing from 56 before a penalty gave him another shot. That led fans to believe his tenure with the Chiefs was nearly over, although coach Andy Reid said after the game he wasn’t ready to announce a change. Cover 32: What every team should do at NFL trade deadline, plus game balls and gaffes from Week 9 | CBS Sports Kansas City Chiefs : Don’t let the 35 points scored on Sunday fool you. The Chiefs still need wide receiver help, and not just a small addition either. They should be in on everyone from Brian Thomas Jr. to Josh Downs. I’d also go at the Jets hard with an offer for Garrett Wilson and make them say no. While a receiver is a clear need, I also think K.C. could stand to add a veteran edge rusher too. ‘It feels like a matter of when’ — NFL Insiders discuss Kansas City Chiefs’ pursuit of WR Brian Thomas Jr. ahead of trade deadline | A to Z Sports Jacksonville has a reason to listen. One factor that could make the Jaguars flinch and trade away a player like Thomas is the need to recoup draft capital, a point Fowler raised during the discussion. ESPN’s Adam Schefter outlined the compensation headed to the New Orleans Saints in the Jaguars’ recent trade for defensive tackle Davon Godchaux. The Saints are receiving a conditional 2028 sixth-round pick. However, that pick could turn into a 2027 sixth-round pick, depending on the conditions attached to the deal. Chiefs kicker Harrison Butker reacts to getting booed off field: ‘It is what it is’ | Entertainment Weekly “It’s part of it, you know,” he told reporters after the game. “I’m booing myself sometimes. People are passionate. Fans are passionate. They want to win games. They want me to make kicks. I want to make kicks. It’s part of it. That’s what you sign up for. I’ve got to do better.” The 10-year veteran is ranked the sixth-most-accurate kicker in NFL history, with an average of 87.1 percent of field goals made. But he’s been struggling significantly this season and currently leads the league with seven missed field goals (over eight games). Around the NF L NFL reinstates Brandon Aiyuk, gives 49ers 2-week roster exemption | The Athletic The news comes three days after Aiyuk and his new agent, Drew Rosenhaus, met with the 49ers’ brass at the team’s business offices in Santa Clara, Calif., with the receiver saying he was 100 percent healthy and seeking reinstatement. Aiyuk had been on the reserve/left squad list — where players are not paid and do not count against the team’s roster numbers — since December and had not been to the team’s facility since. The 49ers have made it clear Aiyuk will never play for them again. Asked about the roster exemption Monday afternoon, coach Kyle Shanahan replied, “It means absolutely nothing to our team. … That’s all administrative stuff to me.” Jaguars land DT Jordan Davis in blockbuster deal with Eagles, marking latest trade ahead of deadline | Yahoo! Sports Jacksonville no longer has a first- or second-round draft pick in 2027 after Monday’s transactions, though the Jaguars still hold their first-round picks in 2028 and 2029. The Jaguars have been to the playoffs only twice in the past nine seasons, and they fell in the wild-card round in 2025, the first under head coach Liam Coen’s watch. While Monday’s transactions were undoubtedly costly for the franchise, the Jaguars feel ready to go for it and make a legitimate postseason run. Whether that is enough for them to run the table in the AFC and make what would be the team’s first Super Bowl remains to be seen. Rams WR Puka Nacua likely to be placed on injured reserve with turf toe, sprained MCL and PCL | NFL.com This marks the latest in a lengthy list of ailments for Nacua this season, as he was affected by psoas soreness throughout training camp and sat Weeks 2 and 3 due to a hip injury, but the turf toe and knee sprain will lead to his longest absence yet. Nacua is set to join fellow star wideout Davante Adams (hamstring) on IR, leaving the Rams with a WR corps of Tutu Atwell, Konata Mumpfield, Jordan Whittington and CJ Daniels, plus a tight end group of Tyler Higbee, Colby Parkinson and Davis Allen that is frequently used in the passing attack. With 45 snaps against New York, he out-snapped teammates in the secondary like safety Alohi Gilman (44 snaps) and safety Jaden Hicks (19 snaps). He has mainly been a staple in defending teams’ quick passes, but he was also used on blitzes a season-high five times in Week 9; he registered two hurries. full_text: HOUSTON, TEXAS - AUGUST 13: General manager Joe Hortiz of the Los Angeles Chargers talks with general manager Nick Caserio of the Houston Texans before a preseason game at Reliant Stadium on August 13, 2026 in Houston, Texas. (Photo by Tim Warner/Getty Images) | Getty Images On Monday following the team’s eighth consecutive loss to begin the season, Jim Harbaugh surprisingly left the door open for the Chargers to potentially make some moves at the deadline after a full week of shutting the idea down. “If something makes sense that will make our team better, now or in the future, Joe Hortiz is going to be open and active in pursuing that,” Harbaugh told reporters. Based on the back-and-forth of the team prior to Tuesday, this leaves Chargers fans in a place of “i’ll believe when I see it.” After multiple offseasons where promises were made to finally get Justin Herbert protected only to have that still be the team’s biggest issue, it’s going to be incredibly difficult for the fans to simply take them at their word. There’s also a likely discrepancy between what the team believes is good enough in fixing that issue and what everyone else would consider to be good enough. This past offseason is a prime example. Hortiz and Harbaugh thought Cole Strange was good enough. Reality immediately told everyone else it was not and that continues to happen with each new game Strange plays in. Then there was the decision to not sign a true-and-tried starter at left guard, instead hoping someone would rise to the top in a group of underwhelming performers and career backups. The words from team leadership have just never quite matched up with the vision and end goal. Does that start to change today at the deadline? Will they bring in more picks to make this offseason re-tool more viable? Will they sit and twiddle their thumbs while looking the other way? Come today’s deadline, we should finally have our answers. And now for today’s links. title: Sean McVay should play the rookies now
summary: The Los Angeles Rams are down Puka Nacua, Davante Adams, Terrance Ferguson, and Jordan Whittington. Those were their top four receiving options atop the depth chart entering the year. The NFL trade deadline passed and the Rams decided to stand pat. There are no reinforcements on the way. They now will be left with Tutu […]
full_text: The Los Angeles Rams are down Puka Nacua, Davante Adams, Terrance Ferguson, and Jordan Whittington. Those were their top four receiving options atop the depth chart entering the year. The NFL trade deadline passed and the Rams decided to stand pat. There are no reinforcements on the way. They now will be left with Tutu Atwell, Konata Mumpfield, Colby Ferguson, Tyler Higbee, Xavier Smith, Brennen Presley, Davis Allen, and Max Klare. From April: CJ Daniels could shake up Rams receiving depth Max Klare: Sean McVay gets his Dalton Kincaid years later LA’s passing game hasn’t worked for most of this year. The offense will now need to right the ship with an unknown cast. A strong running game and an aggressive defense can only take you so far. The Rams have an incredibly thin margin for error for at least the next few games. That probably gets the job done against the Arizona Cardinals and rookie quarterback Carson Beck. It will be an uphill battle in the games that follow versus the Green Bay Packers, Kansas City Chiefs, and San Francisco 49ers. The main problem is that we’ve seen Atwell, Mumpfield, Parkinson, and Higbee for most of this year. None of them have been good enough. They aren’t the answer moving forward. It’s time to play the rookies. Even if it’s different for the sake of change. It’s hard to be worse than Atwell and Mumpfield. If CJ Daniels cannot make an impact, then the Rams are already toast against stiffer competition. The same goes for tight end Max Klare. LA drafted him in the second round. A redshirt year sounds ideal in a vacuum. The Rams no longer have the luxury of keeping him on the sidelines. He might have the most natural talent of any pass catcher left on the roster. The Rams’ approach of leading with patience has led to great results for player development. This time is different. LA has loaded its roster with superstars in hopes of winning a Super Bowl. They need to survive for at least the next three weeks. Asking Daniels and Klare to be the difference may be an impossible task. They might be the only ones even remotely up to the challenge.

title: Rams place another WR on injured reserve
summary: The Los Angeles Rams have placed another receiver on injured reserve this week, as Jordan Whittington will miss at least four games with a back injury. full_text: The Los Angeles Rams have placed another receiver on injured reserve this week, as Jordan Whittington will miss at least four games with a back injury. Whittington was in line to have serious reps moving forward with Puka Nacua joining Davante Adams on IR this week, but now that opportunity will go to someone else. Perhaps Xavier Smith, who the Rams re-signed on Tuesday in a corresponding move. Smith joins Konata Mumpfield, Tutu Atwell, and C.J. Daniels in a receivers room that looks a lot different than it did a few weeks ago. LA Rams Roster Moves: • Reserved/Injured WR Jordan Whittington • Free Agent Signing WR Xavier Smith pic.twitter.com/TbAUH4OMEx — Los Angeles Rams (@RamsNFL) November 10, 2026 Despite rumors like that L.A. inquired about Stefon Diggs , the Rams didn’t trade for any receivers at Tuesday’s deadline. This is the group they are going with. Whittington had just four targets this season, catching two passes for 12 yards. The 22 catches for 293 yards he had as a rookie in 2024 may end up being his best career year when it’s all said and done. Instead, the Rams look to Mumpfield, last year’s seventh-round pick. This play last year has every receiver in the Rams current 11 personnel offense: Konata Mumpfield Tutu Atwell Xavier Smith There was 5 plays last year with this trio. pic.twitter.com/SY3RNYSWuU — Josh (@JoshiosTweets) November 10, 2026 Mumpfield leads all active Rams receivers with 11 catches for 162 yards. Tyler Higbee leads the team at any position among non-injured players, with 28 catches for 287 yards. Kyren Williams has 36 catches for 258 yards. Outside of a 48-yard catch against the Broncos in which Mumpfield was practically uncovered, L.A.’s new number one receiver hasn’t been productive. Aside from that play, Mumpfield has 10 catches for 114 yards and zero touchdowns in the other eight games. He had two catches for 20 yards last week. Atwell, who the team traded for at the start of the season, has been targeted nine times in the past two games, catching four passes for 68 yards. C.J. Daniels has yet to be targeted. So, the Rams bring back Xavier Smith, who had one target and no catches prior to his release. Smith had 18 catches for 303 yards in 2025, however. No News at Deadline Other notable moves on Tuesday had Josh Downs going to the Kansas City Chiefs, Keenan Allen going to the San Francisco 49ers and Brian Thomas Jr. staying with the Jasonville Jaguars . As it stands, adding Smith is the biggest move the Rams made on the NFL’s trade deadline day. Smith’s biggest moment with the Rams came in the 2025 NFC Championship game when he fumbled after halftime against the Seattle Seahawks. Seattle would go on to score a touchdown and ultimately win the game. Was that play the sole reason the Rams lost? No, but it didn’t help. Entering the 2026 season, the Rams brought Smith back as their kick returner and punt returner before waiving him a few weeks into the year . Smith then went to the 49ers, who have since traded for Allen , and decided to move on from Smith. As the Rams enter Week 10, Smith is back in L.A. McVay saw Niners got veteran Keenan Allen for a bag of chips and then said ok, time to lock in and sigh Xavier Smith https://t.co/xDpwBSYgjH — Cyborg Ninja (@thecyborglife) November 10, 2026 Is Smith the player that the Rams needed to make up for the losses of Puka Nacua and Davante Adams? Right or wrong it’s what the Rams just did, and for now, that’s all they did to address their wide receiver room as another trade deadline comes to its end.

With Beckham recently released from the Minnesota Vikings’ roster and reportedly expected to return to their practice squad, the Rams should at least kick the tires on a potential reunion. Vikings release WR Odell Beckham Jr. pic.twitter.com/3jNacrRu5W — NFL (@NFL) November 10, 2026 Beckham already knows Sean McVay’s offensive system, understands the expectations inside the building, and has a history with both McVay and general manager Les Snead. The two enjoyed having Beckham in Los Angeles, and his contributions during the Rams’ Super Bowl run in 2021 showed what he could bring to the offense. Sure, Beckham might not have the same tread on his tires that he once did. Nobody is expecting him to return as the superstar receiver who took the league by storm in New York. However, the Rams don’t necessarily need that version of Beckham. They need another experienced receiver who can provide a legitimate alternative when defenses focus their attention on the remaining playmakers. Matthew Stafford can trust that Odell Beckham Jr can be in the spot that he needs to be. title: Potential Rams trade target Brian Thomas Jr. will not be moved
summary: If the Los Angeles Rams want to fill their increasing large void at wide receiver, they’ll have to look somewhere other than Brian Thomas Jr. According to Jeremy Fowler of ESPN, the Jacksonville Jaguars are planning to keep Thomas, ending months of speculation that the former Pro Bowler could be on the move. This isn’t […]
full_text: (Photo by David Rosenblum/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images) | Icon Sportswire via Getty Images If the Los Angeles Rams want to fill their increasing large void at wide receiver, they’ll have to look somewhere other than Brian Thomas Jr. According to Jeremy Fowler of ESPN, the Jacksonville Jaguars are planning to keep Thomas, ending months of speculation that the former Pro Bowler could be on the move. The Jaguars plan to keep WR Brian Thomas Jr. through the trade deadline, per sources. They have relayed that to interested teams. Coming off multiple big trades Monday, Jacksonville plans to keep its roster intact, barring a surprise. pic.twitter.com/0QxdybXqaN — Jeremy Fowler (@JFowlerESPN) November 10, 2026 This isn’t especially surprising from the Jaguars’ perspective, considering they’ve made it clear they’re going all in on a Super Bowl run this year. In just over 24 hours, the Jaguars have acquired safety Jessie Bates III, and defensive linemen Davon Godchaux and Jordan Davis, sending out a mass quantity of draft picks to get those deals done (including a first, two seconds, a fifth and a sixth). Given that their general manager, James Gladstone, used to work in the Rams front office, their approach is not surprising. But it does leave the Rams with one fewer option if they decide to bolster the receiver room at the NFL trade deadline. Thomas isn’t as good as Puka Nacua, who’s now on injured reserve , nor Davante Adams, who’s missed several weeks already with a hamstring injury . Despite that and despite a disappointing last couple seasons compared to his rookie debut, he’s still a talented player with a combination of speed and skill Los Angeles simply doesn’t have right now. He wouldn’t have fixed all of the passing game’s issues, but certainly could have helped. With this news, the best receiver on the likely trade block is Josh Downs from the Indianapolis Colts . This season, playing for a bad Colts offense with an even worse quarterback in Daniel Jones, Downs has posted 33 receptions for 354 yards and one touchdown, all hovering just below his career averages in terms of raw numbers and per-game efficiency. He’s a slot receiver, having taken over 52% of his snaps there this season, the third-highest rate in the NFL. That’s not a bad thing for this Rams offense, though, and actually should fit in well alongside a (hopefully eventually) healthy Nacua and Adams. Josh Downs, asked if he wants to be with the #Colts : “You know, I mean …” He paused and said under his breath, “You funny for that.” Finished saying: “I said I’m open to whatever, and if they want me to stay here, I’mma stay here, and if they don’t … they’ll trade me away.” pic.twitter.com/zdiVbA9kFH — James Boyd (@RomeovilleKid) November 8, 2026 Plus, the Rams shouldn’t turn their nose up at obviously talented contributors at this point. Beyond that, options are a bit more scant. The Philadelphia Eagles are obviously open for business, which could make Dontayvion Wicks an option. His hands have always been iffy but his route-running is his best skill. Jajuan Jennings has had a solid career, but the former San Francisco 49er hasn’t done anything of note with the Minnesota Vikings this year. Across town, the Los Angeles Chargers haven’t done anything yet ahead of the deadline, but could they be persuaded into moving Quentin Johnston? With this news this morning, one major detail has changed, one remains the same. The receiver with arguably the highest upside on the market isn’t going anywhere. But that doesn’t stop the Rams from needing another wide receiver.

The Rams will need to continue to lean on both backs who can both run, block, catch, and seemingly do whatever the Rams are ask. How well can the run game be without Puka Nacua assisting? title: Raiders sign rookie defensive tackle to roster
summary: In an unsurprising move, the Las Vegas Raiders signed rookie defensive lineman Tim Keenan to the 53-man roster from the practice squad. Keenan takes the roster spot left vacant from the Raiders’ trade of quarterback Kirk Cousins to the Minensota Vikings for a third-round draft pick in 2027. It was likely Keenan would soon be […]
full_text: (Photo by Al Bello/Getty Images) | Getty Images In an unsurprising move, the Las Vegas Raiders signed rookie defensive lineman Tim Keenan to the 53-man roster from the practice squad. Keenan takes the roster spot left vacant from the Raiders’ trade of quarterback Kirk Cousins to the Minensota Vikings for a third-round draft pick in 2027. It was likely Keenan would soon be added to the 53-man roster. He was elevated from the practice squad for the past three games, which is the elevation limit for a season. Keenan was a seventh-round draft pick of the Los Angeles Rams this year out of Alabama. He was waived in September. The Raiders then signed him to their practice squad. Keenan played in all three games he was elevated for and he even started in Week 9 at San Francisco, playing a season high 49 percent of the snaps. He has played in 35 percent of the snaps in his three games. He has a total of seven tackles with four coming against the 49ers. Expect him to continue to be part of the playing rotation for the rest of the season. To replace Keenan on the practice squad, the Raiders signed defensive tackle Chris Williams. He has been in the NFL since 2020 and was part of the Falcons’ and Browns’ programs this year.

title: Raiders trade deadline notes
summary: The Las Vegas Raiders traded quarterback Kirk Cousins to the Minnesota Vikings for a 3rd round pick (the Vikings’ second in the round) Tuesday. it opens the door for the Raiders play No. 1 overall draft pick Fernando Mendoza, who general manager John Spytek confirmed Tuesday afternoon will be the starter moving forward. Here are […]
full_text: (Photo by Ethan Miller/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Las Vegas Raiders traded quarterback Kirk Cousins to the Minnesota Vikings for a 3rd round pick (the Vikings’ second in the round) Tuesday. it opens the door for the Raiders play No. 1 overall draft pick Fernando Mendoza, who general manager John Spytek confirmed Tuesday afternoon will be the starter moving forward. Here are some notes about their deadline decisions: The Raiders, at 4-5, didn’t decide to make it a fire sale. They also didn’t opt to add at the trade deadline either as they have lost five of the last six games after starting 3-0. NFL reporter Jordan Schulz reported that the Raiders did receive recent trade calls on star defensive end Maxx Crosby, but resisted them after a nixed trade with the Baltimore Ravens in March. Because the Raiders have already agreed to trade Crosby once, expect them to receive more calls in the future, including next offseason. There is no word if the Raiders had any interest in pending free agents, wide receiver Tre Tucker and safety Jeremy Chinn. It will be interesting to see if they try to extend them in the offseason. Spytek said he received calls on multiple players without getting into detail. Despite needs at some posts, including at wide receiver and defensive tackle, the Raiders did not add at the deadline. Spytek said the Cousins’ trade is not an indication the team is giving up on the season. Coach Klint Kubiak said Mendoza is prepared, physically and mentally, for this task and he praised Cousin for his influence on the rookie. Spytek said Mendoza has passed every test since being drafted and he helped the Raiders make the tough decision to deal Cousins. Spytek said Mendoza’s play in practice was difficult to ignore. Spytek said he only received calls on Cousins and did not make any himself. The talks with Minnesota emerged Tuesday morning after Carson Wentz’s horrible showing in a loss Monday night. Spytek said the team did not expect this to happen before Tuesday, thus he had no previous conversations with Cousins about it. Spytek said he and Kubiak spent a lot of time before agreeing to the Cousins trade, but, ultimately decided it was best for the franchise.

title: Las Vegas Raiders get their gold mined by the 49ers
summary: The Las Vegas Raiders traveled to Levi’s Stadium in Santa Clara, California, to renew the Battle of the Bay rivalry with the San Francisco 49ers. A rivalry that has meant so much to the two fan bases. Turnovers were the story of this contest. When the clock read zero, the Raiders had committed five turnovers […]
full_text: (Photo by Ezra Shaw/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Las Vegas Raiders traveled to Levi’s Stadium in Santa Clara, California, to renew the Battle of the Bay rivalry with the San Francisco 49ers. A rivalry that has meant so much to the two fan bases. Turnovers were the story of this contest. When the clock read zero, the Raiders had committed five turnovers and allowed 30+ points on defense for the sixth straight week. Kirk Cousins had his worst game as the signal caller for the Raiders. In the first half, he only threw the ball eight times. By the end, Cousins threw three interceptions, with one pick-six after recovering his own fumble. Things simply did not go his way today. Ashton Jeanty regained his starting position and managed 25 yards on six carries. In the passing game where he has made his largest impact, he caught five passes for -5.0 yards. Mike Washington Jr. was subjected to simply awful run blocking, finishing the game with -3.0 yards on six carries with a long of four yards. Bowers played his first game near his hometown of Napa, California, with reportedly around 50 friends and family in attendance. He would punish the 49ers, finishing with 111 yards on seven catches, including a 21-yard score. A questionable spot robbed him of a second touchdown. First half Early on, Raiders defensive playcaller Rob Leonard continued getting his lunch money stolen by an opposing offensive play caller. The 49ers drove down the field on the opening possession in 12 plays, five passes, seven runs and scored. On the second possession, the 49ers ran the ball down the Raiders’ throats. Brock Purdy, the 49ers quarterback, would finish the game with 40 yards rushing on seven carries. Including a rushing touchdown which put the 49ers up 14-0. By the end of the 49ers third drive the Raiders defense surrendered 94 yards rushing, while being on the field for every play except three with 1:52 seconds to play in the first quarter. What we heard from the television broadcasters was that it was 49ers head coach Kyle Shanahan’s goal to run the ball 40 times against the Raiders’ putrid run defense. After going three-and-out on their first drive, Kirk Cousins gets settled in and hits passes to Jack Bech, Brock Bowers, and Jalen Nailor. Driving the Raiders downfield when the end of the quarter makes them switch sides. Cousins finishes the drive off with his team leading with the second rushing touchdown of the year. Drawing the Raiders to within a score. Raiders’ defense continued to allow nearly six yards per carry to the 49ers offense. On 4th and 1, the run blocking of the 49ers knocked the Raiders’ defenders three yards off the line of scrimmage. Raiders followed it up by running some type of zone blitz where both defensive tackles dropped into zone coverage and surrendered a passing touchdown to McCaffrey. After a Raiders offensive possession netting a field goal, the Raiders were down 21-10 and needed a defensive stop to close out the half. Maxx Crosby would get his fourth sack of the season and a false start penalty would end the half. At the end of the half, the 49ers had ran the ball 25 times for 125 yards and two touchdowns. Craziest third quarter in remembrance First play of the second half, Cousins fumbled the football, picked it up and threw a pick-6, 17 seconds into the second half. Exactly what the Raiders could not afford to have happen. To be fair, everything is resting on his shoulders and in order for the Raiders to have any chance of winning any game, he can’t afford to make a mistake. In the retribution drive after the turnover, Cousins came right back, completing seven of seven throws. finishing with a 21-yard touchdown pass to Bowers to level the score at 28-17. Mistakes happen, but atoning for them is critical. With just under 10 minutes remaining in the 3rd quarter, the 49ers offense would take the field for the first time in the second half. Treydan Stukes, the Raiders’ second-round pick, fooled Purdy, intercepted the pass, tried to fall numerous times with no one around to tackle him and stumbled back to the 30-yard line of the 49ers. Momentum shifts are a huge thing, giving the Raiders an opportunity to get it back to a one-score game. However, in the most self-sabotaging way ever, Cousins nearly threw an interception to a defensive lineman; the very next play, Fred Warner peanut-punches the ball out of Bowers hands and the 49ers recover the ball. Four plays later, the Raiders get a 4th-and-short stop and a turnover on downs for the first time in a long time. Five turnovers were committed by both teams in the third quarter alone. 4th quarter…. On the next drive, Cousins hits Michael Mayer for a nice gain and as he fought to reach the goal line, disaster struck. Mayer was tackled and fell on top of a defender, while another 49ers defender punched the ball out of his hands just before he crossed the goal line. Negating a potential score, turning the ball over yet again, giving the 49ers a touchback. From there, the 49ers would drive past midfield with a few runs. But the lack of a Raiders pass rush gave Purdy enough time to find Jordan Watkins open for a 37-yard touchdown catch. On the ensuing possession, the Raiders drove to the goal line again, behind a 33-yard catch-and-run from Bowers that appeared to stretch the ball over the pylon but was ruled out of bounds. Cousins’ quarterback sneak was stuffed when Warner leaped over the pile after the snap. On the next play, Mayer was called for offensive pass interference, negating his own touchdown catch. Followed up with Cousins’ second interception of the game, the second turnover inside the red zone, turnover number four and the third straight turnover. But the hits just kept on coming; in junk time, Cousins would throw his third interception of the day, fourth straight turnover and fifth total. Cousins had Tre Tucker open deep, loaded up, putting his full body into the throw, only for it to fall short and into the waiting arms of a 49ers defender, mercifully allowing this game to come to an end.

title: What Kirk Cousins trade means to Raiders
summary: The Las Vegas Raiders traded quarterback Kirk Cousins to the Minnesota Vikings for a 3rd round pick Tuesday. it opens the door for the Raiders play No. 1 overall draft pick Fernando Mendoza. Here is a look at the key aspects of the decision: Good overall value: Some people may have thought the Raiders could […]
full_text: (Photo by Harry How/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Las Vegas Raiders traded quarterback Kirk Cousins to the Minnesota Vikings for a 3rd round pick Tuesday. it opens the door for the Raiders play No. 1 overall draft pick Fernando Mendoza. Here is a look at the key aspects of the decision: Good overall value: Some people may have thought the Raiders could have gotten more than the Vikings’ second third-round pick for a player who could potentially help them get to the Super Bowl and a player they were desperate to get. In the big picture, this is a nice get for the Raiders. They paid Cousins just $650,000 this season. They got four wins, a mentor to Mendoza and a third-round pick. Not bad. Raiders confident in Mendoza: The Raiders wouldn’t have traded Cousins unless they were confident Mendoza was ready to play. Coach Klint Kubiak constantly talked about a plan and they weren’t going to rush Mendoza. Again, they weren’t blown away with an offer they couldn’t refuse. If they didn’t feel the kid is ready, they would have said no to a pick in the No. 80-90 range. Reportedly, the Raiders have been pleased by how good Mendoza has looked in practice reps recently. Are they still in it? I’d expect Kubiak to say this week that he thinks the Raiders, who are 4-5 and and who have lost five of their past six games after starting 3-0, can still make the playoffs. There was a report Tuesday that the Raiders were hesitant to deal Cousins because they felt like they are still in the mix. But there’s eight games to go and they can make a move. More draft picks are good thing: The Raiders will have plenty of holes to fill on the roster next offseason, so adding another top 100 pick is big. They should have four now. They can use it to acquire more picks. So, this is a valuable piece. the Fernando Mendoza era begins vs the following defenses: Seahawks Broncos Browns Chargers Broncos (again) #3 toughest schedule of defenses for any offense in the NFL from Week 10-15 pic.twitter.com/7UkMzZnXmi — Warren Sharp (@SharpFootball) November 10, 2026 Mendoza has tough challenge: Mendoza will face the vaunted Seattle defense in his starting debut. And the challenging defense parade will not end soon. Mendoza is being thrown to the wolves, but, clearly the Raiders believe it won’t be too big for him to handle. Rookie of the year? Mendoza is in line to get just eight starts, but, according to our friends at FanDuel Sportsbook , he is the betting favorite at +350. It helps that no other offensive rookie is running away with the award. Cousins was a good Raider: Cousins’ finale as a Raider was forgettable with three interception, but he produced and was among the league leaders in several categories. He was a tough, good Raider and helped develop Mendoza. the Raider Nation should forever have fond feelings about Cousins. Raise an In & Out double double in his honor. AOC a snap away: Many people thought Aidan O’Connell could be traded, but, instead the 2023 fourth-round pick is a back up again after being the No. 3 quarterback this season. It won’t be a surprise if the Raiders sign a quarterback to the practice squad to fill out the quarterback room. Also, expect Las Vegas to look to find a veteran backup for Mendoza in the offseason.

title: Kirk Cousins-Fernando Mendoza leads Las Vegas Raiders’ talk in Week 10 NFL Power Rankings
summary: In a surprise twist, the Las Vegas Raiders traded quarterback Kirk Cousins to the Minnesota Vikings shortly before the NFL trade deadline pass on Tuesday afternoon, despite still being alive in the AFC playoff picture with a chance at earning the third and final Wild Card spot. Coincidentally, the primary focus surrounding the Raiders in […]
full_text: (Photo by Cooper Neill/Getty Images) | Getty Images In a surprise twist, the Las Vegas Raiders traded quarterback Kirk Cousins to the Minnesota Vikings shortly before the NFL trade deadline pass on Tuesday afternoon, despite still being alive in the AFC playoff picture with a chance at earning the third and final Wild Card spot. Coincidentally, the primary focus surrounding the Raiders in the Week 10 NFL Power Rankings was when it’s time to turn the reins over to Fernando Mendoza. We have our answer now, but let’s dive into what a few in the media were thinking before the deal took place. NFL.com 21. Las Vegas Raiders Last week: 20 Sunday’s result wasn’t a low point, but it was a sign we’re nearing the transition of quarterback power from Kirk Cousins to Fernando Mendoza. Frankly, the Raiders are still operating on the positive side of matters, playing generally competitive football that is, at minimum, entertaining in most weeks. The defense is disintegrating, though, which doesn’t bode well for their outlook. — Nick Shook Well, the transition is official, and Mendoza’s first start comes this weekend against a very good Seattle Seahawks defense. That’s a tough assignment for a quarterback’s first NFL start, but the matchup could tilt in Las Vegas’ favor since Seattle is struggling to run the ball and will be playing backup quarterback Drew Lock on Sunday. ESPN 21. Las Vegas Raiders Last week: 20 Most important game of the second half: Week 12 at the Browns This will be the Raiders’ last game before their bye week. It could also determine how they handle their quarterback situation for the rest of the year. If the Raiders get at least five or six wins before their weeklong break, and Kirk Cousins keeps playing solid football, they could stick with the veteran signal-caller to capitalize on their playoff window. However, if the Raiders lose to the Browns, they could start Fernando Mendoza for the final five games to evaluate the No. 1 pick. — Ryan McFadden This becomes a moot point after the trade. In fairness to McFadden, the Week 12 game right before the bye easily could have been the swing moment for Klint Kubiak and the rest of the coaching staff when it comes to Mendoza’s first start. The Raiders’ schedule softens up after the down week, and they easily could have been out of contention by then. Bleacher Report 17. Las Vegas Raiders Last week: 17 The Las Vegas Raiders are pretty much what everyone expected them to be during the offseason. They have a few nice pieces and a competent bridge quarterback in Kirk Cousins, but they’re not yet ready to hang with the league’s true contenders. Things felt different during Las Vegas’ 3-0 start to the season and even after a close loss to the Kansas City Chiefs. However, the Raiders are still clearly a year away from having realistic aspirations of a deep playoff run. The question right now is if Las Vegas has enough pieces in place to properly support rookie quarterback Fernando Mendoza when or if they decide to turn the offense over to him. — Kristopher Knox This Sunday and the rest of the season, we’ll find out for sure if the offense has enough pieces to support the rookie quarterback. Having one of the most dynamic offensive weapons in football, Brock Bowers, certainly helps. Also, Mendoza might be able to unlock Tre Tucker, who had a few good games with Cousins slinging the rock. The offensive line is the biggest question mark, as the run game has been an issue all season and the unit ranks 30th in pass-block win rate, according to Sumer Sports . However, ESPN’s pass-block win rate only counts when linemen lose within 2.5 seconds after the snap (Sumer’s doesn’t factor in how long it takes a lineman to lose), and the Raiders are second in ESPN’s ranking. In other words, a quarterback who gets the ball out quickly wouldn’t be under pressure much behind Vegas’ line. Sports Illustrated 20. Las Vegas Raiders Last week: 17 A video with MMQB Podcast teammate Albert Breer from Monday’s show where we argue the merits of Minnesota giving up a first-round pick to Las Vegas for Kirk Cousins. Really? Yes, really. — Conor Orr It wasn’t a first-round pick; it was a third-rounder. So, it feels like general manager John Spytek might have left some meat on the bone, but getting a Top 100 selection for a player whose days in Vegas were numbered is a decent return. Plus, Minnesota takes on Cousins’ $10 million cap hit for next season, clearing the books a bit for the Raiders. The Athletic 20. Las Vegas Raiders Last week: 19 Midseason grade: C On the one hand, the Raiders, a team with low expectations, got off to a shocking 3-0 start to the season. On the other, they’ve now lost five of their last six games, with their lone win coming against the Jets. They’ve been competitive with Kirk Cousins at the helm, but it feels like reality is starting to creep in. — Chad Graff, Josh Kendall This is interesting because the introduction mentions that the expectations each team had entering the season determined the grade. As Graff/Kendall mention, the Raiders entered with low expectations. But owning a 4-5 record when the line for their win total for the entire campaign was 5.5 is just meeting preseason expectations. Huh? That doesn’t make much sense, and I’d be interested to see what their preseason game-by-game prediction was for the Silver and Black. For most people, the Miami Dolphins were widely considered the only “gimme” game in the first half of the schedule. Many had Vegas losing to the Los Angeles Chargers and New Orleans Saints. You can probably throw the New York Jets in there too, with how many offseason additions the Jets made.

full_text: (Photo by Brooke Sutton/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Las Vegas Raiders have traded quarterback Kirk Cousins to the Minnesota Vkings. They are getting a 2027 third-round pick for Cousins. The Raiders had let it up known that they were not interested in trading Cousins, but the Vikings were desperately seeking quarterback help after they have lost the past two games after starting 6-0. Kyler Murray is hurt and hasn’t been effective when healthy and Carson Wentz was dreadful in a loss that was winnable to Buffalo on Monday night. The trade means the Raiders will turn to No. 1 overall draft pick Fernando Mendoza starting Sunday at home against the Seattle Seahawks. Mendoza has only played in a mop-up role in Week 5 at New England. The Raiders wanted to roll with Cousins as long as they have a chance at the playoffs. But Minnesota sweetened the deal and Cousins was, indeed, dealt. He now returns to the Vikings for a chance to win a Super Bowl and the Raiders move to the future.

full_text: (Photo by Alika Jenner/Getty Images) | Getty Images A theme of the past two seasons for the Las Vegas Raiders have been a string of mostly good health. After the Raiders were one of the least injured teams in 2025, that trend has continued this season, which is a nice nod to the team’s medical team and, of course, some of it is simply good luck Going into Week 9, the Raiders had just five starters miss a total of six games. Buffalo Bills , wide receiver DJ.Moore, defensive tackle Ed Oliver, tight end Dalton Kincaid, tackle Spencer Brown. Los Angeles Rams , defensive end Myles Garrett, wide receiver Davante Adams, tight end Colby Parkinson, defensive tackles Poonca Ford and Kobie Turner, cornerback Trent McDuffie, linebacker Nate Landman. New York Jets , running back Breece Hall, defensive end David Bailey, defensive tackle, T’Vondre Sweat. San Francisco 49ers , Wide receivers Mike Evans, Deebo Samuel and Christian Kirk, defensive lineman Gracen Halton. title: Mike Washington sees role reduced

full_text: (Photo by Brooke Sutton/Getty Images) | Getty Images Here is a look at how the Las Vegas Raiders’ 2026 draft class (eight of the 10 picks are on the 53-man roster) fared in a 38-17 loss at the San Francisco 49ers on Sunday and what to look for Sunday at home against the Seattle Seahawks. Fernando Mendoza: The No. 1 overall pick has only played in Week 5 in a mop-up role. Treydan Stukes: The Raiders’ second-round pick played all 73 defensive snaps and had an interception, his second of the season. Stukes is not perfect, but he makes plays. Trey Zuhn: The third-round pick made his second straight start. He had his struggles and left the game with a concussion in the third quarter. His availability for the Seattle game may be in jeopardy. Jermod McCoy: The fourth-round pick played extensively for the second straight games. He played 36 percent of the snaps. He had two pass breakups late in the game. McCoy may be coming into his own and he deserves more reps Mike Washington: The fourth-round pick played 34 percent of the snaps after playing 60 percent in Week 8.His work load reduced as well. He has just six carries for minus-3 yards a week after he had a season high 25 carries for 83 yards. It was a step back for the Arkansas product. Dalton Johnson: The fifth-round pick safety was inactive for the eighth time in nine games. Zeke Masses: The fifth-round pick played 12 defensive snaps, a season low. McCoy seems to have replaced Masses ,a once starter, in the rotation with starter Darien Porter. Malik Benson: The sixth-round pick was a healthy scratch for the second straigth game. We might have to wonder if Benson’s roster spot is in jeopardy if he continues to sit on game days.

title: Raiders news: Who is the greatest player in team history?
summary: This is always a fun debate. The history of the now Las Vegas Raiders is one of the richest in all of team sports. There have so any great players n the history of the franchise. Picking your favorite is no easy and it is subjective. We’ve had these discussions before and will likely again. […]
full_text: (Photo by Sylvia Allen/Getty Images) This is always a fun debate. The history of the now Las Vegas Raiders is one of the richest in all of team sports. There have so any great players n the history of the franchise. Picking your favorite is no easy and it is subjective. We’ve had these discussions before and will likely again. title: NFL trade deadline 2026: Miami Dolphins rumors, updates, and moves
summary: UPDATE: The Dolphins made no trades ahead of the 2026 trade deadline. The NFL trade deadline is Tuesday at 4 p.m. Eastern. While the NFL has lagged behind some other major sports leagues in moves made ahead of the trade deadline, we have seen an increase in deals in recent years. This year, we could […]
full_text: MINNEAPOLIS, MN - OCTOBER 04: Miami Dolphins linebacker Jordyn Brooks (20) looks on after the NFL game between the Miami Dolphins and the Minnesota Vikings on October 4th, 2026, at U.S. Bank Stadium in Minneapolis, MN. (Photo by Bailey Hillesheim/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images) | Icon Sportswire via Getty Images UPDATE: The Dolphins made no trades ahead of the 2026 trade deadline. The NFL trade deadline is Tuesday at 4 p.m. Eastern. While the NFL has lagged behind some other major sports leagues in moves made ahead of the trade deadline, we have seen an increase in deals in recent years. This year, we could see the trend continue, with many rumors already swirling and several teams expected to be sellers over the next couple of days. The Miami Dolphins may be one of those teams that sell this year. After a Week 9 loss to the Detroit Lions on Sunday, Miami fell to 1-7 as it works through the first season of a complete roster rebuild. The Miami front office will be tempted to add draft picks, but who could they trade to create additional selections? We will track all of the rumors, updates, and moves Miami makes over the next few days right here. Will the Dolphins be sellers? Miami could be sellers for many reasons this week, especially given their 1-7 record. The Dolphins tore their roster down to the studs this past offseason, taking on a record $188.8 million in dead money to set themselves up for future success. Continuing to move on from veterans, who might be able to help a team in “win-now” mode while providing Miami with additional draft picks makes sense for both sides. But Miami may be in a position where they aren’t interested in most trade offers. The roster teardown has left the team with few proven veterans who can serve as leaders and role models for younger players. The Dolphins may be content with the players they have, keeping them through the rest of the season and into 2027. No trade can ever be ruled out, but if the Dolphins plan to keep their veterans, they may be in a position to ask for huge draft packages in return for any trades. They can tell other teams that they either meet Miami’s asking price, or the Dolphins will be happy to keep their players. It seems like a good situation for a rebuilding franchise. Possible Dolphins trade bait Miami does have some veterans who might draw interest heading into the deadline: Jordyn Brooks, linebacker Brooks might be the biggest name among the Dolphins rumors swirling around. The veteran linebacker has averaged 163 tackles over his two seasons in Miami and he already has 63 tackles this season. He was selected as a First-Team All-Pro last year and can immediately come in and provide stabilization to a defense if he were to move. The Dolphins, however, identified Brooks as one of the pillars around which the team would be built. They signed him to a contract extension over the summer and seem to like the combination of Brooks and rookie middle linebacker Jacob Rodriguez as the defense’s foundation. Sunday’s opponent, the Detroit Lions, have to be interested in Brooks as a replacement for the injured Jack Campbell. Would they be willing to pay a high premium for the linebacker? Teams that might be interested: Detroit Lions, Dallas Cowboys, Pittsburgh Steelers Zach Sieler, defensive tackle Sieler has become such a fixture in the middle of the Dolphins’ defensive line that it is hard to imagine him somewhere else. Miami has multiple younger defensive tackles who could fill in if a trade happens, with 2025 draft picks Kenneth Grant, Jordan Phillips, and Zeek Biggers all making an impact when they are on the field. It could make Sieler someone the front office would consider moving for the right price. They still have to weigh the costs and benefits of any offer, though. Sieler is a defensive captain who always seems to make a play when the defense needs it; he brings strong leadership to the team. He has also publicly said he wants to stay in Miami, which could be a consideration if the front office wants to prove they are taking care of their own players – if Sieler wanted to make a move to a contender, it could be understandable, but that he wants to stay and work through the rebuild in Miami could be a good example for the team. Teams that might be interested: Jacksonville Jaguars, Minnesota Vikings, Chicago Bears, Green Bay Packers Austin Jackson, tackle Jackson might be the most likely player to be traded this year if Miami makes any deal. The right tackle has struggled to stay healthy throughout his career and, after a solid start in the NFL, injuries seem to have caught up with him. He has struggled this year, especially when left on an island, and the team may have already decided he is not part of their 2027 plans. He is in the final year of his contract and will be a free agent after the season. The Dolphins could look to the draft or free agency to add a right tackle, or move rookie left guard Kadyn Proctor to right tackle next year. Proctor has played really well inside, so leaving him there for his career might be a great option, but Miami’s options are the key part of that discussion. Moving Jackson could land the Dolphins an additional draft pick from a player they expect to leave in free agency anyway. Teams that might be interested: Jacksonville Jaguars, Carolina Panthers, Green Bay Packers Josh Uche, edge Uche could be a factor in the trade talks, especially after his performance against the Lions on Sunday. The 2026 free agent addition signed a one-year deal, and Miami might see the opportunity to turn that signing into a 2027 draft pick. Like Sieler, Uche has said he wants to stay in Miami and be a part of the rebuild, with his belief in head coach Jeff Hafley factoring into that desire. Teams that might be interested: New England Patriots, Philadelphia Eagles, Chicago Bears, Dallas Cowboys Dolphins trades The Dolphins made no trades. title: Dolphins quiet through NFL trade deadline 2026
summary: The Miami Dolphins were projected to be sellers at the NFL’s 2026 trade deadline, but with the 4 p.m. Eastern deadline now come and gone, Miami stood pat with their roster. While most teams that start a season 1-7 would be considered a disappointment and in need of a rebuild, Miami has already embraced the […]
full_text: FOXBOROUGH, MA - JANUARY 4: The Miami Dolphins logo is seen on an equipment bag during the game against the New England Patriots at Gillette Stadium on January 4, 2026 in Foxborough, Massachusetts.(Photo By Winslow Townson/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Miami Dolphins were projected to be sellers at the NFL’s 2026 trade deadline, but with the 4 p.m. Eastern deadline now come and gone, Miami stood pat with their roster. While most teams that start a season 1-7 would be considered a disappointment and in need of a rebuild, Miami has already embraced the restart the franchise has needed and shed most of their veteran players before the season. Those that are on the roster were retained for a reason and, with the deadline now passed, they will hold those roles throughout the remainder of the year. Speculation had focused on Jordyn Brooks. The All-Pro linebacker could have provided a team with a much-needed upgrade, especially if they need an injury replacement. Teams like the Detroit Lions and Dallas Cowboys were believed to be interested in Brooks. Defensive tackle Zach Sieler was another potential trade asset, but both the Dolphins and Sieler seemed to want to keep the veteran in South Florida. News on Tuesday that Sieler sustained a torn biceps muscle during the Dolphins’ Week 9 loss to the Detroit Lions ruled out any possible trade. Miami will now have to decide if they are going to keep Sieler beyond this year, especially with a salary cap number expected to balloon to $20.8 million next year compared to this season’s $11.0 million. The Dolphins could be stingy with any offer they received this year, putting a premium on all of their players and expecting high draft picks in return. The veterans that could be targets for other teams seem to be players Miami plans to keep beyond this year. There was no pressure to move on from a player, agreeing to every trade offer sent, and, ultimately, Miami chose not to make any deal. The day was not completely silent in Miami, however, as a groin injury for quarterback Malik Willis and a torn biceps muscle for defensive tackle Zach Sieler landed both veterans on injured reserve.

full_text: MIAMI GARDENS, FLORIDA - NOVEMBER 08: Malik Willis #2 of the Miami Dolphins runs onto the field prior to the game against the Detroit Lions at Hard Rock Stadium on November 08, 2026 in Miami Gardens, Florida. (Photo by Carmen Mandato/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Miami Dolphins are placing starting quarterback Malik Willis on injured reserve, The Ringer’s Tom Pelissero reported on Tuesday . The move comes just two days after the quarterback was clearly struggling to scramble during the team’s Week 9 loss to the Detroit Lions. The move will keep Willis out of the lineup for at least four weeks; the injury is not considered season-ending. Willis was listed on the injury report the last two weeks with a groin injury. Between Weeks 8 and 9, Willis had indicated the injury had not limited his rushing attempts against the New England Patriots, but it clearly was hampering him against the Lions. According to Pelissero’s report, the Dolphins had Willis undergo an MRI that showed the injury was getting worse and was now a core muscle issue. Surgery will not be required, but the quarterback has to rest until it is fully healed. Kyle McCord will move into the starting role for the 1-7 Dolphins. A 2025 sixth-round draft pick of the Philadelphia Eagles, McCord spent the preseason with the Green Bay Packers before Miami acquired him in a trade as final roster cuts were being made. After spending all of his rookie season on the Eagles’ practice squad, McCord will now make his NFL debut following the Willis injury. Brady Cook, currently on the practice squad, will likely serve as the backup. The Dolphins face the Indianapolis Colts in Week 10, with both teams in contention for the top overall pick in the 2027 NFL Draft. Update: The Dolphins officially announced Willis to injured reserve at 4 p.m. Eastern on Tuesday as all roster moves for the dat became official. Also listed in the move was placing defensive tackle Zach Sieler on injured reserve; Sieler was reported to have torn a biceps muscle earlier in the day . Miami also announced they waived cornerback Reese Taylor.

title: Miami Dolphins mid-season awards: Who is the team MVP through Week 9?
summary: The Miami Dolphins have hit the mid-point of the 2026 NFL season, with nine weeks complete and nine weeks remaining on the schedule. The Dolphins are 1-7 this year as they work through the first season of a complete franchise rebuild, learning and growing as a team with a roster dominated by rookies and younger […]
full_text: MIAMI GARDENS, FLORIDA - OCTOBER 11: Chop Robinson #44 of the Miami Dolphins exits the field at halftime during an NFL football game against the Cincinnati Bengals at Hard Rock Stadium on October 11, 2026 in Miami Gardens, Florida. (Photo by Perry Knotts/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Miami Dolphins have hit the mid-point of the 2026 NFL season, with nine weeks complete and nine weeks remaining on the schedule. The Dolphins are 1-7 this year as they work through the first season of a complete franchise rebuild, learning and growing as a team with a roster dominated by rookies and younger players. Even with the struggles, there have been plenty of flashes of potential that should make fans excited for the future of the team. But who has been the most noteworthy players on the roster so far this season? Here are my picks for mid-season awards from the 2026 Dolphins: Offensive Rookie of the First Half Caleb Douglas, wide receiver One of the Dolphins’ third-round picks this year, Douglas has turned into Miami’s primary perimeter threat in the passing game. Even with missing three games due to injury, Douglas has the team’s third-most targets and receptions, second-most yards, and tied for the lead in touchdowns. His 296 receiving yards are the most in team history in a player’s first five NFL games – the missed time will likely keep him short of Jaylen Waddle’s 1,105-yard rookie record. He has shown explosiveness and has forced opposing defenses to adjust their game plan. He has to work on his drops, including one on fourth down that would have converted for a first down against the Detroit Lions this past week as Miami attempted a comeback, but Douglas’s play thus far has shown Miami has a playmaker for the future. Honorable mention: Kadyn Proctor, guard Defensive Rookie of the First Half Jacob Rodriguez, linebacker This may have been the easiest selection of these awards. Rodriguez is not just making an impact on the Dolphins, but on the league where he is seventh in tackles with 79 in eight games. He is a machine on the field, and he is establishing himself as the foundation for the Dolphins’ future. He has a sack and an interception this year and has been the defensive player caller all year. Honorable mention: Michael Taaffe, safety Offensive Player of the First Half Ollie Gordon II, running back Gordon was supposed to be a depth option and change of pace running back behind De’Von Achane this year. Achane’s injury opened the door for a running back by committee approach for Miami, only for Gordon to explode through the door and make himself a true feature back in the league. He is 16th in the league with 463 yards, but he had no impact on Weeks 1 and 2, carrying the ball three times for seven yards before taking over for Achane during the Week 3 game. His 83 yards per game since becoming the starter would have him seventh in the league. Gordon has carried the Dolphins offense, and he has clearly established himself as a co-starter for when Achane returns in 2027. Honorable mention: Greg Dulcich, tight end Defensive Player of the First Half Jordyn Brooks, linebacker Miami has a dynamic duo at linebacker, with Rodriguez in the middle and Brooks as the weak-side linebacker. Brooks is 13th in tackles with 75 this year and he has continues to be the solid player around whom everyone else plays. Honorable mention: Zach Sieler, defensive tackle Breakout Player of the First Half Malik Washington, wide receiver Miami’s rookies are getting the most attention, especially wide outs Caleb Douglas and Chris Bell. Even Kevin Coleman Jr., the fourth player on the depth chart, is probably mentioned more than the player at the top of the chart, Malik Washington. Getting out from under the shadow of Tyreek Hill and Jaylen Waddle this year, Washington is having himself a very strong season. He is leading the team in targets, receptions, and yards and he is doing it without a lot of fanfare. I would expect Douglas to surpasss him in yards – and maybe he would have already without missing three games – but Washington is the veteran player the group needs, and he is making the most of his opportunity this season. Washington has taken over the Hill role in the offense, being used in motion and all around the lineup, including working out of the backfield as a running back. While the focus may be on Douglas and his big-play ability, Washington has established himself as the do-everything player that can be trusted to make a play when it is needed. Honorable mention: Chris Johnson, cornerback Best Play of the First Half Fake punt versus Detroit Lions & Malik Willis’ quarterback sneak versus Jets Co-winners take this slot. Punter Bradley Pinion’s 46-yard fake punt pass to running back Kaytron Allen against the Lions was perfectly executed. It caught the Lions off guard, converted the first down on 4th-and-3, and was a clear highlight. When the Dolphins’ special teams struggling throughout the year, it was a great special teams play. Dolphins draw up a fake punt of their own! That's two fake punts this game. DETvsMIA on FOX/FOX One Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/caEvejdds1 — NFL (@NFL) November 8, 2026 Willis’ 4th-and-1 quarterback sneak against the Jets may not have been as explosive as the fake punt, but it was more meaningful. Leading 28-25 with two minutes left, the Dolphins chose to go for it from the Jets’ 49-yard line. If they failed to gain the yardage, New York could have tied the game with a field goal as the clock ticked down. Miami lined up in a tush-push formation, with Willis taking the snap and moving forward directly behind center Aaron Brewer. Fullback DJ Herman and running back Ollie Gordon shovers Willis from behind, forcing him through the traffic for the two-yard gain and Miami’s first (and so far only) win. 🚨🚨Miami Dolphins Get Their 1# Win 🚨🚨 With The Malik Willis QB Sneak Dolphins Fans Are Calling It “The Porpoise Penetrator” #Phinsup pic.twitter.com/CCGSWKM0t6 — El Capitan (Chris) The Fins Tail Gate (@thefinstailgate) October 25, 2026 Honorable mention: Malik Willis to Caleb Douglas for 63-yard touchdown Caleb Douglas breaks Miami out of second-half struggles. pic.twitter.com/Y2IMny3BT5 — The Phinsider (@thephinsider) October 25, 2026 Free Agent Addition of the First Half Josh Uche, edge The Dolphins’ pass rush has struggled for much of the season, but when they turn it on, they can disrupt opposing quarterbacks incessantly. Uche plays the compliment to Chop Robinson very well, and he has been a solid veteran presence on the defense. He has 34 tackles and three sacks this season, along with one pass defensed, one forced fumble, and one fumble recovery. In a season when Miami’s free agent focus was on one-year contracts with players to get through the season, Uche has come in and performed well. He could be in position to earn a contract extension after the season. Honorable mention: Malik Willis, quarterback MVP of the First Half Chop Robinson, edge I know this is going to create discussion, but the defense is carrying the Dolphins and Robinson is the spark on the defense. He has been inconsistent, but that is true of the entire Miami pass rusher. He has four sacks this year, which puts him at just 29th in the league, but he is constantly in the backfield disrupting opposing quarterbacks. He will bite too quickly sometimes, giving up the edge against the run to chase the quarterback, only to realize the ball was handed off, something that needs to be corrected. But, Robinson is making an impact for the Dolphins, even if the stat line does not always show it. Honorable mention: Ollie Gordon II, running back

full_text: The Miami Dolphins will be without one of their defensive leaders for the remainder of the 2026 season. According to ESPN’s Adam Schefter, Dolphins defensive tackle and team captain Zach Sieler suffered a ruptured biceps during Sunday’s loss to the Detroit Lions and is expected to miss the rest of the season. Despite the injury, Sieler remained in the game and played 49 snaps on defense and special teams. He is expected to make a full recovery in five to six months. Sieler, 31, has been a fixture on Miami’s defensive line since being claimed off waivers from the Baltimore Ravens in 2019. He recorded consecutive 10-sack seasons in 2023 and 2024 and signed a three-year contract extension with the Dolphins in 2025. Sieler recorded two sacks this season, both of which came against the Minnesota Vikings in Week 4. With Sieler sidelined, Miami is expected to lean more heavily on its younger defensive tackles, including former first-round pick Kenneth Grant, fourth-round selection Jordan Phillips, and seventh-round pick Zeek Biggers, all of whom have been part of the defensive line rotation this season. The news also effectively ends any speculation about a potential trade involving Sieler ahead of Tuesday’s NFL trade deadline. Prior to the injury, he was among the veteran players who could have drawn interest from contending teams.
