title: NFL power rankings: Nick’s picks for how teams stack up before Week 10
summary: No. 1 — Buffalo Bills (6-1) | SAME A defensive effort in which the Bills stopped the Vikings’ Carson Wentz-led offense, while Josh Allen and the offense did enough to secure a pivotal road victory against Minnesota. No. 2 — Chicago Bears (7-2) | SAME Caleb Williams started in his typical efficient self, and it […]
full_text: No. 1 — Buffalo Bills (6-1) | SAME A defensive effort in which the Bills stopped the Vikings’ Carson Wentz-led offense, while Josh Allen and the offense did enough to secure a pivotal road victory against Minnesota. No. 2 — Chicago Bears (7-2) | SAME Caleb Williams started in his typical efficient self, and it looked like he could do no wrong, but then he proceeded to throw four interceptions, and the Bears’ offense stagnated for much of the game after taking a 17-3 lead. The Buccaneers made the game interesting, forcing five turnovers, but Chicago held strong and defeated Tampa Bay, 27-24. No. 3 — San Fransico 49ers (7-1) | SAME Brock Purdy went 17 of 25 for 232 yards with a pair of touchdowns to help the 49ers defeat the Las Vegas Raiders, 38-17. The Raiders kept the game interesting up until about half-time, but the 49ers scored two touchdowns in the third quarter to pull away from the Raiders. The defense forced an insane five turnovers. San Francisco remains a top team in the NFL. No. 4 —Jacksonville Jaguars (6-2) | SAME Jacksonville is one of the hottest teams in the NFL, but they faced a Joe Fagnano’s Ravens team that only scored 10 points. Jacksonville won the game 33-10 and Trevor Lawrence only completed 16 passes. The Jaguars are an excellent young football team playing complementary football. No. 5 — Denver Broncos (7-2) | (6th) 📈 1 spot Denver found a way to earn a tough road win, again! Pat Bryant returned from IR and caught a touchdown from Bo Nix. Jonah Coleman continues to dominate touches as the team’s No. 1 back. Coleman had 17 carries for 57 yards and a touchdown in the game. No. 6 — Cincinnati Bengals (6-2) | (6th) 📈 3 spots The Bengals offense is playing very well. Joe Burrow tossed three touchdowns and 271 yards against the Falcons. Ja’Marr Chase caught ten passes for 155 yards with a touchdown. The rushing attack is still a work in progress for Cincinnati, but the Bengals have now won four games in a row, scoring over 30 points in each matchup. No. 7 —Minnesota Vikings (6-2) | (5th) 📉 2 spots The Minnesota Vikings battled the Bills but lost at home to Josh Allen. The Carson Wentz experience was not enjoyable, as he threw several interceptions and could not move the offense. Minnesota still has the best defense — and possibly the best unit overall — but this offense is bad. No. 8 —Kansas City Chiefs (6-2) | 📉 1 spot Kansas City got right against the Jets in a 35-12 victory. Patrick Mahomes completed 23 of 31 passes for 242 yards with a pair of touchdowns, and Kenneth Walker III rushed for over 100 yards with both receiving touchdowns. The Chiefs dominated an inferior opponent. No. 9 — Detroit Lions (6-2) | (8th) 📉 1 spot Detroit went into Miami and won a gritty game that relied on defensive football. Each team turned the football over once, and neither team earned 300 yards on offense. Kudos to Miami’s defense, but the Dolphins were a fish out of water for the Lions in Miami. No. 10 — Green Bay Packers (6-3) | 📈 3 spots The Green Bay Packers demolished the New England Patriots in their home. They forced four turnovers and gained 478 yards of offense. Jordan Love played out of his MIND, completing 23 of 29 for 372 yards and three touchdowns. Few teams are hotter than the Packers right now, and their defense matched their offense in New England. Green Bay did, however, lose running back Josh Jacobs to a broken finger. The Packers still have concerns, but Love is playing at an MVP rate. No. 11 — Seattle Seahawks (5-4) | (SAME Drew Lock is 2-0 this season for Seattle; he completed 19 of 28 passes for 175 yards and a touchdown in this low-scoring 17-3 win over Arizona. Seattle travels to Las Vegas to play the Raiders before going into a bye week. No. 12— Pittsburgh Steelers (6-2) | SAME The Pittsburgh Steelers were on their bye in Week 9. No. 13 —New York Giants (5-2-1) | (15th) 📈 2 spots The Giants continue to win football games because they’re well coached in every phase. The defense pressured and harassed Joe Milton all game, sacking the young quarterback seven times, while Matt Nagy called a fine game for multiple quarterback. Jameis Winston led the only touchdown drive against Vic Fangio’s defense. The Giants earned their first win in Philadelphia since 2013. No. 14 — Los Angeles Rams (5-4) | SAME The Rams defeated Washington 20-13 on the road, but lost their star receiver Puka Nacua in the last play of the game. Los Angeles is a good team that is well coached, but injuries are stacking up, and a lack of offensive playmakers is problematic. They may receive Terrance Ferguson back soon, but Matt Stafford is losing targets weekly. No. 15 — New England Patriots (5-4) | (10th) 📉 5 spots The Patriots were embarrassed by the Packers, 45-27. They’re an injured squad at receiver and Drake Maye tossed three interceptions and was harassed throughout the game. It was a tough look for New England on defense – they surrendered a surprising 478 yards to Jordan Love and the Packers. No. 16 — Houston Texans (3-5) | (20th) 📈 4 spots The Texans came off the bye week and blew the Chargers out, 44-22. C.J. Stroud went nuclear, finishing 21 of 35 for 384 yards with five touchdowns and a pick. Kayshon Boutte went four for 125 and two; Tank Dell four of 105 for one, and Nico Collins four for 55 with one as well. Houston played to their talent against the worst team in the league. No. 17 — Cleveland Browns (5-3) | (16th) 📉 1 spot Cleveland lost 23-22 in overtime. Shedeur Sanders went 19 of 31 for 297 yards with two touchdowns with exceptional individual efforts from Harold Fannin Jr. and KC Concepcion on the two 64 and 39 yard touchdown passes. Tyler Shough turned it on down the stretch of the game and the Saints found a way to secure victory at the end of the game. Cleveland has a decision to make next week – Sanders or DeShaun Watson? No. 18 — Tampa Bay Buccaneers (3-4) | (17th) 📉 1 spot Tampa Bay has won two games in a row and three of four. The Bucs won last week without completing a pass. They’re a power-run team with an opportunistic, well-coached defense, but the Bears withstood a valiant come-from-behind effort. Tampa Bay lost 27-24. No. 19 — Baltimore Ravens (5-5) | (20th) 📈 1 spot Baltimore lost to Jacksonville, 33-10, but they were forced to start Joe Fagnano, who went 10 of 18 for 60 yards. Baltimore had a creative game plan centered around the wildcat, but Jacksonville was too much in the second half. Baltimore traded for Jacoby Brissett, who should start in Week 10. No. 20 — Carolina Panthers (3-5) | (19th) 📉 1 spot Bryce Young played well against a good defense, completing 28 of 39 for 276 yards and three touchdowns, but as the Broncos do – they found a way to win, 26-21. The Panthers are now 3-5 with three straight losses. No. 21 — Las Vegas Raiders (4-5) | (18th) 📉 3 spots The Raiders turned the football over five times, with three of them being Kirk Cousins interceptions. Brock Bowers caught seven passes for 111 yards with a touchdown on eight targets. The Raiders can’t beat a team like San Francisco on the road while throwing three picks and putting the ball on the ground three more times ( two of which were recovered by the other team ). No. 22 — New Orleans Saints (3-5)| (23rd) 📈 1 spot Tyler Shough led a fourth-quarter comeback to force overtime and finished the game 21 of 35 for 265 yards with a touchdown and 51 yards on the ground. Audric Estime, who was on the Browns’ practice squad last week, rushed for 72 yards and a touchdown for the Saints. title: NY Giants news: Trade deadline day, Cam Skattebo should be ‘full-go’, more
summary: Good morning, New York Giants fans! Here are the stories you need to know as the Giants get set to face off with the Washington Commanders this Thursday. John Harbaugh is Giants’ biggest asset in years. Can he lead them on a dream playoff run? | The Athletic “I thought we had good players,” Harbaugh […]
full_text: Good morning, New York Giants fans! Here are the stories you need to know as the Giants get set to face off with the Washington Commanders this Thursday. John Harbaugh is Giants’ biggest asset in years. Can he lead them on a dream playoff run? | The Athletic “I thought we had good players,” Harbaugh said as he was leaving Lincoln Financial Field as the first Giants head coach to win in this building since Tom Coughlin in 2013. “I didn’t really know the personality of the team, but I think what I learned is these guys have what it takes. They’re tough-minded, they’ve got big hearts and they’re willing to do what it takes. Having what it takes means you’re willing to do what it takes, and they’ve been willing to do it. They work, they believe and they don’t flinch.” Giants radio booth on Nabers as a teammate "It's not a ME thing. It's a WE thing." @CarlBanksGIII shares what John Harbaugh told him about Malik Nabers' leadership behind the scenes during their film breakdown. pic.twitter.com/TDXYL28bLR — Bleav (@BleavNetwork) November 9, 2026 Week 9 NFL Takeaways: Giants working the trade market aggressively | SI.com All of that’s enough to give any playoff-starved fan of Big Blue a sugar high. And yet, they’ll tell you this isn’t about going all in on anything, happy as they are with where the team is. No, under Harbaugh, and with holdover GM Joe Schoen, this is now their default setting. Which, they’ll tell you, has little to do with adjusting any sort of preseason expectation. “No, that’s not how we look at winning,” Harbaugh texted me from the team bus, heading back to New Jersey on Sunday night. “You’re never ONE thing away. This is not addition and subtraction. The math is running on multiple levels of formulas and algorithms and humanity. You have to assess your options and opportunities. Seek value. What makes your team better shorter- and long-term and avoid what hinders your team, even in possibility. It’s a case-by-case decision regarding options. The work is on finding and creating the options. That’s where the stones have to get turned over. We are building day-by-day for what’s coming tomorrow and in the future BOTH.” The five things we learned from Giants’ Week 9 win: The trade deadline priority is clear | New York Post The Giants ended their 13-game losing streak at Lincoln Financial Field in Philadelphia with an inelegant but effective 19-11 victory over the Eagles, providing further separation from first place (the Giants are 5-2-1) and last place (the Eagles are 2-7) in the NFC East. Is finding help stopping the run more important than adding a running back at the trade deadline? Buying or Selling Latest Rumors Ahead of 2026 NFL Trade Deadline | Bleacher Report Giants Are Serious Suitors for RB Jonathan Taylor. The Giants could be an aggressive suitor for multiple reasons. They’re in the driver’s seat in the NFC East, and their lead ball-carrier, Cam Skattebo, missed the previous game with a hamstring injury. Furthermore, this season, when healthy, Skattebo has had ball-security issues, and the Giants benched him in Week 6. He has four fumbles in seven outings (six starts). Also, keep in mind that head coach John Harbaugh had workhorse running back Derrick Henry in his last two years with the Baltimore Ravens. Taylor isn’t the physically imposing ball-carrier that Henry is, but the three-time Pro Bowler is a trustworthy running back who can handle a big workload on the ground and help Big Blue establish a physical offensive identity. Verdict: Buy Chris Simms on Arvell Reese Arvell Reese is one of the best defensive players in the NFL 9 games into his rookie year. pic.twitter.com/DWZOJ0rfpm — Chris Simms (@CSimmsQB) November 9, 2026 Like a true defensive weapon, Arvell Reese is everywhere for Giants | The Record In the aftermath of Sunday’s 19-11 victory over the Eagles, the Giants’ first at Lincoln Financial Field since 2013, D.J. Reader added to the list of what makes Reese special: the intense purpose with which he approaches each snap. “Arvell proved yet again what I already knew, and I see it before every game, man,” Reader said. “He’s got this look in his eyes, he’s just ready to play. He’s gonna be special. He is special. I don’t know any young player that can do the things he does. I’m gonna be honest with you: you’ll have to find him. Maybe the kid in Seattle [safety Nick Emmanwori]. Because, you don’t find a kid that can cover the way he can cover. Come down and fill gaps in the run game. Rush the passer. Doesn’t miss tackles. He’s serious, man, and it’s special to watch. It’s very special.” NFL Week 9: Big takeaways, questions and fantasy spin from Sunday’s games | ESPN.com Linebacker Arvell Reese needed only 2.29 seconds to sack Philadelphia’s Joe Milton in the second quarter. It was the fastest time to a sack for a Giants player in the past 10 seasons when Reese got a free run at Milton and forced a fumble. It was part of a monster game for the impressive rookie, who had 12 tackles, three sacks, three quarterback hits, three tackles for loss and the forced fumble. Mandatory Credit: John Jones-Imagn Images | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect A year after making a pair of franchise-altering deals at the NFL trade deadline, the Jets stayed quiet this year. The only trade they made was a minor one, sending backup safety Andre Cisco to the Detroit Lions in exchange for a future sixth round pick. The Jets did not trade defensive end Will McDonald despite McDonald requesting a deal to a new team and other teams reportedly having interest. Sources: The #Jets have received calls for weeks on DE Will McDonald, including past offers involving a Day 2 pick. But the organization still believes in McDonald’s talent and would like to remain patient with his development. pic.twitter.com/XDPRsEyVFF — Jordan Schultz (@Schultz_Report) November 9, 2026 It probably shouldn’t be a massive surprise to see the Jets stay out of the trade market. At 2-7, there would be no way to justify this team being a buyer. At the same time, a coaching staff and possibly front office fighting for its respective jobs might not be willing to give up quality players in exchange for future Draft picks they might not be around to make. So we ended up with a trade deadline that lacked much activity for this team.

summary: The Philadelphia Eagles waived running back Jaydon Blue on Tuesday, according to an official team announcement. Blue also handled kick returns, logging a mere […]
full_text: PHILADELPHIA, PA - NOVEMBER 08: Philadelphia Eagles running back Jaydon Blue #30 runs the ball during the game between the New York Giants and the Philadelphia Eagles on November 8, 2026 at Lincoln Financial Field in Philadelphia, PA.(Photo by Andy Lewis/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images) | Icon Sportswire via Getty Images The Philadelphia Eagles waived running back Jaydon Blue on Tuesday, according to an official team announcement. Blue served as a third-string backfield option behind Saquon Barkley and Elijah Mitchell over recent weeks. The team clearly didn’t trust him to play much on offense, except in garbage time. Blue also handled kick returns, logging a mere 22.3 average. Here’s a recap of Blue’s transactions with the Eagles since the former Dallas Cowboys draft pick originally joined the team: September 1 — Signed to the Eagles’ practice squad October 17 — Signed to the Eagles’ roster October 20 — Waived by the Eagles October 22 — Signed to the Eagles’ practice squad October 28 — Signed to the Eagles’ roster November 10 — Waived by the Eagles Perhaps the Eagles will look to bring Blue back on the practice squad again if he clears waivers. Blue’s departure from the roster could indicate that Tank Bigsby and/or Will Shipley are healthy enough to play again. Both running backs are now eligible to be activated from injured reserve. But with the Eagles on their bye and not practicing until next week, they won’t necessarily be in a rush to open their 21-day practice windows. Between waiving Blue and trading Jordan Davis, the Eagles now have two open roster spots.

The trade indicated that the Eagles are likely committing to Nolan Smith long term, and with Jonathan Greenard healthy, Ebiketie’s playing time was already reduced. title: Eagles News: ESPN says Jordan Davis trade is a disaster for the Jaguars
summary: Welcome to The Linc, the daily Philadelphia Eagles links roundup at Bleeding Green Nation! I really like Jordan Davis. I wanted the Eagles to draft him and I enjoyed rooting for him. But taking what the Jacksonville Jaguars offered for him was a no-brainer. There were people talking about the Eagles potentially getting trade offers […]
full_text: PHILADELPHIA, PENNSYLVANIA - JANUARY 4: Jordan Davis #90 of the Philadelphia Eagles looks on against the Washington Commanders at Lincoln Financial Field on January 4, 2026 in Philadelphia, United States. (Photo by Mitchell Leff/Getty Images) | Getty Images Welcome to The Linc, the daily Philadelphia Eagles links roundup at Bleeding Green Nation! I really like Jordan Davis. I wanted the Eagles to draft him and I enjoyed rooting for him. But taking what the Jacksonville Jaguars offered for him was a no-brainer. There were people talking about the Eagles potentially getting trade offers for Jalen Carter for a similar price of a first-round pick and a second-round pick. To get that for Davis, who is a lesser player who isn’t trusted to play as much as Carter … it’s insane. Howie Roseman clearly overpaid Davis but he’s very good at not doubling down on mistakes and instead making his wrongs right. Well done by the Eagles. Very interested to see how they utilize their draft picks to help spark the next era of success. Let’s get to the Philadelphia Eagles news and links … NFL trade deadline grades: Deals for Jordan Davis, Jessie Bates III, Andre Cisco – ESPN There’s no other way to start this: This trade is a disaster for Jacksonville. The Jaguars are absolutely right to go for it. Entering Monday, they had a 12.8% chance to win the Super Bowl, per ESPN’s Football Power Index, second highest of any team and best in the AFC. And that’s why I was OK with them rolling the dice on Jessie Bates III earlier in the day. A late-round pick for Davon Godchaux, too? Fine. But first- and second-round picks for Davis? Reckless would be putting it mildly. The numbers do not paint a picture of Davis being someone who is worth anywhere near that type of trade compensation. He has played 52% of snaps for the Eagles. That number is not particularly unusual for a run-stuffing nose tackle, but that’s exactly the point: The Jaguars just dealt first- and second-round picks for a part-time player who helps only against the run! There is no world where that is worth it. Davis has a run stop win rate in the 71st percentile among interior defenders this season. He was in the 93rd percentile in 2025 and the 52nd percentile in 2024. This season, he has a 13.5% run stop rate — the rate at which a player records a tackle on a run that resulted in a successful play for the defense by EPA — per NFL Next Gen Stats, 14th best among defensive tackles with at least 100 run defense snaps and just behind former Eagles teammate Moro Ojomo. In other words, he has been a good run defender, not elite. Eagles are stockpiling draft picks through 2029 – BGN The Eagles surprised just about everyone when it was announced that they were trading Jordan Davis to the Jaguars ahead of the NFL trade deadline, but they got a huge return for their defensive tackle, including a first-round draft pick in 2027 and a second-round pick in 2029. Those two acquistions give Howie Roseman 10 total picks in the first two rounds over the next three drafts, 26 total projected through all rounds. That’s insane! Jordan Davis trade grades: Jaguars-Eagles blockbuster as Jags load up for Super Bowl run – SB Nation Philadelphia Eagles grade: A. I am always going to give a big-time writer’s tilt when it comes to teams accepting the position they’re in. When news first emerged that the Jaguars traded a 1st and 2nd for an Eagles DT we all assumed at SB Nation that Jacksonville was getting Jalen Carter, not Jordan Davis. Philly gave up a player they can replace and got a significant return. This was a very smart move for a team that doesn’t have a shot in 2026 and is playing for next year. Their picks in 2027 can help address their much larger need concerns along the offensive line, and simply improve the team from the bottom up — which needs to happen. This is an example of an incredibly well-oiled franchise taking advantage of a team desperate to make an impact. It wasn’t neccesarily a seller’s market on run stopping DTs, but they made it one anyway. Another trade! Jaguars land their defensive game-changer in Jordan Davis – Big Cat Country There’s always a danger in handing out top grades for blockbuster trades. Draft capital matters, and surrendering a first and second-round pick is a considerable commitment. But the Jaguars have a genuine opportunity to do something special this season. They’ve lost important defensive starters to injury, identified the positions that need strengthening and gone out to acquire established NFL talent. Godchaux brings experience. Bates brings leadership and playmaking ability. Davis brings size, power, youth and the potential to anchor the defensive interior for the foreseeable future. Most importantly, these additions complement a roster that was already performing at an exceptionally high level. James Gladstone and Liam Coen clearly believe this team is ready to compete for the biggest prize in football. Rather than sitting back and hoping their existing roster is good enough, they’ve invested heavily in making sure it is. This is what going ALL IN looks like. The Jaguars have made their intentions abundantly clear, and the rest of the league have just been put on notice. NFL trade grades: Jaguars overpay for Jordan Davis while going all in on Super Bowl chase – The Athletic Eagles grade: A+. This is an impressive return for Roseman, and the Eagles are now loaded with future draft capital. They now have two first-round picks in 2027, and two first-round picks in 2028, their own and the Patriots’ pick from the A.J. Brown trade. They also own two second-round picks in 2029. That is a ton of ammunition to use in whatever fashion Roseman sees fit. They could stick and pick. They could trade any of those picks for veteran players. They could package them to move around in the draft. As our Jonathan Jones wrote in our trade deadline live blog, “What the Eagles have now is total optionality.” This clears the way for the Eagles to extend Ojomo, who is on the final year of his rookie deal. It is always difficult to hand out three large contracts to one position group. The Eagles are also paying Jalen Carter a top-of-market contract. They will incur a palatable dead-money charge of $15.4 million for Davis in 2027, according to figures from Over The Cap. Roseman is doing the right thing, turning a losing season into future opportunity. NFL trade grades: Evaluating every deal made ahead of the 2026 deadline – NFL.com Davis has been a good run defender for his career, but his 13.5% run-stop rate this season ranks 14th among DTs with a minimum of 100 run plays defended — behind teammate Moro Ojomo, I should add — with a 1.8 run stuff percentage (T-58th). Last year, before he got paid, was his best season with a 16.5% run-stop rate (fourth among DTs) with a run stuff rate of 4.3%, behind that of DaVon Hamilton, whom he’s essentially been brought in to replace. There is the risk for the Jags. It feels like a knee-jerk reaction to Hamilton’s injury led to a massive overpay. Davis can be a good player, stuff the middle and can provide a little more pop for a nose tackle in the passing game. However, a first-round pick and a future second? We know DTs have been scarce in this market, but paying that much for a run defender is a lot. But what do I know. Maybe DC Anthony Campanile sees something in Davis that he can unlock. Maybe the Jags really just believe that stuffing the run and eating up blockers so they can get to third-and-long is worth that investment. Maybe next to Josh Hines-Allen and Travon Walker we’ll get a better version. Maybe Davis, having heard all the negative chatter about how the Jags overpaid for him, will be motivated and bring a wrecking-ball attitude to Duval and storm his way through the postseason on a mission. For me, that’s a lot of maybes to hang a first- and second-rounder on. Jaguars may plan for Jordan Davis to play more than 52 percent of the time – PFT In nine starts this…

But Thomas and Ridley were never traded and Downs – a popular target of trade rumors – was dealt to KC. — Gerry Dulac (@gerrydulac) November 10, 2026 Downs, of course, was one of the players traded the day of the deadline, heading from Indianapolis to Kansas City with a seventh-round pick for fourth- and fifth-round selections, all in 2027. It’s worth noting the Steelers do not have a fourth-round pick in 2027. Thomas was ultimately not moved by Jacksonville, the league’s biggest buyer at the deadline, despite several months of trade rumors. Steelers beat writer Mike Kaboly reported that the Steelers were interested in Ridley, but were “soured” by the Titans wide receiver’s recent reported “incident” at Nashville International Airport . “Discussions about a trade” can mean a number of things. It’s unclear just how interested the Steelers were in adding to their wide receiver room during the season. However, Pittsburgh could be getting a reinforcement soon in Michael Pittman Jr., who Steelers head coach Mike McCarthy said was “ getting close ” to a return when talking to media on Monday.

full_text: (Photo by Joe Sargent/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Pittsburgh Steelers are 6-2 and sit atop the AFC North, making them a team that would be a prime candidate to make some moves and improve their roster for a playoff push ahead of Tuesday’s 4:00 PM NFL trade deadline. However, the Steelers opted to sit on their hands and decide their current roster will have to be enough to defend their lead in the AFC North. In what feels like a wide-open AFC, teams near the top of the standings all made major moves. The Jacksonville Jaguars, Denver Broncos, Buffalo Bills, and Kansas City Chiefs all made significant moves to improve their roster as playoff contenders. Jacksonville added three players: Safety Jessie Bates and defensive tackles Davon Godchaux and Jordan Davis. The Broncos added linebacker Daiyan Henley in a trade with their division rivals, the Los Angeles Chargers. The Bills acquired the NFL’s leader in interceptions, Amani Hooker, from the Tennessee Titans. And finally, the Chiefs landed wide receiver Josh Downs from the Indianapolis Colts. 6 wins or better AFC teams… Jags got Davis and Bates Broncos got a starting LB Bills got a safety Chiefs get Josh Downs What are the Steelers doing??? — Andrew Fillipponi (@ThePoniExpress) November 10, 2026 To be fair to the Steelers, it was a quiet deadline for much of the AFC North. The only notable deal to come out of the division within the last week was when the Baltimore ravens acquired Jacoby Brissett from the Arizona Cardinals after the injury to Lamar Jackson. The Steelers were one of just two teams in the AFC to have six or more wins at this moment and make no moves at the trade deadline, as the Cincinnati Bengals made no moves ahead of the deadline. The Steelers have a tendency to remain quiet at the deadline under general manager Omar Khan, and this time around was no different. full_text: (Photo by Patrick Smith/Getty Images) | Getty Images For the second time in three weeks, the Pittsburgh Steelers will play a game with first place in the AFC North on the line. They defeated the Cleveland Browns in Week 8 in a 27-6 blowout, and they will now travel to Cincinnati to face the Bengals on Sunday Night Football. While the Week 10 tilt has tremendous playoff implications, it also marks the first time Mike Tomlin will be in the same building as his former team since stepping down as head coach in January. Tomlin is the lead analyst for NBC’s Football Night in America, which will be on site at Paycor Stadium. For many Steelers, this will be the first time they’ve seen Tomlin since the end of the 2025 season, including linebacker Patrick Queen. “If I see him, I’m gonna talk to him,” Queen said via Destiny Sanchez . “Try to let him do his own thing, I’ll do my own thing. Trying to not make it bigger than what it is. Definitely miss him. Definitely a great person, great coach… I haven’t seen or talked to him since the end of [last] season.” Queen is in the midst of his best season as a Steeler, totaling 59 tackles and six stuffed runs in eight games. title: Steelers Week 10 power rankings roundup: Pittsburgh climbs to top 10
summary: The Pittsburgh Steelers entered their bye week as one of the hottest teams in the NFL. full_text: (Photo by Lauren Leigh Bacho/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Pittsburgh Steelers entered their bye week as one of the hottest teams in the NFL. With four straight wins and sole possession of first place in the AFC North, it was getting hard to deny that the Steelers had found their groove. With no game this past weekend, did the NFL media forget about the red-hot Steelers? Let’s take a look around the internet and see if the Steelers lost or gained any respect during their week off in this week’s power rankings roundup. FOX Sports: No.12 (No. 13 Last Week) “The Steelers probably deserved to move up more on their bye week, considering how unimpressive the two teams in front of them looked on Sunday. But they’ll stay outside of the top 10, knowing they have a huge opportunity to jump next Sunday night when they take on the high-flying Bengals in Cincinnati. That’ll be a huge test for their ancient QB, Aaron Rodgers, to see if he can keep up with Joe Burrow, even a little bit. The Steelers defense could cause the Bengals some problems, but the odds are pretty good that if Pittsburgh is going to win, they’ll have to find a way to win a high-scoring game.” – Ralph Vacchiano The Athletic: No.13 (Last Week No.12) “Four straight wins entering the bye have the Steelers climbing our ranking behind a surging defense. The fear was that this season would end similarly to recent ones in the Mike Tomlin era, but Pittsburgh is playing well enough to inspire hope for the second half.” – Chad Graff and Josh Kendall CBS Sports: No.9 (Last Week No. 10) “They come off their bye with a big game for the division lead against the Bengals. Their defense will be challenged by that passing game.” – Pete Prisco Pro Football Talk: No.7 (Last Week No. 8) “Completing the sweep of the Bengals will be critical to winning the division.” – Mike Florio NFL.com: No.12 (Last Week No.12) “Pittsburgh cruised into its Week 9 bye on a roll after dominating the Browns to take control of the AFC North. An even more important test awaits the Steelers in their return to action this week: a prime-time date with the 6-2 Bengals on Sunday Night Football .” – Nick Shook Yahoo! Sports: No.13 (Last Week No. 13) “The Steelers can take a huge step toward the AFC North title. They play the Bengals on Sunday night and will have a big rest edge. They’re coming off a bye while the Bengals will play right after having a game in Spain, which is a tough turnaround. With a win the Steelers will clinch the head-to-head tiebreaker over the Bengals because of a season sweep.” “In the first meeting, the Steelers won 30-27 and outgained the Bengals 411-352. They allowed Joe Burrow to throw for 282 yards and three touchdowns but also got 292 passing yards from Aaron Rodgers, 127 rushing yards from Jaylen Warren and took advantage of a muffed punt and a huge roughing the punter penalty by Cincinnati in the second half. Sunday’s rematch will go a long way in determining the division champion.” – Frank Schwab USA Today: No.13 (Last Week No.13) “First place in the AFC North will be on the line Sunday night in Cincinnati. And the defense has gotten increasingly stingy for a group riding a four-game heater. Should be a fun one.” – Nate Davis ESPN: No.13 (Last Week No. 13) “For the second time in as many games, the Steelers are facing an AFC North opponent with first place in the division on the line. Quarterback Joe Burrow and the Bengals enter the rematch on a heater, while the Steelers will be well-rested after a bye and beat Cincinnati by a field goal in a high-scoring Week 3 game. With two games against the ailing Ravens also on the Steelers’ schedule, a win against the Bengals would go a long way to securing the division title — and earning a top-four playoff seed.” – Brooke Pryor After a bye week, the Steelers did not move down in any of the rankings we observed. In fact, the Steelers moved up in several, even cracking the top 10 in the CBS Sports power rankings. Pittsburgh travels to Cincinnati to take on the Bengals on Sunday Night Football. With a season sweep of the Bengals with the entire nation watching, it will not only strengthen their chances of winning the AFC North for the second straight year, but it will certainly gain them more respect in next week’s power rankings. Both teams are hot, and Pittsburgh is coming off its bye week. Hopefully, the coaching staff has crafted a game plan during the off time and is ready to roll. The trade deadline is a few hours away, and in the AFC, the Jacksonville Jaguars have sent a loud and clear message about their intentions. People are chattering about Joe Burrow as an MVP candidate, and their offense is red hot. A win not only extends their division lead, but sends a message that this team is a force to deal with in January. For a team with many veterans, one last run at a title would be ideal. title: Steelers 2026 mid-season awards: Offensive Player of the Year
summary: Jaylen Warren was our consensus team MVP of the Pittsburgh Steelers halfway through the 2026 season. Considering the position he plays, it wouldn’t be a shock to see him win Offensive Player of the Year, as well. Will he get the clean sweep, or will another top offensive star for Pittsburgh get the crown? Our […]
full_text: (Photo by Michael Owens/Getty Images) | Getty Images Jaylen Warren was our consensus team MVP of the Pittsburgh Steelers halfway through the 2026 season. Considering the position he plays, it wouldn’t be a shock to see him win Offensive Player of the Year, as well. Will he get the clean sweep, or will another top offensive star for Pittsburgh get the crown? Our staff weighs in with our Steelers mid-season Offensive Player of the Year votes. Pittsburgh Steelers 2026 mid-season Offensive Player of the Year Joey Bray – C Zach Frazier: Jaylen Warren’s breakout starts with the way the Steelers offensive line has been playing since Week 3. Frazier has established himself as arguably the best center in the entire NFL this season. The former West Virginia Mountaineer is the top-graded center this season according to Pro Football Focus. The Steelers offensive line is becoming one of the strongest units on the team, and Frazier is the class of them all. Austin Bechtold – QB Aaron Rodgers: I didn’t want to give Warren both awards, so we flipped the NFL model of the quarterback winning MVP and any other offensive piece winning OPOY. Rodgers has been steady and playing very well under Mike McCarthy. He’s thrown for 1,871 yards and 13 touchdowns in eight games at 42 years old. Of his six interceptions, five have either been on tipped balls, passes off receivers’ hands, or while he was being hit on his arm by an offensive lineman. The stats aren’t eye-popping and indicative of how well Rodgers is playing. Zach Frazier and Max Iheanachor are also playing spectacular on the line and Frazier should be voted an All-Pro. Ryan Parish – RB Jaylen Warren: If you’ve been watching this season, it should come as no surprise that Warren is the best skill player Pittsburgh has. Unless some my colleagues decide to put Frazier in this spot and Warren in MVP, I wouldn’t be shocked if Warren is the unanimous selection here. Ryland Bickley – RB Jaylen Warren: Third in the NFL in yards from scrimmage, Warren finally earned a chance as a clear RB1 this year and never looked back. As I’ve written a few times, the Steelers haven’t had a star offensive weapon like this in years. Warren has been essential in both the run and pass game: Yes, he’s on track for nearly 1,500 yards on the ground, but he’s also second on the team in receiving yards and is somehow averaging more yards per grab than DK Metcalf. Mike Nicastro – RB Jaylen Warren: There’s some overlap here, but Warren gets my vote for Offensive Player of the Year as well. Aaron Rodgers deserves consideration. The veteran quarterback has been mostly good throughout the first half of the season and has provided valuable leadership and stability to Pittsburgh’s offense. However, Warren has simply outpaced him in terms of overall offensive impact. Jason Aponte – RB Jaylen Warren: Yes, Warren is the MVP and OPOY. The reasons given for him as the MVP choice apply here, but in critical moments, Warren delivers. Even when Rico Dowdle is involved and Warren’s opportunities shrink a bit, he remains efficient and reliable. Truly a breakout season for the running back. Jarrett Bailey – C Zach Frazier: May be a bit backwards in terms of how league wide awards go, but in the spirit of spreading out some of these awards, Frazier should get the nod for one of them. He’s become the game’s best center, and the Steelers’ run game would not be what it is without him. He should absolutely be the winner of the Protector of the Year when January rolls around. title: Seahawks 2026 trade deadline recap: Seattle stays put, makes no additional moves
summary: After the acquisition of All-Pro offensive guard Quenton Nelson on Oct. 27 seemingly made the Seattle Seahawks’ intentions clear, general manager John Schneider didn’t have the deadline many were expecting. The Seahawks made no additional moves on Tuesday, despite several reports they were actively exploring the trade market. Including projected compensatory picks, Seattle has 10 […]
full_text: After the acquisition of All-Pro offensive guard Quenton Nelson on Oct. 27 seemingly made the Seattle Seahawks’ intentions clear, general manager John Schneider didn’t have the deadline many were expecting. The Seahawks made no additional moves on Tuesday, despite several reports they were actively exploring the trade market. Including projected compensatory picks, Seattle has 10 selections in the 2027 draft , so the lack of movement was unlikely due to a shortage of assets. While the Indianapolis Colts opted to hold onto superstar running back Jonathan Taylor, he was arguably the hottest trade target leading up to the deadline— and the Seahawks were reportedly one of several teams interested. However, NFL journalist Corbin K. Smith later reported Seattle’s interest “started and ended” during their initial inquiry and given the Colts were seeking a return similar to what Christian McCaffrey generated in 2022 (second, third, fourth and fifth-round picks), it should come as no surprise Schneider opted to hold off—especially considering running backs Zach Charbonnet and Jadarian Price recently returned to action. In the midst of Taylor’s name being connected to the Seahawks, Schneider provided additional context on the organization’s approach with the deadline approaching. During his pre-game interview ahead of Seattle’s 34-17 loss to the Chicago Bears on Nov. 2, the longtime general manager said the team remained engaged in the trade market and were actively exploring potential deals—although he didn’t address any potential areas of interest. NFL insider Jordan Schultz reported on Monday the Seahawks were in the market for a wide receiver to complement superstar Jaxon Smith-Njigba, although no deal came to fruition. It remains unknown who Seattle may have inquired about. Despite Seattle’s decision to stay put, the Minnesota Vikings acquired QB Kirk Cousins and the San Francisco 49ers brought in veteran WR Keenan Allen, further strengthening two of the NFC’s best teams. Although the deal for Nelson was Schneider’s lone move, it worth noting he gave up a similar compensation for wide receiver Rashid Shaheed last season —who played a significant role in Seattle’s Super Bowl victory. While the Seahawks have looked like a shell of how they did last year, Schneider’s proven more trades doesn’t always equate to more success.

summary: We’ve reached NFL and therefore Seattle Seahawks trade deadline week, which often promises to have some interesting deals and rarely actually materializes. full_text: We’ve reached NFL and therefore Seattle Seahawks trade deadline week, which often promises to have some interesting deals and rarely actually materializes. Minor or mid-level deals have happened more recently on deadline day itself, so it’s not like we live in a “nothing happens” world. There have admittedly been prominent in-season trades already this year, including the Quenton Nelson and Jeffery Simmons trades just a couple of weeks ago, as well as Joey Porter Jr going to the Dallas Cowboys, and Marvin Harrison Jr heading for the Houston Texans. For the second year in a row, the trade deadline is during Week 10. The Seattle Seahawks are usually active during the deadline, and this year they’ve pulled off one major trade. Will John Schneider cook up another midseason masterclass like he did for Leonard Williams, Quandre Diggs, Carlos Dunlap, and other names from previous deadline deals? Follow Field Gulls’ trade tracker coverage throughout Monday and Tuesday, and we’ll see what the Seahawks will do as they look to get back on track after a sputtering 5-4 start. Have the Seattle Seahawks made any trades during the regular season? Yes. They acquired longtime Indianapolis Colts guard Quenton Nelson for a 2027 third-round pick and a 2028 fifth-rounder. Who could the Seahawks potentially put on the trade block? No one immediately springs to mind. The likes of Dante Fowler Jr have rarely played this year but likely wouldn’t fetch much on the trade market. Emanuel Wilson being an unofficial healthy scratch is worth monitoring, although similarly he’s not much of a valuable trade piece, and Seattle may not want to risk moving any capable RB given the injury concerns on the depth chart. Which positions would the Seahawks potentially be most interested in? Edge rusher and wide receiver might be two positions of need for Seattle. Rashid Shaheed’s injury and generally underwhelming receiving stats could impact what Seattle does at receiver. The edge rushing room is essentially three deep, and with only Derick Hall and Connor O’Toole under contract beyond 2027, there might be some forward thinking required. The New York Jets’ Will McDonald IV has reportedly requested a trade and could be one to watch. When does the NFL trade deadline window close? At 4 pm ET/1 pm PT on Tuesday, Nov. 10. Latest Seattle Seahawks trade news The Seahawks made zero trade deadline day moves. Notable NFL trade news (Nov. 10) Josh Downs is going from the Indianapolis Colts to the Kansas City Chiefs . The Chiefs will give up a fourth- and fifth-rounder and also get a seventh-rounder in return. The Denver Broncos land Los Angeles Chargers linebacker Daiyan Henley for a 2027 fourth- and a 2028 fifth-round pick. Kirk Cousins is going to the Minnesota Vikings for a 2027 third-rounder , which means the Seahawks will not face Cousins this Sunday. Fernando Mendoza figures to make his first NFL start. The Buffalo Bills are acquiring Tennessee Titans safety Amani Hooker and a fifth-round pick in exchange for a second-round pick. The 49ers are trading a 2027 sixth-rounder to the Colts for veteran wide receiver Keenan Allen. The Eagles are trading pass rusher Arnold Ebiketie to the Cincinnati Bengals for a 2027 sixth-round pick. UPDATE: No they’re not . Notable NFL trade news (Nov. 9) WHOA! The Jaguars just traded for Philadelphia Eagles defensive tackle Jordan Davis , giving up a 2027 first-rounder and a 2029 second. The Atlanta Falcons have traded safety Jessie Bates to the Jacksonville Jaguars for a 2027 second-rounder and a 2028 fifth-rounder. The New York Jets have dealt safety Andre Cisco to the Detroit Lions for a 2028 sixth-rounder. The New Orleans Saints have agreed to trade defensive tackle Davon Godchaux to the Jacksonville Jaguars for a 2028 sixth-rounder, which could become a 2027 sixth-rounder.

full_text: The Seattle Seahawks haven’t made any trade deadline day moves as of yet, but their Week 10 opponent just made a significant move at the quarterback position. Kirk Cousins is reuniting with the Minnesota Vikings, with the Vikings sending a 2027 third-rounder to the Las Vegas Raiders. Anyone who watched Carson Wentz’s all-time bad game on Monday Night Football against the Buffalo Bills could’ve seen a QB move coming. Blockbuster! The Raiders are trading four-time Pro Bowl QB Kirk Cousins to the Vikings for their 2027 third-round pick, sources tell @ringer @netflixsports . Cousins returns to Minnesota for the playoff push, while Las Vegas turns to No. 1 pick Fernando Mendoza. pic.twitter.com/3SvmtZu6er — Tom Pelissero (@TomPelissero) November 10, 2026 The big story as this pertains to the Seahawks is the fact that Fernando Mendoza, the 2026 No. 1 overall draft pick, Heisman Trophy winner, and national champion is poised to make his first career NFL start. Mendoza’s only regular season action came against the New England Patriots back in Week 5, when he went 6/8 for 48 yards in garbage time of a blowout loss. The former Indiana star represents the future of the Raiders organization, and now he’s their present after a half-season of Cousins. Alternatively, if Klint Kubiak and company have reservations about starting Mendoza right now, veteran Aidan O’Connell is the other QB on the roster. But it looks like the Raiders are pivoting to the rookie against one of the league’s best defenses.

full_text: JACKSONVILLE, FLORIDA - NOVEMBER 1: Wide receiver Keenan Allen #10 of the Indianapolis Colts catches the ball for a first down while being defended by cornerback Travis Hunter #12 of the Jacksonville Jaguars in the first quarter at EverBank Stadium on November 1, 2026 in Jacksonville, Florida. (Photo by Parker S. Freedman/Getty Images) | Getty Images The 49ers got Keenan Allen. Was it enough? (Paywall) “He’s not Jauan Jennings, but he can occupy a similar role. He’s been employed mainly as a possession receiver, and has excelled on short targets. Crucially, he’s been most effective on third downs. He’s got a +0.33 EPA when targeted on third downs, and has moved the chains seven times. More than 41 percent of his third-down targets turned into first downs. That’s what Jennings did for the 49ers. Now, he won’t be the blocker Jennings was. But, he’s also a much more natural talent than Jennings. He can play anywhere, and I do mean anywhere. He’s a plug-and-play option at any spot. And while he’s not what he used to be, he’s still got some wiggle.” Agent: Brandon Aiyuk plans to play this season, likely with ‘somebody that knows him’ (paywall) “He had an MRI, he had X-rays, he had a physical exam,” Rosenhaus said of Aiyuk, who had a multiligament knee injury in October 2024 and has not played since. “He’s working out on his own, he’s running routes, he’s catching footballs. He says he’s 100 percent ready to play. We’d be glad to go work out for interested teams if he is released by the 49ers….. I think he’s in a really good place. He met with the 49ers. He did a good job in the meeting with them. He said hello to John Lynch. He met with the team. I just feel like he’s in a good place. And getting to know him over the last week, I’m confident in his future moving forward.” How veteran WR Keenan Allen boosts depleted 49ers’ biggest position of need “Allen signed a one-year, $3.32 million contract with the Colts before this season. The 49ers will owe him approximately half of his $1.3 million base salary for the remainder of the season.” 49ers overreactions: Do Super Bowl chances depend on the health of Mike Evans? “Evans missed his second game in a row due to Achilles tendinitis. He might be out even longer, as the 49ers likely agree: They need him healthy for the games that matter the most. He is a unique talent who makes the offense so much better. Evans has the rare ability to be the difference maker.” 49ers practice and media schedule ahead of Week 10 matchup vs. Cowboys “ Wednesday, November 11 12:35 p.m. – Kyle Shanahan press conference 1:30 p.m. – Practice Thursday, November 12 12:30 p.m. – Practice After practice (approx. 2:10 p.m.) – Raheem Morris press conference Following Morris – Klay Kubiak press conference Following Kubiak – Brock Purdy press conference Friday, November 13 12:35 p.m. – Practice After practice (approx. 1:35 p.m.) – Kyle Shanahan press conference.” 49ers trade for Colts’ Keenan Allen to bolster injury-plagued WR room “Coincidentally, if Allen is able to play Sunday, it will mean playing against the Cowboys two weeks in a row. He had four catches for 26 yards against Dallas in Week 9.” Keenan Allen is the newest member of the 49ers “Allen’s air yards per target is the lowest it’s been since 2017. On targets under 10 air yards, Allen has caught 31 of his 38 targets for 230 yards and a touchdown. That’s the seventh-most yards among all wide receivers under 10 yards. The 49ers average 5.29 yards to go on third down. That’s first in the NFL. To me, this is the Niners giving themselves a reliable veteran option underneath on third down. Allen has a couple of drops this season, but 50% of his targets result in a first down, despite a low depth of target. Brock Purdy’s on-target percentage is over 3% higher than Daniel Jones. Same with his catchable passes. Allen has had targets within the last couple of games that were uncatchable, or he had to obnoxiously adjust to. Allen provides a big body who can block from a condensed split. He’s a competitive blocker, which makes it easier to play him on every down.”

That’s a move that creates a roster spot for wide receiver Keenan Allen. Halton is scheduled to have surgery later this week, according to Kyle Shanahan, who said he’d be surprised if Halton returned to the 49ers this season, even if they make a deep playoff run. The Rams signed wide receiver Xavier Smith off the 49ers’ practice squad. Los Angeles had previously let go of Smith earlier this season. He was the team’s primary returner. But injuries to Puka Nacua, not to mention already missing Davante Adams and Jordan Whittington, led the Rams to bring back a familiar face. Smith had been with the 49ers since October 7. He replaced Dante Pettis on the practice squad, who was placed on injured reserve. The transaction wire showed no moves involving Brandon Aiyuk. That’ll likely be the case until Aiyuk’s unpaid roster exemption expires on November 23.

title: Drew Rosenhaus on Brandon Aiyuk: ‘I definitely expect him to play this season’
summary: The San Francisco 49ers are expected to release wide receiver Brandon Aiyuk, a move that could come as soon as the trade deadline passes. Aiyuk’s agent, Drew Rosenhaus, said he felt like he could help Aiyuk, who was in a “no man’s land” situation that was in “limbo.” Rosenhaus spoke about the roster exemption, the […]
full_text: (Photo by Thearon W. Henderson/Getty Images) | Getty Images The San Francisco 49ers are expected to release wide receiver Brandon Aiyuk, a move that could come as soon as the trade deadline passes. Aiyuk’s agent, Drew Rosenhaus, said he felt like he could help Aiyuk, who was in a “no man’s land” situation that was in “limbo.” Rosenhaus spoke about the roster exemption, the potential of the 49ers releasing his client, and that there will be interest in Aiyuk either way. Rosenhaus said, “I definitely expect him to play this season. Judging by the comments of Shanahan, it doesn’t sound like bringing Brandon back. So when the two weeks are over, it’s my job to potentially find a new team for him. And I’m confident, now that he’s healthy, he will play.” Rosenhaus confirmed that Aiyuk hasn’t paid any of the $13 million he owes the 49ers. “That’s something that we’ll work out separate and distinct from the issue of him playing. Hopefully, we’ll work something out to the benefit of Brandon’s, and something that’s fair. That’s also part of my job.” Rosenhaus shared what he would tell NFL teams about his client on Pat McAfee’s show Tuesday morning: I definitely would tell the teams that he has passed many physicals with the 49ers. He had an MRI. He’s had X-Rays. He had a physical exam, and he passed it with flying colors. He’s working out on his own. He’s running routes. He’s catching footballs. He says he’s 100% ready to play. We’d be glad to go work out for interested teams if he is released by the 49ers. As far as me talking to the teams. I think that, in all likelihood, Brandon would probably sign with a team that knows him. That somebody that is somehow affiliated with him, either in college or the 49ers. That’s just my guess. There’s a lot of that in the NFL. You see people connect the dots where there’s history, where there’s relationships. That’s just my assumption. That something like that could happen. A former coach. Maybe a former player that he played with. Somebody that knows him. And I think he’s in a really good place. He met with the 49ers. He did a good job in the meetings with them. He said hello to John Lynch. He met with the team. I feel like he’s in a good place. And getting to know him over the last week, I’m confident in his future moving forward. Well, it’s a good thing Rosenhaus has known Aiyuk for an entire week. Landing on the practice squad feels like the most plausible outcome for Aiyuk. It may take multiple weeks for him to work his way into playing shape, wherever he lands. That could be Washington, but it also could mean Las Vegas with Klint Kubiak. He was the offensive coordinator during Aiyuk’s career year. Maybe it’s Arizona with Mike LaFleur. He was the 49ers’ passing game coordinator in 2020 when the Niners drafted Aiyuk.

ESPN’s Jeremy Fowler said Broncos tight end Evan Engram has garnered interest, but is unlikely to be traded because the Broncos don’t have a replacement. Fowler also said the Jaguars plan to keep Brian Thomas Jr. through the deadline. The Commanders are listening to offers but, per Ben Standig, are unlikely to trade players before the deadline. The Vikings, off a dreadful Monday night performance from Carson Wentz, are making calls around the league for a quarterback. If you’re the 49ers, making a contender better makes little sense, unless Minnesota overpays for Mac Jones. That situation has Kirk Cousins all over it. The Eagles traded away edge rusher Arnold Ebiketie for a sixth-round pick in the 2027 draft. Ebiketie played under Raheem Morris in Atlanta. Albert Breer reported that the Jaguars made a significant offer for Will McDonald before Monday’s trades. Perhaps that’s a sign that the Jets’ asking price for McDonald is too high. Kyle’s update, 10:25 am PT: Surprise, surprise. Adam Schefter tweeted that the Vikings have identified Raiders quarterback Kirk Cousins as a prime trade candidate. Kyle’s update, 11:00 am PT: The Vikings checked in on Mac Jones, but the price was too high. It makes you wonder what the asking price is and what would make the 49ers cave. Here’s who reported that: Minnesota is calling around on QBs all day. The Vikings checked in on Mac Jones in San Francisco, but the price is too high right now. The name everyone keeps coming back to is Kirk Cousins, as @AdamSchefter said. That's the deal league sources think they're really trying to get… pic.twitter.com/qiJbOMwd9C — Dianna Russini (@DMRussini) November 10, 2026 Kyle’s update, 11:38 am PT: The Bills traded for Titans safety Amani Hooker. title: Keenan Allen is the newest member of the 49ers
summary: The San Francisco 49ers have traded for wide receiver Keenan Allen. It’s the second time the team has made a trade with the Indianapolis Colts. The compensation was a 2027 6th-round pick. So, a couple of weeks after the Niners couldn’t land Jauan Jennings, they went after a similar body type and veteran in Allen, […]
full_text: (Photo by David Rosenblum/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images) | Icon Sportswire via Getty Images The San Francisco 49ers have traded for wide receiver Keenan Allen. It’s the second time the team has made a trade with the Indianapolis Colts. The compensation was a 2027 6th-round pick. So, a couple of weeks after the Niners couldn’t land Jauan Jennings, they went after a similar body type and veteran in Allen, who is 34. Allen played the Cowboys in Week 9. He gets to face Dallas again in Week 10. Allen has 40 receptions for the Colts this season for 351 yards and a touchdown. He’s lined up primarily on the outside in Indy, but the 49ers love condensed splits. Allen has lined up in the slot on 26% of his routes this season. During Monday’s conference call, Kyle Shanahan was asked about the last wide receiver the Niners traded for, Emmanuel Sanders, and how he got acclimated into the offense so quickly: “Where he was in his career. He was the number one receiver for the Broncos at the time, had been for the prior four years and was still at that part in his career. He wasn’t just sitting there available on the street. He was the number one receiver on another team who was out of contention and he was looking to go somewhere else. So, it was just different spots.” Allen is long removed from being a No. 1 receiver, but longevity in the NFL should allow him to find his way quicker than most would in the 49ers offense. Per Next Gen Stats, Allen was the only Colts receiver with at least 50 routes run to post a yards-per-route above league average. Allen’s air yards per target is the lowest it’s been since 2017. On targets under 10 air yards, Allen has caught 31 of his 38 targets for 230 yards and a touchdown. That’s the seventh-most yards among all wide receivers under 10 yards. The 49ers average 5.29 yards to go on third down. That’s first in the NFL. To me, this is the Niners giving themselves a reliable veteran option underneath on third down. Allen has a couple of drops this season, but 50% of his targets result in a first down, despite a low depth of target. Brock Purdy’s on-target percentage is over 3% higher than Daniel Jones. Same with his catchable passes. Allen has had targets within the last couple of games that were uncatchable, or he had to obnoxiously adjust to. Allen provides a big body who can block from a condensed split. He’s a competitive blocker, which makes it easier to play him on every down. Injuries have decimated the 49ers this season. Mike Evans has missed two games in a row and is expected to miss a third. Deebo Samuel will return after missing three games. Christian Kirk made it one game before landing on the Injured Reserve. De’Zhaun Stribling didn’t make it out of Week 1. He’s expected to return before the end of the season. And Ricky Pearsall never made it to the regular season.

title: NFL trade rumors: The 49ers are ‘still lingering on the periphery’ for a wide receiver
summary: Sports Illustrated’s Albert Breer had a trade column on Tuesday morning. In the section where he discussed the Indianapolis Colts wanting to make more moves, he mentioned Josh Downs. Breer listed the San Francisco 49ers among three teams still interested in adding a wide receiver: The Chiefs and Steelers have been the prime suitors for […]
full_text: (Photo by Lachlan Cunningham/Getty Images) | Getty Images Sports Illustrated’s Albert Breer had a trade column on Tuesday morning. In the section where he discussed the Indianapolis Colts wanting to make more moves, he mentioned Josh Downs. Breer listed the San Francisco 49ers among three teams still interested in adding a wide receiver: The Chiefs and Steelers have been the prime suitors for receivers, with the Niners still lingering on the periphery. There was a belief from some teams over the weekend that Downs would be moved to Kansas City for a fourth-round pick. And again, the hope, for the Colts, would be that letting this all play out might sweeten whatever deal they get for the tough, resourceful middle-of-the-field target, who’s at the end of his rookie deal. Perhaps there are two Josh Downs, but that is not a player who has been overly impressive in my eyes this season. If you narrow his performance down to the last three weeks, it’s been underwhelming. He’s only catching 63% of his targets despite 90% of those being on target. He’s primarily a slot receiver, but doesn’t have the make-you-miss ability to create after the catch. When I watch, the separation comes from the scheme. In true man-to-man situations, Downs has failed to hold on to the ball in key moments for the Colts. He does not feel like the type of wideout who would raise the bar for the 49ers. We’ll find out by the end of the day if the Niners share those same sentiments. Here’s Breer on another popular wide receiver on the trade market, Jaguars’ Brian Thomas Jr.: One more Jaguars’ note: I don’t think the moves Monday affect their approach with wide receiver Brian Thomas Jr., and I figured they might at first, given Thomas would be a piece they could move to recoup some of the capital lost in the three trades. The reasoning for that is the same I’ve explained the past couple weeks. Thomas isn’t having a great year. He has 10 catches for 117 yards and two touchdowns. He’s playing 43.0% of the team’s offensive snaps, while Meyers is playing 75.41% and Washington is playing 74.59%. But that doesn’t mean he isn’t bringing value. While the third-year pro isn’t a great fit for Coen’s offense, which values the grit, toughness and after-catch production of Washington and Meyers, he does serve a unique purpose—his ability to threaten the defense downfield is unlike what the other two receivers bring, and opens things up underneath for those guys and in the run game. He’s also a good soldier, and so keeping him as a decoy hasn’t proven to be disruptive to the team. The other thing? He’s under contract next year. So in a year in which the Jaguars feel like they can compete at the highest level, the purpose Thomas serves now is more valuable than what might get back selling low on him, particularly when they can trade him after the season, when rookie Josh Cameron might be ready to replace him. Thomas Jr. has four targets in the past three games. He’s not involved in the Jaguars’ plans. Thomas Jr. needs a fresh start. The good news is, with the 49ers, he wouldn’t need to be “the guy.” Watching him run routes and seeing his targets, the speed is palpable. For whatever reason, Thomas Jr. and Trevor Lawrence aren’t on the same page. The timing is off by a split second, and that’s been the difference between him having a couple of catches and 10 during the past month or so. He’s worth buying low on and would be a great fit for Kyle Shanahan’s offense, the way Thomas Jr. can run away from coverage and stretch the field horizontally. Through the first month of the season, Dontayvion Wicks led Philly with 154 yards on downfield targets. He did that on just six receptions. Wicks hasn’t played since Week 6. He’s under contract through 2027. Drops have been an issue during his career, but the talent and skill set make him a fit for the 49ers. If you’re calling the Eagles about receivers, you’d be foolish not to ask about DeVonta Smith. While unrealistic, he’s a WR1 in every sense. Smith has only played four games this season, but he’s one of the most dangerous receivers in the NFL.

title: Kyle Shanahan on the 49ers’ safety rotation: ‘I don’t think we know what the end goal is’
summary: The San Francisco 49ers got back second-year safety Marques Sigle from an ankle injury in Week 9. We wondered how the safety rotation would work. The 49ers shuffled safeties on the first three drives. Malik Mustapha and Ji’Ayir Brown started. On the second series, it was Mustapha and Sigle. On the third series, it was […]
full_text: (Photo by Brooke Sutton/Getty Images) | Getty Images The San Francisco 49ers got back second-year safety Marques Sigle from an ankle injury in Week 9. We wondered how the safety rotation would work. The 49ers shuffled safeties on the first three drives. Malik Mustapha and Ji’Ayir Brown started. On the second series, it was Mustapha and Sigle. On the third series, it was Brown and Sigle. By the end of the game, Mustapha led the way with 38 snaps. Brown played 30, while Sigle played 27. 49ers head coach Kyle Shanahan was asked what the end goal was with the safety rotation. Shanahan said, “I don’t know what the end goal is. We’ve got three good guys that are playing at a very high level, so you just play that until it plays itself out.” Brown had one of the fastest GPS times for any 49ers player in Week 9 when he made a touchdown-saving tackle on a kickoff return. His goal-line tackle of Brock Bowers also saved a touchdown. Mustapha had a pass breakup and an interception. Sigle had three tackles. Each player allowed a reception of at least 18 yards, but that was the only catch they surrendered. Shanahan continued. “Just like Malik hurt his playing time just because of injuries in training camp, and then kind of the same thing happened to Sigle, who was playing at a real high level before he was hurt. Tig’s been the one who’s stayed consistent and healthy. So, all three of those guys have going, I think if two separate themselves way over another then obviously we would keep those guys out there longer. But, we’ll just keep doing it week-to-week, and we’ll see what it ends up, but it’s a pretty good problem to have.” It’s tough to fault the Niners for relying on Brown, given his clean bill of health this season. Week 9 was one of the first, if not only, times this season where a safety didn’t miss a tackle. That’s a good sign. They won’t run into another Brock Bowers, but the safety group will keep getting tested as the offenses they face get tougher in the second half. Will it be the player who makes the most plays, or the combination that makes the fewest mistakes? Which duo do you think gives the 49ers the best chance to win? Let us know in the comments below.

title: Week 10 NFL Power Rankings: Did the 49ers move up after big win over Raiders?
summary: The San Francisco 49ers blew past the Las Vegas Raiders 38-17 on Sunday, taking advantage of the opposing defense while forcing five turnovers in a dominant win. It was a good all-around performance for the 49ers, who remain tied for the NFL’s best record at 7-1 with the Buffalo Bills. After their big win on […]
full_text: SANTA CLARA, CALIFORNIA - NOVEMBER 08: Jaden Dugger #53 of the San Francisco 49ers celebrates with teammates after intercepting a pass and scoring a touchdown during the during the second quarter against the Las Vegas Raiders at Levi's Stadium on November 08, 2026 in Santa Clara, California. (Photo by Ezra Shaw/Getty Images) | Getty Images The San Francisco 49ers blew past the Las Vegas Raiders 38-17 on Sunday, taking advantage of the opposing defense while forcing five turnovers in a dominant win. It was a good all-around performance for the 49ers, who remain tied for the NFL’s best record at 7-1 with the Buffalo Bills. After their big win on Sunday, where do the 49ers rank in the Week 10 NFL Power Rankings? ESPN: No. 2 The 49ers stayed at No. 2 behind the Buffalo Bills in ESPN’s weekly power rankings, which makes sense given that Buffalo beat the Minnesota Vikings on Monday Night Football in a battle of one-loss teams. The top three included the Jacksonville Jaguars last week. That remained the same this week, while the Chicago Bears climbed up one spot to No. 4 and the Denver Broncos fell one spot to No. 5 despite both teams winning. The rest of the Top 10 remained the same, just in a different order. The Kansas City Chiefs stayed put at No. 6. The Cincinnati Bengals bumped up from No. 10 to No. 7 after a 34-17 win over the Atlanta Falcons. The Vikings fell one spot following their loss to the Bills, landing at No. 8. The Seattle Seahawks actually fell one spot to No. 9 after beating the Arizona Cardinals 17-3. And the Detroit Lions also fell one spot to No. 10 after beating the Miami Dolphins. Looking ahead at the rest of the schedule, ESPN believes Week 12 against the Seattle Seahawks is the most important game left on the docket. The Athletic: No. 2 Just like the previous ranking, the 49ers stay at No. 2 here again behind the Buffalo Bills, earning a midseason grade of an ‘A’. “The Niners have the second-best point differential in the NFL (plus-79), and they hardly broke a sweat Sunday in another multi-touchdown game from Christian McCaffrey,” The Athletic’s Chad Graff and Josh Kendall wrote. “His 37 career touchdown receptions are the most by a running back in the Super Bowl era, surpassing Marshall Faulk.” The Broncos remained at No. 3 here, while the Chiefs moved up one spot to No. 4 and the Jaguars moved up one spot to No. 5. Wrapping up the top 10 were the Bears (No. 6), Bengals (No. 7), Lions (No. 8), Packers (No. 9), and Vikings (No. 10). CBS Sports: No. 2 CBS Sports’s Pete Prisco’s rankings did not see a change inside the top five, meaning the 49ers stayed at No. 2 behind the Bills. “They just keep playing as well as anybody in the NFC, despite their many injuries,” Prisco wrote. “Brock Purdy is in the MVP talk.” The Bills, 49ers, Jaguars, Bears, and Broncos remained the top five here, while the Chiefs, Bengals, Lions, Steelers, and Packers rounded out the top 10. Each of those teams moved up one spot, while the Vikings dropped five to No. 11. FOX Sports: No. 3 The 49ers stayed the same as last week here, only that was at No. 3 behind the Bills and the Broncos. “The 49ers clearly fixed whatever it was that happened to them before the bye week when they lost to the Falcons — a game that now looks like a weird blip on their otherwise stellar season,” FOX Sports’s Ralph Vacchiano wrote. “They came out strong and fast, putting the Las Vegas Raiders in their place quickly. “And the fact that they did it without WR Mike Evans made it even more impressive. Of course, that’s what they do best: Overcome injuries. They’re that good and they’re that deep. They still look like they deserve to be the NFC favorites. And they’re clearly the NFC’s best team.” Behind the 49ers were the Chiefs and Bears, who were in the top five last week. Then came the Jaguars, Vikings, Bengals, Packers, and Lions, with Green Bay making a big jump from No. 15 to No. 9.

title: 49ers News: The trade deadline approaches

full_text: Deebo Samuel is ‘on track’ to return; 49ers open to bringing back veteran defensive tackle “Starting cornerbacks Renardo Green (back) and Deommodore Lenoir (foot) are day-to-day. That’s good news, as both avoided serious injuries. Mike Evans is not expected to return this week. The hope is that Deebo Samuel practices this week. As the team gets healthier at receiver, it’ll be interesting to see who loses a job. KhaDarel Hodge, a practice squad member, contributes on special teams. Based on Week 9’s snap counts, Jacob Cowing would be the odd man out.” The key behind 49ers’ 7-1 start? Big contributions from the team’s youth “Kittle said he loved the Niners drafting the older prospects because they “understand the sense of urgency that comes with football.” Indeed, the idea that the rookie class entered a locker room full of players who have been just short of the franchise’s sixth Lombardi Trophy was immediately evident. “Ever since we got here, everybody was trying to talk about how we’re like an old team or whatever, but we knew we have to contribute,” Dugger said. “When I got drafted, they told me you’re not just coming here to sit. Just coming in with that mentality, I feel like we knew we had to contribute early. I feel like we are just trying to do our job with the opportunities we have.” …. “In other locker rooms, the rookies can be the burdens,” Halton said. “For us, man, we got great vets in here, great guys that’s been through any type of adversity. We really just try to glue to them and that happens within the rookies … Getting the ring, that’s the goal every year. But we really want it bad just to do it for those guys, the vets.” Jordan Watkins is earning Brock Purdy’s trust. The 49ers’ WR has every reason to deliver (paywall) “My little sister,” Watkins said of his motivation. “She’s very similar to me. She’s very outgoing. She’s tall. She’s one of a kind for sure, I’ll tell you that much. And she looks up to me. She looks up to me a lot.” Her name is Abrielle. She’s 12 now, a promising softball player who wears the No. 11 because it was her big brother’s number in college. She’s playing up in age on her travel ball team, so now they’re both fighting to prove themselves….He was 8 years old when he watched police take away his mother, Paula Baker. She battled addiction and spent 18 months incarcerated. He didn’t see her for nearly two years. His father had never been a steady presence. The reunion with mom wasn’t easy after she regained custody. He struggled with resentment. Abrielle kept him tethered to the joy life tried to bury. Watson eventually embraced therapy. His mother eventually built a life in recovery. They repaired their relationship, and he developed into a college prospect. He’d already learned how a difficult beginning didn’t have to dictate the ending. A lesson he needed when a high ankle sprain impacted his first NFL preseason. Then a calf strain derailed his rookie campaign….Watkins keeps up with Abrielle’s softball exploits. She’s playing 13-and-under now. He bragged about her recently striking out three batters while pitching against older girls. He smiled in the 49ers locker room as he remembered competing with her. They’d pitch from the mound she’s got in the yard, see who could throw the most strikes. He’d laugh at her precocious moments, listen to her stories and play games. He sees himself in Abrielle. Her ambition. Her competitiveness. The hunger behind the wide smile. Even her occasional preteen stubbornness. “I try to call her and inspire her as much as possible,” he said. ‘Give her as much advice as I can. But, you know, being a kid, sometimes they don’t want to listen.”….His newest motivation is 2 years old. “Once I had my daughter, it kind of transformed into her,” Watkins said. “Just making sure I’m doing what I can do to be able to provide for her. (Make sure she doesn’t live) the lifestyle that I had growing up.” 49ers minutia minute: Deebo Samuel, CJ West expected back; Mike Evans still on hold (paywall) “ Williams didn’t give up a sack in his first six games but has now allowed one in two straight. Sunday’s came courtesy of defensive end Maxx Crosby. Williams blocked him well at first, but Purdy’s initial read wasn’t open and he had to hold the ball longer than designed, allowing Crosby to slip inside for the sack.” Kyle Shanahan provides 49ers injury updates, discusses Brandon Aiyuk “It has same as how I talked last time on him. I was just told that by [executive vice president of communications] Corry [Rush] when I walked in, so it means absolutely nothing to our team. I think we’ve got a two-week roster exemption. That’s all administrative stuff to me.” 49ers vs. Raiders PFF grades: Best and worst from the game, plus snap counts “Left guard Connor Colby earned an 82.7 overall offensive grade, the highest among all offensive linemen in the game. He also posted a game-best 82.4 run-blocking grade across 39 run-blocking snaps. Meanwhile, right guard Dominick Puni led all players with an 87.5 pass-blocking grade. He didn’t allow a single pressure against the Raiders across 34 pass-blocking snaps.” Brandon Aiyuk reinstated by NFL; 49ers have 2-game roster exemption for receiver “San Francisco has three options. It could release Aiyuk, the scenario that has remained the most plausible throughout the offseason. It could trade Aiyuk, which has long been its preferred option, but it hasn’t found a trade partner and the deadline for a deal is Tuesday at 4 p.m. ET.”

title: 2027 NFL trade deadline: Titans trade Amani Hooker to the Bills
summary: All of the reports out there were that Amani Hooker was not available in a trade. Well, it turns out all that meant was that no one had met Mike Borgonzi’s asking price yet. The Tennessee Titans have traded Hooker and a fifth-round pick to the Buffalo Bills. The Titans get a second-round pick in […]
full_text: CINCINNATI, OHIO - NOVEMBER 01: Amani Hooker #37 of the Tennessee Titans celebrates with teammates after intercepting quarterback Joe Burrow #9 of the Cincinnati Bengals during the fourth quarter at Paycor Stadium on November 01, 2026 in Cincinnati, Ohio. (Photo by Jeff Dean/Getty Images) | Getty Images All of the reports out there were that Amani Hooker was not available in a trade. Well, it turns out all that meant was that no one had met Mike Borgonzi’s asking price yet. The Tennessee Titans have traded Hooker and a fifth-round pick to the Buffalo Bills. The Titans get a second-round pick in return from Buffalo. I don’t love the fact that Tennessee had to send a pick back to the Bills to make this happen, but a second-round pick for Hooker is a pretty good return. Robert Saleh has his work cut out for him now that his best player on the defensive line and his best player in the secondary have been traded at the 2027 NFL trade deadline. Hooker was one of the longest-tenured Titans before the trade. He was a fourth-round pick back in 2019. Even though this is his 8th year in the league, he is only 28 years old. This season, he has 5 interceptions, 3 of which were in the Titans’ last game against the Cincinnati Bengals.
