title: 2026 NFL trade deadline: Will the Titans make any more moves?
summary: The Tennessee Titans already made the biggest move of the 2026 NFL trade deadline when they sent Jeffery Simmons to the Chicago Bears for two first round picks. That deal was made a week and a half before the deadline. It felt like that was just the beginning of moves Mike Borgonzi would be making. […]
full_text: NASHVILLE, TENNESSEE - OCTOBER 11: Calvin Ridley #0 of the Tennessee Titans runs with the ball against the Houston Texans at Nissan Stadium on October 11, 2026 in Nashville, Tennessee. (Photo by Andy Lyons/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Tennessee Titans already made the biggest move of the 2026 NFL trade deadline when they sent Jeffery Simmons to the Chicago Bears for two first round picks. That deal was made a week and a half before the deadline. It felt like that was just the beginning of moves Mike Borgonzi would be making. Now, we sit just hours from the deadline, and the Titans have not made another move. There have been plenty of rumors surrounding guys like Amani Hooker, Tony Pollard, and Calvin Ridley, but to this point, those guys are all still in Nashville. That begs the question: Is Borgonzi done? Let’s take a look at the rumored players and see what makes sense as we approach today’s deadline: Amani Hooker Hooker is the most valuable of the three players who have been subject to rumors. He is coming off a 3-interception game against the Cincinnati Bengals. Yesterday, I asked on Twitter if you would trade Hooker for a second round pick. As of this writing, almost 77% said they would. Hooker is just 28 years old and playing at a high level. Borgonzi would probably need two picks, with one of them being on day 2, to move him. Tony Pollard Speaking of guys playing at a high level, Pollard is currently playing his best football as a Titan. He has 5 touchdowns in the Titans’ last two games. The reports out there suggest that Borgonzi doesn’t want to move him because he is important to Cam Ward’s development. That makes sense, but if he can get a fourth round pick or better for an aging running back, he needs to make that move. The thing that complicates this deal a little further is that there are a few running backs rumored to be available. Jonathan Taylor is at the top of the list. The rumors are the Indianapolis Colts are going to move him. Teams could be waiting to see that deal go down before making their best and final offer to the Titans. Calvin Ridley This one is easy to me. If a team calls and offers a pick, any pick, for Ridley, the Titans should take it. He isn’t going to be here after this year, and he hardly gets on the field as it is. When he does get on the field, he beats up every pass that is thrown his direction.

title: What to make of Commanders, GM Adam Peters at NFL trade deadline
summary: The NFL trade deadline has come and gone. The Commanders didn’t do a gosh darn thing. They weren’t buyers or sellers.   You can expect general manager Adam Peters to say on his PAID interview with 106.7-FM in Washington on Friday that Washington took a bunch of calls and never found what the Commanders considered […]
full_text: The NFL trade deadline has come and gone. The Commanders didn’t do a gosh darn thing. They weren’t buyers or sellers. You can expect general manager Adam Peters to say on his PAID interview with 106.7-FM in Washington on Friday that Washington took a bunch of calls and never found what the Commanders considered value. He’ll also say that Week 9’s should’ve-freaking-won-it result against the Rams had nothing to do with his replies to all those calls for the desirable players on the Commanders roster. Can’t wait ‘til that Friday interview, right? Tune on in? Nah, bro. No need. This was the most predictable result, for two reasons. The first: The Commanders didn’t have much to sell. Not after the Daron Payne injury, anyway. The second: Why give up draft picks to fortify a team that sits at 2-5-1 and wasn’t going to win an NFC East title that looks like a Burger King crown? Fair points, both. Y’all generally prefer analysis from Mark or Portis or Jamual over my opinion, but you’re getting it right here anyway. The Commanders should have sold off parts. Even future Day 2-3 picks provide hope over what’s happening this year. I’ll bill this Thursday night matchup with the Giants as something big in future stories, and I honestly think that they’ll win this upcoming game, but is there anything deep down inside of you that thinks this team (with these coaches) can go on a run? They can’t play good football for four quarters, let alone four games. I’ve covered NFL teams for 18 years now, from the Raiders to the Chargers to the Falcons to the Bears and then here. Did you see any perennial playoff contenders in that list? Nope. I know when a team stinks. So sorry, but this one does. And the smell comes from coaching first and talent second. No amount of trade deadline maneuvers could’ve changed that. Not after Laremy Tunsil got hurt. And then Terry McLaurin? I mean, come on. So Peters was at a trident in the road. Buy or sell or do absolutely nothing? Absolutely nothing, in a strange way, might’ve been the right call. Definitely don’t buy and ditch picks. Don’t take crappy value. I’m new to this market and don’t know folks outside of JP Finlay and Nicki Jhabvala (they’re excellent, btw) well. But a tweet (I refuse to call it X) from Grant Paulsen struck me. I’ll just be real quiet and let you read it in full: I don't understand the logic that 5th to 7th round picks don't matter. Here are ways those picks help you. 1) You can draft players that go on to start and thrive. Unofficially, there are 108 starters in the NFL right now who were drafted in the 5th (52), 6th (33), and 7th… — Grant Paulsen (@GrantPaulsen) November 10, 2026 So, every pick counts, just as much as the individual making it. There’s no way the Commanders think they’re still in it, despite the fact the inconsistency thing is clear from miles away. So, back to my earlier point, sell off parts. Though, is there trust in Adam Peters, the dude making the picks? My guy Mark Tyler says there is not and shouldn’t be. What we’ve got here is a mile marker that you can kick on over, a turning point that was actually a straight road. The Commanders are a team that’s no better or no worse, with a coaching staff that may or may not be here next year. I know I’m supposed to create hope or worry about the future of this team to make sure you keep on clicking (that’s what the digital analysts say), but this team is in neutral and stayed that way at the trade deadline. What should the Commanders have done at the NFL trade deadline? Let us know in the comments below:

A lot has to go wrong to only have 2 wins heading into Week 10, and he’s been working on fixing the mistakes that have plagued the team throughout the season. Penalties, especially pre-snap on offense, have been an issue, along with red zone problems. Quinn said they’ve been extra focused on the red zone over the last two weeks, and fixing the penalty issue continues to be a top priority for everyone. The center position has been an issue for the Commanders all season. They released Tyler Biadasz and have been looking for his consistent replacement since then. Lucas Patrick was signed and quickly took over the position, but he’s in the concussion protocol, and won’t be cleared by Thursday night. That leaves a choice between veteran Nick Allegretti, and 6th-round rookie Matt Gulbin who filled in last Sunday after Patrick exited. Quinn confirmed an earlier report that Allegretti was returning to the starting position he was supposed to have locked down before an injury wiped out most of his training camp. title: Should Washington Commanders move Stefon Diggs at NFL trade deadline?
summary: On Monday, Sean McVay indicated that Puka Nucua is likely to be placed on injured reserve following multiple sprains to the ligaments in his knee, and with Davante Adams still on IR, the 5-4 L.A. Rams may now be motivated buyers for a wide receiver before Tuesday’s NFL trade deadline. One of their possible trade […]
full_text: On Monday, Sean McVay indicated that Puka Nucua is likely to be placed on injured reserve following multiple sprains to the ligaments in his knee, and with Davante Adams still on IR, the 5-4 L.A. Rams may now be motivated buyers for a wide receiver before Tuesday’s NFL trade deadline. One of their possible trade targets could be Washington Commanders wide receiver Stefon Diggs. The Rams are looking to win now, but one of their biggest stumbling blocks could be a lack of cap space to acquire a player at the deadline. There are, however, plenty of playoff contenders who need a receiver. Would the Commanders be willing to part with a DMV native they signed during training camp? And at what cost? Diggs is a proven, valuable commodity to the right team. According to Spotrac , since much of Diggs’ contract is tied to incentives, the team acquiring the Commanders wide receiver would only take on a $2.9 million cap hit. Diggs’ skill set and experience also make him a viable replacement for what Sean McVay will be missing while Nucua recovers from injury. Meanwhile, Diggs wasn’t used much early in Sunday’s game and ended up with three receptions on the day. His final catch, with under a minute left, got the Commanders within striking distance of beating the Rams and demonstrated his play-making ability but also caused some frustration for head coach Dan Quinn. In an interview with WUSA9, Quinn expressed how he would have liked Diggs to finish the play differently. Sometimes five extra yards can cost you more than they’re worth. Dan Quinn explained why he wanted Stefon Diggs to get out of bounds on the Commanders’ final drive instead of fighting for extra yards. Quinn breaks down Washington’s final seconds against the Rams. pic.twitter.com/jgunnTWXFz — Marshall Kramsky (@marshallkramsky) November 9, 2026 Diggs has been Washington’s most productive wide receiver this year, with 30 receptions for 303 receiving yards and 5 TDs, but also five drops, which have cost the team at various times during the season. The mercurial wide receiver also incurred a costly unsportsmanlike conduct penalty in Week 1 versus the Philadelphia Eagles. While the Commanders have significant losses of their own at the wide receiver position, at 2-5-1, their playoff hopes hang on the slim possibility they can overtake the Giants and Cowboys to win their division. A recent article floated Diggs’ trade value as a 2027 fourth-round selection, but that seems a bit steep for a soon to be 33-year-old wide receiver with only half the regular season left. The most likely compensation for any offer would be a 5th or 6th round selection. While Stefon Diggs still provides a proven receiving threat and veteran presence, Adam Peters may have to weigh the team’s current season outlook against the possibility adding more draft capital if the LA Rams or another team comes calling before today’s deadline. Barroso/Europa Press via Getty Images) | Europa Press via Getty Images The Daily Slop – 10 November 2026 Editor’s note: Each day, Hogs Haven compiles a collection of articles, podcasts & tweets from around the web to keep you in touch with the Commanders, the NFC East, the NFL and sports in general, with a sprinkling of other stuff. Enjoy! Commanders links Articles Bullock’s Film Room (subscription) Commanders Protection Plan Fails vs Rams Prior to the start of the season, not many people would have expected the Commanders to beat a Rams team consisting of Matthew Stafford, Puka Nacua, Aaron Donald and Myles Garrett. But the Rams were 4-4 entering the game and it was a game very much there for the taking. The Commanders defense held up relatively well, but the offense struggled to get much going after a strong start. One of the biggest issues the Commanders had on offense was the protection plan. The Rams had star pass rusher Myles Garrett back healthy after he missed most of the season injured. It was the first time the Rams had Garrett and star defensive tackle Aaron Donald on the field together. It’s a formidable pair. Donald may well go down in NFL history as the best interior defensive lineman ever and Garrett might well become the best edge rusher in NFL history. Both are freak athletes and are incredibly hard for even the best offensive lineman to block one-on-one. With such a strong pair of defensive lineman, it would make sense to build an entire game plan around preventing those two players from blowing up the entire offense. The last time the Commanders faced Garrett was in 2024, Jayden Daniels’ rookie season. Kliff Kingsbury was the offensive coordinator then and he put together a strong game plan to try and negate Garrett’s effectiveness . They used run plays, read-option plays, run-pass option plays (RPOs), multiple forms of misdirection, screens. Kingsbury also made sure to play with lots of tempo to tire out Garrett and used no-huddle to attack when Garrett wasn’t on the field and stop him from subbing back in. Most importantly, Kingsbury made sure to get a second pair of hands on him on almost every play. They would slide the line his way when they could, but they would always chip him. Everyone had a go at chipping him, receivers, tight ends and running backs. He never knew exactly who was going to chip him on any given play because of how often they switched it up. It was a terrific plan and Garrett failed to register a single stat in the game, which is a large part of why the Commanders were able to win that game back in 2024. Now, this game in 2026 is a different animal because the Rams also have Aaron Donald to worry about. But offensive coordinator David Blough was on Kingsbury’s staff back in 2024 and I had hoped he might have learned some lessons from Kingsbury’s plan to help deal with Garrett. Unfortunately, the protection plan was poor and nothing like that 2024 plan. The two most basic weapons you have in pass protection are chips and line slides. Chips are where you have a tight end, running back or occasionally a wide receiver align tight to the formation and bump the edge rusher before releasing into their routes. Line slides are when either all of the line, or at least part of it, slides to one side, providing extra help to that side. Far too often in this game, the Commanders didn’t use either of these weapons. The Commanders protection plan against Myles Garrett & Aaron Donald simply wasn't good enough. Commanders OLineman were left 1-on-1 against Garrett & Donald without any help from chips or line slides far too often. I broke down the faulty protection plan: https://t.co/uEhFT1rRBt pic.twitter.com/OLnZNNppNX — Mark Bullock (@MarkBullockNFL) November 9, 2026 Sports Illustrated Hughes’ View: The Commanders’ Center Gamble Left Jayden Daniels Exposed Lucas Patrick’s concussion sent rookie Matt Gulbin in against Myles Garrett while Nick Allegretti stayed on the sideline [Washington’s] latest issue on the offensive line stems from the center position: this past weekend, when their starter Lucas Patrick went down with a concussion, they turned to rookie Matt Gulbin. It’s ironic because Adam Peters and Dan Quinn spent the offseason trying to convince everyone that Nick Allegretti was that guy and would be the center for 2026. Allegretti has played two snaps since his last start, which came at right guard against the Seattle Seahawks in Week 3. In other words, he’s still the same journeyman offensive lineman who came here years ago looking for a chance to start, but better suited as a backup. They tried to sell the fanbase a pumpkin, hoping Cinderella logic would kick in and he’d turn into something more than a dried-up gourd that rots on a warm fall night. When asked about the situation Sunday after the game , Quinn said the staff has been working Allegretti more at guard now: “In that moment, I would have felt comfortable with Nick as well, but I thought, let’s give the guy who’s got the most reps.” Quinn also confirmed Allegretti was healthy. It makes sense that the coach would turn to the player who has practiced the most in the role; the problem is he said this in the preseason: “Nick is one of our smartest players, so that’s a position that you rely on.” Relied on so much that when the team looks for a replacement weeks later in crunch time with the season on the line, they turn to the sixth-round prospect with very little experience. Gulbin gave up a 12-yard sack to Myles Garrett on third-and-5 at the Rams’ 38, leaving Washington facing fourth-and-17, but who could be mad at a rookie who should have been given more help on that play? The Commanders’ protection plan failed when it mattered most Sunday. To read more of this article, CLICK HERE Download the SB Nation app Commanders fans, take command of game day! Follow the action and share every cheer, question and instant reaction with fellow fans on the SB Nation app. Chat live during every game Browse with fewer ads Seamlessly move between communities Enjoy faster commenting and posting Download the SB Nation app on iOS or Android . The Athletic (paywall) The Commanders had a sixth-round rookie blocking Myles Garrett. How did we get here? Look, the Commanders didn’t lose to the Rams 20-13 solely because Patrick got dinged up and Gulbin had to replace him, tasked with trying to help block Myles Garrett and Aaron Donald when he hadn’t played in more than a month and had essentially just one game of experience in his NFL career. “It’s an excuse,” Gulbin said afterward. “I got to go out and do the expectations for the center position. I got to go out there and block them. And I don’t think I did a great job.” Credit for self-awareness. The situation is not of Gulbin’s making, and he can only perform the job in adverse circumstances to the best of his ability. But we’re focusing on Gulbin’s participation and Patrick’s injury and Allegretti’s absence because — well, in some way, the center position drove the talk around Washington’s entire offseason. And here it is, November now, with the Commanders’ season on the brink at 2-5-1, and it’s still dogging them as they head into a short week with a season’s-over-if-you-lose game at the New York Giants on Thursday night. This all sounds familiar, and some of it is definitely a rehash of old material. But it matters. It matters because, with the Commanders trailing by a touchdown and facing third-and-5 late in the fourth quarter, Garrett — playing for the first time in nearly two months — came from his position on the edge to rush up the middle. The issue isn’t that a rookie taken in the sixth round came in as an…

title: Future Hogs Week 10: College football players who could help Commanders
summary: Week 10 of college football was loaded with meaningful games that could go a long way to impacting the College Football Playoff. We have to start with No. 1 Miami. They were down their best playmaker, Malachi Toney, and it showed most of the game. No. 11 Notre Dame took an early lead they never […]
full_text: CHAMPAIGN, ILLINOIS - NOVEMBER 06: Collin Dixon #17 of the Illinois Fighting Illini scores a touchdown against the Nebraska Cornhuskers during the second half at Gies Memorial Stadium on November 06, 2026 in Champaign, Illinois. (Photo by Michael Reaves/Getty Images) | Getty Images Week 10 of college football was loaded with meaningful games that could go a long way to impacting the College Football Playoff. We have to start with No. 1 Miami. They were down their best playmaker, Malachi Toney, and it showed most of the game. No. 11 Notre Dame took an early lead they never relinquished. Notre Dame should move up from No. 11 in the Playoff Rankings while Miami will certainly fall. The Holy War between No. 3 Utah and No. 9 BYU was competitive early, but the Utes shut out the Cougars in the second half to get the win. In the SEC, No. 2 Georgia blew out No. 10 Ole Miss on the strength of quarterback Gunner Stockton’s five touchdowns. No. 13 Tennessee leaned on their defense to end No. 6 Kentucky’s hot streak. No. 5 Alabama went into Baton Rouge and won comfortably over No. 14 LSU. In the Big Ten, No. 8 UCLA remains undefeated after beating Minnesota. With the hopes of the playoffs hanging in the balance for both teams, No. 23 Oregon got the better of No. 12 Ohio State. There will be a few interesting matchups in Week 11. After beating Ohio State, USC will travel to Bloomington to face Indiana. Georgia will look to stay on top of the SEC against Missouri, while LSU will try to keep their playoff hopes alive against Texas. Utah will try to remain undefeated against a dangerous Arizona team. Miami will have their hands full against Duke, a team with excellent young talent. Here are a few players who had a good week and might be able to help out the Commanders. Let me know what you think about these prospects and feel free to post players that stood out to you: Caden Veltkamp | QB | Senior | Florida Atlantic He might not play for a Power Four school, but Caden Veltkamp should get more attention. He’s a big, mobile quarterback at 6’5”, 236 pounds. He’s thrown for almost 3,000 yards, 27 touchdowns, and only five interceptions. Veltkamp can stand tall in the pocket, work through his progressions, and deliver accurate passes. He can vary his passes by putting pace on throws or putting air under them so receivers can run under them. He is mobile enough to navigate the pocket or run for positive yardage, but he usually keeps his eyes downfield to make plays. Veltkamp might be a riser once the draft process starts, but he would make a good developmental prospect. Veltkamp completed 17 of 25 attempts for 210 yards and four touchdowns in the Owls win over UTSA. Caden Veltkamp looked great again last night against UTSA. Him and Easton Messer are arguably the most underrated "small school" QB/WR tandem in the FBS right now. Wake up on Veltkamp if you've been sleeping. pic.twitter.com/gSoXbw2vJ3 — Reason (@the_real_reason) November 6, 2026 Dylan Riley | RB | Junior | Boise State Boise State has put countless running backs into the league. Dylan Riley is next up. The junior is not a big back at 5’10”, 203 pounds, but he is incredibly talented. Riley has plenty of burst to and through the line of scrimmage. For his size, he’s strong and able to maintain his balance through contact. The speed is evident once he gets in the open field. Riley can play in either a zone or gap scheme, but I think he’ll thrive with a team that primarily runs zone. In the passing game, Riley can do more than handle checkdown duties. He’ll get open downfield as well as take short passes for long gains. In a win over Colorado State, Riley ran for 192 yards and two touchdowns on 19 attempts and caught two passes for 88 yards and a touchdown. Dylan Riley really went OFF today pic.twitter.com/cD3nR3a2w3 — Cam Mellor (@CamMellor) November 8, 2026 Top 10 Fastest Max Speed | Week 6 T6 | 21.2 MPH Dylan Riley @dylanriley_24 RB Boise State IGA Score™ : 94.8 #ReelSpeed pic.twitter.com/HLBcUWqnfy — Reel Analytics (@RAanalytics) October 12, 2026 Collin Dixon | WR | Senior | Illinois Illinois got a win against Nebraska and Collin Dixon was a big part of that win. Dixon already has broken the Illini record for most receiving touchdowns in a season with 12. Dixon is 6’1”, 215 pounds, and plays like a strong receiver. If there is press man coverage or contact throughout the route, Dixon isn’t phased by it. At the catch point, Dixon has great concentration and strong hands to make difficult, contested catches. The speed looks sufficient to play at the next level, but I’d like to see a little more route diversity and less plays to scheme him open. Dixon had eight receptions for 129 yards and two touchdowns against the Cornhuskers. Illinois WR Collin Dixon is such a monster. At his best playing through contact. Dixon came into tonight No. 2 in the country in contested catches (14) with a 66.7% contested catch rate pic.twitter.com/0eURD2qVMB — Bobby Football (@Rob__Paul) November 7, 2026 Collin Dixon makes @IlliniFootball history 🙌 He sets a new program record with 11 receiving touchdowns in a single season! Watch on FOX pic.twitter.com/2vHJi1JN5m — Big Ten Football (@B1Gfootball) November 7, 2026 Collin Dixon just set a program record with his 12th TD reception of the season for Illinois pic.twitter.com/XFi5uUC5Pb — Underdog CFB (@UnderdogCFB) November 7, 2026 Jacob Harris | TE | Senior | Wisconsin Wisconsin has quietly put together a nice season where they have the same record as Oregon and Ohio State. One reason has been the play of Jacob Harris . He’s an athletic tight end, surprising given he is 6’6”, 265 pounds. Harris has made several acrobatic catches this season. You can’t expect him to be the fastest tight end at that size, but he gets open with good route running. After he gets the ball in his hands, Harris can be hard to bring down. As a blocker, he holds his ground against defenders. However, he needs to improve his ability to stay attached to defenders, especially in the run game. Harris caught two passes for 70 yards and a touchdown in the Badgers win over Rutgers. JACOB HARRIS GROWN MAN TOUCHDOWN #Badgers pic.twitter.com/IZkRmCLJVm — Carter Lowe (@carterl0we) November 7, 2026 Trevor Lauck | OT | Senior | Iowa How does Iowa keep producing quality offensive line prospects? Trevor Lauck is the Hawkeyes’ left tackle, but he might be better suited to play guard in the NFL. Lauck has NFL size at 6’5”, 315 pounds, and he can move well at that size. He is an aggressive blocker who doesn’t want to block his assignments as much as bury them in the ground. Lauck generates movement in the run game, easily works to the second level, and tries to obliterate whomever gets in his way. He is solid in pass protection, but might struggle with speed around the edge because he lacks great foot speed and arm length. Lauck helped Iowa defeat Northwestern by giving up only one pressure and paving the way for 170 rushing yards. Another week and another game of Trevor Lauck putting on a run blocking clinic. Here he gets out in space and burys the DB pic.twitter.com/VenLixYCwL — Draft Capital Podcast (@TheDraftCapital) November 9, 2026 Trevor Lauck taking Washington’s lunch money #BullyBall pic.twitter.com/GrAIDQe5GR — NFL Draft Files (@NFL_DF) October 30, 2026 Yhonzae Pierre | EDGE | Senior | Alabama Alabama’s defense has carried the Crimson Tide in several games. Their edge rusher Yhonzae Pierre deserves a little attention. He looks the part at 6’4”, 251 pounds, with long arms. Pierre’s calling card is his ability to convert speed to power and bull rush blockers. He can also use his quickness to beat blockers around the edge. What Pierre needs to improve is his hand usage. His hands need to land more cleanly on blockers to make the most of both his length and power. He also needs to develop counter moves when his initial rush stalls. Pierre has shown an ability to be effective dropping into coverage when asked to do so.…

title: NFL trade deadline grades: Deals for Kirk Cousins, Josh Downs, Ryan Neuzil
summary: Was getting Kirk Cousins a home run for the Vikings? Did the Chiefs make a smart move to pick up Josh Downs?
full_text:
NFL analysts Ben Solak and Seth Walder are grading deals from the 2026 trade deadline , which passed at 4 p.m. ET Tuesday.

 When grading trades, we evaluate them for each team based on on-field impact, cap implications, draft compensation and effects within the context of a team's overall short- and long-term outlooks. How confident are we in knowing if this is a good or bad decision? And how big is the impact of this decision? Both questions play a role in our grades, though a low-impact decision can still receive a strong or poor grade. Even with lower stakes, clear-cut wins or losses still matter.

 Here are our evaluations for all 18 deals, including three Jaguars trades from Monday, three quarterback moves for teams in need and multiple deals involving at least one first-round pick.

 

 
 Jump to a trade: 
 Neuzil/Vorhees |  Downs |  Henley 
 Hooker  |  Cousins  |  Allen  |  Davis 
 Godchaux  |  Cisco  |  Bates  |  Brissett 
 Simmons  |  Buckner  |  Nelson  |  Harrison 
 Jurgens  |  Porter | McCarthy 

 
 

 

 Falcons trade C Neuzil to Ravens for G Vorhees 
 Ravens get: C Ryan Neuzil 
 Falcons get: G Andrew Vorhees , 2028 sixth-round pick

 Falcons grade: C- 
 Ravens grade: B+

 The Ravens traded for their second center of this deadline season, with Neuzil heading to Baltimore for Vorhees and a late-round pick. It is a surprising and, at first glance, somewhat confusing deal.

 Neuzil is a solid center who ranks in the 57th and 50th percentile in pass block win rate and run block win rate at the position, respectively. He is in the last year of his contract.

 At first glance, it's a little hard to know each team's plan. Cam Jurgens has been struggling since the Ravens acquired him a little over a month ago. Is Neuzil coming in to start over him? Is one of them moving to guard? Or is this just a pure value play?

 The Falcons have so much cap space in 2027 that they are likely to be very active in free agency and therefore unlikely to receive compensatory picks for players lost. Did the Falcons know they weren't going to bring back Neuzil and dealt him to avoid losing him for nothing? That's possible, though I would have thought they would have managed more of a return. But maybe that's what attracted the Ravens -- they saw this as a value play that could net them a profit in terms of compensatory picks with upside that Neuzil could help them now and in the future.

 I don't mind that for Baltimore, especially since the Jurgens deal already is looking like a mistake. But it's a tougher sell for the Falcons. I would much rather try to re-sign Neuzil to a long-term deal (perhaps they did). If they were going to trade Neuzil, was this really the best they could get? And though the Falcons are hardly contenders, this certainly won't help quarterback Michael Penix Jr . down the stretch.

 

 Backup Corey Levin will presumably start going forward. Vorhees figures to be a depth guard for the Falcons as he was for the Ravens. -- Walder 

 

 

 Colts trade WR Downs to Chiefs 
 Chiefs get: WR Josh Downs , 2027 seventh-round pick 
 Colts get: 2027 fourth-round pick, 2027 fifth-round pick

 Chiefs grade: B+ 
 Colts grade: B+

 Downs is free! The slot receiver is out of Indianapolis and now has a chance to be a major part of the Chiefs' offense down the stretch and, perhaps, during a playoff run.

 Downs has recorded 354 receiving yards on 33 receptions this season (1.2 yards per route run) but has recorded 1.7 yards per route run over the course of his career. But as any fantasy football diehard will tell you, Downs has much more potential than that.

 

 Over his four seasons, Downs has a 68 open score in ESPN's receiver scores , which evaluate a receiver's ability to get open on all routes -- not only the ones when he is targeted. And that 68 score means Downs is well above average. Though this has hardly been a guarantee for past Chiefs receivers, it is possible that playing with Patrick Mahomes will unlock a higher level of production from Downs.

 Kansas City is back to being a contender -- the Chiefs entered Tuesday with a 96% chance to reach the playoffs and a 7% chance to win the Super Bowl -- but their offense hasn't felt as if it has reached its maximum potential. The Chiefs rank only eighth in EPA per dropback but have been able to outperform that because of the rushing success of  Kenneth Walker III .

 Both Rashee Rice (35%) and Xavier Worthy (20%) spend time in the slot, but I expect those numbers will drop with Downs, who aligned in the slot 51% of the time in Indianapolis this season, now on the team. Over his career, Rice's numbers have been slightly worse in the slot (2.3 yards per route run) compared with when he's lined up outside or elsewhere (2.8).

 The price here is similar to what the Seahawks gave up last year for Rashid Shaheed who, like Downs, was in a contract year. Perhaps the Chiefs will re-sign Downs as the Seahawks did with Shaheed but if not, they should be in line for a likely compensatory pick given that Kansas City does not have much cap room in 2027. Given the Chiefs' need to augment the offense and status as a true contender, I think this is a worthwhile addition at this price.

 

 As for the Colts, while I wouldn't have been opposed to them signing Downs to a long-term deal given his age (25) and talent, dealing him is quite logical. They are in the midst of a teardown and if Downs left via free agency, they would not recoup this much value in a compensatory pick -- if they even got one. -- Walder 

 

 

 Chargers trade LB Henley to Broncos 
 Broncos get: LB Daiyan Henley 
 Chargers get: 2027 fourth-round pick, 2028 fifth-round pick

 Broncos: C+ 
 Chargers: B+

 The winless Chargers finally decided to trade a player before the deadline, dealing Henley, in the final year of his contract, to the division-rival Broncos.

 It's an interesting deal because linebacker did not look like a particular need for Denver. Alex Singleton leads all linebackers in run stop win rate this season and Justin Strnad is a good coverage player. Henley's numbers are OK this season. He ranks in the 46th percentile and has allowed 0.9 yards per coverage snap (average for the position) per NFL Next Gen Stats.

 I think it's reasonable for Denver to be adding at the deadline, but this is not trivial draft capital to give up for a player who is going to provide depth or be part of a rotation.

 I'm on board with this move for the Chargers. Though Henley could have been a player they kept around given that he will turn only 27 later this month, he wasn't a difference-maker that they had to hang on to. And if he left in free agency, they would not have recouped this value via a compensatory pick even if they had gotten one -- which was also unlikely given their considerable 2027 cap space.

 

 On the other hand, Denver does have a decent change to recoup a compensatory pick if Henley walks, with both Singleton and Strnad signed into 2027 or later (though Singleton will turn 33 next month).

 Some will criticize the Chargers trading a player within the division, but that is foolish. If anything, the teams the Chargers should most want to take draft capital from ought to be other teams in the AFC West.

 

 The only real question for the Chargers: Why didn't they trade more players? -- Walder 

 

 

 Titans trade S Hooker to Bills 
 Bills get: S Amani Hooker , 2027 fifth-round pick 
 Titans get: 2027 second-round pick

 Bills grade: C+ 
 Titans grade: A-

 As the Bills push for a title run, safety was an obvious place for an upgrade. I thought the answer might be Jessie Bates III , but the Jaguars -- arguably Buffalo's biggest threat in the AFC -- traded for the former Falcons safety  Monday.

 After the team released C.J. Gardner-Johnson last week, Damar Hamlin was left playing next to Cole Bishop , with Geno Stone as the third safety. In Hooker, the Titans upgrade from Hamlin and pick up a player who has been having an impactful season…

title: 2026 NFL trade deadline winners, losers: Kirk Cousins, Josh Downs, Bengals, more
summary: Which teams made the best -- and worst -- moves before the NFL trade deadline? We're making sense of all the action.
full_text:
The  NFL trade deadline  has come and gone. I will forever remember it as the trade deadline in which the Bengals nearly accidentally traded a third-round pick for  Arnold Ebiketie  (more on that below). 

 Identifying winners and losers on deadline day is always tough. The Titans, Howie Roseman and Josh Downs  will be made winners and losers for their efforts not by my words but by the picks they make or games they win over the next two or three years. Of course, we can grade the quality of their work now (spoiler, they are winners) -- but this isn't the real test. The real test is what comes next .

 I have six winners and four losers from this year's trade deadline ranging from players to GMs. Let's dive in.

 

 
 Jump to: 
 Cousins  | Jefferson |  Bengals   
 Downs |  Roseman  |  Taylor  | Poles 
  Titans  | Chargers | Cardinals 

 
 

 

 Deadline winner: QB  Kirk Cousins 
 Cousins is about to have a quarterbacking season for the ages.

 No, he won't set the passing touchdown record or anything. But let's trace the arc here.

 Cousins started nine games for a 4-5 Raiders team that was waiting to turn the page to 2026 No. 1 pick Fernando Mendoza . The entire time he started, he comported himself with the exact attitude and perspective you'd hope to see from a veteran bridge starter.

 "If I'm not the best option, then I don't want to be out there," Cousins said in late October after the Raiders' fourth straight loss. "The organization will do what they feel is best, but I feel that Fernando's done a great job and has a bright future ahead. I'm going to try to go out there and play as well as I possibly can to help us win and give him a great example to learn from until he does go out there eventually."

 A beautiful quote. And it echoes what Cousins has said from the beginning: He was in Las Vegas to help the team win but to also give Mendoza an example of how to prepare, speak, compete and perform as an NFL quarterback. If Mendoza looks competent at any part of the 2026 season (and even beyond), Cousins will receive the share of credit due an angel investor. Even if Mendoza was always destined to play well -- he's the first pick, for crying out loud -- Cousins and the Raiders' patient approach with the rookie will be lauded as a contributing factor.

 

 So, Cousins has that going for him. His arc continues to Minnesota where the power of friendship welcomes him with open arms. Cousins was a Viking from 2018 to 2023, the last two seasons of which were spent under head coach Kevin O'Connell. The Vikings went 13-4 in 2022 with Cousins before he tore an Achilles midway through the 2023 season.

 O'Connell's offense isn't just good for Cousins, it's almost built in his image. O'Connell was the quarterbacks coach with Washington in 2017, Cousins' final season on the team. As O'Connell's path split from Cousins, then reunited with him in Minnesota, it has become increasingly clear how much O'Connell's passing game needs a fearless pocket quarterback with the processing speed necessary to handle all the various route adjustments -- not to mention the velocity to hit intermediate throws. Those features have always been the strength of Cousins' game.

 

 Cousins isn't just reuniting with pals, though. He's joining a 6-2 Vikings team powered by the league's best and most unique defense. The bar for Cousins -- who is 38 years old and doesn't have as big of an arm as he used to -- has simply never been lower. Carson Wentz's Monday night performance against the Bills dropped it to the floor. As long as Cousins can keep the offense on schedule and manage the time-of-possession battle, Minnesota's defense can win multiple playoff games. It's that dangerous of a group.

 What else? He gets to throw to Justin Jefferson . That's sick (see below). Cousins could become the first quarterback to start 18 games (the Vikings have had their bye and the Raiders haven't), so he might indeed get to set a record after all. What a season it'll be for Kirk Cousins.

 
 
 Deadline winner: WR Justin Jefferson 
 Is there any individual happier than the Vikings' star receiver right now? No more barely contained frustration on the sideline while cameras follow his every facial expression. A competent quarterback returns to Minnesota -- one who speaks to this day about how throwing the ball near Jefferson is a path to success.

 Since the start of the 2022 season, Jefferson has averaged 2.73 yards per route run on a 27% target rate when Cousins throws him the football. He has a catch rate of 70% and averages 103.5 yards per game. This season, he was at 2.16 yards per route run at a 30% target share -- the efficiency was way, way down -- with 56.1 yards per game. Almost half as much raw production.

 

 He's about to go nuclear with Cousins under center. You can bet the house on that.

 
 

 Deadline loser: Bengals 
 If you have no idea what happened with the Arnold Ebiketie trade and the compensatory pick formula Tuesday morning, don't worry. You've come to the right place.

 Ebiketie is a veteran edge rusher whom the Eagles signed to a one-year deal worth up to $7.3 million in free agency this past summer. Ebiketie was a regular free agent (i.e., not a player released or cut but whose contract expired with his old team), so he matters in the league's compensatory pick formula. Compensatory picks are additional picks awarded to teams at the end of the third, fourth, fifth, sixth and seventh round of the draft, and they are exactly what they sound like: compensation. When a team loses more qualifying free agents than it signs in a given offseason, it is awarded additional picks based on the value of the players it lost.

 Here's a good example. The Packers lost the following players in free agency in the offseason: Malik Willis (who signed a deal worth $22.5 million in average value with the Dolphins), Quay Walker ($13.5 million), Romeo Doubs ($17 million), Kingsley Enagbare ($9 million) and tackle Rasheed Walker ($4 million). The OverTheCap compensatory pick selections, which are run by a guy named Nick Korte (remember the name!), projected those losses to be worth a third, a fifth, a fifth, a sixth and a seventh, respectively.

 

 The Packers signed only one qualifying compensatory free agent on the other side of that scale: cornerback Benjamin St. Juste for $5 million. St. Juste cancels out one of the Packers' incoming compensatory picks -- in this case, it'll be Walker and the seventh, as that's the pick with the most similar value to St. Juste.

 Now that we understand how compensatory picks work, let's take a look at the Bengals. They lost three free agents in Trey Hendrickson , Joseph Ossai and Noah Fant . They signed two in Bryan Cook and Boye Mafe . But when they tried to trade for Ebiketie , they were acquiring a third player who would have counted against them in the compensatory pick formula. He would have canceled out their one outstanding comp pick, most likely the third-rounder they were in line to receive thanks to Hendrickson's departure.

 We know this because Korte posted it to social media shortly after the Bengals' trade for Ebiketie was announced.

 And then, shortly after Korte's post ... it was reported that the Bengals were backing out of the Ebiketie trade.

 There are a few things to say here. The first is that, had the trade gone through, the Bengals would still have been listed as losers because they lost a third-round pick acquiring a depth edge rusher. That was the worst-case outcome for Cincinnati, and the team successfully avoided it.

 

 The second is, even as the Bengals successfully avoided disaster, it is extremely embarrassing to have disaster avoided by a social media post from a cap analyst. The compensatory pick formula is notoriously weird and tricky, but teams have been manipulating it for years now. title: NFL Power Rankings: Stacking all 32 teams for Week 10, plus important games left
summary: How does every NFL team stack up as we hit midseason? We made our 1-32 list and picked key games in the second half of the season.
full_text:
As the old sports cliché goes, "the next game is the most important one." But that's not true for all 32 teams at the midpoint of the 2026 NFL season .

 The NFC North is the first division in NFL history to have every team at least three games over .500 through Week 9. And on the other end, the NFC South made history as the first division with every team two games below .500 through Week 9. So, the intradivisional matchups down the stretch will be crucial in those divisions. And don't forget about the race for the No. 1 pick, which could come down to a Chargers-Dolphins matchup in Week 16.

 In addition to the 1-32 rankings, we asked our NFL Nation reporters to pick the most important game remaining for each team. Their selections ranged from matchups with postseason implications  to ones that might affect a team's draft standing .

 To form the 1-32 list, our power panel of more than a dozen NFL analysts evaluates how all 32 teams stack up against one another. Here are a couple of highlights from this week's rankings:

 
 The Packers have won five of their past six games, including a 45-27 win over the Patriots on Sunday. Green Bay is among four NFC North teams in the top 11 of these rankings, and it should stay there given the potency of its passing attack.  Christian Watson and Matthew Golden now rank third and fourth in the NFL, respectively, in receiving yards. They're the first duo to each rank top four in the league in receiving through Week 9 or later since Tyreek Hill and Jaylen Waddle for the 2022 Dolphins. 
 Speaking of dominant passing attacks, the Texans climbed five spots in our rankings after 100-plus-yard performances from  Kayshon Boutte and Tank Dell  in Week 9. Granted, they faced  the winless Chargers . But Houston quarterback C.J. Stroud  has eclipsed 300 passing yards in three of his past five games. He ranks seventh in Total QBR this season. 
 
 Let's get into the full list, starting with the same No. 1 team from last week .

 

 
 Jump to a team: 
 ARI | ATL | BAL | BUF | CAR | CHI | CIN 
 CLE | DAL | DEN | DET | GB | HOU | IND 
 JAX | KC | LAC | LAR | LV | MIA | MIN 
 NE | NO | NYG | NYJ | PHI | PIT | SF 
 SEA | TB | TEN | WSH 

 
 

 

 1. Buffalo Bills (7-1) 
 Week 9 result: Beat the Vikings 23-6 
 Week 9 ranking: 1 

 Most important game of the second half: Week 16 at the Broncos 

 

 Any game from the Bills' gauntlet between Thanksgiving and Christmas could be the choice, especially the road trip to New England in Week 13 . But the one matchup that could determine the Bills' chances of home-field advantage throughout the playoffs, and potentially force the road to the Super Bowl to pass through the Buffalo winter, is the Christmas Day rematch of last season's playoff loss . That game marked the fifth time in NFL history that the losing team in a postseason game did not punt once, per ESPN Research. -- Nick Suss 

 
 

 

 2. San Francisco 49ers (7-1) 
 Week 9 result: Beat the Raiders 38-17 
 Week 9 ranking: 2 

 Most important game of the second half: Week 12 vs. the Seahawks 

 

 The 49ers have a real chance to earn the NFC's No. 1 seed, so every week matters the rest of the way. But this game represents a great opportunity to stake an early claim to the NFC West. San Francisco is 3-0 in division games so far, and a win here would make it difficult for the Seahawks to catch up. And while the Rams also lurk (and meet the 49ers again in  Week 14 ), San Francisco needs to put the defending champions away before it can worry about anyone else. -- Nick Wagoner 

 
 

 3. Jacksonville Jaguars (6-2) 
 Week 9 result: Beat the Ravens 33-10 
 Week 9 ranking: 3 

 Most important game of the second half: Week 14 vs. the Steelers 

 

 The Jaguars play at Chicago in Week 13  in a matchup of two of the NFL's best offensive playcallers, but the Steelers game is more significant because of AFC playoff seeding implications. The Jaguars have better than a 98% chance of making the playoffs, per ESPN's Football Power Index , so a victory over the Steelers could earn them a higher seed in a tiebreaking scenario. It also would give the Jaguars a season sweep of the AFC North for the second time in franchise history (2017). -- Michael DiRocco 

 
 

 4. Chicago Bears (7-2) 
 Week 9 result: Beat the Buccaneers 27-24 
 Week 9 ranking: 5 

 Most important game of the second half: Week 16 vs. the Packers 

 

 The Bears need to gain ground in their division after early losses to the Vikings and Packers . Chicago's home rematch with Green Bay on Christmas Day carries significant tiebreaker implications and is the first of three straight NFC North games to end the regular season. The Bears will be in good position to defend their division title if they can pick up two NFC North wins over their next six games, beginning with the Lions on Thanksgiving  before the Dec. 25 matchup with the Packers. -- Courtney Cronin 

 
 

 5. Denver Broncos (7-2) 
 Week 9 result: Beat the Panthers 26-21 
 Week 9 ranking: 4 

 Most important game of the second half: Week 16 vs. the Bills 

 

 A road game against the Steelers (6-2) on Black Friday is close, but as things shape up right now, this Bills matchup could have a lot to say about home-field advantage in the AFC if both teams do their part between now and then. The Broncos already have a win over the Jaguars and have split the season series with the Chiefs. The Broncos have faced the Bills in each of the past two postseasons -- a Denver win at home last season and a wild-card loss in Buffalo in the 2024 playoffs. -- Jeff Legwold 

 
 

 6. Kansas City Chiefs (6-2) 
 Week 9 result: Beat the Jets 35-12 
 Week 9 ranking: 6 

 Most important game of the second half:   Week 12 at the Bills 

 

 If the Chiefs want any shot of earning the AFC's top seed, which would include a first-round bye and home-field advantage in the postseason, they'll have to go on the road and beat one of their biggest rivals. A win over the Bills on Thanksgiving night would also boost the Chiefs' odds of passing the Broncos to win the AFC West crown. The Chiefs have played their best this season when at Arrowhead Stadium, averaging 30.0 points per game.  -- Nate Taylor 

 
 

 7. Cincinnati Bengals (6-2) 
 Week 9 result: Beat the Falcons 34-17 
 Week 9 ranking: 10 

 Most important game of the second half: Week 14 vs. the Chiefs 

 

 The Bengals are favored in every remaining regular-season game, according to the FPI. The only game that is close to 50-50? A home game against Kansas City. After last week's results, Cincinnati has a plus-1.2-point differential in a game that carries the highest matchup quality (92.6 rating). The Bengals believe their Super Bowl aspirations aren't a pipe dream. A late-season win against a familiar rival could be what they need to bolster their belief into reality. -- Ben Baby 

 

 
 

 8. Minnesota Vikings (6-2) 
 Week 9 result: Lost to the Bills 23-6 
 Week 9 ranking: 7 

 Most important game of the second half: Week 10 at the Packers 

 

 If the season ended after Week 9, all four NFC North teams would make the playoffs. For the Vikings, that makes every divisional game critical. They put themselves in great position by defeating the Packers and Bears in consecutive weeks to open the season before losing to the Lions in Week 8. So the most important game is always going to be their next NFC North matchup. That happens to be next week. The Packers are playing much better than they did in Week 1, when they coughed up 22 fourth-quarter points to Minnesota. -- Kevin Seifert

 Week 9 result: Beat the Cardinals 17-3 
 Week 9 ranking: 8 

 Most important game of the second half: Week 12 at the 49ers 

 

 The Seahawks already lost to the 49ers in October. That means a season sweep by their division rivals would give the head-to-head tiebreaker to San Francisco, which already has a 2½-game lead in the NFC West standings. The Seahawks will be coming off their bye when they…

title: NFL Week 10 latest intel, buzz questions, fantasy tips, post-trade deadline news
summary: No deals for Jonathan Taylor, Daniel Jones or Brian Thomas Jr.? Vikings seeking QB answers with their Kirk Cousins trade? Here's the latest intel.
full_text:
It's Week 10 of the  2026 NFL season , and the trade deadline is officially behind us. As the dust settles on all the moves, insiders Jeremy Fowler and Dan Graziano have been calling sources around the league for the latest news and notable buzz.

 For the past month, there has been plenty of trade speculation on Jonathan Taylor , Daniel Jones and Brian Thomas Jr ., among others. But none of those players ended up switching teams. Was there ever any momentum? Why did those three big names stay put? One big name who did get traded was Kirk Cousins , and there are plenty of dominoes there. What now for the Raiders, who will turn to Fernando Mendoza ? And does this deal fix the Vikings' offense amid their push to the top of the NFC North?

 Jeremy and Dan share what they're hearing, answer big questions, hand out useful fantasy football nuggets and empty their reporting notebooks heading into Week 10.

 

 
 Jump to: 
 No Taylor, Jones or BTJ deals? 
 Cousins trade fallout for both teams? 
 Fantasy advice  | More notes, intel 

 
 

 Jonathan Taylor , Daniel Jones and Brian Thomas Jr . were arguably the buzziest names before the deadline but didn't move. Why not? 
 Graziano: In Taylor's case, it's because the "buzz" never lined up with the Colts' desire to trade him . Remember, Quenton Nelson , DeForest Buckner and Keenan Allen were all in the final year of their contracts. Taylor is not. He's 27 years old and signed for two more years. They didn't have to trade him. He can be part of the solution next year and beyond. So, they held firm on their price, asking for a first-round pick or some package of picks that would be reasonably equivalent to that. And no team emerged that was willing to give them that.

 The important thing to remember about Taylor is that the Colts never had an interest in moving on from him to just clear salary or be rid of the player. They like him. He's the only one of their prominent veterans who were extension-eligible last summer and actually got an extension. ( Alec Pierce and Jones were free agents, remember.) So while there were talks, I don't get the sense the Colts were ever eager or close to trading Taylor.

 

 Fowler: The buzz around Taylor persisted because of interest from other teams, the franchise's teardown tone set by the Nelson/Buckner trades and the sheer mileage on the player (1,712 carries). But he's a boon in 2027 for any Indy coaching staff. He's also the team's best player. While Josh Downs clearly wanted out , Taylor wasn't as dug in (though I'm sure he would have welcomed the chance to play for a contender). My sense in talking to teams is that Indy wanted at least a first-round equivalent in any package, and interested teams couldn't get there. I believe Denver gave it a run this week but wasn't comfortable with the return Indianapolis was seeking.

 As for Jones, he was likely Minnesota's backup option to Cousins. It's worth noting that the current Colts coaching staff just doesn't seem eager to play Anthony Richardson Sr . and is much more comfortable with Jones despite his struggles. So, I believe that's a factor in all of this.

 Graziano: Jones, who turns 30 next May, will be a decision for the incoming GM and (possibly) next head coach to make in the offseason. He's scheduled to earn $38 million in 2027. None of that is guaranteed at the moment -- $10.51 million of it becomes fully guaranteed if he's still on the roster on the fifth day of the 2027 league year in March. If Jones finishes the season playing well, and the team can legitimately talk itself into the idea that he'll be better next year further removed from his Achilles injury , that price could make him an attractive option. If not, Indianapolis can cut him without too much pain. It would take on $35.2 million in dead money cap charges in 2027, but that's not as intimidating a number as it used to be.

 Fowler:  Thomas, meanwhile, garnered significant interest, but in the end the Jaguars, a true contender, didn't want to subtract . They only wanted to add. And they value Thomas, though his numbers don't reflect that. He has speed that demands defensive attention.

 Graziano: Thomas doesn't look like an important player for the Jaguars anymore when you check the box score, but look around the league. The Rams are almost out of receivers . The 49ers have been scrambling to fill those spots all season. Injuries happen, and if something should happen to Jakobi Meyers or Parker Washington , the Jaguars believe Thomas is a player who could help them if he suddenly got thrust into a higher-volume role. The Jaguars are very clearly thinking about getting the top seed in the AFC and winning the very next Super Bowl. Maintaining quality depth at premium positions is important.

 

 Fowler: What's tough about Thomas' situation is he hasn't caught a pass in a month, and my sense is the player would have welcomed a fresh start had a trade happened. But that's a lot of talent on which to give up. Thomas was, quite easily, the most gifted athlete on the field when I visited Jaguars training camp. So, while Taylor staying in Indy was a matter of the Colts' high demands, I don't think that was the case with Thomas. The Jaguars could have gotten a quality pick for him. They just didn't seem interested in moving him, even though he could have helped recoup some of the lost capital from Monday's flurry of trades .

 But Jacksonville should probably try to find a way to get Thomas involved more. It will need him in January.

 

 
 What now for the Vikings and Raiders after Kirk Cousins was traded to Minnesota? 
 Fowler: Cousins is comfort food for Minnesota. He's predictable. And more importantly, he's predictable in Kevin O'Connell's offense. He removes at least some unknown variables that could derail a promising season. Kyler Murray hadn't proved to be a fit in this specific scheme (which could have been detected back in, say, March ), and Carson Wentz was just bad. In fact, had Wentz simply played passable football Monday night , I'm not so sure Minnesota would have stretched draft capital to get quarterback help. Murray would have been back from injury eventually and perhaps Minnesota could have adjusted to his skill set.

 But Monday night was dire, so it's time to salvage the season with a quarterback who knows the system and played well in Las Vegas. Cousins is essentially a half-season option with a chance to re-sign. His $10 million roster bonus in 2027 is guaranteed. He has a two-year, $80 million extension that kicks in on the fifth day of the new league year, effectively serving as a poison pill. The Vikings most likely won't pay that, but they can either pay him $10 million to walk away or repackage it in a new deal.

 What the Vikings do at backup quarterback will be fascinating. Either Murray or Wentz can serve as QB2. There's also the option to release one or place one on injured reserve. (Murray already has an injury, and Wentz appeared to hurt his throwing hand Monday night.) Either way, QB1 is solidified, at least for a half-season. And Minnesota didn't have to give up a top-two-round pick to make it happen.

 Graziano: I agree with you and honestly don't believe that the Vikings wanted to trade for a quarterback. They believed Murray would play better than he did in Week 8 in Detroit and obviously didn't know he'd get injured in that game. And Wentz played considerably worse Monday than anyone in the Vikings' building thought he would. So they spent the early hours of Tuesday morning examining the landscape and what was possible, looking at options that included Cousins, Daniel Jones and Geno Smith .

 From what I have been told, the Raiders weren't looking to trade Cousins, who has played well for them and allowed them to hold off on playing  Fernando Mendoza  as long as possible. The Vikings had checked in on Cousins last week to get a sense of what it might cost if they decided to go down that road, but they didn't get the sense…

title: Super Bowl LXI odds: All 32 teams' odds to win the championship
summary: Every NFL team's win total, as well as odds to win the division, the conference and Super Bowl LXI.
full_text:
The NFL trade deadline has passed and a flurry of moves around the occasion have caused some shifts in futures odds. The Jacksonville Jaguars made three big moves on defense by acquiring safety Jessie Bates III  and defensive tackles  Davon Godchaux and  Jordan Davis , which prompted a jump from +850 to +750 to win the Super Bowl, placing them third on the odds board behind only the San Francisco 49ers (+540) and Buffalo Bills (+600).

 

 The Chicago Bears continue to look like true Super Bowl contenders and are just behind Jacksonville at +800 in the title odds. Chicago had moved from 14-1 to 12-1 after acquiring All-Pro DT  Jeffery Simmons , then further to +950 after defeating the reigning champion Seattle Seahawks (16-1) in Week 8. BetMGM recently reported a $100,000 wager on the Bears to win the Super Bowl at +700 odds, a potential $700,000 net payout.

 Chicago is approaching lock territory for the playoffs at -800, per DraftKings odds, but its division rivals in the NFC North -- the Detroit Lions (-330), Minnesota Vikings (-270) and Green Bay Packers (-200) -- are all also odds-on to play in the postseason. Minnesota made arguably the biggest move of deadline day by (re)acquiring quarterback  Kirk Cousins , shortening their Super Bowl odds from 24-1 to 22-1.

 Meanwhile, the Los Angeles Rams , who began the season as big +500 title favorites, are all the way out to 13-1 and are now underdogs to make the playoffs at +110. L.A. fell to those odds following news that superstar wide receiver  Puka Nacua  will be placed on injured reserve due to knee and toe injuries, as well as to make room for improving teams in the NFC.

title: Fantasy buzz: Malik Willis placed on IR, are there any Dolphins you should start?
summary: What does the Miami Dolphins' fantasy football outlook show with starting QB Malik Willis placed on IR?
full_text:
Everything that happens in the NFL has additional context when viewed from a fantasy football perspective. From position battles to injuries and so much more, the news cycle will constantly affect player values.

 Our fantasy football buzz file, with contributions from our ESPN fantasy writers and our NFL Nation reporters, aims to provide fantasy managers with the intel they need as news breaks around the league.

 

 Nov. 10: Malik Willis placed on IR 

 By Michael F. Florio 

 The Miami Dolphins placed Willis on the IR Tuesday due to a groin injury , and he will miss a minimum of four games.

 Willis has averaged 13.1 fantasy PPG while throwing 1,396 yards, six touchdowns and six interceptions. He has run for 232 yards and three touchdowns. While he disappointed in fantasy last week against the Detroit Lions , he was trending upwards having thrown five of his six touchdown passes in the past four games.

 With Willis out, that leaves Kyle McCord as the Dolphins starter. Not only will that be his first career start, McCord has not thrown a pass in the NFL. Willis was a potential streaming option due to the matchup, but that does not apply to McCord.

 

 Additionally, fantasy managers should avoid the Dolphins pass catchers. Malik Washington had been a safe-floor flex option with Willis while Caleb Douglas has flashed his upside at times. Both could be benched -- or even dropped if you have a roster crunch -- until we see that they can produce with McCord. Ollie Gordon II is the only Dolphin that should be started in fantasy football for the time being. Gordon has averaged 13.2 fantasy PPG since Week 3 and the Dolphins have the second-best remaining fantasy RB schedule.

 The Indianapolis Colts D/ST has struggled to find any sort of fantasy success this season, but are in play as a streaming option this week due to the matchup.

 
 Nov. 10: Cook helps Bills overcome tough Vikings defense 
 

 By Michael F. Florio 

 Despite a valiant effort by the  Minnesota Vikings ' defense, the Buffalo Bills ' offense won out on Monday night.  James Cook III  was the lone standout performance, rushing 31 times for 107 yards and a touchdown. Only Jahmyr Gibbs has run for more yards against the Vikings this season. Cook finished with 16.7 fantasy points, enough to be the RB8 for the week. His 31 carries are the second most in any game in Cook's career.

 Josh Allen had his worst fantasy night of the season, finishing with only 12.86 fantasy points. He threw for just 234 yards, with one touchdown and one interception. He also ran the ball six times for 15 yards. That was actually the most fantasy points any QB has scored against the Vikings since Jordan Love in Week 1 (19.48). Allen has a bounceback opportunity next week against the  New York Jets .

 Other notes from Monday's game 

 
 Buffalo's pass catchers were largely held in check. DJ Moore saw only five targets, catching three for 25 yards. In his four full games this season he has a 26% target share and a 41% air-yard share, averaging 14.3 fantasy PPG. 
 Dalton Kincaid caught all three of his targets for 28 yards. He has a rebound opportunity next week against the Jets, who have allowed the fourth-most TE yards. 
 Khalil Shakir led the Bills with four catches for 58 yards. He's a "safe floor" option who can be used in deeper leagues or as an injury/bye week replacement. 
 Minnesota's offense was a slog all night.  Carson Wentz   struggled to make competitive throws all night long, finishing just 8-of-25 for 81 yards, no touchdowns and two interceptions. He also lost a fumble. Wentz was replaced by  Max Brosmer  for the Vikings' final drive, with the team down by three scores. 
 Justin Jefferson  did see 11 targets, but was able to reel in only three of them for 58 yards. He has now finished with single-digit fantasy points in four of his last six games. He's averaging a career-low 56.1 receiving yards per game. It's not his fault, but the team's QB play has dragged him into "boom or bust" WR3 territory! Fantasy managers have to be hoping the Vikings trade for a quarterback. 
 Given the current state of the Vikings' passing attack, fantasy managers cannot trust either  T.J. Hockenson or Jordan Addison . Hockenson finished with 33 yards, while Addison had 28. 
 Jordan Mason led the Vikings with 48% of the team's snaps, Aaron Jones saw 35%. Mason turned eight opportunities into 42 yards, while Jones had six touches for 21 yards. Neither has reached seven fantasy points in the three games since Mason's return. Both can be benched until we see them produce. 
 
 
 Nov. 9: Nacua likely headed to IR 
 

 By Michael F. Florio 

 Puka Nacua is likely to be placed on the IR due to MCL and PCL sprains .

 There is no replacing Nacua on the Rams roster or on fantasy waiver wire. Konata Mumpfield , Jordan Whittington and Tutu Atwell will be the Rams' top receivers. With Davante Adams also on the IR, it wouldn't be a surprise to see the Rams trade for a wide receiver before tomorrow's NFL trade deadline.

 If they do not, expect the tight ends and running backs to be more involved. Tyler Higbee should be added off waiver wires. Also, Terrance Ferguson was set to return last week before suffering a hamstring injury. He should see a lot of volume if and when he is able to return.

 This likely means running back  Kyren Williams will see even more targets. Both he and Blake Corum should be started next week against the Cardinals.

 For those in need of waiver wire targets, check out Eric Karabell's Week 9 waiver wire article .

 
 Nov. 9: Cardinals lose Wilson for the season, await word on Minshew 
 

 By Michael F. Florio 

 Michael Wilson is out for the season due to a neck injury , the team announced Monday. Wilson had established himself as the Cardinals' WR1 and as someone fantasy managers could trust on a weekly basis, but he can now be dropped when waivers run this week. Arizona is extremely thin at receiver after losing both Wilson and Kendrick Bourne to the IR and having traded away Marvin Harrison Jr .

 Devin Duvernay , Simi Fehoko and Reggie Virgil  are the receivers still on the active roster. Zay Jones , James Proche II and Shedrick Jackson are on their practice squad. This likely means more targets and even more defensive attention for Trey McBride . He is the lone Cardinal that is a must-start fantasy option.
